home_pitcher_note: In his one start against Arizona last season, Harang allowed one earned run and six hits with eight strikeouts over eight innings for a no-decision on July 8, won by the Reds, 4-3. This will be Harang's third consecutive Opening Day start.
away_pitcher_note: Webb will be making the third Opening Day start of his career. An Ashland, Ky., native, he grew up a Reds fan and will have a large contingent of family and friends on hand to mark the event.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo led the club in quality starts (22) despite leading the team in losses. His 210 2/3 innings pitched were second to ace Aaron Harang. Reds batters scored two runs or less in 15 of his 34 starts, including four shutouts. On May 6 , Arroyo took a 3-1 loss after he allowed three earned runs on 11 hits in a game at Chase Field.
away_pitcher_note: Haren will make his D-backs debut after being acquired by Arizona in an eight-player deal with the A's in December. The right-hander tied for the American League lead in games started (34) last season and was third with a 3.07 ERA. This will be Haren's second start at Great American Ball Park, and he has made three career appearances against the Reds with a 1-1 record and 5.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: A non-roster invite to Spring Training, Cueto pitched his way into the rotation with a sensational camp that had his team, the opposition and scouts buzzing. This from a 21-year-old that started the 2007 season at Class A ball. At three levels, Cueto was 12-9 with a 3.07 ERA in 161 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis was diagnosed with thyroid cancer last week and will make his first two starts of the season before undergoing surgery April 10. The left-hander posted a double-digit win total for the fourth year in a row in 2007. Davis had a habit last year of working his way into and then out of trouble. One thing you can usually count on from Davis is innings. Last year he worked six or more frames in 19 of his 33 starts and was 11-4 with a 2.30 ERA in those games. Davis has plenty of experience against the Reds from his days with the Brewers and is 6-2 with a 3.40 ERA in 14 career games against them.

home_pitcher_note: The overall numbers for 2007 weren't pretty, but September was sparkling. After going 0-4 with the Braves, Redman bounced around the Minors until joining the Rockies in September. In five games, including three starts, Redman went 2-0 with a 3.20 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Owings struggled throughout the spring with his command. Last year, he made the team as the fifth starter and wound up making 27 starts and two relief appearances. Owings doesn't have overpowering stuff, but overcomes it with competitiveness.

home_pitcher_note: Francis received a fortunate do-over. He was trailing the Cardinals, 5-1, in the bottom of the third on Wednesday when rains hit and washed away the game. Francis had given up an Albert Pujols home run and had walked five -- one shy of his career high. The struggles came out of nowhere for Francis, who had a 3.00 ERA in Spring Training. Francis enters his first official start of 2008 in a place where he is comfortable. he is 26-13 with a 4.36 ERA in 50 starts at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Webb's numbers during Spring Training were not pretty, but he looked to be in midseason form on Opening Day against the Reds. The right-hander allowed two runs over six innings in a 4-2 D-backs win. It was Webb's first Opening Day win in three tries. He's known for his devastating sinker, but has developed his curve and change to the point where he can use both at any time in the game. He particularly likes to go with them when he has two strikes on a batter. Webb posted better numbers in 2007 than he did during his NL Cy Young Award season in 2006, but finished second in the balloting to San Diego's Jake Peavy.

home_pitcher_note: Going into last season, the Rockies thought Morales was their top pitching prospect but they didn't expect him to make the Majors. Injuries forced the Rockies to summon him late in the season, and it turned out swimmingly. Morales, however, struggled with fastball command and pitch selection this spring, but his talent and his power fastball justify his inclusion on the staff to begin the season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will start the year in the rotation as the club takes things slowly with Randy Johnson, who is recovering from his second back surgery in as many years. Gonzalez's ability to both start and work out of the bullpen made him a valuable part of the staff last year. It's a role he figures to fill again once Johnson returns in mid-April. Gonzalez doesn't throw hard, but has a good feel for pitching and changes speeds effectively.

home_pitcher_note: Haren made his D-backs debut last Wednesday and aside from one inning in which he allowed three runs on a pair of homers, he was impressive. Haren was acquired by Arizona in an eight-player deal with the A's in December. The right-hander tied for the AL lead in games started (34) last year and was third with a 3.07 ERA. In two career appearances against the Rockies he is 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Loaiza, who was tagged with the loss after pitching 2 2/3 innings of relief in the rain-delayed Wednesday-night loss, makes his first start of the year after being skipped the first time through the rotation. Although he won the competition against Chan Ho Park in part because of a guaranteed contract, his 4.50 spring ERA was decent enough for a fifth starter.

home_pitcher_note: Davis was roughed up by the Reds in his first start of the year last Thursday in Cincinnati. The left-hander allowed just three runs (two earned) but he walked six and allowed a total of 10 baserunners in 3 2/3 innings. Davis was diagnosed with thyroid cancer last week and this will be his final start before undergoing surgery April 10. Davis posted a double-digit win total for the fourth year in a row in 2007. Davis can usually be counted on for innings. Last year he worked six or more frames in 19 of his 33 starts and was 11-4 with a 2.30 ERA in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley makes his first start of the season after two unexpected relief appearances. He was scratched from his scheduled debut last Wednesday before the first pitch because of a rain forecast, relieved for one-third of an inning only for rain to interrupt play for 74 minutes, then was called on in relief again Friday night in San Diego for two scoreless innings. He is 4-1 with a 2.36 ERA lifetime against Arizona and was 2-1 against the Diamondbacks last year.

home_pitcher_note: Owings put his Spring Training struggles behind him in his first outing of the year against the Rockies on Friday. The right-hander was masterful as he allowed just one run on two hits in 6 2/3 innings. Owings had good command of his fastball -- something he lacked during the spring -- and was able to hit both sides of the plate with it as well as elevate it when he needed to. Owings won one of the team's most important games of the year when he beat the Pirates in an emergency start Sept. 27 in Pittsburgh. Owings doesn't have overpowering stuff, but his competitiveness seems to allow him to overcome that.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda's Major League debut was pretty special, as he held down the Padres, allowing only a solo homer to Brian Giles in seven innings. He struck out four without a walk and made only 77 pitches. Kuroda's out pitch is his splitter, but his fastball touches 93 mph and he uses both sides of the plate.

home_pitcher_note: Webb put to rest the question of whether he could beat the Rockies, allowing just two runs (one earned) on five hits over seven innings on Saturday night in Denver. Webb, who had struggled against the Rockies in 2007, put together his second strong start of the young season. On Opening Day against the Reds, the right-hander allowed two runs over six innings in a 4-2 win. It was Webb's first Opening Day win in three tries. He's known for his devastating sinker, but has developed his curve and change and can use both at any time in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Francis struggled against the Diamondbacks on Saturday, letting up five runs on 12 hits and a walk in 6 1/3 innings.  It was an improvement over his Opening Day washout, when five runs and five walks in 1 1/3 innings were expunged from the record, but it was not enough to satisfy the ace or keep his team in the game. He was especially vulnerable to the longball, giving up three home runs, two after getting ahead of the hitters 0-2 and 1-2, and the third on a 3-1 pitch when his changeup cut back over the plate.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a season of firsts for Haren. He made his first start in Chase Field his last time out and was impressive in allowing three runs over six innings. The right-hander said he got chills taking the mound for the first time in front of a packed house in Arizona's home opener. Haren made his D-backs debut April 2 and aside from one inning where he allowed three runs on a pair of homers, he pitched well. Haren was acquired by Arizona in an eight-player deal with the A's in December.
away_pitcher_note: Morales held the Diamondbacks scoreless on two hits in six innings on Sunday in his first start of 2008. He did struggle with runners on base and faced a lot of two-out traffic, but throughout the outing he hit his spots with a fastball that ranged from 91 to 93 mph. He showed no fear pitching inside to right-handed hitters. This will be his first appearance at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez continues to impress the organization with his flexibility. The right-hander has been a band-aid of sorts for the pitching staff over the past year, pitching in a variety of roles. He figures to be a member of the rotation for a while with Doug Davis headed to the DL. He made his first start of the year last Sunday in Denver after going nine days without pitching and showed no signs of rust as he allowed just one run over five innings. He did not get a decision in the game, which Arizona won in 10 innings. Gonzalez doesn't throw hard, but has a good feel for pitching and changes speeds effectively. He is incorporating a cut fastball more this year and his curveball has improved.
away_pitcher_note: Cook pitched a gem Monday, matching Tom Glavine in an efficient pitchers' duel as the Rockies took their first win at Coors Field. Cook gave up a pair of hits and a run in the first inning, but retired 20 of the next 21 hitters he faced, allowing only one walk the rest of the way as he pitched seven innings on 73 pitches. His good sinker earned 15 groundouts, and he took advantage of an aggressive Atlanta lineup on a cold Colorado night, attacking the bottom of the strike zone and inducing early swings from the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is coming off the best start of his Major League career, having blanked San Diego on three hits for six-plus innings last Wednesday. Sanchez, who throws his fastball in the low-90's, relied largely on his sinker and slider to subdue the Padres. Sanchez struggled against the Diamondbacks last year, posting an 0-2 record with a 12.60 ERA in three appearances.
away_pitcher_note: In a game that will be Webcast for free on MLB.TV without blackout restrictions in Arizona, Johnson will make his first Major League start since June 28, 2007. Johnson underwent his second back surgery in as many years in early August last year, and while his rehab went well, he was around two weeks behind the other pitchers when Spring Training began. The team was extra cautious with him, and he made two Minor League rehab starts for Triple-A Tucson. His last outing was Tuesday night, and he accomplished his goal of getting six innings and 85 pitches in. When he was healthy last year, Johnson showed he could still be an effective pitcher, going 4-0 with a 1.52 ERA in a five-start stretch from May 15-June 10.

home_pitcher_note: Correia's the Giants' No. 5 starter, but he looked like an ace against St. Louis last Thursday when he worked 7 2/3 shutout innings. Still mildly weakened by a case of food poisoning, Correia lacked his full velocity, but steadily worked the Cardinals low and outside to subdue them. Correia's 0-1 with a 2.95 ERA in 10 lifetime appearances against Arizona, mostly in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Owings is proof that Spring Training doesn't mean much. After scuffling for much of the spring, Owings has been outstanding in his first two regular-season starts. In his first outing of the year against the Rockies, he allowed just one run on two hits in 6 2/3 innings. Owings had good command of his fastball -- something he lacked during the spring -- and was able to hit both sides of the plate with it as well as elevate it when he needed to. Then against the Dodgers, Owings helped the D-backs complete a sweep with a 4-3 win. In that game, he allowed three runs on seven hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Although Zito has lost each of his starts, he has pitched progressively better in every one. Last Friday, he was leading St. Louis, 2-1 in the fifth inning, when an error by second baseman Ray Durham paved the way for three unearned runs on an Albert Pujols homer. Continuing to show he's not an automatic out at the plate, Zito also stroked his first hit of the year. He's 2-3 with a 2.73 ERA lifetime against Arizona, including 1-2, 3.93 last year.
away_pitcher_note: Webb has put the issue of whether he can beat the Rockies to rest. Two of the right-hander's three wins this year have come against Colorado. In his most recent start last Friday at Chase Field, Webb held the Rockies to two runs over eight innings of work. It was his second straight start against the team that he had a 5.77 ERA last year. In the first one, he allowed just two runs (one earned) on five hits over seven innings at Coors Field. On Opening Day against the Reds, the right-hander allowed two runs over six innings in a 4-2 D-backs win. It was Webb's first Opening Day win in three tries. He's known for his devastating sinker, but has developed his curve and change to the point where he can use both at any time in the game.

home_pitcher_note: Arizona gave up a lot to get former Oakland ace Dan Haren, and the early returns have met the club's high expectations. Haren has tossed a quality start in each of his three games with Arizona, posting 16 strikeouts against three walks. Haren has yet to go more than six innings, but he did so 20 times last season. Because of Thursday's off-day, Haren will throw on five days' rest. He has never faced San Diego in his career.
away_pitcher_note: On a 95-degree day at Dodger Stadium on Sunday, Maddux looked none the worse for wearing, needing just 68 pitches to get through five innings. Maddux was efficient, throwing 40 strikes and allowing just one walk. He struck out two and relied heavily on his defense to make plays behind him. Maddux allowed just two hits, and Khalil Greene saved a run by smothering a ball up the middle with a runner on second base in the fourth inning to save a run.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez pitched well in his first start, but scuffled the next time out against the Rockies. Gonzalez lasted just three innings as it turned out he was trying to pitch with an infected tooth that caused him to be lightheaded and dizzy at times. The right-hander had dental surgery the following day and the club does not expect it to affect him going forward. His first start of the year occurred in Denver against the Rockies and he allowed just one run over five innings. He did not get a decision in the game, which Arizona won in 10 innings. Gonzalez doesn't throw hard, but has a good feel for pitching and changes speeds effectively. He is incorporating a cut fastball more this year and his curveball has improved.
away_pitcher_note: Young (1-1) allowed a home run to Dodgers leadoff hitter Rafael Furcal on the second pitch that he threw in a nightmare of a start on Saturday at Dodger Stadium. Young struggled with his fastball command, walking four in three innings, all while allowing six earned runs on seven hits. Young allowed three hits to right fielder Andre Ethier, including a two-run home run in fourth inning. Ethier now has four hits, including two home runs, in just five at-bats off Young this season.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson made his first start of the year last Monday in San Francisco and allowed three unearned runs in five innings. It was his first Major League start since June 28. Johnson underwent his second back surgery in as many years in early August last year and while his rehab went well, he was around two weeks behind the other pitchers when Spring Training began. Johnson threw 90 pitches in the game and struggled with his fastball command and uncharacteristically walked four. When he was healthy last year, Johnson showed he could still be an effective pitcher by going 4-0 with a 1.52 ERA in a five-start stretch from May 15-June 10.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf picked up his first victory as a Padre, tossing 6 2/3 no-hit innings in his last start against Colorado on Tuesday. Wolf allowed a two-out single in the seventh inning to Brad Hawpe that broke up the no-hitter. He finished the inning, allowing just the one hit with four walks and nine strikeouts. Wolf had a lot of success with his fastball up in the strike zone, though he got a lot of mileage out of his curveball and changeup. It was his first victory since June 28, when he was pitching for the Dodgers. He developed shoulder problems thereafter and needed minor surgery in September.

home_pitcher_note: Owings is proof that Spring Training doesn't mean much. After scuffling for much of the spring, Owings has been outstanding in his first three regular season starts. In his first outing of the year against the Rockies, he allowed just one run on two hits in 6 2/3 innings. Owings had good command of his fastball -- something he lacked during the spring -- and was able to hit both sides of the plate with it as well as elevate it when he needed to. Then against the Dodgers, Owings helped the D-backs complete a sweep with a 4-3 win. In that game, he allowed three runs on seven hits in seven innings. Finally against the Giants last Saturday, he allowed just one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Correia has worked at least six innings in each of his three starts and has allowed opponents to hit only .225 against him. After allowing Arizona five runs in six innings last Tuesday in an 8-2 Giants loss, Correia insisted that he felt better than he did in the start before that, when he blanked St. Louis for 7 2/3 innings. Correia will definitely pitch carefully to Arizona's Chris Young, who has three hits off him -- all home runs -- in eight career at-bats. Correia is 0-1 with a 3.29 ERA lifetime at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Webb has put the issue of whether he can beat the Rockies to rest. Two of the right-hander's three wins this year have come against Colorado. In his most recent start last Friday at Chase Field, Webb held the Rockies to two runs over eight innings of work. It was his second straight start against the team that he had a 5.77 ERA against last year.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Zito started 0-4 was 2005. He still finished that year with a winning record (14-13) for Oakland while posting the American League's second-lowest opponents' batting average (.221), ranking third in innings (228 1/3) and fifth in strikeouts (171). Zito had the misfortune of bumping heads with Arizona ace Brandon Webb last Wednesday in a 4-1 loss at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe pitched with a bull?s-eye on him against the Braves, getting struck three times by comebackers. His sinker was a little too active, as he walked four in 4 1/3 innings, but it didn't sink when Chipper Jones launched a three-run homer to center field. Two of the five runs against him were unearned because of Jeff Kent error.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has been outstanding since coming over in a trade from the A's during the offseason. The right-hander is 3-0, but he could easily be 4-0 if the D-backs bullpen had held onto a lead in the season's second game. In his last outing, Haren tossed seven shutout innings in a 9-0 win over the Padres. The D-backs have provided Haren with early run support as they've scored 11 times in the first inning over his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley was overpowering for four innings against the Braves with nine strikeouts, but he lost his command in a 35-pitch fifth inning that included three walks. In this one against the D-backs, he'll be looking to avenge an April 8 loss in Phoenix, when he allowed five runs in only 2 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The D-backs scored too late in Gonzalez's last start to get him off the winless list, but he pitched credibly for six innings in Saturday's 10-3 win over San Diego, holding the Padres to four hits. The 25-year-old has a track record for being consistently better on the road than at Chase Field, where he has been victimized for 15 of the last 21 homers he has allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf picked up his second victory of the season by allowing four runs over 6 1/3 innings against Arizona on April 20. Wolf, who walked just one and had seven strikeouts, allowed one run on two hits over the first six innings before running into trouble in the seventh. His fastball command and his changeup were the pitches he relied upon the most against Arizona. This start came on the heels of Wolf tossing 6 2/3 no-hit innings in his previous start against Colorado. Wolf's next start will be against these same D-backs at PETCO Park, where the ball doesn't travel nearly as well.
away_pitcher_note: Breaking down the numbers suggests the Big Unit hasn't pitched badly in his first two starts, but Johnson is anxious for a big W to confirm his comeback. He's gone without a win for 10 1/2 months, the longest stretch without one in his career. Johnson was breezing along against the Friars on Sunday until Justin Huber's three-run homer led to a five-run sixth that helped result in a 9-4 loss at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Germano couldn't continue his early-season success in his fourth start of the season, as his 1.35 ERA ballooned to 5.01 after he allowed five runs in the first inning -- and 10 runs altogether -- in a 3 1/3-inning outing against the Houston Astros on Monday. The Astros feasted off Germano's mistakes and took full advantage of pitches up in the strike zone. The 10 earned runs (on 10 hits) were the most Germano has allowed in his career. He allowed the first seven batters to reach base before getting an out.
away_pitcher_note: Arizona's double threat (still working the stick for a .308 average) goes for his fifth win in as many starts -- which would put him nearly two months ahead of his rookie pace of last season, when he didn't win No. 5 until June 20. This will be his first appearance of 2008 against the Padres, whom he didn't beat in three 2007 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy failed in his second bid for victory No. 4 in his last start on Tuesday against the Astros, allowing four runs in six innings, with two home runs to former Padre Geoff Blum and a two-run shot by Hunter Pence that erased a Padres lead. Peavy felt like the home runs were byproducts of a ballpark that favors hitters, calling it "Williamsport distance." Either way, he'll get a shot at the Diamondbacks for the first time this season. No National League team hit Peavy as well as the Diamondbacks did last season, as his ERA was 3.86 in five starts, though he struck out 16 Arizona hitters in an April start in Phoenix that ended in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Webb is off to his typical hot start. The right-hander started the 2005 season 6-0 and opened the 2006 campaign with franchise-best 8-0 mark. His last outing against the Giants was a bit of a struggle for him as he allowed three runs over six innings, but he hung in there to pick up the win as the D-backs held off the Giants, 5-4, at Chase Field. Webb won the NL Cy Young Award in 2006 and finished second in the voting last year to the Padres' Jake Peavy, his opponent in this finale of a three-game series.

home_pitcher_note: Haren had a bit of a rough outing against the Dodgers his last time out as he allowed six runs -- five earned -- in just 4 2/3 innings. The Dodgers made the right-hander work hard early and simply wore him down. Haren threw 29 pitches in the first inning, 21 in the second and 26 in the third. Though he felt good coming out of the bullpen to start the game, Haren did not have his usual good command and that combined with the patient approach by the Dodgers proved to be his undoing. Haren was acquired by the D-backs from the A's in an eight-player deal in December.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson avenged his poor outing against the Rockies with a stellar start versus the Reds on Wednesday, allowing two runs over seven innings with a walk and six strikeouts. Sampson was efficient, needing just 88 pitches. The right-hander said he worked on several things in between his shortest start of his career and this one, including working to avoid flattening his sinker, which hurt him in his prior outings. He's trying to stay back on his back leg and drive more toward the plate. Sampson made two appearances versus the D-backs last year, allowing six runs over a combined 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez picked up his first win of the year in his last start on Wednesday as he allowed three runs on seven hits over 5 1/3 innings at Dodger Stadium. The D-backs prevailed, 6-4. His first start of the year came in Denver against the Rockies and he allowed just one run over five innings. He did not get a decision in the game, which Arizona won in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cassel likely earned himself another start by performing well during his Astros debut on April 24 in Cincinnati. The right-hander yielded three runs over five innings and held the Reds scoreless through his final three frames. Cassel is not a hard-thrower, but he's consistently in the strike zone and gets quick outs. His effort vs. the Reds resulted in his second career big league win.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson had his finest outing last time out against the Padres at PETCO Park. The Big Unit picked up career win No. 285 by allowing just one run over six innings. Johnson has now made three starts since beginning the year on the disabled list due to back surgery and he appears to be rounding into form. His fastball picked up a couple mph's last time out and he seemed to have better command of it.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon has produced a quality start in each of his five outings with nothing to show for it. The right-hander walked six in his last start on April 25 against the Cardinals, but held them to two runs and took a no-decision when the Astros came back to win, 3-2. Chacon faced the Diamondbacks in one relief appearance in 2007, allowing one earned run over two-thirds of an inning. In his career, Chacon is 2-6 with five saves in 18 games against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Owings may not make this start depending on how his sprained right ankle responds to treatment. If he is not able to go, Webb will start here and the team will plug Owings back in at some point. He hurt the ankle in his last start when he doubled and rolled the ankle when he stepped on the bag and had to leave the game. Owings wasn't at his best for the first time this year in that outing last Saturday against the Padres. The right-hander struggled with his command in the second inning as he hit a batter and walked three during a four-run San Diego rally.
away_pitcher_note: Maine threw 100 pitches in five innings against the Braves Saturday. One was wild, and allowed a run to score. He also allowed a run in the first before finding some sense of rhythm. He has yet to complete the seventh inning in his five starts, and, after a Spring Training which prompted teammates to anticipate a special season, he has yet to have a special outing.

home_pitcher_note: Webb just keeps rolling right along. In his last outing against the Padres on Sunday, he allowed one unearned run over six innings as he outdueled Jake Peavy for the 2-1 win. Hot starts are nothing new for Webb. The right-hander started the 2005 season 6-0 and opened the 2006 campaign with franchise-best 8-0 mark. Webb won the NL Cy Young Award in 2006 and finished second in the voting Peavy last year.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's most recent start, Friday night against the Braves, was his least effective. He walked three of his first five batters and surrendered nine hits �- including a two-run home run by Kelly Johnson -- in 5 1/3 innings. He is winless in his two most recent starts, having allowed nine runs and 19 hits in 10 1/3 innings. He has taken two steps back since pitching seven shutout innings against the Nationals on April 15.

home_pitcher_note: The former A's right-hander has combined with Brandon Webb to create one of the top one-two punches in the National League. In his last outing, Monday night at home in a 5-3 victory over the Astros, Haren went 7 2/3 innings and was perfect for the first four before allowing two runs on three hits and two walks in the fifth. Manager Bob Melvin said afterward that Haren had his best stuff of his six Arizona outings. In that game he also had an RBI double, giving him two runs driven in this season. Haren was obtained from the A's on Dec. 14 in an eight-player deal that sent six prospects to Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: The only hits Santana allowed in his 5 2/3 innings against the Pirates on Tuesday in his most recent start were two home runs, the sixth and seventh he has surrendered in 40 1/3 innings. The first, by Nate McLouth, was the first allowed by Santana in the first inning in six starts this season. He surrendered 10 in first innings last season, when he led the American League in home runs allowed with 33.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer made his Major League debut Tuesday night and it's one that few who watched will forget. The right-hander was summoned from the bullpen with two outs in the third and proceeded to retire all 13 batters he faced. Scherzer, who was the D-backs' No. 1 pick in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, struck out seven and his electric fastball reached 98 mph at times during the dominating performance. Scherzer takes Edgar Gonzalez's spot in the rotation. He throws a slider and changeup in addition to the fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer gave the Phillies 5 1/3 innings in his last outing, Wednesday against the Padres, but he was hurt by the long ball -- a pair of them, to be exact. Moyer gave up nine hits and four earned runs while throwing 98 pitches, 62 for strikes. It was only the second time in six starts that he surrendered more than three earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson scuffled in his last outing against the Astros, allowing six runs on nine hits over four innings. That came on the heels of his best outing of the year when he beat the Padres at PETCO Park for career win No. 285. Johnson allowed just one run over six innings in that game. He has made four starts since beginning the year on the disabled list due to back surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey provided another flawed but, in a perverse way, impressive start Thursday night against the Padres. He allowed 11 base runners in six innings, but held the Padres' less-than-fearsome offense to one run. He had pitched effectively three times in his five most recent starts -- a 1.74 ERA in 20 2/3 innings -- but has one loss and two no decisions in the three games. Call it growing pain, but he does seem to be making progress.
away_pitcher_note: Webb became the Major Leagues' first 11-game winner with his second successive effective start, holding Pittsburgh to one run and three hits over seven innings and driving in a run during the Arizona Diamondbacks' 3-1 victory on June 6. The right-hander has permitted only one extra-base hit -- Jason Bay's RBI double while giving up nine hits and one run in 16 innings over his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Santana doesn't expect the bruised left shoulder he suffered Friday in San Diego to interfere with his next assignment. The off-day Monday benefits him in that regard. He allowed one earned run in six innings (100 pitches). The one unearned run was the result of his throwing error. Since he lost his first Shea Stadium start, he has a 3-0 record -- and the team record is 4-0 -- in four starts. He pitched to no decision against the D-backs in Phoenix May 4, allowing one run in six innings in a Mets victory.
away_pitcher_note: Haren received a no-decision in his last start at Pittsburgh on Saturday. He pitched seven innings and allowed three runs and five hits. The right-hander struck out six and walked one. He admitted that he didn't have his best stuff, but he battled for seven innings in a game the D-backs won, 4-3.

home_pitcher_note: Davis wasn't nearly as effective in his fourth start since having surgery to remove his cancerous thyroid gland. Davis, making his 20th career start against Pittsburgh, took a 1-0 lead into the fourth only to allow six of the final eight batters he faced to reach base in a 6-4 loss to the Bucs on Sunday. Davis lasted 3 2/3 innings and gave up five runs on seven hits and four walks.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has not won in four straight starts after a 5-1 getaway. On Sunday at Yankee Stadium, he gave up four runs and six hits in five-plus innings. Not too bad, but not good enough in a 6-3 loss. Greinke returns to Arizona where he had one of his most bizarre games. On June 10, 2005, he surrendered a franchise-record 11 runs and equaled a club record by giving up 15 hits. But he also hit a home run, his first big league hit, and oddly enough had no pitching decision because the Royals came back before losing, 12-11.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson limited the Pirates to six singles and struck out three in 5 2/3 innings in his last start, a 5-3 loss on June 9. He was hurt by three errors -- including one by himself. He was also hurt by wildness; of the five batters he walked, four scored. He has surrendered a total of seven earned runs in his last two outings, both losses.
away_pitcher_note: Hochevar shut out the Yankees for six innings Monday, then gave up a two-run homer to Alex Rodriguez that tied the game and ended his outing. It was a very good one, though. Hochevar gave up just four hits and walked no one, allowing just the two runs. Now that he's gone through two tough indoctrinations, at Fenway Park and Yankee Stadium, the rookie should be ready for almost anything. This will be his first exposure to Interleague Play and he comes up against a tough club in the Diamondbacks.

home_pitcher_note: Owings was roughed up in his last start Tuesday night at Shea Stadium. The right-hander allowed five runs (four earned) on eight hits over 4 1/3 innings. It was just the latest in what has been a string of poor performances. Over his last three starts, he is 0-2 with a 9.22 ERA and he has lasted just 13 2/3 innings over that stretch. He opened the season by winning his first four starts and had a 2.42 ERA in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Meche pitched well enough to win on Tuesday night. He limited the Rangers to one run on four hits in six innings but the Royals let the game get away. Meche, however, accomplished his mission of avoiding a big inning. He got a severe test with the bases loaded and no outs but held the damage to one run. Meche managed to keep the ball down and posted his best outing since May 4, when he had seven shutout innings at Cleveland. Meche has a 10-4 record against National League clubs and is 1-0 in two games against the Diamondbacks.

home_pitcher_note: Webb did not have his best stuff in his last outing against the Mets. He was removed after allowing three runs over five innings. Webb was struck on the right hip by a line drive off the bat of Carlos Delgado in the fourth inning, but manager Bob Melvin said the reason Webb was taken out after throwing just 58 pitches was because he wanted to give him a break after all the innings he has thrown this year. It was the first time that Webb did not get a decision this year. It snapped a two-start winning streak which saw him compile a 0.56 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: For the eighth time in 10 starting assignments, Duchscherer allowed two runs or fewer in his last start. He pitched seven strong innings against a fierce Yankees lineup, surrendering just one run on five hits while walking one and striking out four -- his lone mistake being a home run off the bat of Jason Giambi. It was the sixth time he pitched at least six innings and the ninth time he walked two batters or fewer. Duchscherer has only faced Arizona once in his career, and it came as a relief pitcher. In one inning, he allowed a run on two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Haren did not get a decision in his last start, against the Mets, but he certainly pitched well enough to win. The right-hander allowed just two runs on five hits over six innings. Unfortunately for him, he was up against Johan Santana, who tossed seven scoreless innings. The D-backs rallied for two runs in the eighth and two in the ninth before eventually winning the game in the 10th. Haren was acquired in an eight-player deal with the A's last December.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton had a strong 6 2/3-inning outing in his last start, against the Yankees, but one pitch was enough to hand him his third straight loss. After getting through the first five innings unscathed, he loaded the bases in the sixth and gave up a grand slam to Hideki Matsui. As usual, Blanton didn't get much run support in the 4-1 loss. This will be his first career start against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Davis pitched seven shutout innings in his last start against the Royals, but he gave up four walks and six hits in his no-decision. Davis has been struggling with command, allowing 23 walks and 43 hits in 38 1/3 innings in 2008. The left-hander hasn't won since May 23, his first start since he had a cancerous thyroid removed.
away_pitcher_note: Other than giving up a season-high six walks, Smith threw a solid five-inning outing against the Giants in his last start. He gave up one run on just three hits while striking out four in five innings. After the game, Smith noted he wants to work on his control and, thus, last longer in games, but "a win's a win." He has never faced Arizona, the team that selected him in the sixth round of the 2005 Draft.

home_pitcher_note: Baker became the first Twins pitcher to record four strikeouts in an inning in his last start against the Brewers. In his second straight quality start where he pitched six innings and allowed just three runs, Baker tied his career high for strikeouts with nine. The right-hander has started to find his form following a month-long absence from the rotation due to a groin strain. Next up for Baker will be his first career start against the Diamondbacks at the Metrodome. He is 1-0 with a 2.49 ERA in four starts there this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Big Unit was roughed up in his last outing, allowing eight runs (seven earned) and 10 hits to the Kansas City Royals. In recent outings, Johnson had been the victim of a lack of run support and poor defensive play behind him, but against the Royals, he was flat out roughed up. For Johnson, who hasn't won since May 18, it was his third consecutive loss after starting the season 4-1.

home_pitcher_note: Unlike his previous start against the White Sox in which he found trouble with a big inning, Blackburn avoided such problems against the Indians. The right-hander delivered his seventh quality start of the season, pitching six innings and allowing just two runs on seven hits in his outing at Progressive Field. Blackburn will now return home to face the Nationals for the first time in his career. The Metrodome has been kind to Blackburn this season, as he's 3-2 with a 6.37 ERA in six starts there.
away_pitcher_note: Owings has had a string of four consecutive poor outings. He has allowed 21 runs the last 19 innings for an ERA of 9.94, raising his season ERA to 5.18. Against the Royals, he was one batter away from escaping a fifth inning unscathed, but allowed a grand slam to David DeJesus, as part of his seven earned runs. Owings has never faced the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez went seven innings on Tuesday against Washington, giving up one earned run on five hits. He struck out only one but didn't surrender a walk. The Twins won 2-1. It was a needed quality start for Hernandez, who was 6-1 record with a 3.90 ERA on May 13, but had since struggled mightily. In his last six starts, the veteran had sputtered to an 0-3 record with a 9.38 ERA. After lengthy bullpen sessions with pitching coach Rick Anderson, Hernandez believes he has everything ironed out. He will rely less on his fastball and more on his slider and sinker. The veteran will next get a shot at Arizona, with whom he pitched last season.
away_pitcher_note: Webb was roughed up in his last outing against the A's at Chase Field. The right-hander felt like he had his good stuff when he warmed up, but the A's wound up scoring seven runs against him in just 3 1/3 innings. Webb lacked the command that he typically has particularly when it came to his sinker. After walking six guys in his previous eight starts, Webb allowed five free passes. In his start before that, he was removed after just five innings against the Mets as the D-backs tried to give him a bit of a breather since his velocity had recently been down.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander looks for his third win of the month and his first three-game winning streak since winning 20 in 2007. Beckett held the Reds scoreless over seven innings on Sunday at Great American Ball Park, allowing just six hits while fanning six and walking two. Beckett makes this start on seven days of rest after the Red Sox built in a break for him simply for maintenance reasons. Beckett earned a win against the Diamondbacks last June, allowing two runs over eight innings. In his career against Arizona, Beckett is 1-3 with a 5.65 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Haren had his finest outing of the year Wednesday night against the A's at Chase Field. The right-hander held his former team to just one run on four hits over seven innings. Haren threw more cut fastballs than he normally does, in part because he figured the A's were more familiar with his repertoire than other teams. He began using the cut fastball this spring but got away from it early in the season. It's an important pitch for him because it gives him something to throw rather than just a straight fastball when he falls behind in the count 1-0 or 2-0.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson continues to make the most of his callup from the Minor Leagues, first filling in for the injured Daisuke Matsuzaka and now for Bartolo Colon. Though Masterson labored a bit in his last start, he still earned the win against a heavy-hitting Phillies team. In that one, Masterson gave up four hits and two runs over five innings, throwing 92 pitches. Opponents are hitting .176 against Masterson. The righty has allowed 22 hits over 36 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis had a strong performance for the second consecutive outing, allowing just one run on three hits over six innings. He also had a season-high eight strikeouts. The one run he did allow was a bloop single to Oakland left-fielder Jack Cust. Davis is 3-2 against the Red Sox over his career, with a 3.78 ERA in 33 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield has given up three earned runs or less in each of his last five starts since allowing eight runs in five innings against Oakland on May 23. He's gone at least seven innings in all of those outings, but is just 1-2 in that span. His last outing resulted in a 5-4 Red Sox loss to the Cardinals. Still, his ERA has continually dropped in each start from its highest point of the season on May 23 -� it rose to 5.19 after that rough outing against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson has dropped his last four starts and over that span has a 7.77 ERA. In his last outing against the Twins, he allowed seven runs on 11 hits while tossing his first complete game since Aug. 24, 2006. Six of the seven runs came during the third inning and only two of the six hits that inning were hit hard. Johnson has allowed 10 or more hits in back-to-back starts for the first time in his career and his outing against the Twins was the first time he had struck out one or fewer batters since Aug. 4, 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Any worries about a setback after his 132-pitch performance on June 15 at Tampa Bay were erased in his last start. In seven innings at Oakland, Nolasco posted another quality start, yet he wasn't involved in the decision. The right-hander allowed three runs on seven hits. His strikeouts were down to three, after he set a career high of 12 at Tampa Bay. Yet, Nolasco threw 103 pitches, and exited with the game tied. On May 21 at Dolphin Stadium, Nolasco beat the Diamondbacks, giving up one run on three hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Owings pitched well in his last outing, against the Twins, but he had little to show for it, as Minnesota put together a six-run seventh inning to win the game. The right-hander cruised through the first six innings, allowing just two hits. In the seventh, Joe Mauer led off with a bunt single, and the floodgates opened. Owings left with the game tied at 1, but Chad Qualls couldn't stop a Twins rally.

home_pitcher_note: With a little more luck, Miller could have had a better outing in his last start. His line read: five runs (four earned) in four innings. But in a four-run third, a mental mistake led to three extra runs coming home in the inning. In all, he threw 86 pitches. On the road trip, he was 1-1, including an impressive seven-innings, one-run performance at Seattle on June 16. On May 22, Miller beat Arizona, giving up no runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Webb rolled through the first four innings of his last start, against the Twins in the Metrodome. The right-hander allowed just three hits and held a 3-0 lead. But the fifth inning started out poorly when left fielder Conor Jackson lost a ball in the roof and things quickly spiraled out of hand. When all was said and done, the Twins managed five runs in the inning and Webb took the loss. In his previous outing, he was roughed up by the A's at Chase Field. Oakland scored seven runs against him in just 3 1/3 innings. In that game, Webb lacked the command that he typically has, particularly when it came to his sinker.

home_pitcher_note: With some better luck, Olsen could have ended his winless streak in his last outing. Instead, after exiting with a 3-2 lead after seven innings, the lefty settled for a no-decision against Tampa Bay. Olsen hasn't won since May 6 against Milwaukee, a span of nine starts. The lefty is 0-3 in those games. He gave up two runs on four hits with four strikeouts and two walks in his no-decision to the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has been outstanding in his last two starts. Last time out, against the Red Sox, he outdueled Josh Beckett by tossing seven shutout innings in a 2-1 Arizona win. The right-hander allowed just two hits and walked one, while fanning five. Prior to that start, he held his former team, the A's, to just one run on four hits over seven innings. Haren threw more cut fastballs than he normally does, in part because he figured the A's were more familiar with his repertoire than other teams. He began using the cut fastball this spring, but he got away from it early in the season. It's an important pitch for him because it gives him something to throw rather than just a straight fastball when he falls behind in the count, 1-0, or 2-0.

home_pitcher_note: Davis has shown great command in his last three outings and it's showed up in the results -- he has allowed just four runs in 20 innings over that span. Despite those numbers, he does not have a win to show for it. In his last outing, against the Red Sox, he allowed just one run through seven innings, but reliever Chad Qualls allowed two inherited runners to score in the eighth, plus two of his own and the D-backs wound up losing the game, 5-4. Davis' best pitch is a cut fastball, though he also throws a curveball and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Bush didn't quite have no-hit stuff Tuesday, but he was plenty effective in limiting the Braves to four hits and one run in seven innings. Bush has now allowed just two runs and six hits in his past 15 innings. Tuesday's win was his first of the season on the road (1-5). Bush is 4-0 with a 3.55 ERA in four career starts against the D-backs. He last faced them on Aug. 21, 2007, when he allowed two runs on six hits in six innings. He also struck out six in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson is eager to see the calendar flip to July as he dropped all five of his starts in June. In his last outing, he pitched well against the Red Sox at Fenway Park, but Tim Wakefield was better in a 5-0 Boston win. Johnson allowed just two runs over six innings. It was a far better start than the one he had in Minnesota before that when he allowed seven runs on 11 hits while tossing his first complete game since Aug. 24, 2006. Six of the seven runs came during the third inning. Johnson is still stuck on 288 wins for his career.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan allowed four runs on nine hits in six innings Wednesday against the Braves, taking his second loss in as many starts. He has now given up 10 runs (seven earned) in his past two starts. Suppan struck out five Wednesday, but left too many pitches over the middle of the plate. Braves pitcher Jorge Campillo recorded two hits off Suppan. Still, it was an improvement from the 1 2/3-inning, six-run disaster against Baltimore in his previous start, which was his shortest outing since May 1998. Suppan didn't factor in the decision June 2 against the D-backs, when he allowed three runs on seven hits and struck out six in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Petit will be making his first start of the season for the D-backs. He was recalled June 28 to fill Edgar Gonzalez's roster spot. His only decision of the year came April 26 in San Diego, when Tadahito Iguchi hit a walk-off home run in the 13th inning. Petit is 0-1 with a 3.00 ERA in six innings against the Brewers in his career.
away_pitcher_note: McClung received a no-decision in his last start against Minnesota. The right-hander was touched for five runs on nine hits while going 4 2/3 innings. The outing caused his ERA to climb by nearly half a run. McClung will next start against Arizona. On June 3, McClung received his third win of the season by going six innings and allowing only one earned run against the D-Backs in a 7-1 Brewers victory.

home_pitcher_note: Webb lost his first game of the season against the Marlins, after nine victories, but got a measure of revenge in his last start. It wasn't easy as Webb lasted only six-plus innings and left with two on and no out in the seventh. But Webb showed flashes of his early-season form in the victory. He struck out eight and was particularly effective once Florida got runners in scoring position in the second, third and fourth innings. He left four of that runners stranded. What may have helped Webb as much as anything is that he received a nice jolt of run support. A five-run sixth inning put the game away for Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Parra halted Minnesota's 10-game winning streak in his last start. He went seven innings of shutout ball while allowing only two hits and recording six strikeouts in a 5-1 Brewers victory at the Metrodome. Parra's next start will complete a four-game series against Arizona. He went seven innings and only allowed one earned run while striking out eight in a 10-1 Brewers victory against the D-Backs on June 4.

home_pitcher_note: Haren finished a distinguished June in style, which bodes well for him as he begins working on July. He was 3-0 in the month -- despite a ninth-inning foldup in his last start that cost him a victory -- and the D-backs won two other games in which he pitched. Over 41 innings in June, he gave up just six earned runs. When last seen, Haren put away the Marlins for seven innings without much resistance, avenging one of his defeats. He allowed five hits and walked two, striking out seven and allowing only one unearned run. He has lasted at least six innings in all but one of his 17 starts. It is an understatement to say he has been everything the D-backs thought they were getting when they plucked him from Oakland in the offseason.
away_pitcher_note: Has the shine worn off Baek? Baek has lost his past two decisions, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings against the Mariners on June 28. Baek, who was traded to San Diego a month ago for reliever Jared Wells, has allowed a combined 10 earned runs in his past two starts. Control is certainly not an issue with Baek, who has walked just one in his past 11 1/3 innings, but his ERA has risen to 5.43. Clay Hensley was recalled from Triple-A Portland on July 1. He might he be a candidate to claim a spot in the Padres rotation as some point.

home_pitcher_note: It wasn't his best outing, but Davis finally picked up his third win against the Brewers. He allowed three runs on five hits in 5 2/3 innings, striking out three and walking four. Davis had allowed just 16 earned runs in his previous six starts, none of them wins. Davis missed the Padres in two series this season, but he won his last outing against them in 2007, allowing one run on six hits over seven innings on Sept. 4.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy was unspectacular in his last outing, against the Mariners, and even he knew that that wouldn't be good enough to get a win. He secured a quality start by going six innings but gave up three runs on 10 hits while striking out six. He's 0-2 in his last three starts, but he has still not allowed more than three runs since May 14, his last game prior to going on the disabled list. He returned June 12 against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson had a miserable start the last time out, lasting just 3 2/3 innings, allowing eight hits and seven runs, including three home runs against the Brewers in a loss. The 44-year-old left-hander toiled on the mound, throwing all of 93 pitches in the effort. The Big Unit has lost six consecutive starts and hasn't won since May 18. Johnson is 15-5 with a 2.44 ERA in his career against the Padres, and is 1-1 against them in two starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Banks was upstaged by Colorado's Aaron Cook in his last start, though he didn't pitch too badly himself. Banks, the former waiver-wire claim from Toronto, allowed no runs through four innings. But Banks, who has helped hold together an injury-riddled rotation, ran into trouble during the fifth inning. Banks allowed four runs over five innings in losing his third consecutive start. Still, Banks has a 2.89 ERA and hasn't faced the Diamondbacks before.

home_pitcher_note: Making his second start since coming off the disabled list after having left shoulder tendinitis, Perez retired the first 11 Marlins hitters in order and threw 21 of his 23 pitches for strikes in the first three innings. The 30-year-old left after allowing one run on five hits while striking out three in 6 2/3 innings. Perez's night ended after a 1-hour, 33-minute rain delay ensued with a runner on second and two outs in the seventh. He finished throwing 77 pitches -- 53 for strikes -- and lost his chance at the win when reliever Charlie Manning gave up a two-run homer to the first batter he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Webb was let off the hook in his last start by an unpredictable ninth-inning rally by the D-backs. The right-hander, just named to the National League All-Star team, allowed five earned runs in six innings to the Brewers. Webb, who is still tied for first in the Majors with 12 wins this season, is 3-2 with a 3.13 ERA in seven games in his career against the Nationals. In his first start against the Nationals on May 31, he threw a shutout.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan put together another quality start, allowing three runs on five hits over six innings. The rookie left-hander struck out three and walked three for the no-decision as the Nationals' bullpen gave up two seventh-inning runs and Washington's offense couldn't close the gap in a 5-3 loss to the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Owings missed his last start on Wednesday against the Brewers because of an injured gluteus muscle suffered in his previous start while running to cover first base. Yusmeiro Petit filled in nicely against the Brewers, going six innings, allowing just two hits and one run in a no-decision. Through his last nine starts, Owings is 2-6. Against the Nationals, Owings is 1-1 with a 3.57 ERA in three starts in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Bergmann turned out yet another quality start, something becoming more commonplace among Nationals starters. He pitched six innings and gave up just three runs, two earned, striking out five. He threw 64 strikes in 104 pitches. However, the Nationals' offense couldn't get any runs across in a 3-0 loss to Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Haren, recently named to his second All-Star Game, was the NL Pitcher of the Month for June, during which he was 3-0 with a 1.32 ERA in six starts. He could easily have had more wins with better run support. He leads NL starters with a 5.15 strikeout-to-walk ratio and is tops in fewest walks per nine innings with 1.53 and WHIP at 0.98. In his five no-decisions this year, he has a 2.81 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick turned in his third consecutive quality start Sunday against the Mets, allowing one run in six innings. Though Kendrick allowed eight hits and two walks, he was able to work out of several jams. In three different innings Sunday, Kendrick stranded a runner on third base. The Phillies are now 13-5 in Kendrick's starts this season, the best record among Phillies starters. Kendrick earned the victory in the Phils' 20-2 win over the Cardinals on June 13, in which he pitched seven innings, allowing one earned run.
away_pitcher_note: If it weren't for a couple mistake pitches to Scott Hairston, Davis might have had a different result his last time out against the Padres. Davis had his longest outing of the season, throwing eight innings and 122 pitches, allowing three runs on seven hits. He pitched well enough for the win, but like it has been the case for him several times this season, Davis picked up the tough-luck loss. Davis is 2-1 with a 2.92 ERA in six starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Eaton is coming off a clunker against the Mets, as he allowed eight runs -- six earned -- in a career-low 2 2/3 innings. The right-hander allowed 10 hits and a walk. His first loss against New York pushed his career ERA against the Mets to 4.08. He'll try his luck this time against a struggling Diamondbacks team. He is 3-5 with a 4.23 ERA in 14 career starts against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson was back in vintage form in his last outing against the Padres, allowing just one run on three hits, striking out 10. The Big Unit picked up his first win since May 16 after losing his last six starts. After working on mechanics with pitching coach Bryan Price, Johnson is now just 11 wins away from 300. Against the Phillies, Johnson is 10-3 with a 2.61 ERA in 19 starts in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels will take the Phillies into the All-Star Break with his only start of the season against Arizona. The lefty is coming off a nice outing against the Cardinals, though the Phillies lack of offense left him with a no-decision. He surrendered three hits, though two of them were home runs. Hamels is a likely candidate to start the first game after the Break as well.
away_pitcher_note: Webb, who entered the weekend leading the Major League lead in wins with 13, is having another stellar season and could very well win 20 for the first time in his career. He is coming off a start in which he threw six shutout innings against the Nationals. All four of his losses, however, have come in his past 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Davis had a quality start in his last outing against the Phillies, but got no decision as the D-backs bullpen spoiled a two-run lead. He allowed three runs on five hits and gave up a homer to Ryan Howard. Davis will be pitching on a full week's rest. In games which he has had at least six days of rest, Davis is 13-10 with a 4.01 ERA in 27 starts in his career.
away_pitcher_note: He didn't duplicate his nearly perfect one-hitter, but Hiroki Kuroda pitched well enough to win against the Marlins. He complained that his breaking ball wasn't as sharp, but it was still a quality start. Don't be fooled by the losing record. He's left four games with leads that the bullpen was unable to protect. In his only Chase Field start, he allowed nine hits in 5 2/3 innings and took the defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Haren was spectacular in his last outing in Washington, holding the Nationals to just one run on three hits in eight innings. Still, the All-Star could not pick up the win as the D-backs bullpen blew two saves in the late innings. Against the Dodgers, Haren is 2-1 with a 4.15 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley went into the break by overpowering the Marlins, striking out a career-high 13 in seven innings. He's won five of his last six decisions and lowered his ERA to 3.25. Billingsley is 0-2 with a 9.72 ERA against the Diamondbacks this year, including a 6-4 loss in which he fanned 12 in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Just as his other fellow starters had experienced on the last road trip, Webb pitched well enough to win against the Phillies, but Chad Qualls allowed four runs in the eighth inning to spoil his gem. Webb is 9-2 with a 2.61 ERA when pitching on at least six days of rest, and is 9-3 with a 2.78 ERA in 14 starts against the Dodgers lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe pitches in this game so he'll be sure to miss pitching in Coors Field in the series that follows. He was perfect in his last start for 6 2/3 innings while beating Atlanta. In his last 10 starts, he has lowered his ERA from 5.34 to 3.85. He'll be pitching on 10 days rest.

home_pitcher_note: The Big Unit was probably already in line for his 290th career win against the Phillies, but his two-run double certainly helped his own cause last time out. After going winless in eight starts, Johnson has won two in a row. Johnson missed the Cubs at Wrigley Field, but has never lost to the Cubs in his career, going 12-0 with a 1.98 ERA in 13 starts, including three complete games and an average of more than 10 strikeouts a game.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Harden's second start for the Cubs since he was acquired in a six-player deal from the Athletics. In his debut at Wrigley Field on July 12, he struck out 10, his third career double-digit strikeout game, and threw 5 1/3 scoreless innings. Harden was pulled after 96 pitches. The Cubs will be keeping an eye on his pitch count in hopes of avoiding injury.

home_pitcher_note: Petit will get the nod instead of Micah Owings, who was needed to pitch in relief on Monday due to a depleted bullpen. Petit last pitched on Friday in relief and allowed one run over three innings against the Dodgers. The right-hander has made one start this year -- an emergency start in place of Owings -- and did not get a decision despite allowing just one run in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis went 10 days between starts, and he seemed to benefit from the time off. The right-hander threw seven shutout innings on July 11 against the Giants, giving up three hits. Marquis is needed to step it up in the second half. He has a career 25-33 record after the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Davis had his shortest outing of the year the last time out, but was given a great deal of run support against the Dodgers. Pitching on a full week's rest, he lasted just three innings, giving up five runs (four earned) on five hits and three walks. He didn't factor into the decision. Against the Cubs, Davis is 7-5 with a 3.39 ERA in his career in 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly bounced back from his shortest outing of the season in his last start before the All-Star break with one of his best starts of the season Friday night at Houston. Though he wasn't involved in the decision, Lilly went seven innings, allowing just one run on a Carlos Lee homer and just six hits total. He is 1-2 with a 2.73 ERA in five career appearances against the D-backs, including 0-1 with a 3.00 ERA in one start at Chase Field. He beat Arizona at Wrigley Field on May 9, allowing one earned run on three hits over seven innings in a 3-1 Cubs victory.

home_pitcher_note: For the third time in a row, Sanchez finished his day without a quality start in his last outing, when he allowed four runs in 5 1/3 innings. The lefty pitched fairly well, striking out eight batters, but he tired in the sixth and left after walking two and loading the bases. Following a stressful 26-pitch first inning, Sanchez said he lost his release point late in the game. Since reeling off six wins in sevens starts in May and June, he hasn't won a game in three weeks.
away_pitcher_note: Haren was spectacular in his last outing, going seven innings, allowing just four hits and two walks and no runs against the Dodgers at Chase Field in what D-backs manager Bob Melvin called a must-win game. The All-Star leads the Majors in quality starts this season with 17, including nine consecutive. Against the Giants, Haren is 4-4 with a 3.58 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum tied a season high for runs allowed (five) in his previous outing. He lasted six innings and struck out eight, but walked four in a loss. After struggling early, Lincecum zoomed through the fifth and sixth before surrendering a three-run homer in the seventh. The righty threw 121 pitches, one off his career high, and has thrown 110 or more in four of his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Webb was superb in his last outing, going eight innings, allowing just one run on six hits against the Dodgers, but still he was denied his 14th win when closer Brandon Lyon allowed five runs in the top of the ninth. Webb is 11-5 with a 3.22 ERA against the Giants in 21 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Zito has won his last two decisions, including a three-run, six-inning effort last Tuesday against Washington. This is consistent with his pattern of strong second halves. Entering this year, Zito had gone 64-31 with a 3.36 ERA after the All-Star break. He's also 3-1 with a 3.64 ERA in his last five starts. Zito has faced the Diamondbacks three times this season, losing twice and recording a 6.32 ERA, although two of those efforts were quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson certainly hasn't looked like a 44-year-old on the mound in his last three starts. After going winless in his previous eight starts, Johnson regained his dominant form, winning his last three starts, allowing just five runs on 10 hits in 19 1/3 innings. The last time out, the Big Unit won career game No. 291, as he shut out the Cubs for seven innings. Against the Giants, Johnson has two no-decisions on the season, despite allowing just two earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux was cruising along in his last start on July 23 in Cincinnati, looking as if he might snap a stretch of 13 consecutive starts without a victory. After tossing five scoreless innings, Maddux ran into trouble in the sixth inning, as the Padres dropped a ball during a rundown that extended the inning. Reliever Cla Meredith then came in and allowed two runs on a home run. All told, Maddux, who is being mentioned in trade rumors, possibly with the Dodgers, allowed two earned runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Owings slides back into the rotation after a pair or relief appearances. The right-hander has struggled since a 6-2 mark to star the season. He's been working with pitching coach Bryan Price on a mechanical issue. Owings front shoulder has a tendency to fly open which drops his elbow and therefore rather than getting his hand on top of the ball he gets on the side of it causing lots of lateral movement and results in wildness.

home_pitcher_note: Padres manager Bud Black said Young will join the team during their visit in Pittsburgh and should start on Tuesday against the Diamondbacks. Young has missed 54 games this season after being hit by a line drive in face off the bat of Cardinals first baseman Albert Pujols. Young suffered a nasal fracture and a laceration on his nose. Tuesday's start will be his first since May 21. Young is 1-3 with a 5.08 ERA against the Diamondbacks in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Davis wasn't exactly lights out in his last start. After allowing a first-inning homer to Derrek Lee, Davis settled down for three innings before allowing three runs in the fifth to the Cubs, as he picked up the loss. It was, however, an improvement from his last start, when he allowed five runs (four earned) in three innings against the Dodgers. Against the Padres, Davis is 6-3 with a 3.36 ERA in 75 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Baek gave the Padres a second consecutive solid start against the Pirates on July 25. He gave up four runs on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings. The outing came after the right-hander tossed 6 1/3 quality innings against the Cardinals on July 20. Manager Bud Black thought his pitcher battled but left too many pitches up in the zone, evidenced by the two home runs he surrendered to Pirates first baseman Adam LaRoche. Baek threw six scoreless innings and picked the win in his lone career start against the Diamondbacks back on the Fourth of July.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has given the D-backs everything they could have hoped for when they dealt six prospects to Oakland for him in December. The right-hander was masterful in his last outing against the Giants at AT&T Park as he allowed two runs on nine hits over eight innings. Haren pitched two scoreless innings in the All-Star Game earlier this month.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe had his sinker working on Saturday, holding the Nationals to just one hit over eight outstanding innings. The sinkerballer walked just one and struck out four, showing that when his stuff is on, he's very difficult to beat. Lowe has a win and a no-decision in two starts against the D-backs this season.
away_pitcher_note: Webb seemed to have better command of his sinker in his last start against the Giants. He battled Tim Lincecum in that game before prevailing 5-3 thanks to a three-run eighth inning rally off the Giants bullpen. Webb allowed three runs on four hits over seven innings. Two of the runs came on a two-out bloop single to center by Aaron Rowand on a sinker that was nearly in the dirt.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw produced his best outing of the season Sunday against the Nationals. He threw six-plus scoreless innings to pick up his first career victory, yielding four hits and a walk without allowing a runner to reach third. He also struck out five in his economical 86-pitch effort. The rookie established his fastball and curveball early while pitching aggressively and getting ahead in the count. That came on the heels of his five-run, 10-hit shellacking in three innings July 22 in Colorado. Kershaw has given up three runs or fewer in seven of his 10 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson is riding a scoreless-innings streak of 15 as well as a four-start winning streak. The left-hander was on top of his game against the Giants last Sunday as he tossed seven shutout innings. It was the second straight start in which he held the opposition scoreless for seven frames. Johnson is eight wins away from 300 for his career. Johnson didn't allow a walk against the Giants and has given up just two free passes in his last 26 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda committed a mental lapse of throwing to the wrong base and it opened the door for a five-run rally with two outs by the Giants. He lasted only 3 2/3 innings in that game, one start after allowing five runs in six innings in Colorado, which was one start after his two-inning outing in Arizona coming out of the break. His three-start ERA is 13.11.
away_pitcher_note: Petit takes over the spot in the rotation of the recently demoted Micah Owings. Petit has pitched well in two spot starts this year, both in place of Owings. Against the Brewers on July 2, he allowed one run over six innings. His other start was July 22 against the Cubs and he allowed one run over five innings in that one. Petit doesn't have an overpowering fastball but mixes his pitches well and has a good feel for how to attack hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson came up clutch in his first Dodgers start, throwing six scoreless inning in a win over the Giants. It was his first Major League victory in two years, but this could be his last start in a while with Brad Penny possibly returning from the disabled list next weekend. Johnson complained that his command was lacking, although you couldn't tell by the fact that he had no walks.
away_pitcher_note: Davis is coming off his best outing of the year. In his last start in San Diego, Davis took a perfect game into the seventh inning, but eventually allowed a base hit to Padres outfielder Brian Giles. Still, Davis picked up the win, finishing the game allowing just two hits and no runs in 7 2/3 innings. Davis is 2-2 with a 1.40 ERA in his career at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Haren has won each of his past three starts, but his last outing against the Padres on Wednesday did not start well. Haren allowed a pair of first-inning runs as he had trouble keeping his split-finger fastball down. It was a rare early outburst against him as he had allowed a total of one run in the first five innings in his previous seven starts. Haren settled in and allowed just one more run before departing after seven. He gave the team a scare in the fifth when he suffered a cramp in his right hamstring while running the bases, but stayed in the game and appeared fine.
away_pitcher_note: Moans of frustration could be heard from every part of PNC Park when Herrera gave up three first-inning runs in his last start on Tuesday. The Pirates rookie was hit hard, but was never knocked out. He came back to throw a decent five-plus innings, striking one and surrendering only six hits. The outing marked the second consecutive solid start by Herrera. He'll toe the mound for his fifth career Major League start against the Diamondbacks.

home_pitcher_note: Webb was on top of his game in his last start against the Dodgers as he allowed just one run on six hits over eight innings to become the Majors first 15-game winner. After a bit of a lull, Webb is back on a roll having won his last four decisions. He's been particularly tough on the Dodgers in his career having won eight of his last nine starts against them and the only game he didn't win he held them to just one run over eight innings and left with a lead.
away_pitcher_note: Duke is glad to see July over with, finishing the month 0-4 with a 9.51 ERA. He has allowed five runs or more in each of his last five starts and remains winless since June 9. Duke's location has been the problem. The lefty is missing his spots consistently and missing a lot of them up in the strike zone. Duke's last win actually came against Arizona in a start in which he allowed just two runs on five hits in six innings. He is 1-1 with a 5.29 ERA in three career starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson won his fifth straight start and the 293rd of his career, as he allowed just one unearned run on five hits over six innings against the Dodgers last Friday at Dodger Stadium. During his five-start win streak, he has allowed just five earned runs in 32 1/3 innings and he has not allowed an earned run in his last 21 innings. The Big Unit has located his pitchers better during the streak thanks to finally feeling locked in with his mechanics.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens picked up a win in his first Major League start this season, going six shutout innings. It wasn't exactly dominant, as he allowed five hits and four walks in the outing. However, Karstens showcased an impressive offspeed repertoire when needed. Whether he relies so heavily on his slider and curveball moving forward remains to be seen. The Pirates acquired Karstens in a deal with the Yankees, and he will remain in the Pirates' rotation after spending the first four months of the season in Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: Petit didn't have his best outing against the Dodgers in Los Angeles. The right-hander allowed three runs on five hits over five innings. His big mistake was a fastball that he left too far out over the plate that Manny Ramirez clubbed for a homer. Petit took the place of Micah Owings in the rotation after Owings was sent to Triple-A Tucson. Petit lacks overpowering stuff but has a good feel for pitching and excellent control.
away_pitcher_note: Morton regained some confidence while allowing the Brewers two runs over seven innings on Saturday. The 24-year-old right-hander, who had been 1-3 with a 9.53 ERA in his previous five starts, allowed just one hit during the first six innings and showed more consistency with his control. He has allowed at least one homer in five of his last six starts. This will be his first career appearance against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis went from high to low in a hurry in his last start, as the Dodgers roughed him up for five runs in just 1 2/3 innings. It was quite a contrast from the start before, when he carried a no-hitter into the seventh against the Padres. This time around, Davis lacked command and when he fell behind hitters, he had to come over the plate with his stuff and they made him pay. He is better off when he can work the corners.
away_pitcher_note: Jorge Campillo scattered six hits and struck out six in seven shutout innings against the Brewers on Sunday. The 29-year-old right-hander's only trouble came in the seventh, but he struck out the final two batters to end the inning and the threat. He is 3-0 with a 1.26 ERA in his past five starts. Campillo started against the D-backs earlier this season, on May 24, but had to leave after the fourth inning when a blister formed on his right index finger. In that start, he had allowed two hits and struck out three in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Haren struggled with command his last time out against the Pirates, but thanks to 13 runs of support, the All-Star right-hander picked up his fifth consecutive win. He struggled early on, allowing three first-inning runs, but the D-backs roughed up the Pittsburgh pitching staff for their biggest offensive explosion of the season. Haren has given up seven runs in just 11 2/3 innings, but still is 2-0 in his career against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens was victimized by multiple miscues and some inconsistent control while allowing the Giants four runs in six innings on Monday. The 22-year-old rookie had allowed just one earned run in his four previous road starts combined.  His only previous appearance against the D-backs came on May 26, when allowed eight hits in 4 2/3 innings. His struggles that day could have been blamed on a blister that affected him for three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Webb was true to his form in his last outing, giving up only one fly-ball out in his complete-game victory over the Pirates. He cruised through the first eight innings, not allowing a single runner past first base until the ninth inning.
