Webb made quick work of the Bucs, too, as the time of the game didn't even eclipse two hours. Against the Braves, Webb is 2-2 with a 1.90 ERA and two shutouts in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton regained the grip on his sinker and used it to produce 13 groundouts while earning his first Major League win since Aug. 14, 2005, on Tuesday night.  While tossing seven solid innings against the Giants, he showed the tenacity that had been lacking in his previous two starts this season. The veteran southpaw, who missed the past two seasons while recovering from separate elbow surgeries, says he's felt more confident after each of his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez picked a bad time to remind everyone he's still only in his first full Major League season. He dominated in July, going 5-1 with a 1.74 ERA, but against the Nationals he reverted back to the mistakes that plagued him earlier this season. He threw with plenty of velocity against Washington but couldn't find the plate, walking a season-high six batters in five innings. He also gave up six runs, the most he's surrendered since May 27. Jimenez said the problem was with his mechanics -- his left shoulder got too far ahead of the rest of his body when he went through his motion.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson was outstanding in his last outing against the Pirates, but the bad news for he and the D-backs was that Jeff Karstens was a little better. Johnson held Pittsburgh to just two runs over 7 1/3 innings and did not walk a batter while fanning seven. Karstens, though, carried a perfect game through 7 2/3 innings before winding up with a two-hit shutout. The loss snapped Johnson?s five-start winning streak and left him stranded at 293 career wins.

home_pitcher_note: Francis's return from shoulder inflammation started off sweet but quickly turned sour against the Nationals. He gave up just two hits in four innings before unraveling in the fifth and sixth, giving up five runs. Three of those runs came off two home runs by Lastings Milledge. Francis has now given up a team-high 19 homers this season. The lefty had great location with his fastball early, but it began to cut in on him as the game progressed, which allowed the Nationals to take advantage. Francis said he felt no pain in his shoulder after the game, but both his sinker and his four-seam fastball were thrown with noticeably less velocity than usual.
away_pitcher_note: Davis struggled again in his last outing against the Braves, lasting just 4 1/3 innings, giving up seven runs on nine hits, picking up the loss. It was Davis' second consecutive bad outing after taking a perfect game into the seventh inning in San Diego July 29. In his last two starts, Davis has lasted a combined six innings and has given up 12 earned runs in the last two games.

home_pitcher_note: Rusch is starting in place of Aaron Cook, who is resting an unspecified amount of time with general fatigue. That may turn out to be a good thing for the Rockies. Rusch has been Colorado's most consistent starter over the past few weeks, winning four straight decisions since July 9. In his most recent start, against the Padres, Rusch gave up two runs in six innings to beat his former club. The key to the 33-year-old's success has been his ability to manage games and throw strikes. In his past six starts, Rusch has issued just three walks compared to 20 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren lost his last start, which turned out to be a 5 1/3-inning debacle. He allowed six runs on 10 hits to the Braves, striking out five as he picked up the loss. Things started to unravel toward the end of his outing and afterward, as seven runs ended up scoring in the sixth inning. The $44 million man has struggled a bit recently. Despite winning four starts in a row, in his last two starts has given up a total of 10 runs in 11 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had one of his best outings of the year against the Reds in his last start, allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings. He was perfect through 4 2/3 and used mostly two-seamers and fastballs for the first three frames before turning to his curveball in the fourth. Rodriguez is 2-2 over four career starts vs. the Diamondbacks and has a 4.50 ERA. He has not faced Arizona this year.
away_pitcher_note: It's been the same old story for Webb recently. The Cy Young frontrunner has put together seven consecutive quality starts and has won his last four outings. The last time out, Webb was a double threat, as he got the job done on the mound and with the bat, belting a two-run double off Braves starter Mike Hampton. At Minute Maid Park, Webb is 2-0 with a 1.21 ERA in 22 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Backe bounced back from one of his worst performances of the season to throw one of his best, allowing one run on four hits in seven innings against the Giants. He struck out six and said he felt much more comfortable with his fastball, which he used about 80 percent of the time. He will face Arizona for the first time this season and just the second time in his career. Backe allowed five runs in 12 innings against the D-backs in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Petit last saw game action on Aug. 7, when he allowed two runs over five innings against the Braves at Chase Field. As the fifth starter, his spot was skipped when the D-backs had this past Monday off. His versatility has been important for the D-backs as he has spot started when needed before finally joining the rotation. As a starter this year, Petit is 1-2 with a 3.00 ERA in four games. In nine relief appearances, he is 0-1 with a 3.29 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt did not have his best start against the Giants, but it was enough to survive as he was able to strand nine baserunners. He allowed three runs and struck out four on 10 hits. Oswalt is facing Arizona for the first time this season. He is 6-1 with a 2.57 ERA all-time against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson continued his march towards 300 wins as he was victorious last Tuesday night against the Rockies in Coors Field. The Big Unit, who now has 294 wins, allowed just two runs on five hits over six innings. In his last seven starts, Johnson is 6-1 with a 1.77 ERA. His lone loss came against the Pirates when he allowed just two runs in 7 1/3 innings, but was outdueled by Jeff Karstens, who took a perfect game into the eighth.

home_pitcher_note: Davis scuffled early in his last outing against the Rockies as he a pair of runs in the first and one in the second. Command, as always, was the difference for Davis. When the left-hander gets ahead of hitters he's able to expand the zone. When he falls behind he has to come in with his fastball and gets into trouble. He settled down after the first two innings against the Rockies and allowed just one more run before departing after five.
away_pitcher_note: Banks had his worst start as a Padre in his last outing on Wednesday when his command was amiss. Banks allowed seven earned runs on five hits over 4 1/3 innings, which also marked his shortest start this season. The six walks (one was intentional) were a career high for Banks, who had more than two batters just once since moving into the Padres starting rotation in May. Banks served up a home run to Prince Fielder and later allowed a three-run triple to Corey Hart after falling behind in the count.

home_pitcher_note: Haren was his old self in his last start against the Rockies on Thursday. The right-hander got better as the game went along and wound up allowing just two runs on seven hits over eight innings. The outing came on the heels of back-to-back starts in which he allowed a combined 10 earned runs. Haren recently signed a four-year, $44.75 million extension.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy was dominant in his last start against the Brewers at home. Peavy threw six innings of shutout ball before giving up one run in the seventh. The Brewers managed only four hits off the ace who picked up only his fourth win in his last 10 starts even though his ERA is 2.32 over that span. Peavy has a 1.42 ERA at home this season compared to 4.14 on the road. The last time he gave up more than two runs at home was June 29 against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Webb leads the Majors in wins and seems to be on his way to his second National League Cy Young Award in three years. His last start was on Friday against the Astros at Minute Maid Park, where he allowed just two runs on four hits in eight innings. Webb has won his past five starts and his past seven decisions.
away_pitcher_note: In his Major League debut, Reineke found a rhythm after a tough first inning to record his first career win. He did it all, including getting his first big league hit, RBI and run scored. He finished the game with a line of three runs on five hits with five strikeouts and three walks in five innings. Reineke admitted to being nervous in the beginning of the game but was proud to have contributed to a win. His reward is another start as Chris Young, who he was brought up from Triple-A Portland, continues to heal from a strained right forearm.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson deserved a better fate in his last start, against the Astros. The Big Unit made one mistake, but it wound up costing him the game. His split-finger fastball to Ty Wigginton drifted back out over the plate and was hit for a three-run homer. That proved to be all the scoring in the game, as Roy Oswalt combined with Jose Valverde on a two-hitter. Johnson has 294 wins and will make eight more starts this year, including this one.
away_pitcher_note:
Sanchez was able to notch a win against the Cubs on Saturday despite not having his best stuff. The 24-year-old said he was having a hard time getting his breaking ball over, and because of that, he ended up issuing a season-high five walks and left after throwing 96 pitches -- 54 for strikes -- in 5 1/3 innings. 
But Sanchez did a good job of getting out of jams and gave up just one run on three hits while striking out six in his fourth start since coming back from shoulder surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Petit has pitched well given his inconsistent schedule. As the team's fifth starter, he pitched on seven days' rest in his last start. He got the win in that one, as the D-backs beat the Astros, 11-5. Petit allowed two runs on four hits over seven innings. In his last three starts, he is 1-2 but has a 3.71 ERA. Petit doesn't overwhelm you with his stuff, but he commands it well and has a good feel for pitching.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad did a nice job of getting out of jams while giving up two runs in six-plus innings against the Cubs on Sunday. Through the first three innings, Volstad tossed 63 pitches and put six runners on base but didn't surrender a run. But, after cruising through the next three without allowing a run, the 21-year-old started off the seventh by giving up two hits and left the game. After that, the Cubs put eight runs on the board -- two charged to Volstad -- and he had to settle for the second no-decision of his rookie year.

home_pitcher_note: Since taking a perfect game into the eighth inning against the Padres on July 29, Davis has struggled. His last outing -- also against the Padres -- showed that he might be turning the corner. The lefty allowed a pair of runs on seven hits over six innings. The biggest key for Davis is throwing strikes early in the count. When he does that, he's able to expand the zone. When he falls behind, he has to come in with his fastball and gets into trouble.
away_pitcher_note: A dubious distinction came to an end the last time Nolasco took the mound. The 25-year-old right-hander recorded his first career complete game, beating San Francisco, 6-0, last Tuesday at AT&T Park. The complete game snapped a string of 301 straight games by Florida pitchers without a complete game, which is a Major League record. Nolasco struck out 11 and walked just one, while allowing just two hits. It was also the Marlins' first complete-game shutout since Dontrelle Willis blanked the Phillies, 3-0, on Sept. 10, 2006. The 12 wins also was a personal high for Nolasco, who won 11 as a rookie in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy had an uncharacteristic outing the last time out against the D-backs at Chase Field. Before he even took the mound, he had a 4-0 lead, and the ace couldn't hold onto the lead as the Padres fell, 8-6. In Peavy's previous six starts, he had only received 12 runs of support. The game was anticipated to be a pitchers' duel with Dan Haren on the mound for the D-backs. It will be the same exact pitching matchup when the two teams face each other on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Haren threw a season-low 82 pitches in his last start, but still lasted six innings despite allowing a season-high 11 hits, which produced five runs for the Friars. Haren is 6-1 in his last seven starts. He will likely need better results than Wednesday's to defeat Jake Peavy for the second time in five days. A victory Monday would tie Haren's career high of 15, set last year.

home_pitcher_note: In Reineke's second career big league start, he may have pitched well enough to win, but he went up against Cy Young front-runner Brandon Webb, who outpitched Reineke in Arizona. The rookie had his first quality start, but made a few mistake pitches, most notably to Conor Jackson, who smacked a two-run double in the fifth inning off Reineke. He'll get the same team and the same opposing pitcher the next time out.
away_pitcher_note: Webb might have had his best sinker in his last outing against the Padres, limiting them to just three hits across seven innings as he picked up his Major League-leading 19th win. Webb had a little bit of a scare in the sixth inning when a Kevin Kouzmanoff line drive hit him on his ribs, but the right-hander should be on schedule to make his next start against the very same team and pitcher he beat the last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Baek returns to PETCO Park after allowing five runs in seven innings in a road loss to the Giants on Aug. 22. Normally, a return to PETCO Park sits well with pitchers. Not Baek, though. He's 0-8 with a 5.97 ERA at home since being acquired from the Seattle Mariners in May. Baek did set a career high with eight strikeouts but was victimized when the Giants scored five runs in the fourth inning of his last start. His stuff looked good at times, especially when Baek was able to throw his curveball. But a few pitches up in the strike zone hurt him.
away_pitcher_note: It was an outing much like several others in 2008 for the Big Unit the last time out. Poor defense behind him and a lack of run support foiled the 44-year-old left-hander in his bid for career win No. 295. Johnson allowed just one earned run, but still could not pick up the win against the Marlins. If he were to join the 300-wins club in 2008, he likely will have to win the remainder of his starts. Against the Padres, Johnson is 2-1 this season.

home_pitcher_note: Amid concerns of a stiff back, Davis had one of his better outings on Sunday, when he limited the Marlins to three runs in seven innings. For the first time all season, he didn't walk a batter, but he still was outpitched by Marlins starter Ricky Nolasco. Against the Dodgers, Davis is 1-1 this season in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda dominated the Phillies for the second straight start Sunday evening, giving up one run on two hits in six innings. Kuroda has thrived in August after a rough end to July, compiling a 3-1 mark and a 2.10 ERA this month while yielding one run in four of his five starts. That stretch started with a one-run, seven-inning win over the D-backs at Dodger Stadium, but Arizona has hit him in his two starts in Phoenix.

home_pitcher_note: Haren pitched well against the Padres his last time out. The right-hander allowed two runs on nine hits over seven innings of work. He struck out a season-high 11, the third time in his career that he has reached double digits in strikeouts. While he gave up plenty of hits, Haren was able to pitch out of jams adjusted from his previous start against the Padres, when they jumped on him for three runs in the first inning.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley tossed another quality start on Monday in Philadelphia, giving up three runs on seven hits in six innings despite struggling at times with his control, as he walked five (two intentional) and ran up a pitch count of 107. Still, the outing accounted for his ninth consecutive start in which he's yielded three runs or less, and he's compiled a 3.04 ERA in that time. Billingsley has struggled against the D-backs this year, going 0-3 with a 7.71 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his quest to become the National League's first 20-game winner since 2005, Webb was knocked around by the Padres at PETCO Park the last time out, as he allowed six runs and didn't even last five innings for just the second time all season. Webb had one bad inning and gave up a three-run homer to Brian Giles. Maybe pitching under the national limelight on ESPN against the Dodgers -- a team he has had great success against in his career -- will help him get win No. 20.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe did not deserve to lose Tuesday's start in Washington when he threw a complete game of eight innings and gave up just two runs on six hits, but the Dodgers' struggling offense made that so. After a disaster outing in St. Louis, Lowe has thrown four straight quality starts, compiling a 2.28 ERA in that time. He is 1-1 with a 3.78 ERA in three outings against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: It was like deja vu all over again for the Big Unit the last time out. He handed the bullpen a one-run lead after seven strong innings against the Padres, but for the second time in as many starts, the bullpen blew the game, and Johnson was denied his 295th career win. With the way manager Bob Melvin has the starting rotation aligned, Johnson will make six more starts in 2008, meaning he would have to win the remainder of his games to reach the 300-wins club in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro returns to the rotation after a brief stint in the bullpen. He was bumped thanks to a strange schedule that provided four off days in less than two weeks. The right-hander was actually going well, with three wins and a 3.60 ERA over his last three starts, but Chase Field presents a challenge for a pitcher who has been much more effective at new Busch Stadium than on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Petit has been pitching like an ace the last few times out, but the right-hander hasn't pitched on a consistent basis, with several off-days for the D-backs down the stretch. Manager Bob Melvin has gone with a four-man rotation recently, which has given Petit starts about once every nine days or so. Petit allowed just one run on two hits in his last start against his former team, the Marlins, as he picked up his third win of the season. Petit is 2-0 with a 1.23 ERA in 7 1/3 innings against the Cardinals in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright has looked like almost the same pitcher since his return from a finger injury. In two starts since coming off the disabled list, he's allowed 12 earned runs in 12 innings, with six strikeouts, one walk and one home run allowed. The one thing he hasn't done is get a lot of swings-and-misses, but his command has been good enough that he hasn't needed them. When Wainwright starts getting fruitless swings, you'll know he's all the way back.

home_pitcher_note: Davis had a decent outing his last start, tossing five innings, allowing just two runs on eight hits and three walks, and he picked up the win against the Dodgers. Davis seems to be back on track after scuffling in three straight starts, allowing 16 runs in 11 innings. The left-hander is 4-5 with a 5.05 ERA in 13 career games against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse ended a string of so-so performances his last time out, but he still couldn't get a win. He was outstanding in Houston, allowing two runs over eight innings, but a late game-tying homer cost him the W. Still, there's reason to be at least somewhat concerned. Lohse has been much, much better at home (3.16 ERA) than on the road (4.97), and he has a lifetime 5.50 ERA at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe stepped up big time his last time out and outdueled Brandon Webb with Lowe's seventh quality start in his last eight appearances. Lowe threw six scoreless innings, allowing four singles. He will switch spots in the rotation with Chad Billingsley to remain on a five-day cycle and, more importantly, avoid pitching at Coors Field later this month.
away_pitcher_note: Haren said he is going through a mechanical funk. In six starts in August, Haren had a 5.63 ERA and gave up six homers, raising his ERA from 2.62 to 3.24. D-backs manager Bob Melvin thinks Haren may have to adjust his approach now that National League teams are starting to see more of the right-hander. In his last outing, Haren gave up five runs on 10 hits in six innings, picking up the loss against the Dodgers at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Blessed with a lead Saturday, Billingsley knew what to do with it. He took a critical start into the eighth inning before running out of gas and picked up a team-high, as well as career-high, 13th win. He's gone 10 consecutive starts without allowing more than three runs and has pitched at least six innings in seven of his last eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight outing, Webb was roughed up by a National League West rival in search of his 20th win of the season. Webb lasted just 3 1/3 innings against the Dodgers on Sunday night, allowing eight runs -- six earned -- on eight hits. The ace also couldn't find the plate, as he had five walks -- two intentional. The Dodgers put the game out of reach in the first inning when Andre Ethier hit a solo home run and Casey Blake hit a three-run shot four batters later.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw rebounded from a pair of poor outings on the road with a masterful performance Tuesday against the Padres. He pitched better than his stat line of three runs in seven-plus innings, as he yielded just three hits and two of the runs scored after he left the game in the eighth. Kershaw credited a tip from Derek Lowe to keep his front leg back in part for his stellar outing. He had racked up a 15.63 ERA in his previous two starts, both losses, but went 2-0 with a 1.45 ERA in five consecutive quality starts before that.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer will get Sunday's start in place of Randy Johnson, who is suffering from what the club says is left shoulder fatigue. This is expected to be a one-start break for Johnson, who is next scheduled to pitch on Aug. 13. Scherzer was 1-1 with a 2.72 ERA in 13 games (10 starts) for Triple-A Tucson. He made his Major League debut on April 29 against the Astros and fanned seven in 4 1/3 innings to set an Arizona record for a pitcher making his debut. Scherzer has held right-handers to a .159 average in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum was uncharacteristically wild in his last start against the Rockies on Tuesday. He gave up five runs on five hits and threw two wild pitches to go along with two walks in five innings. His biggest mistake was leaving a changeup over the plate against Troy Tulowitzki, who hit it into the stands for a two-run homer. Lincecum took the no-decision, breaking a stretch of three straight starts with a win. It was also the first time he didn't toss a quality outing in his past seven starts, dating back to July 20th.
away_pitcher_note: While Petit has done a nice job in the No. 5 role for the D-backs this year, his last outing was probably his poorest. The right-hander allowed five runs on four hits in 4 2/3 innings against the Cardinals at Chase Field. The home run ball hurt him, as Troy Glaus and Yadier Molina each hit two-run homers in the game, while Felipe Lopez added a solo shot. Petit does not have overpowering stuff, but he generally has excellent command and is able to hit his spots and work ahead in the count.

home_pitcher_note: Zito recorded one of his best performances as a Giant against the Rockies on Wednesday. The left-hander maintained sharp control of all his pitches and allowed just two runs on four hits while striking out five in eight innings. His only major mistake came when he gave up a solo home run in the fifth. It was the third time he's pitched eight innings in his past seven starts, and he improved to 7-5 in his past 13 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis did not get a decision in his last start, on Wednesday against the Cardinals at Chase Field. The lefty didn't pitch too poorly, as he allowed three runs on eight hits in six innings, but he left trailing, 3-0. The D-backs staged a late rally and won the game, 4-3, with a pair of ninth-inning runs. It's been an up-and-down year for Davis. He's struggled when he hasn't had his good command, but when he's been able to throw strike one and work ahead in the count, he's been very effective.

home_pitcher_note: Hennessey, recalled from Triple-A Fresno last Monday, replaces Kevin Correia, who has lost three of his last four decisions and owns a 7.84 ERA in his last two starts. Hennessey is no stranger to the rotation, having started 40 games for the Giants in 2004-06. He began this season in San Francisco's bullpen but was optioned to Fresno after recording a 12.94 ERA in 11 appearances. Hennessey is 0-2 with a 4.73 ERA lifetime against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has fallen on hard times of late. The right-hander has pitched poorly in two straight starts and four of his past six. He took the loss against the Dodgers on Friday night, when he allowed five runs in just four innings. Haren said he felt like he had good stuff in the game and felt completely healthy; it was simply a matter of the Dodgers taking advantage of the mistakes he made. The second half has been somewhat of a struggle for Haren over the past two seasons as well, but he says he is as strong as ever.

home_pitcher_note: Webb struggled his past three times out and has a 12.51 ERA in those starts, the last two of which came against the Dodgers. The struggles come on the heels of an eight-game winning streak. There's been much speculation about Webb's health, but the right-hander maintains that he is completely healthy. He was hit in the ribs with a comebacker in the start before his struggles began, but he said it has not bothered him. Webb's command has been spotty, and he has left his signature slider up in the zone during his losing streak.
away_pitcher_note: Harang looked solid on Sunday against the Cubs, but one bad inning almost did him in. With the game tied at 1, Harang led off the seventh inning by beaning the first two batters -- his first two hit batsmen of the year -- to kick-start a two-run Cubs rally. The Reds saved Harang from his 16th loss of the season, though, as they rallied for three runs in the ninth inning to get their ace off the hook. All told, the 30-year-old right-hander went seven innings, gave up three runs on six hits, struck out five and walked three to go along with his two hit batsmen. Harang has not seen the Diamondbacks since Opening Day, when he went six innings, allowed three runs (two earned) and struck out six in taking his first loss of the season. Lifetime, Harang is 2-3 with a 1.70 ERA in seven starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson was scratched from his last start with shoulder fatigue. It was the first start that Johnson had missed all season, which is somewhat remarkable given the fact that he is coming off his second major offseason back surgery in as many years. Johnson was bothered by the fatigue in his previous start against the Cardinals and had his first poor start of the second half as he matched a career high with four home runs allowed. Johnson has 294 career wins, with his last victory coming five starts ago, on Aug. 12
away_pitcher_note: Volquez missed his second bid for 17 wins when he got a no-decision during Monday's 5-4 comeback win over the Brewers. Because of an elevated pitch count that reached a season-high 119 after just 5 2/3 innings, he was finished rather early. In that span, he gave up four earned runs and five hits with three walks and 10 strikeouts. Over his last two starts, Volquez had 23 strikeouts but a pair of no-decisions to show for it.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will take the spot of Yusmeiro Petit in the rotation. The rookie earned the start based on how he performed last Sunday when called on to replace the injured Randy Johnson. Scherzer struck out 11 in five-plus innings in that game, but did not get a decision in what proved to be an Arizona loss. Scherzer has shown improvement in his changeup and slider, which has given the organization confidence that his long-term future is as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since Aug. 24, Cueto flashed good stuff and had no problems finding the plate. His only problem was the long ball, as he surrendered two solo shots to Alfonso Soriano -- enough to put him behind before he departed with 5 1/3 innings under his belt. The 22-year-old right-hander allowed five runs -- two of which scored on Soriano's third home run of the night, hit off reliever Jared Burton -- on eight hits while striking out three and walking just one. Cueto has yet to face the D-backs since he made his dazzling Major League debut against them on April 3. In that effort, the young right-hander tossed seven innings, gave up one run on just one hit and struck out 10 to pick up the win.

home_pitcher_note: Davis has been the club's most consistent pitcher over the past month while Dan Haren and Brandon Webb have struggled. The left-hander tweaked his mechanics a bit to short his arm action. That's allowed him to stay on top of the ball and command all of his pitches and work ahead in the count. Davis has problems when he falls behind in the count because he doesn't have overpowering stuff. In his last outing he allowed two runs on six hits over 5 1/3 innings against the Giants. He did not get a decision in the game, which the D-backs lost, 5-4.
away_pitcher_note: Hennessey earned another start with a sparkling four-hitter over six innings against the Diamondbacks in San Francisco on Wednesday. He walked three and struck out three in his first Major League start in two years. Hennessey was on the Opening Day roster but struggled in 11 relief appearances. He made 21 starts with Triple-A Fresno, throwing three complete games.

home_pitcher_note: What's going on with Haren is a mystery. The right-hander has struggled of late, but swears the cause is not physical. Rather Haren feels he's been thinking too much, trying too hard and just needs to go out and throw again. In his last outing against the Giants, he did show some improvement in allowing just one earned run. But he seemed to struggle with his command and ran up such a high pitch count early that he was gone after four innings having already thrown 99 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Cain endured his shortest outing of the season last Thursday at San Diego, yielding six runs and nine hits in 3 1/3 innings as the Giants lost, 11-3. He's 0-3 with a 7.71 ERA and 33 hits allowed in 21 innings over his last four starts. Cain hasn't faced Arizona this season. He was 1-0 with a 2.31 ERA in three starts against the Diamondbacks last year and is 3-2 with a 3.49 ERA against them for his career.

home_pitcher_note: Webb finally got that elusive 20th victory of the season the last time out, as he threw eight shutout innings, allowing just five hits. The win snapped a three-game losing streak for Webb and a six-game skid for the D-backs. Webb had allowed at least six runs in each of his last three starts. The right-hander became the first National League pitcher to reach 20 wins since 2005. Against the Giants, Webb is 12-5 with a 3.25 ERA in 22 starts in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez broke a six-decision losing streak, spanning nine starts, when he lasted six-plus innings to win last Friday at San Diego, 5-2. Showing no signs of the shoulder trouble that landed him on the disabled list in August, Sanchez struck out six and induced three comebackers while besting San Diego ace Jake Peavy. Sanchez has faced Arizona three times this season, posting a 1-1 record with a 7.24 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After missing a start with shoulder fatigue, Johnson came back and threw an excellent outing in his last start, going six innings, allowing just one run on five hits. He had a pitch limit of around 100, and he was right there at 98. The only run he allowed was in the first inning on an RBI double by Joey Votto, but the D-backs lost to the Reds in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum topped himself last Saturday at San Diego, recording his first professional complete game in a 7-0, four-hit shutout. With 12 strikeouts, Lincecum recorded his eighth double-digit strikeout effort of the year, tying Ray Sadecki (1968) for second-most in San Francisco history. Only Jason Schmidt (nine in 2004) has more. Lincecum threw a career-high 138 pitches against the Padres, following a 127-pitch performance against Arizona on Sept. 8, so the Giants will watch him carefully out of concern for his health.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched decently against the Dodgers, but one bad inning in the fourth did him in. He allowed three runs in the frame and three hits. All told, the left-hander gave up four runs on seven hits, struck out five and walked three in five innings. It was De La Rosa's first loss since Aug. 21, when he gave up two runs in six innings in Los Angeles.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer was lights-out in his last start on Sunday against the Reds at Chase Field, throwing six innings of two-hit, one-run ball. The rookie had nine strikeouts to three walks, but still is searching for his first Major League win, despite having a team-low ERA of 2.80 for starters. After just 14 big league appearances, Scherzer has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Cook pitched his best outing since the All-Star break on Sunday against the Dodgers, but he still fell short in his bid to tie the Rockies' single-season win record after Greg Maddux pitched equally well. Cook threw eight shutout innings while surrendering eight hits and striking out two. His location was much better than it had been in recent outings, and he kept his sinker low to induce 17 ground-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Giants, Davis pitched seven strong innings. He wasn't involved in the decision for the third consecutive game, but it may have been the best Davis had pitched in about two months, as he walked no batters and allowed only one unearned run on a dropped fly ball in the outfield. Davis has faced the Rockies only once this year, taking a no-decision on Aug. 13, when he threw five innings, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits at Coors Field in a 6-5 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Reynolds didn't last long in his first start since July 4. The 6-foot-7 righty lasted just two innings plus five batters after giving up seven runs on nine hits Monday against the Padres. Reynolds was optioned to Triple-A Colorado Springs after giving up seven runs in 1 1/3 innings on Independence Day and spent his time there working on his location and mechanics. The work didn't pay off in Reynolds' return, and he was clearly frustrated after the game.
away_pitcher_note: It was back to basics in Haren's last start. After going four starts without a win, Haren tossed the first shutout of his career, limiting the Giants to just four hits. He tied a career high by striking out 12 batters. It took Haren 117 pitches to finish the Giants off after needing 99 to get through four innings in his last start. Haren admitted he had lost a bit of confidence in himself after being roughed up in recent starts, but he seemed to get it all back again. Haren is 2-0 with a 1.92 ERA in two starts against the Rockies this year.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer was done in by one ugly inning on Wednesday in Cincinnati, pitching exceptionally well except for a three-homer fourth frame. He's looking to finish strong in his first full season as a Major League starter, and it's already fair to say the season has been a success. Wellemeyer leads the team in strikeouts and is going to top 180 innings -- likely with a sub-4.00 ERA. That's a pretty nice year.
away_pitcher_note: Webb picked up his National League-leading 21st win of the season the last time out against the Giants at Chase Field, throwing seven innings, allowing three runs -- two earned -- on eight hits. He didn't know it at the time, but his second-inning two-run double proved to be pretty decisive in a 7-6 win. With two more starts left, Webb can tie Curt Schilling for the second-highest season win total in a season in franchise history with 23.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse finally got a win to show for his solid efforts recently, giving him 14 victories to equal a career high. Over his last six starts he's averaged 6 1/3 innings per game with a 3.08 ERA, yet he only has one win. There's a lot to like about the way Lohse is pitching, though, with or without the victories. He's struck out 23 against seven walks in his past four starts. And on Thursday against the Reds, he did the one thing he hadn't been doing: he avoided the one big hit when he got in trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson escaped a first-inning jam by allowing just one run after the first three hitters of the game got on base. That was all the Big Unit ended up allowing the entire game as he matched Giants ace Tim Lincecum pitch for pitch. He was in line for his 295th career win until Juan Cruz allowed a game-tying homer in the eighth. Johnson, who recently missed a start with shoulder fatigue, saw his velocity drop to the high 80's. He took an unconventional approach on Thursday, throwing several breaking balls to retire the Giants hitters, the most breaking balls manager Bob Melvin said he has ever seen Johnson throw in a game.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright bounced back from a subpar outing by beating the Cubs over the weekend, but he still didn't pitch up to his own standards. With one start left to make a mark on the season, he'll be looking to finish with an 11th win and a positive note to go into the winter. The Cardinals are 14-5 when Wainwright starts this year, making it clear just how much they missed him when he was out from early June to late August.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is still looking for his first big-league win despite pitching well in all his starts. His last outing against the Rockies was typical of the way his year has gone. The right-hander scattered seven hits and allowed just three runs over six innings, but a lack of run support cost him in a 3-2 defeat. A hard thrower, Scherzer's fastball reaches the upper 90s. His secondary pitches -- slider and change -- have gotten better as the year has gone on.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro's last opportunity to salvage an often-frustrating season comes at home against Arizona. He actually pitched better than his line (six innings, five runs, three earned) his last time out, limiting the damage after a number of defensive missteps behind him. He may be a tired hurler, since he headed home to Florida to be with his wife and newborn twins between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Davis deserved a better fate than he received in his last outing against the Rockies. The left-hander allowed just two runs over six innings and left with a 3-2 lead only to watch the bullpen give it up. Arizona eventually got the win, but it came too late for Davis, who has received no-decisions in each of his last four starts despite not allowing more than three runs in any of those games. This will be Davis' final start of the year and he will finish with a below .500 record for the first time 2003.

home_pitcher_note: Haren will be making his final start of the 2008 regular season. The right-hander has gotten back on the winning track after a rough stretch at the end of August and beginning of September. In his last outing, he allowed three runs over six innings to the Rockies in Coors Field. All three of the runs scored on Garrett Atkins' fourth-inning homer. In his start before that, he tossed his first career shutout as the D-backs beat the Giants, 2-0.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies scratched the fatigued Aaron Cook (16-9, 3.96 ERA) and turned to Hirsh, who will be making his first Major League start this season and first since last Aug. 7, when he suffered a broken fibula when hit by a line drive from the Brewers' J.J. Hardy. This season, he suffered a rotator cuff sprain in Spring Training, spent most of the year at Triple-A Colorado Springs (4-4, 5.80 ERA), and made three relief appearances for the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Webb is looking to become the first pitcher to record 23 wins in a season since Curt Schilling and Barry Zito each did it in 2002. Webb has won his last three starts after being unsuccessful in three tries to pick up his 20th win. In his last outing against the Cardinals, Webb allowed two runs over seven innings of work and struck out Albert Pujols to end the seventh with a runner on and the D-backs clinging to a one-run lead.
away_pitcher_note: Rusch, starting because rookie Greg Reynolds had struggled mightily during his September callup, is making his first start since Aug. 14. Since his last start, Rusch has gone 0-1 with a 3.31 ERA in 13 relief appearances. In eight starts since joining the Rockies, Rusch is 4-2 with a 4.89 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson was roughed up in his last outing in St. Louis, allowing five runs in six innings, four of which came in the first inning. Unlike his previous five starts, where he ended up with five no-decisions despite posting a 3.22 ERA, Johnson was never in the game, thanks to the one bad inning. The Big Unit, who hasn't won since Aug. 12, said he hasn't been this frustrated on the mound since 2004.
away_pitcher_note: In a sense, Jimenez's first full season in the Majors is a success. Jimenez carried a 6.46 ERA in April and by the end of June was 2-8 with a 4.71 ERA. Thanks to strong work since then, Jimenez has become one of three Rockies pitchers to finish in double figures in wins. That's the first time that has happened since 2003, when Darren Oliver went 13-11, Jason Jennings went 12-13 and Shawn Chacon went 11-8.

venue_name: US West Sports Complex, Hi Corbett Field

home_pitcher_note: Webb is making his fourth consecutive Opening Day start and his first at Chase Field. The right-hander finished second in the balloting for the National League Cy Young Award last season. While he scuffled against the Rockies in 2007, Webb was 3-0 against them in 2008 with a 3.07 ERA. Fast starts are commonplace for Webb, who is 18-2 in the season's first month over his career. Last year he won his first nine starts of the year. Webb has no explanation for the hot starts, but it certainly is not due to good springs. This year he was 1-2 with a 5.82 ERA with his final outing coming in a Minor League game. Webb has also possessed a devastating sinker, but in recent years he has developed his curve and change into extremely effective pitches, particularly the change. Webb has been elected to three straight All-Star Games and has not allowed a hit in two innings during the Mid-Summer Classic. A workhorse, Webb has been on the disabled list just once in his  big league career and has thrown 208 innings or more in each of his five full seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Cook emerged to be an All-Star last season. He has always had an exceptional sinkerball, but last year he grew by being able to get more strikeouts (a career-high 96). His next step is becoming more effective against left-handed hitters, who hit .297 last year and have batted .299 against him in his career. Toward that end, he devoted much of his spring to perfecting a slider to work inside against them, and his sinker and changeup can be effective in getting weak contact. The Rockies also could use a repeat of the first month of last year, when Cook went 4-1 with a 2.41 ERA in six starts while the rest of the rotation pitched poorly. Cook has been competitive but doesn't have strong numbers against the D-backs -- 1-1 with a 5.19 ERA in three games last season and 5-4, 5.14 in 18 career appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Haren is starting his second season for the D-backs after coming over from Oakland in an eight-player deal in December 2007. The right-hander had an outstanding spring in which he worked on adding a cut fastball to his repertoire. Haren got off to a good start last April when he was 4-1. Against the Rockies in 2008 he was 3-0 with a 3.33 ERA. He was 11-4 last year at Chase Field.
away_pitcher_note: The second half of last season and this spring have been a charmed time for Jimenez. He went 8-3 with a 3.68 ERA in 14 starts after last year's All-Star break, signed a contract for four years and $10 million during the winter and starred for the Dominican Republic during the World Baseball Classic. During Spring Training, Jimenez showed the ability to get ground balls with his sinking fastball and his changeup, and used his four-seam fastball and curveball for strikeouts. The question is whether he has learned enough to be a steady pitcher during the season's early days. This spring, he worked on a habit of overthrowing when he's tired. If he can manage his energy better, he can become a top pitcher.

home_pitcher_note: Davis was limited to 146 innings last year, his lowest total since 2003, due to a battle with thyroid cancer. This spring, he was set back with some soreness in his left triceps, but by the end of the spring he seemed to be fine. Normally Davis is an innings-eating pitcher who compiles double-digit win totals. Prior to last year he had not won fewer than 11 games in four years. He had a 4.09 ERA in two cames against the Rockies in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Morales counts as the biggest success story of the Rockies' Spring Training, bigger even than the emergence of top outfield prospect Dexter Fowler. Last year, Morales was considered the best of the Rockies' prospects. He was called up late in 2007 and helped the club to its World Series appearance. But last year, when asked to begin the year in the starting rotation, he showed poor fastball command and an inconsistent delivery. He went to the Minors in late April and did not return. It wasn't until after the year that he informed the club that he had battled back issues since Spring Training. A healthy Morales showed better command this spring, and the Rockies believe he can be dominant when he has a good fastball and mixes in a changeup that's special. But one question lingers: Does he have the patience and knowledge of himself to adjust quickly when he gets out of kilter?

home_pitcher_note: Garland will be making his first start as a D-back. The right-hander was signed as a free agent to take the place of Randy Johnson in the rotation. Garland spent last season with the Angels and was with the White Sox for parts of eight seasons before that. His numbers were not pretty this spring, but he spent most of the Cactus League action working on incorporating a cut fastball as well as using his curve more.
away_pitcher_note: He won the job by default in a lackluster competition for the fifth starter's job. He's a rookie, making this rotation very young, and he burst on the scene at the end of last season and in the playoffs with some untouchable relief. The club wanted him in the bullpen when Spring Training started.

home_pitcher_note: Petit is starting in place of Brandon Webb, who was scratched because of stiffness in his shoulder. Webb told reporters after giving up six runs in just four innings on Opening Day that his shoulder stiffened up after the third inning. Petit was used in a swing role last year, pitching in long relief when needed, but also making several spot starts much like this one. Overall he appeared in 19 games with eight starts. The right-hander does not have overpowering stuff but has a good feel for pitching, and excellent control.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda was placed on the 15-day disabled list Friday with a mild oblique strain, so Stults gets the promotion from Triple-A and the start against the Diamondbacks. Stults lost out to James McDonald in the competition for the fifth starter's spot. He had a rough spring, dealing with the death of his mother just before heading for Arizona. In six Spring Training appearances, Stults had a 9.49 ERA with four strikeouts and eight walks in 9 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Haren was outstanding in his first start of the year. He held the Rockies to just one run on three hits over seven innings. The right-hander fanned nine and did not walk a batter. Unfortunately for him, one of the hits was a solo home run by Troy Tulowitzki. The homer came on the first pitch of the fifth inning and was all the runs the Rockies would need in a 3-0 win. Haren had a good spring, in fact the club limited his innings towards the end because he had been so efficient with his pitches early in camp that his innings total got a little high.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf let a one-run lead slip away and couldn't get out of the sixth inning in a loss to San Diego. He was charged with four runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings. Afterward, he criticized himself for not being aggressive enough with his approach, nibbling on the corners instead of challenging hitters to put the ball in play. Wolf has not won his first start of a season since 2003.

home_pitcher_note: Davis did not have one of his better outings on Wednesday as he allowed four runs on four hits in five innings and the D-backs lost to the Rockies, 9-2, at Chase Field. Things didn't start on a good note for the left-hander as he allowed a home run to Dexter Fowler on the game's first pitch. He settled in for a couple of innings after that, but the Rockies were able to put up a three spot against him in the fourth. Davis was limited to 146 innings last year, his lowest total since 2003, due to a battle with thyroid cancer. This spring, he was set back with some soreness in his left triceps, but by the end of spring seemed to be fine.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer hasn't really been quite right at any point this year, whether it be in Spring Training or his first start. He's identified a mechanical key that he believes will solve the issue, so the hope is that he'll be sorted out in time for Monday's game. He'll need to be, as he's pitching in one of the National League's most hitter-friendly ballparks.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will be making his season debut. He was set back in January when his shoulder was a little stiff and he received a cortisone shot. Since that time he has not complained of any problems with the shoulder. The right-hander started for Class A Visalia on Thursday and allowed two runs (one earned) on one hit and four walks over 4 2/3 innings. He was dazzling in his Major League debut last year when he struck out seven in 4 1/3 hitless innings of relief. It was the longest debut outing in modern Major League history by a pitcher who retired every hitter he faced.
away_pitcher_note: It's hard to imagine how Carpenter can improve on his first start, which incidentally brought his first win since the 2006 World Series. He showed outstanding stuff and command with all of his repertoire, and he was efficient enough to get through seven innings on 92 pitches. Now he'll try to repeat that showing at a tough ballpark for pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: Garland won his first regular-season game in a D-backs uniform last Friday when he held the Dodgers to three runs on five hits over seven innings. The right-hander had allowed just one run over 6 1/3 innings before giving up a two-run homer to Casey Blake in the seventh on a sinker that stayed up a little more than he would have liked. Garland, who was signed as a free agent in January, also drew a key walk during a five-run third-inning rally.
away_pitcher_note: One down, 30 or so to go, but in the early going Pineiro looks very good. He pitched a fine game in his season debut on Friday night against Houston. However, he's often pitched very well at Busch Stadium. Now he'll have to do it on the road, at a tough park for pitchers, in Phoenix. Still, Pineiro has been excellent since the start of Spring Training, and he and the Cards are confident that he can enjoy a better year in 2009 than he posted in '08.

home_pitcher_note: If Brandon Webb had rejoined Arizona's rotation in this game, as had been advertised, Sanchez would have faced a Cy Young Award winner for the second game in a row, but that will not be the case. Sanchez fared poorly last Saturday against San Diego's Jake Peavy, surrendering five runs and four hits while walking five in 4 2/3 innings. Sanchez struck out seven, but flamed out quickly after fanning five of the first six batters he faced. The Diamondbacks have tormented Sanchez, who's 1-5 against them lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Haren was originally scheduled to start on Saturday, but with Brandon Webb going on the disabled list the team decided to bump everyone in the rotation up a day. Because of Thursday's off day, everyone will still be pitching on the fifth day. Haren was outstanding in his first two starts, but came away with nothing to show for either of them. In 13 innings this year he has allowed three runs yet the D-backs offense has not given him any support so both games wound up being losses. In his last game against the Dodgers he allowed two runs (one of which scored on a little invoked "four-out rule") and took a 3-1 loss. He held the Rockies to just one run on three hits over seven innings in his first start, but the D-backs fell 3-0.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum endured his second sub-par outing in two 2009 starts at San Diego, yielding four runs and 10 hits in 5 1/3 innings. Though Lincecum's secondary pitches, such as his off-speed deliveries, remain effective, his fastball command continues to be short of his Cy Young Award-winning best, which has made all the difference. The Giants hope that the support of the home crowd and Lincecum's success against Arizona (3-1, 2.23 ERA in six lifetime starts) will bode well for him.
away_pitcher_note: Davis was originally scheduled to start on Sunday, but with Brandon Webb going on the disabled list, the team decided to bump everyone in the rotation up a day. Because of Thursday's off day, everyone will still be pitching on the fifth day. Davis was outstanding in his last start against the Cardinals at Chase Field. The left-hander allowed just two runs over eight innings. One was a homer by Albert Pujols and the other an opposite-field shot by Brian Barden. Unfortunately for Davis, the D-backs offense was once again quiet and he took a 2-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: The future Hall of Famer will face his former teammates for the first time in his 22-year career. The Diamondbacks weren't born when Interleague Play began in 1997, and by the time they came into existence Johnson was pitching for them. Nor did they cross paths during his two seasons with the New York Yankees (2005-06). Johnson did face the D-backs last month in Cactus League play and excelled, allowing two hits in three shutout innings while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer made his season debut on Tuesday night against the Cardinals and allowed three runs on five hits over five innings. The right-hander started the year on the disabled list after a stiff shoulder in January put him a couple of weeks behind the other pitchers this spring. Scherzer was long gone by the time Tuesday's game was decided, a 7-6 Arizona win in 10 innings. Scherzer was dazzling in his Major League debut last year when he struck out seven in 4 1/3 hitless innings of relief. It was the longest debut outing in modern Major League history by a pitcher who retired every hitter he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Garland has had two polar opposite outings with the D-backs. He won his first regular-season game when he held the Dodgers to three runs on five hits over seven innings. The right-hander had allowed just one run over 6 1/3 innings before giving up a two-run homer to Casey Blake in the seventh on a sinker that stayed up a little more than he would have liked. Garland, who was signed as a free agent in January, also drew a key walk during a five-run third inning rally. In his most recent outing, on Wednesday against the Cardinals, he allowed seven runs on seven hits over 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis has pitched the Rockies to wins over the Phillies and the Cubs. He went seven innings and gave up one run against the Cubs on Wednesday, and his best inning might have been his last. After running into trouble in the sixth, he pitched an efficient 1-2-3 seventh. Marquis has pitched well at all National League West venues but hasn't had the best of fortune at Chase Field. He is 0-3, but with a 3.60 ERA and .211 batting average against.

home_pitcher_note: Petit will get the starting nod on Tuesday in place of Brandon Webb, who is on the 15-day disabled list with stiffness in his right shoulder. Petit also took Webb's turn last time through the rotation. The right-hander cruised through the first three innings in that game before running into trouble in the fourth. Orlando Hudson homered and Russell Martin doubled home a pair to cap the inning. Those three runs were the only ones allowed by Petit in five innings. The Arizona bullpen, though, fell apart that night in an 11-2 D-backs loss.
away_pitcher_note: Morales makes his return from a stint in the Minor Leagues, where the Rockies temporarily kept Morales because they didn't need a fifth starter. The 23-year-old left-hander was sharp in his lone Major League start this season, allowing just one run on four hits against the Diamondbacks in the Rockies' third game of the year. In his career against Arizona, Morales is 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in three starts. In his lone start at Colorado Springs, Morales threw six scoreless innings against Reno.

home_pitcher_note: Haren could easily be 3-0 right now instead of 0-3. The right-hander has allowed one run in two of his starts and just two in the other, yet has gotten little if any run support as Arizona has scored just one run total in the three games that he has started. His last start, on Friday against the Giants, was typical. He allowed just one run over six innings and did not walk a batter while fanning six, yet came away with a 2-0 loss. In a rare show of emotion, he slammed his helmet and bat when he was pinch-hit for in the top of the seventh inning. In 19 innings this year, Haren has allowed just 12 hits and walked three while striking out 17.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched his way out of trouble for 5 1/3 scoreless innings against the Dodgers on Friday but was denied his first win of the season. De La Rosa allowed five hits and four walks but pitched out of several jams to keep the Dodgers scoreless. But the Dodgers came back for four runs in the seventh against the Rockies bullpen as De La Rosa was saddled with the no-decision. The left-hander is 1-1 with a 2.53 ERA in seven appearances against the Diamondbacks, who signed him as an amateur free agent in 1998.

home_pitcher_note: Davis followed up one of his best starts in a D-backs uniform with an even better one against the Giants on Saturday at AT&T Park. The left-hander tossed eight shutout innings, outdueling Tim Lincecum for a 2-0 win. The game was scoreless until the ninth, when Chris Young laced a two-run double to left. Davis threw more curveballs in the game than he usually does, and he cut back on the amount of times he went to his cut fastball, though the lefty still threw between 20 and 25 cutters. Over his past two starts, Davis has allowed two runs in 16 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After entering last Saturday's start with a 7.56 ERA in his first two outings, Lincecum blanked Arizona for eight innings, walking none and matching a career high with 13 strikeouts. He received no decision in a 2-0 Giants loss. Obviously, Lincecum regained his Cy Young Award-winning form, partly because he detected a flaw in his delivery. His front (left) foot was landing three inches closer than usual to the right-handed batter's box, diminishing his velocity and throwing his pitches askew.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has struggled to keep his pitch counts down in his two starts this year and the biggest culprit is walks. The right-hander has walked six and fanned seven over 10 innings. In his last outing, he walked four and allowed one run over five innings as the D-backs fell to Randy Johnson and the Giants, 2-0. Scherzer started the year on the disabled list after a stiff shoulder in January put him a couple of weeks behind the other pitchers this spring. Scherzer was dazzling in his Major League debut last year when he struck out seven in 4 1/3 hitless innings of relief. It was the longest debut outing in modern Major League history by a pitcher who retired every hitter he faced.
away_pitcher_note: In his third attempt at career victory No. 296, the Big Unit finally secured the elusive win as he shut out Arizona, his former team, on one hit through seven innings. Johnson no-hit the Diamondbacks for six innings until Augie Ojeda doubled to open the seventh. Johnson downplayed facing his former team, but he admitted that returning to Chase Field could be an emotional experience for him. Johnson might have benefited from receiving an extra day of rest before facing Arizona last Sunday; he'll have an extra day of rest this time, too.

home_pitcher_note: Garland pitched well his last time out, holding the Rockies to two runs (one earned) on six hits over 6 2/3 innings. Garland did a nice job of keeping the ball down, which is always a key for him. His two starts before that were polar opposites. He won his first regular-season game when he held the Dodgers to three runs on five hits in seven innings, but against the Cardinals, he allowed seven runs on seven hits in 3 2/3 innings. The right-hander was signed by the D-backs to a one-year deal with a mutual option for 2010 during the offseason.
away_pitcher_note: Throwing ball four often has been Cain's downfall in his relatively brief career. But he has issued only five unintentional free passes in three starts this season. Even with intentional walks, Cain has averaged 2.8 walks per nine innings, compared to 3.8 last year, 3.6 in 2007 and 4.1 in 2006. Cain's 3-3 in 10 career starts against Arizona, including 2-2, 4.08 in six outings at Chase Field. Victimized so frequently by poor run support in the previous two seasons, Cain has received seven and six runs while he has been on the mound in his two victories this year.

home_pitcher_note: Haren could easily be 4-0 right now instead of 1-3. Prior to his last start, Haren had received a total of one run of support in three games. The D-backs finally scored some runs for him against the Rockies last Wednesday when they put together a two-run rally in the seventh. Haren allowed just six hits over seven innings to pick up the 2-0 win. His 0-3 start marked the first time a pitcher had started the year losing his first three games while having an ERA under 2.00 since Juan Cruz did it for the Cubs in 2002. With every at-bat potentially a game-changer, Haren did not give in to Colorado hitters and wound up walking two. Overall he has walked just three and fanned 17 in his 19 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a win in his last start but pitched well enough to get a "W." Trouble is, he was outpitched by Johnny Cueto. In Lilly's last two starts, he has not given up an earned run in 13 2/3 innings, and has 10 strikeouts. Against the Reds in his last start, he did not walk a batter over seven innings, giving up five hits. Lilly used his curveball more against Cincinnati. It did the trick. The Reds' only score off him was set up by a throwing error he made fielding a bunt.

home_pitcher_note: Petit has taken Brandon Webb's place in the rotation while the right-hander recovers from shoulder stiffness. In two starts, Petit has allowed five earned runs in 10 innings. Unfortunately the bullpen has struggled both times he has pitched -- in his first outing against the Dodgers, which resulted in an 11-2 loss, and his last time out against the Rockies, which turned into a 9-6 Arizona loss. Petit has filled the spot-starter/long-relief role for the D-backs the past two seasons. Though he doesn't possess overpowering stuff, he has a good feel for pitching and generally has good command.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano took the loss in his last start against the Reds and Aaron Harang. Big Z gave up four runs on seven hits over seven innings while striking out seven. He didn't get much help from his defense -- or himself -- as the Cubs misplayed a couple of balls and Zambrano made a throwing error on a pickoff and the runner eventually scored. Zambrano is 1-2 with a 4.88 ERA in four career starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Any pitcher besides the reigning NL Cy Young Award winner would be a welcomed sight for Davis. The left-hander faced Giants ace Tim Lincecum in his last two starts, pitching eight innings in his first outing against San Francisco and six innings in the second. Davis struggled with his curveball in his last outing against the Giants and was charged with nine hits and five earned runs in the loss. He should be feeling confident at the plate after picking up an RBI against Lincecum.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster kept the Cubs in the game in his last start but didn't get much help. Facing the Cardinals, he gave up three runs on seven hits and one walk over six innings. Dempster struck out six in his second straight no-decision and third in four starts. Dempster said he felt good, but got into jams. He did not get a decision in his only start against the D-backs last year, giving up two earned runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan lasted six innings in his last outing on Saturday at Houston, and did not figure in the decision. He allowed only four hits, but two of those were home runs by Carlos Lee and Michael Bourn. One of the four runs the Astros scored was unearned and Suppan left for a pinch-hitter with the game tied at 4. Seeking his second win in a row, he struck out four, walked three and threw 98 pitches. Suppan has a 3-3 record and 4.43 ERA for his career in eight games against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer cruised through the first four innings of his last start against the Giants, but ran into a buzzsaw in the fifth. The right-hander allowed four runs in the inning and ended up on the short end of a 5-3 decision. Scherzer is still looking for his first Major League win after 19 big league games, 10 of which have been starts. Scherzer began the year on the disabled list after receiving a cortisone shot in his right shoulder in January. He has yet to pitch past the fifth inning this year in large part because his pitch count tends to rise early in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Parra pitched five innings in his last outing, Sunday at Houston, before being lifted for a pinch-hitter with the Brewers trailing by one. He gave up five hits and three runs, but only one of them was earned. He struck out four, walked three and threw 97 pitches. Parra felt he had better command of his fastball against the Astros, and manager Ken Macha was pleased to see him throw more changeups. Parra has allowed only one earned run in two games, a total of 13 innings, in his career against Arizona. That gives him an 0.69 ERA vs. the Diamondbacks.
away_pitcher_note: Garland has pitched well in three of his four starts this season. In his last outing against the Giants, he allowed just one run through the first seven innings. The Giants were able to break through against him in the eighth with the big blow being a three-run homer by Pablo Sandoval, which came after Garland had passed the 100-pitch mark. His one rough outing came against the Cardinals when he allowed seven runs in just 3 2/3 innings. He has victories against the Dodgers and Rockies to his credit.

home_pitcher_note: Looper worked without his good fastball on Monday against the Pirates and he made it work, using a higher than usual number of changeups and cutters to match a career high with seven strikeouts in five respectable innings. He was charged with two earned runs, which wasn't bad considering the first four Pirates hitters reached safely in the first inning, and he was in line for his third consecutive win before reliever Carlos Villanueva surrendered a tying, two-run double in the eighth. He has a 4.08 ERA against the Diamondbacks, but only two of his 28 appearances against Arizona have been starts. Both were in 2007, and both were no-decisions after Looper surrendered a total of nine earned runs in 9 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Haren could easily be 5-0 right now instead of 2-3. In his first three starts of the year -- all losses -- the right-hander received one total run of support. In his last start against the Cubs, Haren was on top of his game. He allowed a leadoff homer to Alfonso Soriano, but only gave up two more hits the rest of the way as he tossed the seventh complete game of his career. Haren helped himself out offensively in the fourth inning when he chopped a two-run double down the left-field line. His 0-3 start was the first time a pitcher had started the year losing his first three games while having an ERA under 2.00 since Juan Cruz did it for the Cubs in 2002. Overall, he has walked just five and fanned 36 in his 35 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Five days after carrying a no-hitter into the eighth inning in Philadelphia, Bush surrendered his first hit to the third batter he faced on Tuesday. It was one of six Pirates hits off Bush, who lasted just five innings and surrendered five runs, four of them earned. Four of the runs scored on two-run doubles by Wisconsin natives -- the first by Eric Hinske in the third inning and the other by Jason Jaramillo in the fifth after Bush brushed the jerseys of Pirates hitters with consecutive pitches. He'll aim for better command against the Diamondbacks. Bush is 4-1 with a 4.15 ERA in five previous starts against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Petit has taken Brandon Webb's place in the rotation while the right-hander is on the disabled list with shoulder stiffness. The right-hander struggled in his last start against the Cubs on Tuesday. After working two scoreless innings, he gave up a three-run homer to Alfonso Soriano. That seemed to open the floodgates as one inning later the Cubs chased him from the game with a four-run rally. In two starts prior to that, Petit allowed five earned runs in 10 innings. Unfortunately the bullpen struggled both times. Petit has filled the spot-starter/long-relief role for the D-backs the past two seasons. Though he doesn't possess overpowering stuff, he has a good feel for pitching and generally has good command.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Kershaw posted a quality start at Coors Field, holding the Rockies to three runs on four hits and four walks in six innings, striking out four. His damage came in a two-inning stretch, when the left-hander walked three and balked in a run in the third, then yielded a two-run homer and the lead in the fourth. Kershaw recovered well, holding Colorado hitless for his final two innings and watching his team reclaim the lead in the top of the seventh. His poise under pressure was a definite sign of growth for the quickly maturing southpaw.
away_pitcher_note: Davis' outstanding start to the year has been somewhat overshadowed by teammate Dan Haren. Davis tossed seven shutout innings his last time out against the Cubs on Wednesday at Chase Field. The left-hander didn't look like he would be able to go seven after throwing a whopping 50 pitches. He was able, however to adjust and take advantage of the Cubs' hitters aggressiveness over the next several innings to hang around. Davis has thrown at least seven innings in three of his five starts and has gone eight innings twice, including an impressive 2-0 win over the Giants on April 18.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver was tabbed as the Dodgers' fifth starter on Saturday, starting instead of the struggling James McDonald, who is now one of the club's long relievers. Weaver pitched well in his lone appearance this season, allowing no runs over four innings in relief of McDonald on Thursday. Tuesday will be Weaver's first Major League start since Sept. 28, 2007, with the Mariners. Weaver is 2-2 with a 3.71 ERA in eight career starts against the Diamondbacks.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer might have had the best start of his young career Thursday when he shut out the Milwaukee Brewers for six innings, striking out seven and allowing one walk with five hits. The Arizona offense didn't back him, however, and the 1-0 lead Scherzer had when he left was lost by the bullpen in a 4-1 loss. It was the most pitches Scherzer had been able to throw (107), with an effective cocktail of changeups and sliders along with an electric fastball, which he used regularly to strike out slugger Prince Fielder three times. Still, the 24-year-old is in pursuit of his first Major League win.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy went into his last start on May 1 with a 5.74 ERA and an uncanny lack of command in his previous starts. He got back on track during a no-decision against the Dodgers, tossing eight scoreless innings, allowing two hits with one walk. Peavy had eight strikeouts and said following the game that he wanted to be more aggressive with the Dodgers' dangerous lineup. It worked, as he avoided trouble all night and never let a runner get as far as second base. It was the longest outing at Dodger Stadium, a place where he's 6-1 with a 3.08 ERA for his career. This will be his first meeting against the Diamondbacks this season.
away_pitcher_note: Garland kept the Brewers off the scoreboard for six innings Friday before getting charged with a pair of runs in the seventh, though his team rallied to prevent a hard-luck loss. The right-hander dropped his ERA more than half a run in the outing, and enjoyed a particularly notable inning when he struck out Milwaukee's Ryan Braun, Prince Fielder and Mike Cameron with the tying run in scoring position and nobody out. It was the first time in 15 career outings that Garland had appeared for longer than three innings and walked no batters. Only two starts fit that description in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Young bounced back from a rough start on April 27 when he allowed a career-high eight runs in three innings in a loss to the Rockies on April 27. How big a bounceback? Well, consider Young allowed one run in seven innings on six hits with one walk and five strikeouts. All this against what is regarded as one of the top lineups in the National League. In the fifth inning, Young froze Manny Ramirez with a dandy curveball for a called third strike. That start looked a lot like the one on April 22 in San Francisco where Young tossed seven scoreless innings in a no-decision against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: After non-existent run support cost Haren losses in his first three starts, the Diamondbacks have done enough to get their ace of the moment back to .500. For the first time in his career, Haren struck out double-digit batters in consecutive outings, punching out 11 Milwaukee Brewers on Saturday to follow up his 10-strikeout, complete-game performance in Chicago one start earlier. Haren did all of this without his breaking pitch, which he said he struggled to locate, but that didn't stop him from recording a dominant eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Petit didn't bounce back resoundingly after three starts' worth of struggle in the early going, but he did enjoy better results Sunday in Milwaukee. The right-hander allowed three runs -- two on back-to-back homers and another on a two-out infield single -- on four hits in five innings. Manager Bob Melvin said he never suggested Petit's starting spot was in jeopardy prior to the outing, so it seems probable that the young hurler will get more opportunities with Brandon Webb on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Martis threw a complete game and gave up one run his last time out. It was the first nine-inning complete game by a Nationals pitcher since Pedro Astacio went the distance against the Braves on Aug. 15, 2006. It was also the first by a Washington hurler at Nationals Park. Martis' only blemish was giving up a solo home run to Colby Rasmus in the seventh inning. Before the home run, Martis was nearly perfect. In fact, he didn't give up a hit for 4 2/3 innings, and allowed just five hits and no walks overall, while striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: Davis did not have one of his better outings in his last start against the Dodgers on Monday. The left-hander allowed four runs on five hits in 4 1/3 innings. Davis walked four in the game. Afterwards he said he felt like he was trying to be too fine with his pitches, which led to him falling behind in counts and putting hitters on. He was helped out in the second inning by a triple play, the second in franchise history, when Casey Blake hit a liner to shortstop Josh Wilson, who started the 6-4-3 triple play. Davis is in the final year of a three-year extension he signed after being traded to Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: After picking up his fist win of the season on Monday against the Astros, Lannan admitted to not having his best stuff. But a win is a win. Lannan allowed four runs -- three earned --  on nine hits over six innings. After struggling to get through the fifth inning, he came back out the sixth and got the Astros' sixth, seventh and eighth hitters on consecutive groundouts.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has been the victim of poor run support in his short big league career. In five starts this year, the D-backs have scored a total of six runs for him. It was more of the same his last time out against the Dodgers on Monday, when his teammates managed just one run for him. Scherzer allowed three runs (two earned) in the first inning of what turned out to be a 3-1 loss. The former No. 1 pick is now winless in 21 games (12 starts) dating back to last year when he made his debut by striking out seven Astros in 4 1/3 perfect innings. Scherzer started the year on the disabled list after experiencing shoulder stiffness in January that required a cortisone shot.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen started for the Nationals on Tuesday afternoon at Nationals Park, and by the time he left the game after five innings, the Astros had a 5-2 lead. It was the first time since April 7 that Olsen didn't have a quality start. On Sunday, Olsen will face the Diamondbacks for the fourth time in his career. He is 0-2 with an 8.47 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Garland pitched well against the Padres at PETCO Park in his last outing as he tossed seven shutout innings in a 3-1 win. The right-hander likes pitching at PETCO. In two career games there he has allowed one earned run in 14 innings. Garland pitched his way into and out of trouble a few times in the game, but was able to make his pitches when he needed to. Three double plays behind him certainly helped as well. Garland was signed as a free agent in January after the D-backs let Randy Johnson go to San Francisco. Four of Garland's six starts this year have been very good, one was so-so and one bad. Garland has faced the Reds once in his career and picked up a win as he allowed one run over eight innings.
