away_pitcher_note: In a 15-3 loss to the Brewers on Wednesday, Arroyo tied his season high with nine earned runs allowed with seven hits, three walks and two home runs over one-plus innings. He threw only 46 pitches. It was Arroyo's worst outing since June 24, 2008, at Toronto, where he allowed 11 hits and 10 earned runs over one-plus innings. That game was the start of a huge turnaround for Arroyo, who went 15-6 with a 3.76 ERA, over last season and 2009, before Wednesday. Ironically, Arroyo's two worst starts have come after he said he's felt the best coming out of the bullpen from pregame warm ups. He also allowed nine runs over 5 2/3 innings on April 25 vs. Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Haren didn't have one of his better outings in his last start as he allowed three runs on eight hits over six innings in a 4-3 10-inning loss to the Padres. The right-hander did not figure in the decision. Uncharacteristicly, he was not able to hold leads of 2-0 and 3-2. His biggest frustration came in the fifth when he retired the first two hitters but then walked the pitcher. The Padres followed the walk with three straight hits to tie the game at 2-2. Haren has been one of the league's top pitchers. He lost his first three starts because his offense scored a total of one run for him in those games.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the first time Owings has faced his former team since he was traded to the Reds from Arizona in September as a player to be named later in the Adam Dunn deal. Owings did deliver a pinch-hit, game-winning double to beat the Diamondbacks right after switching teams. During a 6-5 win over the Brewers on Thursday, when he delivered an RBI triple for the go-ahead run, Owings pitched six innings for the victory and looked better than his line indicated. He allowed five runs (four earned) on seven hits with one walk and four strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Augenstein will have his contract selected from Double-A Mobile in order to start Wednesday's game against the Reds. The right-hander, who will be making his Major League debut, is taking the spot of Yusmeiro Petit, who in turn was taking the spot of injured ace Brandon Webb in the rotation. In five starts this year, Augenstein was 5-0 with a 0.78 ERA. Augenstein went a combined 7-5 with a 2.74 in 2008, splitting the season between Arizona's two Class A level teams. He was the team's seventh-round pick out of the University of Florida in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto has given up just three earned runs over his last 33 2/3 innings for a 0.81 ERA over his last five outings. Until Friday, he hadn't allowed more than one walk in any of his previous four starts. During a 6-4 win over the Cardinals on Friday, the right-hander worked seven innings and allowed five hits and two walks with three strikeouts while throwing 98 pitches. He left the game with a 6-1 lead. The lone run scored on a groundball double play that ended Cueto's career-high scoreless streak at 15 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his victorious 115-pitch effort against the Phillies on Saturday, Vazquez should benefit from the one extra day of rest he'll receive entering his first start against the Diamondbacks since 2003. The only runs he surrendered in 7 2/3 innings against the Phillies came courtesy of a pair of solo homers. After allowing just one home run in his first five starts, the 33-year-old right-hander has seen each of the eight runs he's combined to allow in his past two outings come courtesy of the long ball. During his past six starts, Vazquez has worked 40 1/3 innings, recorded 57 strikeouts and issued just seven walks.
away_pitcher_note: Davis pitched well in his last time out, but did not come away with a win because his offense struggled to score off Nationals starter John Lannan. Davis allowed one run on four hits over six innings and left trailing, 1-0. In his start prior to that against the Dodgers, Davis struggled allowing four runs on five hits in lasting just 4 1/3 innings. Afterwards he said he felt like he was trying to be too fine with his pitches, which caused him to fall behind in the count.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami has shown definite improvement over his past two starts, limiting the Mets and Phillies to two runs in each start. While pitching six strong innings in Philadelphia on Sunday, the right-hander notched his first win in five starts and didn't allow a homer for the second successive start. While focusing on keeping his pitches low, Kawakami has limited some of the extra-base hits that were a problem during his first month in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Remarkably -- considering his pedigree (first-round pick in 2006 First-Year Player Draft) and spectacular Major League debut -- Scherzer remains winless in 22 games and 13 starts. He is 0-7 despite a solid 3.39 ERA, making him just another hard-luck pitcher on the Arizona staff. In his last start, Sunday against the Nationals, he allowed three homers for the first time in his budding career.

home_pitcher_note: While winning his fourth consecutive start with seven solid innings against the Mets on Monday night, Lowe provided one of his best performances of the season. The 35-year-old sinkerballer held the Mets hitless through the first 3 2/3 innings and limited them to just one extra-base hit -- a seventh-inning leadoff double. He has allowed two earned runs or less in three of his past four starts. Having pitched the previous four seasons with the Dodgers, Lowe is familiar with the Diamondbacks. He was 3-1 with a 2.05 ERA in five starts against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: Garland got shelled by the Reds on Monday, yielding seven runs on 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings. He constantly left balls up in the zone, and Cincinnati made him pay. The D-backs had won Garland's past four starts, three of which were quality outings, including his seven shutout innings May 5 in San Diego. The durable right-hander has now failed to get into the fourth in either of his two losses while pitching into the seventh in his five other starts.

home_pitcher_note: After taking a step forward with his first victory since Opening Day one start earlier, Nolasco took two steps back last Wednesday against the Brewers, lasting just 3 2/3 innings and allowing eight runs. He gave up single tallies in the first three frames and then endured a nightmarish two-out rally oozing with bad luck -- with virtually no well-struck baseballs but five runs scoring. He did take responsibility, however, for two-out walks to the No. 7 and No. 8 hitter, starting a rampage of nine straight Brewers reaching base. The right-hander has yet to find the groove he had for much of last year.
away_pitcher_note: Haren could give Johan Santana and Cliff Lee a good argument as the Majors' premiere hard-luck pitcher. He's taken one loss essentially for every two runs he has allowed. He's been on the losing end of two of the D-backs' three shutouts and, in his last start, Arizona was again scoreless throughout his seven-inning stint. But the right-hander hasn't let the pressure of tight games affect his pitching.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins can breathe easy -- at least for now as their ace right-hander is good to go. Johnson came out of the game early in his last start against the Brewers at Miller Park on Thursday, going just four innings, giving up three runs (two earned) on three hits while walking five and striking out three. The 25-year-old hasn't gone less than that since June 23, 2007, when he went three innings against the Twins. The reason: Johnson said he felt a little tired in his trapezoid/shoulder area. But after getting a little ice, he did his regular throwing off flat ground the day after his start, and Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez said, barring a setback, he should be ready to go when his turn comes again. That next turn will come against the D-Backs, a team he threw seven shutout innings against in his only career start.
away_pitcher_note: Garland was scheduled to start Sunday's game in Atlanta, which got postponed by rain. He got shelled by the Reds on Monday, yielding seven runs on 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings. He constantly left balls up in the zone, and Cincinnati made him pay. The D-backs had won Garland's past four starts, three of which were quality outings, including his seven shutout innings May 5 in San Diego. The durable right-hander has now failed to get into the fourth in either of his two losses while pitching into the seventh in his five other starts.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad was looking sharp early on in his last start against the Dodgers on Friday, throwing five scoreless innings while only giving up one hit. But things started to unravel in the sixth, and the 22-year-old ended up taking the loss while giving up four runs on seven hits in six-plus innings. Volstad gave up three runs in a sixth inning that saw him throw 26 pitches and allow Los Angeles to tie the game. The Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., native still hasn't recorded a win since April 14. In his only other start against the Diamondbacks, Volstad took the loss while giving up four runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis was scheduled to pitch Wednesday anyway after Sunday's rainout, so he will be going on normal rest. Davis had a rough outing his last time out, in more ways than one. The left-hander made a crucial throwing error that led to a two-run second inning for the Braves, and he also took exception in the seventh when he was lifted for a pinch-hitter after just 80 pitches. The D-backs wound up losing the game, 4-3.

home_pitcher_note: After Tuesday night's 5-3 loss, the Marlins announced Penn will make his first start as a Marlin in Game 2. Penn last made a big league start in 2006, while he was with the Orioles. Because he has been used as a long reliever, Penn will be on a pitch count between 60-70 pitches. The right-hander has made 12 relief appearances, and he's logged 17 2/3 innings. His last outing came on Sunday, when he threw 2 1/3 innings on Sunday against the Dodgers, striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: After Sunday's game at Turner Field was rained out, Augenstein was originally scheduled to pitch on Thursday. Now, he'll be going on six days' rest. Augenstein made his big league debut last week against the Reds at Chase Field, allowing five runs in 6 1/3 innings. One of the reasons he had such tremendous success at Double-A Mobile was his ability to throw strikes, and he displayed that in his debut, walking two -- one of which was intentional. Augenstein is taking the spot of Yusmeiro Petit, who in turn was taking the spot of injured ace Brandon Webb in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Things didn't really get off on the right foot in Miller's first start since April 20 on Saturday, but the 6-foot-7 southpaw weathered it and ended up with the win against the Dodgers. Miller needed 30 pitches -- only 13 of them strikes -- to get out of a one-run first inning and put the leadoff man on in each of his first four frames. But the 23-year-old kept his team in the game through five innings, which saw him give up two runs on four hits while striking out four, walking four and throwing 98 pitches -- 55 for strikes. Miller is 1-1 with a 2.13 ERA in two career starts against the D-Backs.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer was scheduled to pitch Friday, on five days' rest, after the D-backs' rainout at Turner Field on Sunday. But with a doubleheader scheduled for Wednesday after a second straight postponement on Monday, he was moved up to Thursday. Scherzer finally picked up his first big league win last Saturday night in Atlanta. Because of some poor run support and bullpen issues, it took the right-hander until his 24th appearance and 14th start to accomplish the feat. Scherzer was on top of his game against the Braves, allowing just four hits in six shutout innings. The key play in the game was a fake-to-third-throw-to-first pickoff play in the first that turned a first-and-third with one out situation into an inning-ending double play. Scherzer cruised from that point forward.

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old Cahill had a two-game winning streak snapped last time out with the shortest outing of his brief Major League career. He lasted just 2 1/3 innings, allowing a season-high seven runs on seven hits. It was only the second time in his first big league season he allowed more than two earned runs. His next start against Arizona will mark his first against a National League opponent. He'll attempt to lower his home ERA, which is almost double that of his ERA in road games.
away_pitcher_note: The D-backs reached down for Minor League right-hander Billy Buckner to fill this slot. Buckner allowed three runs in 16 2/3 innings for Triple-A Reno in his recent efforts to get the attention of Arizona manager A.J. Hinch. Overall with Reno, Buckner's 2-2 with a 3.81 ERA in 28 1/3 innings and has allowed just one home run. Buckner will be making his first start as a D-back and his first in the Majors since a Sept. 27, 2007, encounter for Kansas City against the White Sox, which he lost. Buckner began the season on the D-backs' 25-man roster. He pitched four innings over three games, surrendering seven runs. He allowed seven hits and walked four, striking out three.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, who signed a Minor League deal with the A's in February and did not earn a spot on the team as a non-roster invitee to Spring Training, was recalled from Triple-A Sacramento on Tuesday and will make his first start for Oakland against the only team for whom he's played in the big leagues. Gonzalez was 3-2 with a 5.22 ERA in seven starts at Sacramento, his last appearance being among his best -- he gave up a run on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings. Gonzalez, 26, started last season in Arizona's starting rotation but was moved to the bullpen after six starts. He's 14-21 with a 5.97 ERA in 80 Major League games, including 35 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren lost a start on Monday at Land Shark Stadium, as the 29-year-old pitched three innings of one-run ball and threw 56 pitches before rain began to fall hard in the top of the fourth. After a one-hour, 36-minute rain delay, the D-backs had their second straight road game postponed. In his last official start, on May 12, Haren gave up three runs on six hits while striking out five and not walking a batter in seven innings against the Reds. He has now turned in a quality start all eight times he's taken the mound this season. In his only career start against the Athletics, Haren gave up one run in seven innings, earning the win.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired in the trade that sent Joe Blanton to the Phillies last summer, Outman appears to be hitting his stride as a member of Oakland's young starting rotation. A 24-year-old rookie whose fastball sits in the low- to mid-90s, Outman, who has 96-97 in his back pocket when needed, turned in his second consecutive quality start Tuesday against the host Rays, scattering three hits and a walk while striking out a career-high six over six shutout innings on the way to a no-decision. His previous time out, Outman beat the Royals with a similar line: one run on three hits and two walks with four strikeouts over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on seven days' rest, Garland bounced back from a rocky outing in a win against the Marlins on Tuesday. The 29-year-old gave up two runs -- one earned -- on seven hits while striking out three and walking one. Garland started off the game pitching five shutout innings, allowing just five baserunners in that span, but gave up a solo home run to Hanley Ramirez with one out in the sixth. He finished throwing 80 pitches and could've kept going, but with the D-Backs trailing, 2-1, in the top of the seventh, manager A.J. Hinch opted for a pinch-hitter for Garland with two runners in scoring position. In 17 career starts against the A's, Garland is 4-11 with a 5.22 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Although it has yet to be officially announced, this would be Davis' turn in the rotation. During a loss in Game 1 of a doubleheader on Wednesday, the 33-year-old right-hander said he "battled himself more than he battled the Marlins." He gave up six runs on six hits while walking five and striking out four and left after 4 1/3 innings. Upon his departure -- after throwing 101 pitches (53 for strikes) -- reliever Jon Rauch came into the game and gave up four runs on a wild pitch and a three-run homer that proved to be the difference. For his career against the Padres, Davis is 8-3 with a 3.05 ERA in 14 games -- 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Say this for Gaudin, he was markedly better in his first start at PETCO Park on Wednesday than he was in his previous start May 14 against his former team, the Chicago Cubs. In that game, Gaudin walked seven in 4 1/3 innings in a 11-3 loss. Gaudin allowed one hit in that start but four earned runs. His command was an issue, as it was at times against the Giants on Wednesday when he walked four in six innings. But he limited the damage to one run on five hits with three strikes. Command is still an issue and something the Padres will want him to work on before his next start against the Diamondbacks.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer pitched well enough to win, but came away with a no-decision in his last start against the Marlins on Thursday in South Florida. The right-hander allowed just three runs on six hits over six innings and struck out 10, but left with his team down 3-1. The D-backs eventually rallied to win the game, 4-3. Wins have been hard to come by for Scherzer. He finally nabbed his first in the big leagues May 16 against the Braves in his 23rd appearance and 14th start. The biggest play of that game turned out to be a fake-to-third-throw-to-first pickoff play in the first inning that resulted in a inning-ending double play and the Braves were not able to recover as the D-backs rolled to a 12-0 win. Scherzer has had trouble pitching deep into games this year because of high pitch counts.
away_pitcher_note: Correia, a  former Giant, got a start against his old team on Thursday and allowed one run in 6 1/3 innings, needing just 81 pitches to get one out into the seventh inning. Correia has allowed six earned runs over his last three starts spanning 19 1/3 innings as he continues to show signs of improved mechanics -- something on which he has worked hard with pitching coach Darren Balsley. The key is a slower, more deliberate and controlled delivery. "It's still feeling good; I was really efficient with my pitches," Correia said. "Overall, I thought I made some pretty good pitches."

home_pitcher_note: Buckner had long waited to get a Major League start with the D-backs. A second-round pick by the Royals in 2004, he made 10 relief appearances for the D-backs in 2008 after being acquired during the offseason. Buckner made the team out of Spring Training as a reliever, but was shipped to Triple-A Reno after just three relief appearances. His performance last Friday in Oakland when he allowed just one run over 7 1/3 innings earned him another start. Buckner's best pitch is a 12-to-6 curveball, but he showed he could get batters out with his sinker and changeup as he did not have a good feel for the curve against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: A day after using his no-trade clause to shoot down a proposed deal that would have sent him to the Chicago White Sox, Peavy turned in another strong start against the Chicago Cubs, one of the teams he was nearly traded to this past offseason. Peavy had to work hard for outs early on, which drove up his pitch count, but he still allowed two hits over six scoreless innings, striking out 10 but walking four. "When you give up a couple of hits and strike out 10 in six innings, that's a pretty good outing," Padres manager Bud Black said. In Peavy's last two starts, he has allowed one run over 15 innings, including a complete-game victory over the Reds on May 17 in which he threw 92 strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Haren had one of his poorest outings his last time out, against his former team in Oakland. The right-hander allowed five runs on nine hits over seven innings. The five runs came courtesy of four Oakland homers, the most Haren had ever given up in a single game. Ironically, Haren said he had very good stuff in the game, but missed his spots, and when he did the A's made him pay. Haren's start before this one lasted just three innings, thanks to a rainout in South Florida. That could have contributed to Haren being somewhat rusty and not sharp against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Lowe continued to eat innings put the Braves in a position to win, going 7 1/3 innings and earning his sixth win of the season during Saturday's victory over the Blue Jays. The Braves' ace pitched his 2,000th career inning during that game, which saw him allow just two runs on five hits. Lowe has now allowed two runs in each of his past three starts. Pitching for the Dodgers, Lowe went 5-1 with a 2.05 ERA against the Diamondbacks last season.

home_pitcher_note: Garland did a good imitation of a tight-rope walker in his last start against the A's at Oakland-Alameda Coliseum. The right-hander allowed nine base runners in the first five innings of the outing, yet somehow managed to keep the A's off the board in that span. Garland tempted fate once too often and allowed three runs in the sixth as the A's beat the D-backs, 6-2. All three of the runs came on Landon Powell's first big league homer. Garland said after the game that he simply did not have his good command and the ball did not feel good in his hand. Signed as a free agent to replace Randy Johnson in the rotation, Garland has success when he's able to keep the ball down near the knees. When he gets it up near the belt he runs into trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Although it isn't obvious from his stat line, Jurrjens wasn't as sharp in his Sunday start against the Blue Jays as he has been in recent starts. Jurrjens went six innings and allowed just two earned runs, but surrendered eight hits and two walks on 102 pitches in a no-decision. He had gone at least seven innings in his previous three starts. On the season, Jurrjens has been among the league's best starters. He has allowed more than two runs in just one start and has won his last two decisions. Jurrjens last pitched against the Diamondbacks on August 9 of last year, going six innings and earning a win.

home_pitcher_note: Davis has found it hard to get a win lately despite pitching well. In his last outing, he seemed well on his way to a win against the Padres. Davis allowed just one run through seven innings and the D-backs had built a 7-1 lead. However, things fell apart for the D-backs in the eighth as the bullpen imploded and allowed five runs to pull the Padres to within 7-6. One inning later, Chad Qualls blew just his second save of the year and the D-backs wound up losing, 9-7, in 10 innings. Davis is in the final year of a three-year contract extension he signed after coming over in a trade prior to the 2007 season.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez has allowed five earned runs or more in three of his past six outings and allowed two earned runs or less in the other three starts that encompass this span. Making his recent inconsistencies more maddening is the fact that the majority of the struggles encountered during each of those three losses were experienced in the fifth or sixth innings. While working seven innings and getting a no-decision during his May 15 start against the Diamondbacks, the 32-year-old right-hander allowed two earned runs and registered 10 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer had to go 22 games and 13 starts before getting his first big league win, but the right-hander now has two in his last three starts. Last time out against the Padres, he was dominating through seven innings as Arizona built a 6-0 lead. Scherzer tired in the eighth and gave up a homer and single to lead off the frame before being removed. The bullpen struggled, allowing three more runs to score and pull the Padres to within 6-4. Despite a heart-stopping ninth, which he watched from the training room, Scherzer picked up the win as the D-backs held on, 6-5. The right-hander struck out 10 in the game and did not walk a batter. He picked up his first big league win May 16 against the Braves in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen's control has hurt him during his first two career starts. After throwing just 43 of 80 pitches for strikes during his Major League debut on May 21, the 23-year-old right-hander returned Tuesday and issued just two walks in 5 1/3 innings against the Giants.  The most costly walk was issued to Tim Lincecum with two outs in what would become a four-run second inning. Medlen's inability to retire Lincecum provided further proof that he's allowing his nerves to get the best of him during pressure situations.  He ended Tuesday's outing by retiring the final 11 batters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Welcome back, Hiroki Kuroda. He won Opening Day, strained an oblique muscle in a bullpen session two days later and hasn't pitched for the Dodgers since. He's coming off a pretty shaky rehab appearance at Class A, but manager Joe Torre can't wait to get him back into the rotation. The Dodgers are looking for an innings-eater, which he is when he's healthy, and that is all they are hoping for at this point.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner nibbled at the strike zone a little too much in his last start and paid the price with a 8-5 loss to the Padres. The right-hander gave up a two-run homer in the first to Adrian Gonzalez on a fastball that caught too much of the plate. On the night, Buckner allowed five runs on seven hits over five-plus innings. In his first start of the year against the A's on May 22, he allowed just one run over 7 1/3 innings. Buckner's best pitch is a 12-to-6 curveball, but he showed against the A's that he could get batters out with his sinker and changeup as he did not have a good feel for the curve in that game.

home_pitcher_note: His last time out, Wolf might have pitched his best game since returning to the Dodgers. He took a shutout into the eighth inning at Wrigley Field, chased by Bobby Scales' pinch-hit homer. To that point, he had struck out seven with one walk and allowed only one runner as far as second base. Wolf has throw six or more innings in his past five starts and entered his last start with seven no-decision in his previous eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren was outstanding against the Braves in his last outing. The right-hander helped an overworked bullpen by allowing just two runs over eight innings. Haren's control has been outstanding all season and his no-walk, eight-strikeout performance against the Braves was another example. In 71 innings this year, Haren has fanned 71 and walked just nine. Haren showed his ability to make adjustments and think along with hitters as he realized Chipper Jones was looking for an off-speed pitch in the third when he drove in a run with a double. So when Haren faced him with one on in the eighth, he threw him a fastball with two strikes and caught Jones looking.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Billingsley was a tough-luck loser at Wrigley Field, where he allowed only two runs over seven innings while taking his second successive defeat. Billingsley struck out seven without issuing a walk, although he had to dodge three jams with runners on third base. He finally lost a shutout in the seventh on a solo homer by Koyie Hill, and he lost the game on a sacrifice fly.
away_pitcher_note: Garland will put to the test his reputation of following up some of his worst starts with some of his best. He was knocked around for nine runs in 2 2/3 innings on Friday by the Braves, and merely getting out of Chase Field should help him. Garland's home ERA (8.71) is more than four times higher than his figure on the road (2.13). Interestingly, the 10-year veteran has never before pitched in Dodger Stadium, although he did defeat the Dodgers in his first start as a D-back, on April 10.

home_pitcher_note: It was a dramatic turnaround for Gaudin in his last start on May 31 against the Rockies. Coming off a start in which he allowed seven runs and five walks in a no-decision against the Diamondbacks, Gaudin struck out the side in the first inning against the Rockies and took a shutout into the seventh. He allowed one run on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings, striking out a season-high nine batters. His ball had a lot of movement on it and he spotted his fastball well. Better still, he didn't walk a single batter, marking the first time this season he has walked three or fewer batters in a start.
away_pitcher_note: Davis pitched well enough to win in his last start, but instead came away with a no-decision against the Braves at Chase Field. The left-hander allowed two runs on seven hits over seven innings. Both of the runs came in the third inning, and Davis was lights out after that. The D-backs managed to rally and tie the game before winning in 11 innings. Since 2004, Davis is second among National League pitchers with 173 starts, 103 of which have been quality ones. This is the final year of a three-year extension he signed after coming over the Arizona from Milwaukee prior to the 2007 season.

home_pitcher_note: Correia was victimized by the hard-hitting Phillies in his last start, allowing a season-high 10 hits and four runs (two home runs) in a loss at PETCO Park. Correia, who had allowed five home runs in his previous nine starts, allowed a solo shot to Chase Utley and another solo shot to Ryan Howard, a bomb that sailed well over the wall in center field. Correia mixed in some nice curveballs, striking out Howard twice, but the Phillies were able to get on top of his fastball more often than not. After a stretch of three good starts, Correia has now allowed 10 earned runs in his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer had the worst outing of his Major League career against the Braves last Sunday at Chase Field. The right-hander missed with his location, particularly against left-handed hitters, and Atlanta punished him for it. Scherzer gave up a career-high eight runs on 10 hits while lasting just 3 2/3 innings. Three batters into the game, the Braves led 2-0 and a two-run homer by Chipper Jones in the third added to the woes. Garret Anderson's three-run shot in the fourth capped Scherzer's day. Prior to that start, Scherzer had won two of his previous three starts after going 22 games and 13 starts before getting his first big league win.

home_pitcher_note: Geer got off to a rough start in his last outing on May 30 against the Rockies when he allowed three runs in the first inning -- right after the Padres had scored three runs of their own on an Adrian Gonzalez home run. But Geer settled down thereafter and he pitched into the seventh inning, when a lost fly ball in the twilight eventually led to two runs. Still, Geer was happy with the way he rebounded against the Rockies. "After those three runs, I really felt bad. But I started making my pitches and got into a groove." Geer's final line was five earned runs over 6 2/3 innings with one walk and three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren deserved a better fate in his last outing, leaving with a 5-1 lead after seven innings. The D-backs bullpen, though, imploded, allowing five runs in the eighth inning in what turned into a 6-5 loss. That was far from the first time that Haren has come away from a game without a deserved win. The D-backs scored a total of one run in his first three starts of the year. One thing you can count on from Haren is that he is going to throw strikes. In 78 innings this year he has fanned 78 and walked just 10 while holding opponents to a .201 average.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy will start on Monday after departing on Tuesday following one fitful inning with what was called an upper repository infection. Peavy allowed four runs on three hits and two walks in the first inning of a loss to the Phillies as his velocity was down from the mid-90s. Oddly enough, it wasn't Peavy's ankle tendinitis that felled him, an injury he had been working with the training staff to get right before the start. Padres manager Buddy Black said Peavy's ankle may still be a slight issue.
away_pitcher_note: Garland took the loss in his last outing, against the Dodgers, but he deserved a better fate. The right-hander allowed just one run over six innings in what turned out to be a 1-0 loss for Arizona. The lone run came in the sixth inning when James Loney tripled on a ball to left that Gerardo Parra dove for and could not catch. Casey Blake followed with a sacrifice fly. Garland made some mechanical adjustments after allowing nine runs (eight earned) in his last outing. More important, though, Garland said he made a mental adjustment. "Last game, I think I gave up on myself," Garland said. "It wasn't there and I didn't dig deep enough and go find it. I pretty much made up my mind from right after that game that it wouldn't happen to me again the rest of my career."

home_pitcher_note: Buckner was pushed back a few days due to Thursday's off day, and the D-backs desire to keep Dan Haren and Jon Garland as close to regular rest as possible. Buckner has been outstanding in two of his three starts since joining the rotation. His last time out, against the Dodgers, he held them to just four hits in six shutout innings at Dodger Stadium. That was similar to his first start, when he allowed just one run over 7 1/3 innings against the A's in Oakland. In both of those games, Buckner was aggressive in the strike zone and mixed his pitches well. In the middle start, when he allowed five runs in five innings against the Padres, Buckner nibbled at the zone a little too much. He does not possess a dominating fastball so he must hit his spots with it and use his out pitch -- a 12-to-6 curve -- effectively.
away_pitcher_note: Cain has mostly avoided the lousy luck -- poor run support or leaky relief pitching -- that plagued him in previous seasons. One exception occurred on April 26 of this season, when he pitched well enough to win at Arizona. He yielded one run -- a Mark Reynolds homer -- and four hits in seven innings, but the Giants ultimately lost, 5-4, in 12 innings. Cain is 3-3 with a 3.18 ERA in 11 career starts against Arizona. Much of his success has been due to his toughness with men on base. The right-hander has limited opponents to a .111 batting average with runners in scoring position, the best in the Majors through last weekend.

home_pitcher_note: Davis finally got back into the win column last Friday in San Diego. The left-hander tossed six shutout innings in an 8-0 Arizona win. It was his first victory since April 29 a span of six starts. Davis allowed three hits and walked four while striking out five. He pitched well enough to win in his start before that, but instead came away with a no decision against the Braves at Chase Field. The left-hander allowed two runs on seven hits over seven innings. Both of the runs came in the third inning and Davis was lights out after that. The D-backs managed to rally and tie the game before winning in 11 innings. This is the final year of a three-year extension he signed after coming over the Arizona from Milwaukee prior to the 2007 season.
away_pitcher_note: Zito ended a personal four-game losing streak in his most recent start despite showing less than his best. Last Friday at Florida, he threw just 59 strikes out of his 95 pitches and was removed after walking the first two batters in the sixth inning. Yet he allowed only one run in five innings and earned the win in San Francisco's 2-1 triumph. Zito has consistently downplayed his own record while prioritizing the team's fortunes, but as he said afterward, victories are "the last thing we control, but it's the first thing people mention."

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer did not pitch poorly in his last start, but he did not pitch great, either. The right-hander tossed five shutout innings against the Padres at PETCO Park, but ran up his pitch count in the process because once again he struggled to hit his spots. Scherzer walked five and allowed three hits in the five innings. In fairness, Scherzer did leave with a 2-0 lead and could have easily picked up the win. The Arizona bullpen, though, gave up a six-spot in the sixth and the D-backs wound up losing 6-4. In his outing prior to that, Scherzer had the worst game of his Major League career against the Braves. He missed with his location, particularly against left-handed hitters, and Atlanta punished him for it. Scherzer gave up a career-high eight runs on 10 hits while lasting just 3 2/3 innings. Three batters into the game, the Braves led 2-0 and a two-run homer by Chipper Jones in the third added to the woes. Garret Anderson's three-run shot in the fourth capped Scherzer's day.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez didn't exactly get off to a rousing start in his efforts to duplicate the excellence he sustained last June, which he completed with a 5-1 record and a 3.10 ERA in six games. In his last start, Sanchez lasted only 4 2/3 innings while allowing eight hits and all of the Marlins' runs in a 5-4 Giants defeat last Saturday. It wasn't a completely dismal performance by Sanchez, who threw 67 strikes in 101 pitches and struck out seven, matching a season high. Sanchez must continue that trend to build his durability, which has been lacking this season. He has pitched past the sixth inning just once, largely explaining why he has recorded just two quality starts out of 10.

home_pitcher_note: Haren's last start was emblematic of the way his season has gone -- he pitched outstanding, but came away with no decision. The right-hander allowed just one run on four hits over seven innings Sunday afternoon against the Padres and left with a seemingly safe 6-1 lead. The bullpen, though, gave up five runs in the ninth and the D-backs wound up winning 9-6 in 18 innings. In his previous start against the Dodgers, Haren left with a 5-1 lead after seven innings. This time the bullpen imploded in a five-run eighth inning as the D-backs went on to lose 6-5. The frustration started early this year for Haren when the D-backs scored a total of one run in his first three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton is coming off two strong outings against Pittsburgh to even his record. He held the Pirates to three hits and one run in seven innings on May 31 in Pittsburgh, and he allowed just one run on five hits on June 5 in Houston, moving past Jim Deshaies and into third place on the club's all-time left-handed strikeout list in the process. Hamtpon is 7-8 with 5.56 ERA in his career versus Arizona. He lost his only outing against the D-backs last season.

home_pitcher_note: He was not pinpoint with his command, but Garland managed to get through the first four innings against the Padres in his last start without allowing a run. He was eventually charged with six runs on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings for the loss, his fourth in a row. Garland has not won a game since giving up two runs in six innings against the Marlins on May 19, but still racks up innings. He's pitched at least six innings nine times in his 12 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt's next start was pushed back a few days because of a sore wrist. His up-and-down season suffered another road bump in his previous start, against Pittsburgh on Saturday, when he allowed nine hits and six earned runs in six innings. Oswalt went 0-2 with a 3.94 ERA in April, 1-0 with a 5.34 in May and won his first start in June before losing on Saturday. The right-hander won his only start against Arizona last season and is 7-1 with a 2.25 ERA in nine starts versus the D-backs in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Buckner will be the first to admit that he didn't have his best stuff and that he struggled with his execution his last time on the mound. Against the Giants, he was charged with eight runs and 13 hits in 5 2/3 innings for the loss. After an efficient start, he struggled in the middle innings and was doomed when the Giants had consecutive three-run innings in the fifth and sixth. His mettle was  tested after giving up a 433-foot home run to Pedro Sandoval. Buckner has never faced the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time this season, Moehler didn't make it past the third inning against Chicago. Moehler gave up five runs on eight hits and was taken out after the third against the Cubs in his last start. In his first start of the season, the 37-year old gave up seven runs on eight hits and was taken out after just 1 1/3 innings on April 8 versus Chicago. In his career, Moelher is 1-1 with a 5.82 ERA over four starts versus the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Meche pitched his third straight effective game last Wednesday night at Cleveland, shutting out the Indians for seven innings on four hits. He also notched 11 strikeouts to match his career high. Although he had no decision in two of his last three games, he's given up just three earned runs in a total of 20 innings in that stretch. By moving his push-off foot closer to the first-base side of the rubber, he's improved his offspeed pitches and his location has been much sharper. Last year Meche beat Arizona, 8-3, with 7 1/3 strong innings and 10 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Davis is looking to rebound from his shortest outing of the season, a four-inning start against the Giants on Wednesday, and get back on track. The veteran left-hander has one win in his last eight starts and went the entire month of May without a win. In his last outing, Davis was charged with five runs (two earned) on six hits in the 101-pitch outing against the Giants. Davis is 2-2 with a 5.01 ERA in his career against the Royals, a familiar foe that dates back to his American League days with Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke pitched seven strong innings in his last outing at Cleveland but had no decision as the bullpen lost a 3-1 lead and the Royals lost, 4-3, in 10 innings. That left Greinke with two no-decisions and a loss in his past three starts. Against the Indians, he rebounded splendidly after getting whacked around at Toronto and showed that he hadn't lost a thing despite that one-game glitch. When Greinke faces Arizona, it always brings back memories of his worst-ever outing in 2005. He gave up a franchise-record 11 runs but also cracked a home run, his first Major League hit, off the D-backs' Russ Ortiz.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer continues to make progress and took a big step in his development in his last outing against the Giants on Thursday, when he pitched a career-high 7 2/3 scoreless innings and a career-high 116 pitches. His ability to throw his slider and his changeup proved to be the difference in the 2-1 victory and the franchise is hopeful he will continue to grow as a pitcher. With an off-day scheduled in between starts, Scherzer is pitching on an extra day of rest. He has never faced the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar was masterful in his last start, throwing a complete game while allowing just one run against the Reds. Hochevar needed just 80 pitches to throw the first complete game of his professional career. He also lowered his ERA from 7.85 to 5.60. He struck out just three, but kept the ball down and kept Cincinnati off balance all night. It all added up to a great night for Hochevar, who started the season in Triple-A Omaha. The former No. 1 Draft choice made his 2009 debut on June 12 against Oakland and preceded to give up eight runs in two innings. But after a rocky beginning, Hochevar has come on strong. He's 2-0 in his last two starts, allowing just three runs in 15 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: It's hard to pitch much better than Haren did in his last start. The right-handed pitcher threw a two-hit complete game in the 8-1 win against the Astros. Haren was in complete command of his pitches and only walked two hitters. He struck out seven. His only blemish was a solo home run by Carlos Lee. The victory marked Haren's second complete game of the season and the eighth of his career. It was his first  two-hit complete game.

home_pitcher_note: A streak of three quality starts ended for Washburn at Coors Field, where his own wildness and some bad luck parlayed into an Interleague Play loss. Three of the batters Washburn walked and one that he hit scored runs in the setback. An errant throw to first base that would have ended an inning produced one of the five runs he surrendered in a six-inning stint.
away_pitcher_note: Garland was charged with three runs on six hits in seven innings in the D-backs' 6-4 loss to the Astros on Saturday. The right-hander threw 98 pitches and gave up a two-run home run to Lance Berkman on the way to his fifth consecutive defeat. He remains resilient. Garland's attitude combined with improved effectiveness on the mound could bode well for the D-backs the remainder of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander was going to get two extra days between starts, but a shoulder ailment to Erik Bedard scrapped those plans and Vargas will make his eighth start of the season. He has struggled a bit in his last two outings, which prompted the idea of giving him some extra rest. Vargas has a terrific changeup, but didn't use the pitch often enough in his start against the Rockies and was rocked during a five-run fifth inning. It didn't help that he was working with a rookie catcher.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner is looking for his second victory of the month and hoping to rebound from two consecutive subpar starts. In his last start, Astros shortstop Miguel Tejada hit an RBI double off Buckner for the visitors' first run of the game in the first inning, and Lance Berkman followed with a two-run home run to extend the Astros' lead to 3-0. Buckner was eventually charged with six runs on five hits in five innings for the loss. In his previous start against the Giants, he was charged with eight runs and 13 hits in 5 2/3 innings for the loss. He has been plagued with poor execution of his pitches but is confident he can bounce back in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander continues to perform like a potential All-Star selection, tossing a two-hit shutout over the Padres in his last outing. He has now surrendered three earned runs in his past 37 2/3 innings, a 0.72 ERA. When he has all four of his pitches -- two-seam and four-seam fastball, slider and curve -- working the way they have in his last five starts, he's a tough pitcher to face.
away_pitcher_note: Davis has one win in his past nine starts, but has pitched better than his record would indicate. Last time out, against the Royals, he allowed four runs (three earned) over 5 2/3 innings in what would turn out to be a 5-0 loss. His last win was on June 5 in San Diego, where he worked six shutout innings. The time before that he allowed just two runs in seven innings but came away with no decision. Davis can be frustrating to watch at times. He is a slow worker who puts plenty of baserunners on, but also seems to be able to work his way out of jams. Davis could be trade bait in July as he is in the final year of a three-year, $22 million extension.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer is riding a two-start winning streak. In his last outing against the Royals at Kauffman Stadium, he allowed two runs over six innings in a 12-5 win. It wasn't always pretty as the right-hander allowed 12 baserunners, but he managed to work out of numerous jams as the Royals stranded six in the first three innings against him. In his start prior to that, Scherzer lasted a career-high 7 2/3 innings and threw a career-best 116 pitches as he beat the Giants 2-1 at Chase Field. Scherzer has allowed two runs in 18 2/3 innings over his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison was activated from the disabled list after two rehabilitation outings and allowed three earned runs over five innings Wednesday in his first start since May 25. He is 4-2 with a 4.20 ERA over his last seven starts to lower his season ERA from 9.20 to 5.43. Harrison is 2-2 with a 5.28 ERA in five starts on the road this season. He has never faced the Arizona Diamondbacks.

home_pitcher_note: Haren had his usual outstanding stuff in his last outing against the Royals in Kansas City. The right-hander went seven innings and allowed just two runs. He did not walk a batter and fanned six. Haren still had plenty left in the tank after seven, but considering his high workload in his previous few starts, the D-backs decided to give him a relative break at 98 pitches. Haren has been the team's most consistent pitcher and should have a better record to show for it. The D-backs bullpen has blown several large leads for him, and in his first three starts of the year the D-backs provided a total of one run of support.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla threw six innings and allowed three earned runs on Thursday against the Astros. His start was a tale of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde -- he threw 64 of his 107 pitches in the first and sixth innings. It was his sixth quality start of the season. Padilla has a 3.38 ERA over his past eight outings, which has lowered his season ERA from 8.27 to 4.79. He has finished six innings in seven of his past nine starts after averaging 4 2/3 innings in his first three outings. In five road starts, Padilla is 2-1 with a 3.90 ERA over 32 1/3 innings pitched. In eight games (six starts) against the Diamondbacks, he is 3-3 with a 4.84 ERA over 35 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The good news for Garland is that he pitched better in his last outing. The bad news is that this start comes at Chase Field, where he has certainly not had a home-field advantage. This year on the road Garland has a 2.60 ERA in seven starts. At home, his ERA is 7.82. His last start was against the Mariners at Safeco Field and he tossed seven shutout innings. He pitched in and out of trouble as he allowed eight baserunners on the night. Garland did not get a decision as the bullpen gave up the 3-0 lead he left them. Seattle rallied for four runs in the eighth, including two on a pinch-hit homer by Ken Griffey Jr.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman lost, 6-4, to the Giants on Friday while giving up five runs in six innings, snapping his four-game road winning streak. He is now 0-2 with a 4.76 ERA in his past three starts. He has a 3.18 ERA in 11 starts this season and in 35 starts over the past two years, he is 11-10 with a 4.56 ERA. Opponents are hitting .230 off him this year but they are hitting .300 with runners in scoring position and .360 in those situations with two outs. He has made just one relief appearance in his career against the Diamondbacks.

home_pitcher_note: Buckner was a tough-luck loser in his last outing, against the Mariners at Safeco Field. He allowed two runs through six innings and almost escaped a rally in the seventh, but Ichiro Suzuki's chopper up the middle tipped off his glove and bounced into right field. So instead hitting into a rally-killing double play, Suzuki reached and the M's went on to score a pair of runs. It was a much better performance for Buckner, who allowed 14 runs in his previous two starts over a span of 10 2/3 innings. When Buckner is effective he is getting outs early in counts and locating his curve ball. When hitters work him deeper in counts he has a tendency to struggle to find an out pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Facing his older brother, Jeff, for the first time, Weaver had his worst outing of the season, giving up more than four runs for the first time in 14 starts. Lasting 5 1/3 innings, Weaver yielded six earned runs on 10 hits and three walks, striking out four hitters. He had given up six earned runs at home in his previous 53 2/3 innings this season. Weaver retired the first seven men he faced but wasn't the same after Russell Martin homered with one out in the third, suddenly losing his command. Weaver is facing Arizona for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Davis was in position for a much-deserved win in his last start against the Mariners but came up short. The left-hander allowed just one run over seven innings of work but two costly errors in the late innings proved costly. First baseman Tony Clark dropped the ball on a throw from Mark Reynolds in the ninth inning that led to the game-winning run. Davis is seeking his first win since pitching six innings against the Padres on June 5.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey followed a winning, seven-inning effort in San Francisco with eight innings in a home loss to the Dodgers, a team he had dominated in the past with a 5-1 record and 1.50 ERA in 54 innings. He yielded four earned runs, two on a James Loney homer, while getting nicked for nine hits and walking four. He struck out five hitters. Lackey has never faced the D-backs. He's 2-1 with a 6.10 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer pitched a career-high 119 pitches in six innings against the Rangers in his last start, cruising to his third victory in a row. Using a steady dose of fastballs and offspeed pitches, Scherzer was able to keep the Texas hitters off balance. He racked up seven strikeouts in the 8-2 victory and appears to be honing his craft and building arm strength. He is brimming with confidence and continues to develop as a Major League pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: In his 11th start in an Angels uniform, Palmer finally tasted defeat, at the hands of the scorching Rockies on Monday night at home. Palmer lasted 4 2/3 innings, surrendering six earned runs on seven hits and five walks. He struck out five. His previous high in runs allowed was five, and the 4 2/3 innings matched his briefest outing in a starting role. Palmer has never faced Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo's latest start in Toronto on Wednesday didn't go much better than his previous one. He allowed seven runs over 3 2/3 innings including five runs in the first inning before he got his first out. He allowed eight hits and three walks over his outing, an 8-2 loss to the Blue Jays. Arroyo will look to get back on track against the Diamondbacks. He is 1-2 with a 5.97 ERA in seven starts against Arizona for his career.
away_pitcher_note: Haren continues to dominate National League hitters despite a win-loss record that might indicate otherwise. In his last start, he threw seven solid innings against the Rangers in a 2-1 in a season-high 116-pitch effort. He struck out eight batters and continues to be among the NL leaders in ERA, strikeouts, innings pitched and batting average against. He threw 95 pitches in the first five frames against the Rangers yet still managed to pitch seven innings in the defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was roughed up for his second straight start in Toronto on Thursday. The right-hander pitched six innings, allowing five earned runs and five hits, while striking out four and walking three in a 7-5 win over the Blue Jays. Cueto will try to return to form against the Diamondbacks. He is 1-0 with a 1.50 ERA in two starts against Arizona in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Garland has not won since May 19, a span of seven starts. In fairness, there were a few games during that stretch when he pitched well enough to win. His last outing against the Rangers was not one of them. The right-hander allowed six runs (four earned) on eight hits over 6 1/3 innings in what turned out to be a 9-8, 12-inning loss. His start prior to that, however, was a dandy. He tossed seven shutout innings in that one only to walk away with a no-decision. There has been a significant home/road split for him this year. In eight games at Chase Field, he is 2-4 with a 7.51 ERA while in seven road starts he is 2-3 with a 2.60 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Harang is usually one of the Reds' most reliable starters. But he was shelled in a 9-2 loss to Cleveland on Friday. He allowed five earned runs on 10 hits while walking one and striking out three batters in just 4 2/3 innings. Harang will look to get back on track Thursday against the Diamondbacks. He is 2-4 with a 1.66 ERA in eight starts against Arizona in his career.
away_pitcher_note: With Monday's off-day, the D-backs had the luxury of skipping the fifth starter's spot, and that's a good thing since they optioned their fifth starter -- Billy Buckner -- to Triple-A Reno after his last start. Davis has pitched better than his record indicates. His last two times out are prime examples of that. Davis allowed just one run over seven innings, but walked away with a no-decision, on June 21 against the Mariners. In his last start, Davis gave up one unearned run over seven innings but once again took a no-decision as the D-backs lost, 2-1. Davis' name has come up in trade rumors because he is in the final year of his contract.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched six mostly smooth innings in his last start, a win at Oakland. Fans and professional observers alike sometimes hold their breaths whenever De La Rosa gets into a tough situation, mainly because there have been stretches when he would get tripped up by one bad inning. But he is 4-1 in his last five starts, mainly because he's been able to work through early problems.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer had won three straight before his last start, when he gave up four hits, walked three and gave up eight runs -- just three earned -- in 4 1/3 innings of a 12-8 loss to the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Cook is making a case for his second successive All-Star Game appearance. He is 5-0 with a 1.75 ERA in his past five starts, and his five wins in June led the National League. In going eight-plus innings and holding the Athletics to one run during a 3-1 victory on Sunday, Cook used his four-seam fastball against the left-handers in the lineup and had more fly-ball outs (10) than ground-ball outs (nine).This is the first time Cook will face the D-backs since Opening Day, when he gave up six runs and seven hits in a 2 1/3-inning pratfall at Chase Field.
away_pitcher_note: Petit, who has been on the 15-day disabled list since May 9 with a strained right shoulder, recently completed a rehab assignment with Triple-A Reno. In his last outing with the Aces, he pitched three innings and allowed three runs (two earned) and five hits. He was 0-1 with a 6.89 ERA in five starts for Reno. He takes the spot of Billy Buckner, who was sent down on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez had yet another solid outing in the Rockies' 4-2, 13-inning loss to the Dodgers on Monday night. He yielded one hit in the first four innings and went seven innings total, with two runs on five hits and four strikeouts. A few small executions issues tripped him, such as a poor pitchout and a balk that moved runners before he gave up a two-run single. Facing the D-backs should bring good memories. Jimenez threw seven scoreless innings against Arizona in his first start of the season, a 3-0 Rockies victory on April 7.
away_pitcher_note: Haren dominated the Reds is his last start on Tuesday. He pitched seven innings and only allowed one run on four hits while striking out nine. Haren also helped his own cause at the plate. He hit the first homer of his career and also doubled in the D-backs' 6-2 victory. He lowered his National League-leading ERA to 2.19 in the victory. Against the Rockies this season, Haren is 1-1 with a 0.64 ERA in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garland's winless streak continued on Wednesday against the Reds despite another impressive performance. He pitched six innings and allowed one run on six hits in his sixth consecutive loss. Garland hasn't won a game since May 19, a span of eight decisions. Over that stretch he is 0-6 with a 4.81 ERA. Garland will look to end the slide against the Padres, against whom he is 1-1 with a 3.95 ERA in two starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Silva lasted four innings in his last start for the Padres. He exited after surrendering six runs, three earned, in a disastrous fourth inning that led to a 6-1 loss to the Astros at PETCO Park. Silva, who allowed all of his five hits in the fourth inning, walked one and struck out two. Padres manager Bud Black reiterated that Silva couldn't face the blame for a throwing error that led to three of the runs. "He could have wiggled out of there, but the one error came back to bite us," Black said. "His fate could have been different."

home_pitcher_note: The bullpen cost Davis his fourth win on Thursday, blowing a 2-1 lead in the ninth inning against the Reds. Davis was impressive again but didn't factor in the decision for the third consecutive start. He allowed just three runs in 21 innings over those three starts. Coincidentally, Davis' last win was against the Padres on June 5. He pitched six innings and allowed three hits in an 8-0 win in San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: In a 7-2 loss to the Astros at PETCO Park, Correia broke his previous streak of five consecutive quality starts. He allowed six runs on eight hits in five innings of work. Most disappointing to Correia was the three-run homer he surrendered in the fifth inning, which put the Padres down 6-0. As the effective staff ace now that Chris Young and Jake Peavy are on the 15-day disabled list, Correia has carried heightened responsibility on his shoulders. "I didn't have the command. I didn't have the same stuff that I was throwing the last few starts," Correia said. "That's going to happen, but I was battling through. I just kind of gave it up that last inning. That's the only inning that bothers me."

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has been the recipient of some horrible defense in his past two starts. Last time out, against the Rockies, he allowed five runs, but only three of them were earned thanks to three errors, including a dropped fly ball in center by Chris Young. That was nothing, though, compared to his previous start, against the Angels at Chase Field. In that one, Scherzer allowed eight runs, but only three were earned. The D-backs committed four errors in the game and were booed by the home crowd. Despite the poor play behind him, Scherzer has pitched fairly well. At times, though, his pitch count can run up in a hurry and prevent him from pitching deep into games.
away_pitcher_note: After three consecutive quality starts, Gaudin took a step backward in his last start against the Dodgers on July 3, allowing five runs in the first inning in an eventual loss to Los Angeles. The command issues that bothered Gaudin earlier in the season came back as he walked two in the first inning and four over five innings. All told, Gaudin allowed six runs, the most he's allowed since June 12 against Anaheim. Gaudin allowed one hit over eight scoreless innings in his previous start against Texas, but could never find get into a groove against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Petit needs to pitch well in order to keep his spot in the rotation. The right-hander was on the DL from May 9 until July 3 with right shoulder problems. He did not pitch well during his injury rehabilitation assignment, but the team had few options for the spot at that time and needed to activate him. This is the spot in the rotation that was Brandon Webb's, but the D-backs' ace has not pitched since Opening Day. Arizona has tried several candidates in this spot, including Billy Buckner and Bryan Augenstein, but they're still looking for someone to stake a claim.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Miller earned a win for the first time since June 6. The left-hander held the Pirates to three runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings while striking out four and walking one. However, the Bucs were able to hit the long ball against the 24-year-old. Miller allowed two home runs for the first time all season and had only allowed three on the year prior to the game against Pittsburgh. The four-year veteran is looking to win back-to-back games for the first time the season when he faces the D-backs in his next start. Miller took a loss the last time he faced Arizona despite allowing just two runs over seven innings on May 21.

home_pitcher_note: Haren was named to the National League All-Star team on Sunday by Phillies manager Charlie Manuel. The right-hander has been consistently outstanding all season. Of his 17 starts, 16 have been quality -- six innings or more with three or fewer runs allowed. Last time out, against the Rockies, Haren allowed three runs (only one earned) over seven innings. He has not allowed more than two earned runs in a start since May 23 in Oakland, a span of eight starts. Overall, Haren has allowed more than two earned runs just three times this year.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco won his fourth straight start his last time out, throwing eight shutout innings against the Pirates. It was the second straight eight-inning performance for Nolasco, as he continues to pitch well since returning to the big leagues. Over his past four starts, the right-hander has posted a 0.96 ERA and struck out 32 batters over 28 innings. In his last start, Nolasco struck out 12, good enough for second most in a game for his career.

home_pitcher_note: Garland was saddled with another no-decision in his last outing against the Padres. The right-hander allowed three runs in six innings and left with the game tied. He has not won since May 19, a span of nine starts. His number do not look great, but they are skewed by a few really poor outings. In four starts he has allowed six or more runs, which pushes his ERA up. Only three times this year has he failed to go at least six innings in a game. The May 19 win was against the Marlins in Florida as he held the Fish to one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: West's development as a big league starting pitcher continued Monday night against the San Francisco Giants, and he went through some growing pains. The 23-year-old walked three and yielded five runs in six innings. He is winless in his last two starts (in which he's allowed 10 earned runs in 10 1/3 innings). This will be his first start against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis finally got a much-deserved win in his last start. That was his first win since June 5. That win as well as the one in his last start came against the Padres. In the most recent one he allowed just two runs over 6 1/3 innings. Davis has deserved more wins, but has struggled from a lack of run support and some poor outings by the bullpen. In his previous three starts before getting the win against the Padres he had allowed two earned runs in 21 innings yet came away with nothing to show for it. He can be frustrating to watch at times as he walks more than his fair share of batters and there always seem to be runners on base. However, the veteran finds a way to pitch himself out of trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson regained his control on the mound Tuesday against the San Francisco Giants but still lost. One start removed from his wild 3 1/3 inning effort against the Washington Nationals, he allowed three runs on five hits in seven innings but received zero runs of support. The right-hander is winless in his last three outings and lost in his May 19 start against the Arizona Diamondbacks, yielding three runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter finished the first half strong, but after his busiest half-season since 2006, he can probably use the extra couple of days that the All-Star break will afford him. He'll be pitching on six days' rest after finishing off the first half with a Friday start at Wrigley Field. Carpenter hasn't pitched much at home this year, making only four starts, but he's been good at Busch Stadium. He's only allowed one homer in 26 innings in St. Louis in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Garland is ready to start a new type of streak.  In his last start, Garland pitched eight sharp innings to end a nine-start winless streak with his first victory since May 19. He allowed seven hits and a run, with one walk and five strikeouts. Starting with two outs in the third, he faced the minimum 16 batters. He has pitched at least six innings in 15 of his 18 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Cards' Opening Day starter worked very hard as the first half wound to a close, but he's also been on a roll. Over his last four starts before the break, Wainwright went 3-1 with a 1.39 ERA, averaging more than eight innings per start. Over his last 12 starts, Wainwright has averaged 7.4 innings per game, and he's racked up 82 strikeouts against 27 walks. He hasn't allowed a homer since June 21.
away_pitcher_note: Haren allowed one hit in a scoreless inning in Tuesday's All-Star Game, throwing 12 pitches. In his last start before the berak, he pitched his first shutout and third compete game of the year in an 8-0 victory against the Marlins. Haren has been effective all season. Of his 18 starts, he has pitched at least six innings or more and allowed three or fewer runs in 17 of them. Haren has not allowed more than two earned runs in a start since May 23 in Oakland and, overall, he has allowed more than two earned runs just three times this year.

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro had about the quietest excellent first half of anyone in baseball. Because he was unjustly saddled with nine losses, the quality of Pineiro's pitching was obscured. He has been very, very good this year. And he's been even better at home. In seven starts at Busch Stadium, Pineiro has averaged just over seven innings per start, he sports a 2.55 ERA and he's allowed exactly one home run. Overall, Pineiro has allowed one walk in his last five starts and one homer in his last 12.
away_pitcher_note: Petit is hoping the second half of the season starts a lot better than the way the first half ended for him. In the rotation because of the injury to Brandon Webb, the right-hander appeared on his way to his first victory of the season in his last start before the Marlins rallied for 10 runs in one inning to cruise to a 14-7 win at Chase Field. Petit had taken a shutout into the sixth before allowing a two-run home run to Jorge Cantu on an 0-2 pitch and a solo shot by Jeremy Hermida that ended his night.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched one shaky inning of relief for the Rockies on July 12 in their comeback win over the Braves. He allowed two runs on two hits. In his last start, De La Rosa tossed 6 1/3 innings July 8 in Colorado's 10-4 victory over Washington. He allowed three runs on five hits, walking three and striking out five. De La Rosa has won six of his last seven starts after a rocky 0-6 record with four no-decisions to start the season.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins made Davis work his last time out, forcing the left-handeder to throw 99 pitches in a four-inning outing. Davis struck out seven but issued three walks and gave up five runs in the loss. The outing was Davis' shortest since pitching four innings against the Giants on June 10.

home_pitcher_note: Cook struck out eight to match a career high in his last start, when he tossed six innings en route to a dominating 10-1 Rockies win over the Padres. He allowed one run on eight hits and walked four. Cook described the game as "really weird" considering that he allowed more baserunners than usual for a quality start. "I pitched with a lot of guys on base, gave up a lot of hits, but the defense came up huge behind me, and I was able to get some strikeouts when I needed to," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer, who is still seeking his first win since a victory against Texas on June 23, shined against the Padres, limiting the San Diego offense to two runs over seven innings while racking up nine strikeouts. The right-hander continues to show improvement on the mound and could develop into a staple of the D-backs' rotation in the future. He's pitched at least six innings in five of his last six outings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Jimenez struck out a season-high 10 batters in the Rockies' victory over the Padres. He tossed seven innings, allowing three runs on three hits. With the Rockies holding a 5-1 lead, he gave up two runs in the fifth inning that breathed some life into the struggling Padres' bats. "[Jimenez] is inches away from being a very special player, but we're not there yet." Rockies manager Jim Tracy said. "[He needs to] get to the point where the mindset is such that when you build a 5-1 lead, there's very little doubt as to where the game is headed. That's what we're working on."
away_pitcher_note: Garland pitched well enough to win in his last outing, but came away with a loss as the D-backs fell, 6-1, to the Cardinals at Busch Stadium. Garland allowed just two runs over six innings. Both of the runs came on homers by Albert Pujols. The first homer to Pujols came on the first pitch of the fourth inning while the second came on a 3-0 pitch when he was leading off the sixth. In his start just prior to the All-Star Break, Garland picked up his first win since May 19, a span of nine starts. He has pitched better than his numbers would indicate. A few outings in which he was really hammered has skewed his ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Haren logged another outstanding outing his last time out against the Cardinals as he allowed just one run over eight innings. The right-hander has now recorded quality starts in 17 of his 18 outings this year and leads the Majors in ERA. Haren was selected to his third straight All-Star Game and tossed a scoreless inning of relief in the Midsummer Classic. Though many thought he should have gotten the start in the game, it went to the Giants' Tim Lincecum instead. He has allowed a total of three earned runs in his last four starts and just one run in his last two (17 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Morton won his first home game as a Pirate as he tied a career-high by throwing seven shutout innings. He got stronger as the game wore on as he gave up just three hits. Morton has one career start against Arizona, throwing seven shutout innings in a win on Aug. 7 last season. This will be Morton's fifth road start of the season, compared to just two at home. The righty is 1-1 with a 3.94 away from PNC Park this year.

home_pitcher_note: Petit had probably his best outing of the year in his last start against the Cardinals at Busch Stadium. The right-hander allowed just two runs on three hits over six innings. Walks wound up costing Petit. He walked four in the game, but the crucial two came back-to-back with two outs in the fifth to load the bases for St. Louis pitcher Joel Pineiro. Pineiro hit a slider into left for a two-run double that proved to be the difference in the 2-1 Cardinals win. Petit is filling in Brandon Webb's spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Duke lost at home for just the second time in his last seven decisions at PNC Park. And it was all the result of one inning-long hiccup. Duke kept the Giants off the scoreboard in six of the seven frames he pitched, but San Fransisco's four-run sixth was enough to do the lefty in. His pitches started elevating, and Duke allowed four consecutive doubles. Though he continues to pitch well, Duke has now lost four straight starts and hasn't won on the road since April 25. Duke is 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA in four career starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Even though Davis has struggled in his last two starts -- 13 earned run given up in six innings -- manager A.J. Hinch believes he will bounce back. After all, in four previous outings before his mini-slump, Davis had a 1.32 ERA in 27 1/3 innings. Despite his record, Davis has pitched well this season and for him to continue to be effective he must be able to jam right-handed hitters with his two-seam fastball instead of throwing them in the dirt -- which is what happened in his last start. He's 6-6 with a 5.22 ERA against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has not been able to finish six innings in any of his last six starts, though he's not pitched too poorly in his most recent two. Still in his first full season as a Major League starter, Ohlendorf continues to work toward increasing his stamina late in games. His changeup continues to develop as well, though it's still not reliable 100 percent of the time. The Pirates still believe there is a little more velocity in his arm, though it's questionable whether or not anyone will see that the rest of this season.

home_pitcher_note: With the All-Star break looming, manager A.J. Hinch saw the perfect opportunity to avoid overusing Max Scherzer by pushing the youngster to the back of the rotation after the break. He wanted to get Scherzer into the 180-innings range by the end of the season. After a 13-day layoff, Scherzer's first start after the break was not a happy one. It was an uneven performance that he labored through. He threw 61 of 95 pitches in the first two innings and yielded four runs on seven hits -- albeit with six strikeouts -- in four innings. He received a no-decision as the Diamondbacks rallied for a 6-5 win. Scherzer said he needs to throw first pitch strikes if he's going to bounce back from this performance.
away_pitcher_note: Vasquez rebounded from a tumultuous outing against the Phillies and pitched a career-long 6 2/3 innings in his first start back after the break. After nitpicking with his pitches too much to be successful earlier this month, Vasquez got back to pounding the zone and went to a three-ball count just once. Of the 29 hitters he faced, he threw two or fewer pitches to 13 of them. Vasquez allowed only two runs, both coming on two-out RBI singles.  This will be Vasquez's first career start against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: The month of July has been a cruel one for Garland. On the one hand, he's thrown five consecutive quality starts in July in which his ERA is 2.73. However, he only has one win -- and two losses -- to show for it. In his last outing, Garland pitched effectively in hitter-friendly Coors Field as he yielded three runs on five hits with five strikeouts in seven innings. But alas, he received a no-decision. In two career starts against the defending champion Phillies, Garland is 0-1 with a 9.90 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Jamie Moyer has had an up and down past couple weeks. He allowed eight hits and five runs in five innings Wednesday against the Cubs at Citizens Bank Park. He threw seven shutout innings against the Marlins on July 16. He preceded that with six runs in five innings against the Reds on July 9 and one run in 6 1/3 innings against the Mets on July 4. Moyer approaches the end of July with a 5.65 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Dan Haren is not a pitching machine after all. In his last start, the right-handed pitcher was charged with four run on eight hits in five innings against the Pirates. He threw 98 pitches in his shortest outing of the season and later admitted he struggled with his command. The outing marked only the second time this season that Haren had allowed more than three runs in a game. On May 23, he was charged with five runs in seven innings against Oakland but rebounded shortly after, allowing three runs or fewer in the 10 starts that followed. He gave up a total of eight earned runs in June and has allowed six earned runs in four starts so far this month.
away_pitcher_note: Cole Hamels is 6-5 with a 4.66 ERA after he allowed four hits and three runs in seven innings Thursday night in a 9-4 victory over the Padres at Citizens Bank Park. His record and ERA are not bad, but they are not anywhere near where he expects himself to be. Hamels is a World Series MVP. He is an ace. He is somebody who is expected to roll out of bed and pitch seven innings with minimal effort. "Saving the best for last, come on," Hamels joked. "I'm a second-half pitcher. Check the stats."
