The statistics show Hamels entered Thursday's game 26-19 with a 3.99 ERA before the All-Star break and 17-9 with a 3.05 ERA after the break.

home_pitcher_note: Petit has shown flashes of effectiveness. He's also been inconsistent.  His last time on the mound, the right-hander was charged with six runs on nine hits in 4 1/3 innings for the loss against the Pirates, his fifth loss of the season.  He pitched six solid innings in his previous outing against the Cardinals but struggled with his command in the start that followed.  Two-out walk in the fourth inning against the Pirates led to one run and Pittsburgh tacked on four in the fifth to cruise to victory.
away_pitcher_note: Happ, who has been the source of trade rumors in recent weeks, is 7-1 with a 2.97 ERA this season. He suffered just the second loss of his career Friday against the Cardinals at Citizens Bank Park. It was his first loss in 32 appearances - his last coming June 30, 2007. Happ's eight-game win streak tied the Phillies' all-time rookie record with Bob Miller (1950) and Al Orth (1895). "I never thought I wasn't (human)," Happ said. "It was a good run. I'm looking forward to next time, trying to keep us in the game." Happ allowed 10 hits and five runs in six innings against the Cardinals, but many of those runs came off bloop hits. "Sometimes it's better to be lucky than good," Cardinals manager Tony La Russa said. "Happ deserves better than the runs that were scored."

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez allowed a walk and four consecutive hits, leading to three runs in the first inning Sunday in Houston. He escaped the inning because one runner was caught stealing and another was thown out at the plate. Then he pitched six scoreless innings, allowing four more base runners. All that led to his second straight victory and renewed faith in his renaissance season. Now he faces one of his former teams, a team he has faced once since the beginning of the 2006 season. Hernandez beat the Diamondbacks in the Metrodome as a member of the Twins June 22 last year, allowing one earned run - three over all - and nine hits in seven innings. He has a 10-6 record in 18 career starts against them, but most of the personnel he faced is gone now. Chad Tracy - four hits, including two home runs in 16 career at-bats - is the onlt D-Backs player with more than eight career at-bats against Hernandez.
away_pitcher_note: Davis recovered nicely from two previous ugly outings in his last start, when he blanked the Pirates through six innings of a 7-0 victory -- only his third win in 16 starts since April. He still battled his control, going to full counts on nine batters, but managed to pitch out of trouble against the overanxious Pirates -- something that could also work to his advantage against the offensively struggling Mets. The lefty has always had decent stuff and numbers, yet the D-backs have lost 29 of his past 44 starts since the end of May 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Perez, who awkwardly acknowledges, "walks are part of the game," surrendered another four in his most recent start, one that lasted merely five innings. And he allowed two home runs as well in what became a no-decision against the Rockies at Citi Field. He has yet to reach the seventh inning in the four starts he has made since returning to the rotation July 8. He has this dubious distinction; through Sunday, all other pitchers in the big leagues had produced three starts in which their walks equaled or exceeded their innings pitched. Now, including the Monday game against Rockies, Perez has produced five such performances in nine starts. He faces the Diamondbacks in his next start, against whom he has a 1-5 record and 5.01 ERA in eight career starts. But he didn't face them last season and has an 0-1 record and 2.08 ERA in his two most recent starts, one in 2006 and the other in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer was lights out against the Pirates in his last outing. He held the Bucs to five hits in seven scoreless innings with eight strikeouts and no walks. Scherzer has been the victim of poor defense behind him at times this year and it has cost him some wins. The D-backs have won his last three starts, though he only has one win during that period. Over his last nine starts, the D-backs are 6-3 and he has a 2.72 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: With a nastier fastball and the natural sink that led to double plays in two tight situations, Pelfrey pitched quite effectively against the Rockies in the Mets' 4-0 victory at Citi Field Tuesday. He allowed seven hits and three walks, hit a batter and struck out five in 6 1/3 innings. The victory was his first in three starts and his fourth in 15. Now he opposes the Diamondbacks, against whom he has produced a 4.42  ERA and 0-2 record in three career starts (18 1/3 innings). Pelfrey has a 4-2 record and 3.90 ERA in 11 starts at Citi Field this season. The D-Backs roster is not particularly familiar with him (52 composite at-bats).
away_pitcher_note: Garland has put together six consecutive quality starts (six or more innings, three or fewer runs) and has pitched better than his numbers would indicate. When Garland has been bad, he has been really bad, which has ballooned his ERA. Four times he has allowed six or more earned runs in a start. Garland has been critical of the defense behind him in his past two starts. Last time out, he allowed six runs but only three were earned. He got a no-decision in his start before that despite allowing just three runs over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wednesday's rainout and the subsequent doubleheader put the Mets in need of a spot starter for Monday's series finale against the D-backs. Rather than use Tim Redding, who has been pitching in relief and is not fully stretched out, the team decided to promote Nelson Figueroa, who has been pitching brilliantly for Triple-A Buffalo. Figueroa's last Major League assignment came in April, and his last outing against the D-backs came in April 2002, against a team that included Luis Gonzalez, Steve Finley and Mark Grace.
away_pitcher_note: Haren said that facing the Phillies' lineup (the opponent in his most recent start) was like pitching in the All-Star Game. The Phillies made him work hard, fouling off pitches and running the right-hander's pitch count up early. Haren left after five innings having already thrown 117 pitches. It was the second straight start in which he has lasted just five innings, the only two times that has happened to him this season.

home_pitcher_note: Duke allowed just six hits over seven shutout innings against the San Francisco Giants Wednesday afternoon but still came away with a no-decision. A lack of offensive support has been a continued theme for the lefty: He's received nine total runs in his nine losses this season. Duke finished July with a 3.67 ERA but exited the month with a 1-3 record in five starts. He won in his last outing against the Arizona Diamondbacks, yielding three runs over 6 1/3 innings on July 24.
away_pitcher_note: Petit had his finest outing of the season last Wednesday against the Phillies at Chase Field. The right-hander handled the NL's best lineup and made it look easy. Philadelphia managed just two hits against him through the first six innings and he retired 13 in a row before allowing two hits to open the seventh. Petit does not have overpowering stuff, so he needs to hit his spots and keep the ball down. When he does that, he can have some success; when he doesn't, it can be ugly as his 6.75 ERA can attest.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf closed out July by earning a victory against the Nationals in his last start. He gave up two runs on six hits in 6 1/3 innings. The right-hander has been solid at PNC Park this season, going 7-2 in 11 starts while posting a 3.34 ERA. Ohlendorf has pitched against Arizona once this season, on July 25. He took the loss despite surrendering three runs - two earned - in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis did not pitch particularly well in his last start against the Mets on Friday, but he did get the job done. The left-hander allowed four hits and walked six in six innings, but managed to allow just two runs. That can be typical of Davis, who tends to allow a lot of baserunners, but more often than not pitches his way out of trouble. At the end of one of his outings, it is not uncommon to look at the final score and wonder how exactly he got there. Davis does not give into hitters, which contributes to the walk total, but he also can try to be too fine at times, which compounds the problem.

home_pitcher_note: Hart, who was one of the acquisitions in the Pirates' trade with the Cubs on July 30, makes his Pittsburgh debut. It will be the fifth game and first start of his career at PNC Park, where he is 1-0 with a 9.00 ERA. Hart hasn't faced Arizona this season, but the right-hander has won his last three starts overall, giving up six runs in 17 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer had a disastrous fourth inning against the Mets in his last outing on Saturday night and it prevented him from getting a win. Following his best start of the year, the right-hander held the Mets scoreless through the first three innings. But in the fourth, he wound up allowing five hits and four runs. Even more damaging to his chances for a win was the fact that he threw a whopping 38 pitches in the inning, which caused manager A.J. Hinch to take him out. In his start before that, Scherzer tossed seven scoreless innings allowing five hits and no walks while striking out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Balester had another solid outing on Sunday, pitching 5 2/3 innings and giving up two runs on five hits against the Pirates. He ended up with a no-decision. Balester still needs to make improvements. He must attack the hitters more when the count is 0-2.
away_pitcher_note: Garland had one of his finest outings of the year last time out against the Mets. The right-hander allowed two runs in a complete-game 5-2 win at Citi Field. The key for Garland was his command and the fact that he was able to use all of his pitches. He has put together seven quality starts in a row -- six or more innings, three or fewer runs -- and has pitched better than his numbers would indicate. When Garland has been bad, he has been real bad, which has ballooned his ERA. Four times he has allowed six or more earned runs in a start. A potential free agent at the end of the year with the D-backs holding a $10 million option, Garland is pitching for his next contract.

home_pitcher_note: Mock started on Monday and was erratic against the Pirates. He lasted four-plus innings and gave up three runs -- two earned -- on seven hits. The three runs were scored in the bottom of the first. It didn't help that the Nats made two errors behind him. When Mock left the game in the fifth, the bases were loaded with no outs. Interim manager Jim Riggleman inserted Tyler Clippard to try to stop the bleeding. Clippard ended up being the pitching hero by not allowing a run to score.
away_pitcher_note: Haren did not have his best stuff last time out against the Mets at Citi Field. The offense staked him to a 6-0 lead, which usually is more than enough, but the right-hander had to hang on for a 6-5 win. The five runs allowed matched the most he has allowed in a start this year. He took the loss in his start before that against Philadelphia. He said that facing the Phillies' lineup was like pitching in the All-Star Game. The Phillies made him work hard, fouling off pitches and running the right-hander's pitch count up early. Haren left after five innings having already thrown 117 pitches. It was the second successive start in which he has lasted just five innings, the only two times that has happened to him this season.

home_pitcher_note: Martin struggled against the Marlins on Tuesday, lasting 4 1/3 innings and giving up three runs on six hits. Florida took a 1-0 lead in the first inning when Nick Johnson singled under the glove of Adam Dunn at first base to score Chris Coghlan. Three innings later, Cody Ross and Josh Johnson hit solo home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Petit has had the two best games of his career in his last two outings. Against the Pirates last Tuesday in Pittsburgh, he had a no-hitter through seven innings before allowing a single to Ronny Cedeno in the eighth. It was the only hit he would allow in eight innings. In his start before that the right-hander handled the NL's best lineup in the Phillies and made it look easy. Philadelphia managed just two hits against him through the first six innings and he retired 13 in a row before allowing a pair of hits to open the seventh. Over his last two outings, Petit has combined to throw 14 scoreless innings and he has allowed just five hits over that span. Petit does not have overpowering stuff so he needs to hit his spots and keep the ball down.

home_pitcher_note: Davis looked to be on the way to a tough-luck loss in his last outing before the D-backs rallied to beat the Pirates in Pittsburgh. Davis allowed a pair of runs over seven innings. The D-backs rallied for three runs in the eighth to take a 4-2 lead and Davis wound up with his second win in three starts. After a rough pair of outings, Davis has allowed just four runs in 19 innings over his last three starts and is 2-0 over that stretch while the D-backs are 3-0 in those games. In his start prior to his last one he got a no decision against the Mets. He held New York to two runs over six innings. Davis does not give into hitters, which results in his high walk total, but he also can try to be too fine at times which compounds the problem.
away_pitcher_note: Rather than pitch against the Padres, Pelfrey became a padre. The birth of his first child Thursday pushed his 22nd start back two days. Now he pitches in Phoenix rather than San Diego and with seven days rest. The Diamondbacks were his last opponent. Pelfrey lost his start against them Aug. 2 at Citi Field, allowing three runs in five hits and three walks in five innings. He threw 107 pitches. He has averaged merely 5.4 innings in his past 12 starts after a run of five in which he averaged 6.9. Pelfrey's ERA on the road is 5.75, and five of the nine home runs he has allowed have come in the 51 2/3 innings he has pitched away from Citi. He is winless with three losses and a 5.91 ERA in four career starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer has struggled in his last two outings, but offensive support has helped him avoid losses and instead come away with no decisions in those games. His last time out against the Pirates he held them to two runs through the first five innings before the Pirates scored three off him as part of a four-run sixth that chased him from the game. Over his last two outings he has allowed nine runs in 9 1/3 innings. It's quite a contrast to his start prior to that stretch which also came against the Pirates on July 26. In that game he held the Bucs scoreless for seven innings while striking out eight.
away_pitcher_note: Sometimes Hernandez get past his first-inning troubles. Sometimes he compounds them in subsequent innings. In his most recent start, Thursday against the challenged Padres, he allowed two runs in the first inning, four in the third and a seventh before his five-inning workday was complete. He allowed eight hits, four walks, and each of the walks begat a run. Now he faces the D-backs, the team that beat him at Citi Field July 31. He allowed two runs in six innings. He has split two decisions against them since the beginning of the 2006 season. Hernandez beat the D-backs in the Metrodome as a member of the Twins on June 22 last year, allowing one earned run -- three over all -- and nine hits in seven innings. He has a 10-7 record in 19 career starts against them, but most of the personnel he faced is gone now.

home_pitcher_note: Garland took a no-decision Friday in six innings against the Nationals, but probably deserved better. Handed a 5-0 lead in the second inning, Garland could not hold it, but his problems stemmed from a pair of defensive miscues by center fielder Gerardo Parra. First, Parra misplayed a single into three bases, leading to an unearned run. Two innings later he started forward on a line drive over which sailed over his head. That play was ruled a double, and led to a three-run inning off Garland.
away_pitcher_note: Perez was Good Ollie against the Padres on Friday night. He gave his best and longest performance of the season, allowing two hits, two walks and a run in 6 1/3 innings. And he threw merely 93 pitches, a virtual day off for his arm. He didn't win, but he reminded colleagues of the pitcher they rarely have seen since last August. Now he faces the D-backs, the team he faced Aug. 1 at Citi Field. The Mets won that game, he didn't. He was removed after only five innings, having walked five batters and thrown 112 pitches. He allowed two earned runs in that start and now has a 2.50 ERA in 18 innings (three starts) against the D-backs in the last four seasons. But he is winless. He has pitched merely six innings -- they were scoreless -- in Chase Field in the same timeframe.

home_pitcher_note:
Once the National League Cy Young front-runner, Haren has been far from an ace over his last four starts, surrendering 16 runs in 23 innings. His latest effort was a loss in which he threw six innings and gave up five runs at Washington.
"It's no secret, I'm scuffling right now," Haren said. "I really haven't had a great rhythm the last few times out. I'm trying to find it right now. I just have to try to dig myself out of a hole, the best I can."
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw certainly pitched well enough to win Saturday night against the Braves. He struck out 10, walked one and gave up just two hits in one of his strongest outings of the season. After being unable to last at least six innings on Aug. 3 for the first time since July 1, Kershaw didn't hesitate to go after the Atlanta hitters. He struck out two batters in each of the first three innings, as his fastball and curveball appeared especially lively. Kershaw is 0-0 with a 2.70 ERA in two career starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis has put together four straight good starts. The D-backs have won all four of those games and Davis is 3-0 with a 2.08 ERA in that span. Last time out against the Mets he allowed a pair of runs on four hits over seven innings in a 7-4 Arizona win. According to an ESPN.com report, Davis was recently placed on waivers by the D-backs. The left-hander, though, does not seem to be bothered by the news and said if he got traded to a contender it would be a "win-win" situation. Davis is a free agent at the end of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda responded to the tension of the Dodgers-Giants rivalry as if he was pitching in October. Kuroda allowed one run on six hits over 6 1/3 innings and stopped a three-game losing streak. He was given an extra day of rest for his shoulder and the result wasn't bad. Kuroda has four consecutive quality starts and the Dodgers are 6-1 in his last seven starts. Kuroda is 1-3 in five starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Petit could not follow his two exceptional starts with a third, as the red-hot Nationals pounced on him for nine hits and four runs -- three earned -- in four innings. Petit was lifted from the game for a pinch-hitter in the top of the fifth, ending his afternoon at 83 pitches. "I struggled with command," Petit said. "I was leaving the ball up at the plate and they hit it. My command on both sides was not working good.
away_pitcher_note: Randy Wolf allowed a third-inning run after a leadoff walk, but otherwise shut down the Giants for eight strong innings and his eighth quality start in his last nine outings. The Dodgers have scored 32 runs in Wolf's last three wins and he now leads the staff in innings pitched. Wolf is 7-3 lifetime against the Diamondbacks, 1-0 this year.

home_pitcher_note: The D-Backs will be getting their first look at Hanson, who has lived up to his billing while posting a 2.53 ERA in his past 11 starts. The 22-year-old right-hander, who is considered to be the game's top right-handed prospect, registered nine strikeouts and won his second consecutive start on Tuesday night against the Nationals. He has allowed two earned runs or less in three of his past four outings.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer rebounded from a pair of poor outings to beat the Mets in his last start. The right-hander allowed two runs on eight hits in 6 2/3 innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out eight in that game. In his two starts prior to that, he allowed a total of nine runs in 9 1/3 innings. One of the keys to the improvement for Scherzer was his aggressiveness in attacking left-handed hitters, something he felt he had gotten away from.

home_pitcher_note: Not bad for a first effort after more than 10 months away from the game. In his Phillies debut, Martinez allowed seven hits, three runs and one walk, striking out five in five innings during a 12-5 victory over the Cubs at Wrigley Field on Wednesday. Martinez had made just three rehab starts after spending most of the season in the Dominican Republic before he faced the Cubs. Martinez considered the outing a good start to what he expects will be stronger performances in the future.
away_pitcher_note: Garland got a no-decision in his last start but deserved better. The right-hander allowed three runs -- two earned -- over six innings as the D-backs fell to the Mets, 6-4, at Chase Field. Not only was one of the runs against him unearned, but the D-backs missed many an opportunity to give Garland more than just a 1-0 lead through five innings. Arizona stranded 11 men in the first five frames. Signed by the team as a free agent, Garland has been as advertised: A guy that will keep his team in ballgames while also chewing up innings. His 149 1/3 innings trail only Dan Haren on the staff.

home_pitcher_note: In eight strong innings Thursday against the Cubs at Wrigley Field, Lee allowed six hits, one run and three walks and struck out eight. He is 3-0 with a 1.13 ERA in three starts with the Phillies. He has allowed 16 hits, three runs and six walks in 24 innings. He has struck out 24. Opponents have hit just .193 against him. To put that into comparison, CC Sabathia went 3-0 with a 1.88 ERA in his first three starts last season after the Indians traded him to the Brewers. He allowed 17 hits, six runs, five earned runs, one home run and six walks in 24 innings. He hit two batters and struck out 24. Opponents hit .205 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Haren pitched well in his last outing, against the Dodgers, allowing just one run on six hits over eight innings and outdueling Clayton Kershaw. It was a good bounce-back game for Haren, who had struggled some in his previous four outings. Over that span, he allowed 16 earned runs in 23 innings -- not necessarily awful, but not up to the standards he set in the season's first half. One of the keys for Haren his last time out was his ability to get left-handers out, something that he had struggled with in his previous four games.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton battled through seven innings against the Braves on Friday, scattering seven hits and allowing just one earned run to take a no-decision. The right-hander struck out just two batters and benefited from some brilliant defensive plays by his outfielders, but he left the game after the seventh with the score tied at 2. Blanton's only other career start against the D-backs came last season. In that outing, he allowed eight earned runs over three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis has put together five good starts in a row following a two-start hiccup in which he struggled. Davis walked a tightrope in his last outing, against the Dodgers, walking four and allowing six hits over six innings. True to form, though, he found a way to pitch his way out of jams and wound up allowing just three runs. He did not get a decision in the game, as the D-backs rallied for two runs in the ninth to tie it before winning in the 10th. According to multiple reports, Davis was placed on waivers last week and was claimed by the Brewers. The two teams were unable to work out a deal, and Davis -- a free-agent-to-be -- will remain with Arizona the rest of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt received his career-high 14th no-decision after allowing eight hits and five runs in six innings on Sunday against the Brewers in Milwaukee. He gave up a two-run homer to Ryan Braun in the first and another two-run homer to Prince Fielder. Oswalt is 0-1 in two starts against the Brewers this year, having allowed 18 hits and eight runs in 12 1/3 innings. Oswalt is 13-8 in 27 career starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Petit showcased his capabilities when he nearly no-hit the Pirates on Aug. 4. But that phenomenal start -- when he allowed just one hit and no runs in eight innings -- is looking more like an anomaly, at least at this stage in the 24-year-old's career. In two outings since, Petit has allowed 10 earned runs, 18 hits and four home runs in just eight innings. His 6.47 ERA is highest in the National League among pitchers who have thrown at least 60 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler will fill the hole in the rotation left by Mike Hampton, who was placed on the 15-day disabled list with a left shoulder strain. Moehler's last start was against the Brewers. The right-hander was decent in five innings pitched, giving up 10 hits but allowing just three earned runs in taking a loss. He hasn't won a decision since July 20 against the Cardinals. He is 2-6 with a 6.44 ERA at Minute Maid Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer was hurt by one big six-running inning -- and his own costly throwing error -- during his last outing, a 9-4 loss to the Braves. The 24-year-old righty allowed all nine runs, but only three were earned. "Max was OK," D-backs manager A.J. Hinch said. "The wheels came off in the third." Before that, Scherzer had been pitching well, going 5-2 with a 3.52 ERA between June 1 and last Sunday. He allowed no runs and struck out seven in 4 1/3 innings during his only career outing -- a relief appearance -- against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Norris lost for the first time in his big league career last time out against the Marlins. After cruising through the first three innings, scattering two hits, Norris allowed five runs over the next three innings. He was unable to work out of the sixth after loading the bases and walking in a run, the third run of the inning. In his first and only meeting with Milwaukee, he tossed six innings, allowing two runs on three hits, and struck out a season-high seven.
away_pitcher_note: Battling stormy Philadelphia rains, Garland allowed five earned runs on 11 hits in 5 1/3 innings during his last outing. The weather was not the problem, he said. Rather, in a three-run third inning, he was hurt by defensive miscues, and later in the game, as his pitches flattened out, he surrendered two solo home runs. He had thrown eight quality starts in his past nine outings entering Tuesday. In three career starts against the Astros, Garland is 0-1 with a 4.26 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cain won his first two starts following the All-Star break but has gone winless in five starts since, despite compiling a respectable 2.97 ERA in that span. Cain has proven somewhat susceptible to the long ball, yielding five home runs in his last four starts. He's 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in two starts this season against the Diamondbacks, receiving no decision against them on April 26 despite allowing one run in seven innings, then earning the win in the Giants' 9-4 triumph on June 9 while lasting 6 1/3 innings and yielding all of Arizona's runs.
away_pitcher_note: Haren allowed three home runs during his last start, an 8-1 debacle against the Phillies. He has allowed at least one homer in six consecutive outings and 22 homers this year, surpassing last years total of 19. Since his ERA dipped below 2.00 on July 18, the 28-year-old righty has gone 2-3 with a 5.75 ERA, allowing 42 hits, nine homers and 23 earned runs in 36 innings. "Something I hadn't been doing earlier is making mistakes, Haren said. "It seems like every mistake I make now, I'm paying for it."

home_pitcher_note: In case no one has noticed, Sanchez is on a roll. In his last start, Sanchez struck out eight in five innings and allowed just one unearned run, even though he was pitching without fastball command. Instead, the lefty relied on his slider to record his punchouts. Sanchez has won four of his past six decisions and has a 2.90 ERA since he was reinserted into the rotation. However, Sanchez owns a career 2-6 record with a 5.70 ERA against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Davis struggled against the Phillies in his last outing, hurt by walks, poor defense behind him and a few big extra-base hits. He surrendered six runs (five earned) in five innings, and it could have been worse had he not stranded the bases loaded in the fourth. Before Thursday, though, Davis had been on a roll, allowing just eight earned runs in 32 innings (2.25 ERA) over his prior five starts, all D-backs wins.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie Martinez is learning his trade during the playoff chase. Unfortunately, he hasn't lasted more than five innings in any of his four starts. Martinez gave up six runs, five earned, on nine hits in five-plus innings Saturday to get a no-decision in a 14-11 loss to the Rockies. Martinez only threw 73 pitches after a 67-pitch outing in his previous start. However, his one mistake to Ian Stewart resulted in a three-run home run that tied the game at 6. Martinez is still searching for his first quality start and has a 5.59 ERA since being recalled on Aug. 5.
away_pitcher_note: Petit pitched well in his last start on Friday but came away with a loss nonetheless as the D-backs fell, 1-0, to the Astros at Minute Maid Park. The right-hander allowed just four hits and walked two over six innings. The lone run of the game came when Jeff Keppinger's fifth-inning double scored Hunter Pence. It was a good bounceback game for Petit, who had allowed seven runs on nine hits in lasting just four innings against the Dodgers on Aug. 16. Petit had a two start stretch in which he did not allow a run in 14 innings from July 29-Aug. 4.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer is riding a two-start losing streak and has won just two games since June 23. The right-hander allowed four runs on seven hits over five innings against the Astros last Saturday in Houston. Scherzer was more aggressive with his pitches early in the count, which was something he had to work on after allowing nine runs in his start before that to the Braves in Atlanta. The Astros, though, were relentless at the plate and Scherzer's inability to put away Kaz Matsui and Geoff Blum with two strikes helped lead to his downfall against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Bazardo makes his fourth career start and second of the season for the Astros. The right-hander, who made his 2009 debut Aug. 8 after spending most of the season at Triple-A Round Rock, gave up six hits, four walks and two runs in 4 2/3 innings in Saturday's win at Milwaukee, though he didn't get a decision. At Triple-A Round Rock this year, he was 9-6 with a 3.20 ERA in 23 games, including 20 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garland did not have his best stuff in his last outing against the Astros but wound up getting his first win since Aug. 2. The D-backs scored five first-inning runs for him and added another in the second to give him a 6-0 lead. Garland allowed the Astros to creep back into the game as he allowed four runs on 10 hits over six innings, but he pitched his way out of jams when he needed to.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will get another shot at the Diamondbacks, who roughed him up Sunday in Houston. Norris allowed six hits, three walks and six earned runs in one inning in his first career start against Arizona and fifth start of his career. In his first two Major League starts, he was 2-0 with a 1.38 ERA. In his past three starts, he's 1-2 with an 11.57 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Haren pitched well enough to win but didn't get much offensive support in his last outing. The right-hander held the Giants to two runs on six hits over seven innings at AT&T Park. One of the runs came on a Juan Uribe homer while the other scored when Haren uncorked a wild pitch. Reliever Jon Rauch gave up a game-deciding three-run homer in the eighth. It was a good bounce-back game for Haren, who allowed six runs on nine hits in five innings against the Phillies. In the first half of the season, Haren was 9-5 with a 2.01 ERA in 18 starts. Through eight starts in the second half, Haren is 3-3 with a 4.59 ERA. In one start against the Astros this year, on June 12, Haren tossed a complete game, allowing one run on two hits.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is coming off one of his best starts of the season, even if in a losing cause. Against the Cardinals on Tuesday in St. Louis, he gave up three hits, one run and one walk in seven innings. He gave up a run in the walk and retired 18 of 19 batters during one stretch. He's 7-2 with a 2.34 ERA in his past 12 starts and has held the opponent to one run or fewer in nine of his past 10 starts.  He's 0-0 with a 1.35 ERA in three starts this year against the Cubs, allowing 15 hits and striking out 17 batters in 20 innings. For his career, he's 4-4 with a 3.84 ERA in 13 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Randy Wolf has stepped up while the Dodgers have been sagging. He ran his win streak to four with a clutch effort at Coors Field, limiting the torrid Rockies to one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings. Most importantly, Wolf is consistently eating innings. He's pitched at least six innings in each of his last 12 starts and has 10 quality starts in his last 11 outings. The Dodgers are 18-10 in his starts. He's 2-0 against Arizona this year, 8-3 lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: Davis seemed on his way to certain victory in his last start as he handled the Giants easily through the first seven innings at AT&T Park. To that point, the lone San Francisco run had come on a Juan Uribe homer. Davis got the first two outs of the eighth before allowing a walk and single. In came closer Chad Qualls and he allowed a three-run homer to pinch-hitter Bengie Molina. Davis wound up without a decision and the D-backs took a 4-3 defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Vicente Padilla did a respectable job in his Dodgers debut at Coors Field, limiting the hot-hitting Rockies to two runs on six hits in five innings with one walk and four strikeouts. Padilla was clocked as fast as 96 mph and he was in trouble on in the two-run third inning. He was lifted for a pinch-hitter with the score tied in the top of the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Petit tweaked his mechanics a bit after allowing seven runs on nine hits in four innings to the Dodgers on Aug. 16. He now turns a little more away from the hitter during his windup. It adds a little more deception, which is important because Petit does not have overpowering stuff. Since making the adjustment, Petit has allowed just one run over 12 innings. His last time out, against the Giants, Petit tossed six shutout innings, allowing just four hits. In his start prior to that, Petit allowed one run over six innings in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley lasted less than six innings for the first time since Aug. 2 against the Braves. He gave up four runs on seven hits in five-plus innings of a 4-2 loss. After a perfect 1 2/3 innings, Billingsley gave up a run in the second and two runs in the third. He later allowed another in the sixth before exiting. He will look to get back on track against the D-backs, who he is 1-0 against this season.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer, who like other members of the Arizona starting rotation has suffered his share of tough losses, gained a measure of redemption in his last outing, when he earned a win for the first time while allowing more than two runs. But his troubles in that 14-7 victory over Houston had much to do with a huge early lead softening his customary intensity. Manager A.J. Hinch is going to shorten the leash on the 25-year-old, who has already worked more innings (139 1/3) than all of last season between Tucson and Arizona (109).

home_pitcher_note: Jon Garland will be pitching as scheduled at Dodger Stadium, but instead of facing the Dodgers for the Diamondbacks, he'll be facing the Diamondbacks for the Dodgers after Monday night's trade. He is coming off seven shutout innings against the Astros. Garland is an innings-eater who has been especially effective recently because of his changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner will be making his first start since being recalled Monday from Triple-A Reno. The right-hander will face former teammate Jon Garland, who was dealt to Los Angeles on Monday night. Buckner has appeared in 10 games and made seven starts for the D-backs this season. This is his third stint in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel was effective in his last outing, when he held the Giants to four hits and two runs in five innings. Manager Jim Tracy pulled him for Franklin Morales at the first sign of trouble, but Hammel has proved more often than not he's capable of beating such problems. Still he has to be better at home, where he is 2-3 with a 6.47 ERA in 12 games, 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren picked up the win in his last start against the Astros last Sunday at Chase Field. The right-hander allowed three runs on seven hits over six innings. In his last two starts, he has allowed five earned runs in 14 innings. Haren was dominant in the season's first half, compiling a 2.01 ERA in 18 starts. The second half has been a different story as he has a 4.50 ERA in nine starts. In three starts against the Rockies this year, he is 2-1 with a 0.90 ERA, and in those 20 innings, he has fanned 24 and walked just two.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies picked up Contreras from the White Sox, for pitching prospect Brandon Hynick, just before Monday's deadline for acquiring players to be eligible for a postseason roster. Contreras went 5-13 with a 5.42 ERA for the White Sox. But Contreras has big-game experience and will be facing NL hitters not familiar with him. Manager Jim Tracy said as long as Contreras spots his fastball properly, he can baffle hitters with his split-finger pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Davis did not get a decision in his last start, which came against the Dodgers last Monday at Dodger Stadium. The left-hander allowed three runs on five hits over six innings in a game the D-backs won, 5-3, in 10 innings. Davis has not won in his last four starts, though he has pitched poorly in only one of those games. In two starts against the Rockies this year, he is 0-2 with a 14.73 ERA. In a July 20 start at Coors Field he lasted just 2 1/3 innings -- his shortest outing of the year -- and gave up eight runs.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa couldn't command his fastball and had a hittable changeup in the first inning of his last start, at home against the Mets. But he grabbed control of his mechanics and gave the Mets absolutely nothing thereafter. De La Rosa held the Mets to no further scoring and four hits in six total innings.
away_pitcher_note: Petit has pitched well for the better part of the past two months. There had been speculation that he would lose his spot in the rotation, but over his last seven starts he has a 3.00 ERA. That number goes down to 1.54 if you remove one start in which he allowed seven runs in just four innings. Last time out against the Dodgers, Petit got a no-decision despite allowing just two earned runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer helped the D-backs secure a series split in Los Angeles last week, earning a 4-1 win on Wednesday, when he allowed one run on seven hits and a walk while striking out four over 7 2/3 innings. The win put him on a bit of a roll, going 2-0 with a 3.95 ERA over his last two starts.  He has faced the Dodgers one other time, on May 5 in L.A., putting up a quality start but taking a loss. He pitched six innings and allowing three runs (two earned) on four hits and two walks while striking out four. Though he has won twice as many games at home, his ERA is 0.76 better on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is expected to return after an extra day off. He sustained a bruised calf when struck by a line drive in the first inning against Arizona last Tuesday, but he hung in there to allow one run in 5 1/3 innings for his second effective start since being picked up by the Dodgers. He escaped a first-inning jam after a mound meeting with pitching coach Rick Honeycutt resulted in an immediate five extra miles per hour on his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Buckner rejoined the D-backs from Triple-A Reno last week and started against the Dodgers, giving up four runs on eight hits in six innings and taking the loss. After having success in Reno, Buckner knows that he needs to carry that over into the big leagues to help his chances of winning a spot in the rotation next year. Buckner has incorporated a cut fastball into his repertoire and has changed his approach on the mound as well. "I'm a different pitcher than I was last time I was here," said Buckner, who is in his third stint with the team this year.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley took a perfect game into the fifth against Arizona on Wednesday, then things unraveled. He allowed a two-run homer to Brandon Allen and a pair of RBI infield singles in the four-run inning. His mechanics were much improved from previous shaky outings. He has one win in his last five starts and only three in his last 14. He's now 7-5 lifetime against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Haren faced the Rockies for the fourth time this season, and after yielding a run in each of the first two innings, he changed his game plan, getting away from his fastball and relying on his cutter and splitter before finally moving to his curve, which he said he threw more often than he ever has in Coors Field. He wasn't satisfied with his stuff, but it was good enough to get him through six innings with only the two runs on seven hits and a walk while striking out eight.
away_pitcher_note: Garland gets the chance to beat his former team a second time. Garland overcame early-innings jitters in his Dodgers debut to contain the D-backs on two runs for seven innings, retiring the final 14 batters he faced. He was clearly strong enough to keep going, but gave way to closers George Sherrill and Jonathan Broxton.

home_pitcher_note: Davis pitched pretty well in his last outing, but came away with a loss nonetheless. The lefty allowed three runs on seven hits over six innings as the D-backs fell, 4-1, to the Rockies. Davis has gone 0-2 in his last five starts with a 4.70 ERA. His last win came on Aug. 10 against the Mets, part of a three-game winning streak. Davis will be facing his former team for the first time this year. In four career starts against Milwaukee, Davis is 1-1 with a 5.49 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This is Yovani Gallardo's spot to pitch, but the Brewers are concerned about their budding ace's workload so they are essentially skipping his spot in the rotation. An off-day during the week allows the team to use Looper here on regular rest, and he's coming off a fine outing against the Giants at Miller Park in which he allowed only one run and matched a season high with seven innings. Looper got some help after he surrendered successive singles leading off the sixth inning when San Francisco's Aaron Rowand grounded into a 5-4-3 triple play, the first turned by the Brewers in 10 years. He's 7-3 away from Miller Park this season despite a 5.03 ERA, a half-run worse than his ERA at home.

home_pitcher_note: Mulvey is taking the place of Yusmeiro Petit in the rotation, likely for the rest of the season. The club wants to get a look at the right-hander acquired in the deal that sent Jon Rauch to the Twins. Mulvey is no stranger to being traded. A second-round pick by the Mets in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, he was dealt to the Twins as part of the Johan Santana deal. Mulvey, who was 5-8 with a 3.93 ERA in 24 starts for Triple-A Rochester this year, has appeared in two games in relief for the D-backs since joining the team on Sept. 1. He made his big league debut on July 20 with the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Bush's availability was briefly in doubt before his start against the Cardinals on Monday, but he delivered seven strong innings in a tough-luck loss to Chris Carpenter. Bush was cleared to pitch after receiving assurances from head physician William Raasch that the discomfort in his right triceps was a normal part of healing. Bush spent about two months on the disabled list with microtears of the muscle, the result of a line drive off his arm in early June. In his first two starts back, Bush has surrendered 13 runs in eight innings, but he limited St. Louis to two runs on seven hits with no walks and three strikeouts. A few more outings like that one would give Bush something positive to think about over the winter.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer was hurt by the long ball in his last start. The right-hander allowed four runs over seven innings to the Dodgers, with three of the runs coming via homers. Manny Ramirez and James Loney hit back-to-back homers to open the second inning and Ronnie Belliard hit one with one out in the fourth. In his previous start, Scherzer tied his career high for his longest outing when he lasted 7 2/3 innings against the Dodgers in Dodger Stadium. Scherzer only allowed one run in that game as he picked up his second win in as many starts.
away_pitcher_note: This was scheduled to be Manny Parra's turn in the rotation, but he exited his last start after only one inning, complaining of neck spasms.

home_pitcher_note: The former Giant fared well against his old team on Tuesday, though it went for naught. Correia allowed three runs and eight hits in six innings against a team he was very familiar with. Correia allowed a solo home run to Aaron Rowand and had five strikeouts and one walk. He got a nice mix of ground-ball (six) and fly-ball outs (six) and kept the Padres close in a game where they couldn't go much against 20-year-old Madison Bumgarner in his Major League debut. It was another quality start for Correia, who was making his 29th start of the season. The 114 pitches were the most he has thrown all season.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner is pitching to position himself for a spot in the rotation next year. He pitched well in his last outing, allowing just one run on five hits over seven innings against the Dodgers at Chase Field. The right-hander was helped by a defense that matched a team record by turning five double plays behind him. The curve is probably Buckner's best pitch and he has worked this season on developing a cut fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Five days after tossing six scoreless innings in a victory over the Dodgers, LeBlanc went after another NL West bigwig, the Giants. Other than allowing a two-run home run to leadoff hitter Andres Blanco in the third inning, LeBlanc pitched pretty well, getting 11 ground-ball outs over seven-plus innings in a victory at AT&T Park. LeBlanc walked three and struck out three and allowed four hits. In his last two starts since being promoted from Triple-A Portland, LeBlanc has allowed two runs in 13 innings with six hits allowed, a far cry from his early struggles with the team in June (seven runs in 4 1/3 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Haren pitched well enough to win in his last outing, but came away with a no-decision instead as the D-backs beat the Dodgers, 4-3, in the bottom of the ninth inning at Chase Field. Haren allowed three runs on seven hits in 7 1/3 innings in the game. The Dodger hitter that did the most damage against him was Manny Ramirez, who drove in a run in the first inning with a single and hit a solo homer in the fourth. Haren left with the game tied, 3-3, and the D-backs won it when Mark Reynolds drew a bases-loaded walk.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres could go another route here instead of Mujica, who looked very good in a spot start on Friday, allowing two hits in four shutout innings against the Rockies. In a game where Mujica was expected to throw between 40-60 pitches, the right-hander threw 56 pitches over his four innings. He was replaced by Sean Gallagher. Mujica didn't walk a batter and had three strikeouts in his short stint. If the Padres decided to use a true starter against the D-backs, it could be left-hander Cesar Ramos, who was recalled from Triple-A Portland earlier in the week.
away_pitcher_note: Davis has not won in his last six starts. In fairness, only two of those can be characterized as poor outings. His last time out against the Brewers was one of them as he allowed 11 hits and five runs before being removed with no outs and the bases loaded in the fourth inning. It was his second-shortest outing of the season. Davis is pitching for a contract. The left-hander is in the final year of a three-year extension he signed prior to the 2007 season. Davis has said he would like a three-year deal this time around as well.

home_pitcher_note: Mulvey's first Major League start did not go as he'd hoped. The right-hander allowed six runs on 11 hits in just four innings against the Brewers at Chase Field. Mulvey is taking the place of Yusmeiro Petit in the rotation likely for the rest of the season. The club wants to get a look at the right-hander acquired in the deal that sent Jon Rauch to the Twins. Mulvey is no stranger to being traded. A second-round pick by the Mets in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, he was dealt to the Twins as part of the Johan Santana deal. Mulvey, who was 5-8 with a 3.93 ERA in 24 starts for Triple-A Rochester this year and has appeared in two games in relief for the D-backs since joining the team on Sept. 1. He made his big league debut on July 20 with the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis faltered against a team he had handled well this season when he allowed five runs to San Diego on Sunday as the Rockies fell 6-3 in the series finale.  In his previous two starts against the Padres, Marquis yielded just one run over 16 innings, but San Diego touched him for three runs in the decisive sixth after he walked Everth Cabrera with the bases loaded, one of three unintentional walks in the inning.  After having his start bumped up one day but still pitching on normal rest, Marquis faces an Arizona team that scored six runs against him in a loss on April 20.

away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander has pitched well and should have a few more wins if it weren't for a leaky bullpen. He has gone seven innings in three starts, giving up two earned in two of them, and is 0-1 in those three outings. Overall has four starts with two earned runs or fewer, but he is just 1-1 in those games with the victory coming in his first start of the season against Pittsburgh. Lopez, pitching for his fifth organization since making his big league debut with San Diego in 2000, is a hard-nosed pitcher in that he doesn't have overpowering stuff but he never gives into hitters and battles like it is the last time he will ever pitch in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson was not especially sharp in his last outing, when he tied a career high with six walks over six innings. He did earn the win, however, improving his record to 3-1 on the season and lowering his ERA to 2.64 after allowing just one run on six hits. The right-hander continued his strong start to the 2010 campaign, which has seen him allow no more than three runs in his first seven starts. In six career starts against the D-backs, Hudson has been dominant, going 4-0 with a 1.61 ERA. He has allowed just nine runs -- eight earned -- on 34 hits in 44 2/3 innings against the D-backs.

Volstad has been impressive of late, even in his latest defeat. The right-hander had won two straight decisions before falling to the Cubs at Wrigley Field. He gave up four runs in six innings. What hurt him were four walks. Other than that, he continues to find a way to work into the later part of the game. He has thrown 22 innings in his last three outings, giving up seven runs.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson has pitched better in his past two starts, with one at-bat seemingly doing him in both times. In his last start, against the Dodgers, it was Manny Ramirez's three-run double off the wall in the seventh inning that was the difference between a win and a loss. It's been a struggle for much of the season for Jackson, and he gets himself into trouble when he is not aggressive early in counts. When he falls behind, hitters are more easily able to gear up for his mid-90s fastball. With that in mind, John Hester will catch Jackson in this start because manager A.J. Hinch thinks Hester helps him be more aggressive with the fastball. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are Jackson's third team in three years; he pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers before last year. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and change.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson is his old ace self lately. The 26-year-old hasn't given up more than three earned runs since Opening Day, sports a 2.25 ERA in his last four starts and hasn't walked a batter in his last two outings -- a span of 13 innings. His last time on the mound, Johnson got the no-decision after matching Mets ace Johan Santana pitch for pitch for seven innings. He gave up just one run, scattered three hits and struck out seven. But in a 1-1 game with runners on first and second and two outs in the bottom of the seventh, Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez was forced to pinch-hit for Johnson, so his outing finished after 95 pitches (71 strikes). In three career starts against the D-backs, Johnson is 2-1 with a 1.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner will be recalled from Triple-A Reno to make this start. This is the spot in the rotation that Cesar Valdez occupied the past two times through it. With the bullpen scuffling, though, the team elected to use Valdez in relief. Buckner lost out to Rodrigo Lopez for the final spot in the rotation during Spring Training. He was the front-runner going into camp but pitched poorly in his last few outings. In seven starts for Reno, Buckner is 3-1 with a 3.53 ERA. He has gone at least six innings and allowed three or fewer runs in his past five starts. Buckner has a very good curveball, and the club told him at the end of the spring that he should throw it more and his cut fastball less.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has been Arizona's best pitcher this year. In his last start, against the Braves, Kennedy did not receive a decision because another meltdown by the bullpen cost him. The right-hander tossed six shutout innings before Brian McCann led off the seventh with a home run. After allowing back-to-back singles later in the inning, he was removed with a 4-1 lead, only to watch Juan Gutierrez give up a three-run homer to tie the game. Kennedy appeared in just one game for the Yankees in 2009 and four in Triple-A after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. The right-hander came in the same three-team trade that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer is the Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde of the Giants pitching staff. At home, he's cool, calm and collected with a 2-1 mark and a 3.04 ERA. On the road, it's a completely different story. Away from the friendly confines of AT&T Park, it's a cruel world for the right-hander, who's 0-2 with a 9.49 ERA on the road. He's 1-3 with a 4.79 ERA against the Arizona Diamondbacks for his career, and he pitched fairly well in his only start at Chase Field. He wouldn't mind facing Adam LaRoche, though, as the first baseman is a lifetime .192 hitter (5-for-26) against him. Keep Stephen Drew away from Wellemeyer, however. Drew has six hits in nine at bats against Wellemeyer.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez was magnificent in his last start against the Braves. The right-hander allowed just one run over eight innings in an 11-1 win. Lopez could have gone out for the ninth, but the club elected to give the bullpen some work with such a big lead. Lopez has pitched at least seven innings in his past three starts and has been one of the club's most reliable starters. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. He came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff years ago. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and changeup. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum has thrived against Arizona, as is the case with most opponents. He has averaged more than seven innings per start against the D-backs while compiling a 5-1 record with a 1.87 ERA in nine appearances. He has allowed the D-backs only 48 hits in 67 1/3 innings. Lincecum will be pitching on his usual four days' rest instead of the five he received before his last outing, a 2-1 triumph over Houston on Saturday. Lincecum worked eight innings but said afterward that he didn't feel as sharp as usual, so the extra rest might actually have hampered instead of helped him.

home_pitcher_note: Haren had a really rough outing against the Braves on Sunday and afterward said: "That's as bad as I've been as a Diamondback probably." He gave up seven runs (six earned) in a season-low 4 1/3 innings on eight hits and three walks. It was the fourth time in nine starts Haren had given up four-plus runs in an outing and the second time he's been charged with seven runs. In six career starts against the Blue Jays, he is 4-1 with a 5.77 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Thankfully Morrow bounced back against the Rangers on Sunday following his disastrous outing vs. Boston on May 10, when he was shelled for six runs over just 1 2/3 innings. The right-hander held a potent Rangers offense to just two runs over six innings, with eight strikeouts. What made the outing more encouraging is that Morrow only issued one walk, as oppose to the six he unleashed against the Red Sox. The key for Morrow, who has electric stuff, is to become more consistent with his new delivery -- a lowered arm slot -- and limit the walks which have plagued him from time to time this season. Morrow has only lost once this season when he issues two or fewer free passes, going 3-1 over that span.  Morrow will square off against the D-backs on Friday, a team he has yet to face over his four-year career.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson finally had his first dominant start in a D-backs uniform. The 26-year-old hurled eight shutout innings in a win against the Marlins on Monday night while striking out a career-high 12 batters. Jackson had a no-hitter through four, put only two runners in scoring position and retired six of the last seven batters he faced -- five via strikeout. What's perhaps most impressive is that Jackson didn't really have much command of his fastball, especially early on. His success was mainly the result of a slider that was cutting better than it has all season. For his career against the Blue Jays, Jackson is 2-3 with a 3.82 ERA in 12 games (11 starts).
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight game, Eveland was unable to pitch beyond the fourth inning, on his way to earning his third loss of the season. Eveland surrendered five runs -- three earned -- while giving up nine hits and four walks against the Twins on Monday. While Eveland was unspectacular to say the least, he was also the victim of some poor defense. First baseman Lyle Overbay made two crucial errors on a single play in the fourth inning, resulting in a four-run frame to chase Eveland from the ballgame. Eveland has now allowed eight walks, 15 hits and nine runs over his past two starts. In his career, Eveland is 0-1 with a 0.00 ERA over three relief appearances against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Making his first start of the season after some success in the Minor Leagues, Bucker gave up two runs in five innings but suffered the loss against the Marlins on Tuesday, when Josh Johnson hurled seven shutout innings. Buckner had trouble the second time through the order, and his control failed him in the fourth, when he allowed a run during a six-pitch stretch that saw him issue two hit-by-pitches and a walk. In the fifth, he surrendered back-to-back two-out doubles off the left-field wall. The 26-year-old gave up six hits and threw 56 of his 90 pitches for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: The Blue Jays have gotten exactly what they need from their ace. He has eight quality starts in nine tries, the Jays have won in his last four starts, and all three of his wins have come following losses. In addition, his tip helped straighten out Brandon Morrow's mechanics, and that's just the type of leadership Toronto wants from its big arm. He followed up a seven-inning, two-hit shutout in Boston by going another seven against Minnesota and allowing just one run, and hell hope to keep that momentum rolling against the D-backs, one of baseball's highest-scoring teams.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin, a rookie, had scoreless starts against the Giants and the Dodgers, but struggled in his next two, against the Nationals and the Cubs outside of the division. Good news: the D-backs are his opponent Tuesday at Coors Field. But throwing quality strikes and staying ahead in counts means more to Chacin's chances of success than division affiliation.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy was bruised up pretty good by an Aaron Rowand comebacker in Kennedy's May 19 start against the San Francisco Giants. But the pain didn't stop him from retiring 13 straight Giants, and it won't stop him from taking the mound against the Colorado Rockies. Kennedy will also do so on something of a roll: The young right-hander has turned in four straight quality starts, most recently limiting the Giants to one run on three hits over eight frames; he struck out a career-high nine. Kennedy will be facing the Rockies for the first time and will have to adjust to the hitter-friendly confines of Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez held the Dodgers to one run and two hits in seven innings of his last start, but wound up on the losing end of a 2-0 final. Jimenez could have prevented the run had he properly fielded a hard smash back to the mound on the play that drove home the winning run. Still, Jimenez has 49 strikeouts against 20 walks while being consistently dominant.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez was "less than his best," according to his manager and himself following his May 20 start against the San Francisco Giants at Chase Field. He allowed six earned runs on 10 hits over five innings, most significantly coughing up a 5-2 lead immediately after he was afforded it. Lopez said his pregame bullpen session portended anything but positive results, and that's just how it shook out. That's not to say confidence has been lost in Arizona's No. 4 starter. Entering his previous start, he had pitched at least seven innings in three consecutive outings and was sporting a 3.81 ERA. Lopez, who made 14 starts for the Rockies in 2007, last faced them in August '09, when, as a member of the Phillies, he allowed two runs in two innings of relief.

home_pitcher_note: You know how baseball is. Numbers measure players and in the final analysis do so accurately. But there's more to them than meets the box score sometimes. Yes, Hammel gave up five runs and six hits in 6 2/3 innings of a loss to the Royals on Friday night. But he had no run support until he left the game, three runs came on two pitches to the same batter (Jose Guillen), and two other runs came after he left. To last that long while pitching through a sore groin -- a situation that has to be watched -- represented a positive for Hammel.
away_pitcher_note: To put it bluntly, Haren hasn't been himself. In his most recent start, kicking off Interleague Play on Friday against the Toronto Blue Jays, the D-backs ace allowed four solo home runs over eight frames. He struck out eight. Haren said afterward he made a concerted effort to mix in a greater portion of four-seam fastballs and pound the inner half of the plate to discourage opposing batters from sitting on his cutter, his best pitch of late. While his results were better against the Jays, Haren is 10 starts into his 2010 season and his ERA is still near five. The All-Star right-hander will look to right his campaign against the Colorado Rockies. Haren last faced the Rockies on April 26: He allowed just two runs (both earned) on five hits over eight innings to record the win.

home_pitcher_note: Cain once again fell victim to the Giants' struggling bats in his last start against Oakland, when he was saddled with the loss despite allowing only one run on five hits in eight solid innings. It was the third straight losing decision for Cain, who regained his command (one walk) after walking 17 batters in his previous four starts combined (27 2/3 innings). Cain is 4-4 with a 3.86 ERA in 14 career starts against the D-backs. In his last start against Arizona on Sept. 22, 2009, Cain was chased after 2 1/3 innings after giving up seven runs on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Saturday evening at Chase Field, Jackson again failed to post back-to-back quality starts. Opposing the Toronto Blue Jays, the D-backs' No. 2 starter yielded five runs on six hits over 7 2/3 frames. A three-run, eighth-inning home run marred an otherwise solid outing. Jackson did strike out nine Jays batters and has whiffed at least seven in each of his last four starts. He has yet to really establish himself as a force in Arizona's rotation, however. Perhaps gearing up for a National League West rival will spur him toward greater success: Against the San Francisco Giants all-time, Jackson is 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in two games.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing against Oakland, Sanchez held the A's to only two runs on three hits. But for the third time this season, Sanchez suffered a loss despite holding opposing bats to no more than three hits or two runs as he and the Giants lost, 3-0. Sanchez cruised until the seventh inning, when he gave up an RBI double to Oakland's Jake Fox and was removed in the eighth after leading off the inning with a walk. Sanchez has lost to Arizona more than any other team throughout his career, six times in 15 career appearances (12 starts). However, Sanchez made two of his final three starts of 2009 against Arizona, winning both while pitching into the sixth inning each time.
away_pitcher_note: Before Sunday's series finale with the Blue Jays, D-backs manager A.J. Hinch said he planned for Buckner to start against the San Francisco Giants. Then, against the Jays, Buckner allowed eight runs (seven earned) on 11 hits; he didn't record an out in Toronto's five-run fifth inning. The 26-year-old right-hander said afterward that he missed his desired location on a few of his pitches, but that the Jays also hit some of his so-called pitcher's pitches. Buckner, who has enlisted the advice of teammate Dan Haren regarding "minimizing the damage," is a safe bet to pitch in San Francisco. In four career appearances (two starts) opposing the Giants, Buckner is 0-1 with a 7.62 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After a 24 scoreless-inning slump by the Giants offense, Wellemeyer received the gift of run support in his last outing. Against Washington on Tuesday, Wellemeyer faced little trouble until the seventh, when he was pulled after giving up three straight singles to open the inning. The Giants bullpen allowed in one run on a sacrifice fly, but that was it as Wellemeyer finished with a final line of two runs on four hits and two strikeouts. Wellemeyer's last start against the D-backs was forgettable, as he gave up five runs on four hits -- three of which were home runs -- in a 13-1 pounding. Wellemeyer holds a 1-4 record and 5.61 ERA in eight career appearances (four starts) against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has been the club's most consistent pitcher this year. In his last outing against the Rockies at Coors Field, Kennedy searched for a pitch that would work for him, but never could find it. Still, he managed to keep his team in the game, allowing just three runs in five innings of work. Two of the runs came via homers from Brad Hawpe and Troy Tulowitzki. Kennedy did not get much offensive support as the D-backs fell, 3-2. He appeared in just one game for the Yankees in 2009 and four in Triple-A after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. The right-hander came in the same three-team trade that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley had to endure defensive and electrical failures at Wrigley Field in his most recent start, but he still came away a winner, the first Dodger to win six games this year. He went 5 1/3 innings and allowed 10 hits, although several of his innings were extended by poor fielding behind him. But he was good enough to run his win streak to four. Billingsley continues to insist his turnaround after a bad finish last year and slow start this season is to simplify his approach and focus on the fastball and curveball that got him to the Major Leagues. He went 4-1 with a 2.61 ERA in May, including a win in Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez faced an uphill battle in his last outing starting opposite Colorado's Ubaldo Jimenez at Coors Field. Lopez allowed a first-inning homer, and just missed escaping a jam in the third when he allowed a two-out, two-run triple to Brad Hawpe. He eventually left the game trailing 4-0 after six and the D-backs went on to lose 7-3. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. He came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.

home_pitcher_note: Now manager Joe Torre is calling John Ely "a God-send." Ely keeps throwing strikes, and even in defeat against the Cubs, he couldn't have been much more impressive, taking a three-hit shutout into the eighth inning at Wrigley Field. All five of the rookie right-hander's five starts have been six innings or longer. He's fun to watch pitch, sometimes compared to Mark "The Bird" Fidrych for his energetic enthusiasm on the mound. He's made a believer out of Torre, who pushed him back a day to give his arm extra rest because he expects him to be starting regularly from here on out. He went 3-1 with a 2.18 ERA in five May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has struggled mightily this year, and that has left him searching for answers. Following his last start when he allowed eight runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Rockies, Haren took stock of his year to date. His conclusion? That his stuff is there, but he is not executing pitches and he is giving up far too many homers. Hitters are still swinging and missing as evidenced by his strikeout total. So far in 74 innings, he has allowed 16 homers. Last time out, the Rockies hit four, including three in a row at one point. It is a trend that he knows he has to reverse if he hopes to start posting more Haren-like numbers.

home_pitcher_note: By default (Charlie Haeger's toe injury), Monasterios gets another start after a respectable five innings (two earned runs) against Colorado at Coors Field on Friday night, good enough for the win when the Dodgers rallied in the top of the sixth inning. Monasterios needed only 67 pitches to get that much done. He's 2-0 with a 2.20 ERA, better results than the club could have hoped for a Rule 5 Draft rookie who had only three appearances above Class A coming into the season. Monasterios has been a starter for most of his Minor League career and said he feels more comfortable in that role because he can use all of his pitches, including a deceptive changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson has pitched better of late after a rough start to the year. The right-hander took the loss in his last start against the Giants at AT&T Park. In that game, he allowed just three runs on four hits over seven innings, but his mound opponent that night, Matt Cain, threw a one-hitter. When Jackson is at his best, he is aggressive early in games with his fastball. If he falls behind in the count, he runs into trouble because hitters are more able to dial up to hit his mid-90s heater. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are his third team in three years. He pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers before last year. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and changeup.

home_pitcher_note: The D-backs have not named a starter for this game. With an off-day Thursday, they could skip the fifth spot in the rotation and start Ian Kennedy on regular rest. If it's not Kennedy, it could be Dontrelle Willis, whom the D-backs acquired on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Cook held the Dodgers to three runs, one earned, in 6 1/3 innings on Saturday night at Coors Field. But that was at Coors. Cook carries an 0-3 record and 7.04 ERA on the road into his start at Chase Field, but believes he's pitching with more control. In his career, he has a 4.18 road ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Willis will be making his D-backs debut. The left-hander was acquired along with cash from the Tigers on Tuesday for right-hander Billy Buckner. Willis appeared in nine games for the Tigers, eight of them starts, and was 1-2 with a 4.98 ERA. Willis, 28, won a job in Detroit's rotation this spring and had quality starts in three of his first four outings. But he struggled in May, going 0-1 with a 6.52 ERA, and the Tigers elected to remove him from the roster to make room for Max Scherzer. Command became a serious issue for Willis in 2008, and he spent much of the season on the disabled list with forearm and knee injuries. He started last season on the DL with what the club called an anxiety disorder.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin racked up six strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings against the Dodgers on Sunday, but his four runs allowed were too much to overcome. Chacin will be facing the D-backs for the second time in two weeks, after beating them on May 25.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez will oppose Jimenez for the second time in three starts. With Thursday's off day, the D-backs are giving Lopez an extra day after he was taxed hard in his last outing against the Dodgers. Lopez went eight innings and threw 115 pitches. He allowed four runs (only two of which were unearned thanks to a pair of errors by second baseman Kelly Johnson). Lopez suffered a 7-3 loss to Jimenez on May 26 at Coors Field. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. He came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: With a four-hit shutout of the Giants on Monday, Jimenez became the fourth pitcher in Rockies history to reach 10 wins before the All-Star break. Shawn Chacon (2003), Aaron Cook (2008) and Jason Marquis (2009) had 11 before the break in their big years and Kevin Ritz won 10 before recess in 1996. But Jimenez needed just two months of the season to do his damage. In the victory over the Giants, Jimenez, who dominated the D-backs with the fastball in his last meeting with them on May 26, threw 79 fastballs, but also 14 curves, 16 sliders and 16 changeup/split-finger pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Haren gave a gutty performance his last time out against the Dodgers when he threw a career-high 126 pitches while holding Los Angeles scoreless for eight innings. The right-hander, though, came away with no decision after Matt Kemp hit a walk-off homer for the Dodgers in the 10th. Prior to the start, Haren had struggled mightily. In his start prior that he allowed eight runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Rockies, So far in 82 innings, he has allowed 16 homers.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe is coming off his best start of the season, an eight-inning, one-run performance against the Phillies on Wednesday, and has won four of his last five starts, including the last three straight. He also struck out a season-high seven in his last start. Lowe was walking batters at nearly the same rate he was striking them out, but he seems to have gotten a handle on that the last two starts. Going into his second-to-last start, a seven-inning, one-run game against the Pirates on May 28, Lowe had 33 strikeouts and 28 walks. He's struck out nine and walked two since.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson enters his 13th start of 2010 coming off his best outing thus far. Last Wednesday, the D-backs' No. 2 starter shut out the Dodgers for nine innings. He allowed just three hits and struck out six but didn't factor into the decision. After a rough start with his new club, the right-hander is 2-1 with a 2.27 ERA over his last four starts. Seeking continued success, Jackson makes his first start against the Braves. In two career relief appearances versus Atlanta, he yielded one run over three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen moved into the rotation from the bullpen when Jair Jurrjens went down at the end of April, but he's making a case to stay. He said he had all his pitches working the best they have all season in his last start, a career-high 7 1/3 innings at Dodger Stadium. Medlen allowed three runs, two earned, struck out four and walked none in the 4-3 win, his second straight victory. Medlen pitched well in his only career start against the D-backs in 2009, allowing four hits and one run in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has notched quality starts in six of his past seven starts, but the latest effort wasn't exactly "quality." On Friday against the Colorado Rockies, the D-backs' No. 3 starter yielded six runs on five hits over six frames. While he wasn't helped by a teammate's crucial fielding error -- hence the three unearned runs -- Kennedy did allow three Rockies home runs, the last of which put Arizona in a 6-3 hole. Kennedy admitted after the game that he missed location with his fastball at times. Because his changeup is such an integral part of his repertoire, command of the fastball is a significant indicator of Kennedy's success. He will have the opportunity to get back on track against the Atlanta Braves. In his lone career start against Atlanta on May 14, Kennedy allowed three runs (all earned) on seven hits over 6 1/3 frames; he struck out five but didn't factor into his team's decision.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami became the first Braves pitcher in 85 years to lost his first eight decisions out of the gate in his last start, against the Dodgers.
