But Kawakami has gone at least six innings in his last four starts, all of which which were quality starts except for the last, when he let up five runs in 6 1/3 innings. His strikeout rate is low, at about 4.5 batters per nine innings, but he has struck out twice as many (36) as he has walked (18). The D-backs roughed Kawakami up on May 14, knocking him out after 4 1/3 innings and three runs allowed. Oddly enough, he struck out a season-high seven in that game.

home_pitcher_note: In his D-backs debut Saturday, opposing the Colorado Rockies, Willis pitched into and out of trouble for six innings. What really matters: He held the potent Rockies lineup scoreless. The lefty's final line: five hits, four walks and three strikeouts. Despite the win and the ovation he received from the faithful at Chase Field, Willis appears to still have issues with his command. Forty-six of his 106 pitches landed outside of the strike zone, and his increased pitch count forced his exit. Manager A.J. Hinch said that while Willis can be "effectively wild," he had far too many three-ball counts. Willis will make start No. 2 in a D-backs uniform against the Atlanta Braves. Given his days in the National League East as a Florida Marlin, he is 6-5 with a 4.92 ERA in 18 career starts versus the Braves
away_pitcher_note: Hanson bought 40 tickets for friends and family Saturday in Los Angeles, and there were plenty more people than that in the stands when he took the mound close to home, and he didn't disappoint. Hanson tossed his third straight win and third straight quality start in a game that was, until the seventh inning, a pitcher's duel. He went six innings, allowed two runs and struck out six. Hanson hasn't lost since the D-backs beat him on May 15, when he let up five runs on seven hits in seven innings. He also struck out a season-high 10 in that game. Hanson's been much better on the road, posting a 2.19 ERA in six starts compared to a 5.40 mark in as many starts at Turner Field.

home_pitcher_note: Sunday against Ubaldo Jimenez and the Rockies, Lopez allowed three runs on nine hits over seven innings; he struck out six in defeat. If nothing else, the veteran right-hander has kept his team in ballgames. He posted his second consecutive quality start on Sunday. Part of the reason he hasn't won since May 15 is simply competition: Lopez has had to face with some of the game's best hurlers, including Jimenez, Tim Lincecum, Tommy Hanson and others. His likely Cardinals counterpart, Jaime Garcia, is no slouch either, so Lopez will have to be extra fine with his pitches to stay in contention. The veteran right-hander is 2-1 with a 5.25 ERA in four career starts versus St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia was solid yet again on Sunday when he limited the Brewers to just two earned runs over six innings. He did allow eight hits and two walks but was able to keep his composure and pitched out of a few jams. Friday will mark Garcia's first career start against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Haren wasn't quite as good Monday as he was in his previous start, when he shut out the Dodgers for eight innings, but he wasn't half-bad either. The D-backs' ace allowed three runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings, finishing his outing one out short of Arizona's eighth straight quality start. In his next start, Haren will be seeking his first second-straight win since proving victorious on April 20 and 26. Saturday, he faces the St. Louis Cardinals, which drafted him in the second round of the 2001 First-Year Player Draft. In three career starts against his former club, Haren is 3-0 with a 4.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ottavino was effective against the Brewers on Saturday, allowing two runs on five hits over five innings but was stuck with a no-decision in just his second carer big league start. It marked an improvement over his first start, however, as he allowed four runs and six walks over 5 2/3 innings against the Cubs in his debut on May 29. The rookie right-hander has never faced the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: One start after dominating the Dodgers (nine shutout innings), Jackson was only so-so Tuesday night against the Braves. While he did keep the D-backs in the game, Arizona's No. 2 starter allowed four runs on nine hits over six innings. A sign of Jackson's endurance: He had pitched at least seven innings in four straight starts prior to Tuesday. The right-hander is also doing a better job of keeping the ball in the park: He hasn't allowed a home run in three consecutive outings after yielding seven June dingers. Jackson faces St. Louis next; he allowed four runs on seven hits over eight innings in an April 21 no-decision opposing the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter was in a groove against the Dodgers on Monday when he tossed seven scoreless innings but was stuck with a no-decision as the Cardinals were shut out for the sixth time this season. Carpenter, though, said his cutter is starting to come around and is feeling better than he did earlier in the season, and the stats certainly prove it as he is 2-0 with a 0.83 ERA dating back to May 28. He is 4-0 with a 2.09 ERA in nine career appearances (eight starts) against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: The righty continues to make a push toward a possible All-Star appearance. Even on nights when Buchholz doesn't have his best stuff, he gives the Red Sox a chance to win. Take, for example, his last start, when he gave up three earned runs over seven innings, despite walking four and only striking out one. He took the loss in that one, being outpitched by former teammate Justin Masterson. Buchholz has given up three earned runs or less in his last six starts. He has pitched six times at Fenway this season, going 3-3 with a 3.38 ERA. This will be Buchholz's first career appearance against the D-backs. Opponents are hitting .233 against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: Wednesday against the Braves, Kennedy threw a career-high seven shutout innings, but didn't factor in the game's decision. The D-backs' No. 3 starter allowed just three hits and struck out six, but walked a career-high five. "I'm just glad they didn't come back to bite me," Kennedy said of the free passes, "because five walks is a lot." Kennedy has collected quality starts in each of his previous three outings. The young right-hander hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in a game since April 29. Next on Kennedy's agenda is the Red Sox. Despite his brief Major League stint with the New York Yankees, Kennedy has never opposed the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty had a rare letdown in his last start, as he was unable to hold a 5-0 lead against the Indians. Lester took a no-decision in that one, a game the Red Sox lost in the bottom of the ninth. Hurt by his share of seeing-eye hits, Lester gave up nine hits and six runs over six innings, walking one and striking out eight. Before that, he had allowed two earned runs or less in eight of his last nine starts. In seven Fenway starts this season, Lester is 4-1 with a 3.02 ERA. Opponents are hitting .209 against him. This will be Lester's first career appearance against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Manager A.J. Hinch elected to skip Dontrelle Willis' slot in the rotation at least in part to keep Lopez on his normal rest. On Friday against the St. Louis Cardinals, Lopez yielded five runs on six hits over seven innings. He had retired 16 straight Cardinal batters before allowing Brendan Ryan's three-run home run in the seventh, his final inning. Lopez is now 0-3 over his past five starts, and he hasn't won since May 15. Given his five seasons as a Baltimore Oriole, Lopez has pitched against the Red Sox 26 times (20 starts), compiling a 10-9 record with a 4.53 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The big righty has pitched better his last few starts and is coming off his best outing in a while. In a 12-2 win over the Phillies, Lackey gave up six hits and two runs, walking none and striking out three. He is 3-0 over his past four starts. In seven Fenway starts, Lackey is 5-1 with a 5.10 ERA. Opponents are hitting .291 against him. Lackey has made just one career start against the D-backs, giving up just one unearned run over seven innings in a no-decision. He is a career 18-11 pitcher in June with a 3.38 ERA, his best in any month.
away_pitcher_note: Saturday against his original Major League team, the St. Louis Cardinals, Haren was mostly spot-on. He allowed just two runs on six hits and struck out nine over eight innings. He has pitched eight or more innings in five of his 14 2010 starts. The right-hander won consecutive starts for the first time since April 20 and 26. While he continues to lower his uncharacteristically high ERA (4.61), Haren has also improved his strike-throwing; he's walked a total of two batters in his past five outings. In six career starts against Boston, Haren is 2-3 with a 2.65 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga has recorded two straight no-decisions since his near-perfect game on June 2 against the Indians. But he's been good enough to earn wins in both starts. He allowed only two earned runs in each game and walked a combined three batters. However, he only recorded two strikeouts, total. This is credit to his ability to find the bottom of the strike zone and induce opposing hitters to uncomfortable flyball and groundball swings.
away_pitcher_note: Willis is making his third start for the D-backs after being acquired June 1 in exchange for Minor League right-hander Billy Buckner. Willis had been designated for assignment by the Tigers after going 1-2 with a 4.98 ERA in eight starts and one relief appearance. Control continues to be an issue for the left-hander. In 10 innings with Arizona, he has allowed just two runs on eight hits, but he has walked 10 and fanned five. The high pitch counts have forced his exit early in games. Willis' last outing was June 10 against the Braves, when he allowed a pair of runs on three hits and six walks over four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello is best known for his sinker. But of late, he hasn't had good command of the pitch and it has been running up in the strike zone, instead of staying down. In Porcello's last start against the White Sox on June 9, he surrendered eight runs in 3 1/3 innings. Because the Tigers had an off day on Monday, manager Jim Leyland opted to skip Porcello to give him extra time to try to regain command of his go-to pitch. "If he gets the sinker back the way we want it to be on a consistent basis, then we think everything else will fall into place as well," Leyland said.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson will face off against his former team after being dealt to the D-backs during the Winter Meetings in a three-team trade that also included the Yankees. The right-hander got a no-decision in his last start against the Cardinals at Chase Field, but certainly deserved a better fate. He scattered eight hits and allowed just a pair of runs over 6 2/3 innings. He also got a no-decision in his start prior to that against the Braves at Chase Field when he allowed four runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: To say Scherzer's last start was a battle would be an understatement. Scherzer struggled from the get-go on Tuesday against the Nationals. He found himself falling behind in counts and threw 81 pitches through four innings. Scherzer admitted he didn't have good command early in the game, but after allowing three earned runs through the first four innings, he settled in as it progressed and made it through the sixth inning to earn his first win since striking out 14 batters in 5 2/3 innings on May 30 against Oakland. He still showed his ability to fan batters on Tuesday, striking nine Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy will face off against Max Scherzer. The pair were part of the three-team trade that also sent Edwin Jackson to the D-backs. The right-hander has been the club's most consistent starter this season. Last time out against the Red Sox at Fenway Park, though, he did not have his best stuff and Boston wound up hitting him for six runs on nine hits over six innings. In his start prior to that, he allowed just three hits in seven shutout innings against the Braves, but came away with a no-decision in Arizona's 2-1 win.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez would like to have two pitches back from his last start against the Red Sox. On both occasions he shook off catcher Chris Snyder's sign and each resulted in a ball leaving Fenway Park. The Red Sox managed four runs on those two hits alone as they went on to a 6-2 win. Lopez allowed all six of the runs on 10 hits while lasting seven innings. In his start prior to that, he allowed five runs over seven innings against the Cardinals. Three of the runs came in his final inning of work when he allowed a homer to Brendan Ryan.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett suffered his third consecutive loss in an ugly outing against the Phillies on Wednesday. He didn't survive the fourth inning for the first time this season, surrendering six runs on six hits with four walks. That included back-to-back home runs served up to Ryan Howard and Jayson Werth. Burnett has an even 9.00 ERA over those three losing starts. He is 3-2 with a 3.67 ERA in five career starts against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: After a so-so April (4.50 ERA) and a miserable May (6.08 ERA), Haren appears to finally be himself in June. In four starts this month, the D-backs ace is 2-1 with a 2.96 ERA and a 25-to-5 strikeout-to-walk ratio. After facing the Boston Red Sox on Thursday (six runs, four earned, allowed on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings), the veteran right-hander will face another American League East bully, the Yankees. In seven career starts against New York, Haren is 4-0 with a 3.77 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte lost for just the second time this season on Thursday against Philadelphia, allowing three runs (two earned) on six hits in seven innings. It was the 11th time this year the lefty surrendered two earned runs or fewer -- tops in the AL. Pettitte's big mistake was a 2-2 cutter that Shane Victorino snuck inside the foul pole for a two-run fifth-inning homer. He is 2-5 with a 4.24 ERA against the D-backs in his career. The last time he started in Chase Field in a Yankees' uniform, he gave up six runs in two innings in losing Game 6 of the 2001 World Series.

home_pitcher_note: After his fifth slot in the rotation was skipped in Boston, in part because of a busted finger nail on his left hand, Willis pitched on Friday in Detroit. Against his former Tigers teammates, Willis allowed five runs, all earned, on five hits over five innings. In three starts since joining Arizona, the veteran left-hander is 1-0 with a 4.20 ERA but, more glaringly, has walked 14 batters in 15 innings. Willis will attempt to regain his control on the mound on Wednesday against one of the most patient clubs in the Majors. In one career eight-inning start against the New York Yankees, Willis is 0-1 with a 2.25 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez was a tough-luck loser on Friday against the Mets, the victim of the Yankees' being shut out at home for the first time in exactly one year. The right-hander yielded only one run on three hits in seven innings, striking out four while falling -- however undeservedly -- to 6-6 on the season. He will return to Arizona, where he went 11-15 in 2005 for the D-backs. He is 5-3 against his former team with a 3.74 ERA in 14 starts, and he is 6-8 with a 4.06 ERA in 21 career starts at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann bounced back from his first loss of the season nicely on Saturday, when he gave up two runs in six innings while facing the Marlins for the second consecutive time. Niemann really only made two mistakes -- the solo home runs he gave up to Hanley Ramirez and Chris Coghlan. Other than that, only two runners reached base, as the 6-foot-9 right-hander gave up three hits and one walk while striking out seven and throwing 89 pitches (54 for strikes). Niemann, making his first career start against the D-backs, now has a quality start in 11 of his 14 outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson continues to be a workhorse for the D-backs. On Saturday against his former team, the Detroit Tigers, Jackson allowed three earned runs on nine hits over 7 2/3 innings. He has pitched six innings or more in nine straight starts. Next, the right-hander faces another former team in the Rays. Jackson, who pitched for Tampa Bay from 2006-08, won in his lone career start against the Rays, an eight-inning performance in which he allowed three earned runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Price was the victim of a couple of mistake pitches and some defensive miscues in a loss to the Marlins on Sunday. Facing off against Marlins ace Josh Johnson, Price gave up four runs (three earned) on six hits while walking two and striking out nine. The Marlins took a 2-1 lead on him in the fifth, when B.J. Upton dropped a line drive and Ben Zobrist took a bad route on an eventual triple. In the sixth, Florida got two more when Sean Rodriguez lost a fly ball and Wes Helms hit a two-run homer. Price, who had a streak of three straight wins snapped, will be facing the D-backs for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: There's a reason that Kennedy is often said to be untouchable when it comes to trade discussions. He's pitched that well. On Sunday against the Detroit Tigers, the young right-hander allowed three runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings. Unfortunately for the D-backs, who had afforded their starter just one run of support, Kennedy yielded all three on two dingers in the seventh. Still, he has notched quality starts in four of his past five outings. Next up -- the Rays. In four career starts against Tampa Bay, Kennedy is 1-2 with a 6.64 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Aside from a seven-inning, three-run performance against Toronto on June 10, this has been a rough month for Davis -- and even the nice outing he had in that game was a loss. Following a 4 1/3-inning, 103-pitch game against the Padres at home, Davis has now lost all four of his starts this month. He will look to get back on track Sunday against the D-backs in his 15th start of the season. After throwing six innings or more in three of his first five starts, the right-hander has done so just three times in his last nine, and he attributes most of his struggles to lack of fastball command. He and manager Joe Maddon continually stress the important of commanding the heater, and Davis has failed to do so as of late, especially in his last start when he threw 58 of his 103 pitches for strikes and recorded five walks to just one strikeout. Sunday will be the first time he has faced Arizona in his young career.
away_pitcher_note: On Monday against the New York Yankees, Lopez allowed three runs on eight hits over eight innings, collecting his first win in seven starts. The veteran right-hander deftly avoided the long ball; he had allowed home runs in six straight outings prior to Monday. He is 3-0 this season when he keeps the ball inside the ballpark. Next on his agenda is a road start in Tampa Bay. In 20 career games -- 15 of which were starts -- opposing the Rays, Lopez is 11-6 with a 4.29 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter was again brilliant against the team that drafted him and developed him, the Toronto Blue Jays, when he faced them for the second time in his career on June 23. Carpenter who pitched a one-hit shutout against the Blue Jays at his first homecoming on June 14, 2005, earned a 1-0 victory with an eight-inning three-hitter. Carpenter had some trouble with his curveball early against Toronto, but survived admirably until the pitch came around for him. His only loss this year was to the Houston Astros on May 13. His two starts against Arizona this season were no-decisions, and he has a 4.15 ERA in those starts. He is 4-0 with a 2.36 ERA in his career against Arizona, which includes nine starts and one relief outing.
away_pitcher_note: Tuesday against the Yankees, Haren allowed three runs on six hits over seven innings. Despite pitching well, he suffered his second straight defeat. The D-backs' No. 1 pitcher continues to be a strike-thrower: In five June starts, he's whiffed 33 and walked six. Next, Haren will face St. Louis, his original team, for the third time this season. He is 2-0 versus the Cardinals this season despite the fact that he's allowed nine earned runs in 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright lasted four innings in taking the loss to the Jays on June 24. He had gone 51 starts in which he had lasted at least five innings. His shortest start before the one at Rogers Centre was also four innings -- Sept. 13, 2008, at Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Willis doesn't seem to be improving in a D-backs uniform; he seems to be declining. Wednesday against the Yankees, Willis lasted 2 1/3 innings. He threw 66 pitches; just 27 were strikes. He exited the game having allowed two runs on one hit and seven free passes.

home_pitcher_note: Little by little, Suppan gets closer to what the Cardinals are expecting. St. Louis is not asking the veteran right-hander to be a world-beater, just an innings-eater. In three games as a Cardinal, Suppan has done a decent job of keeping the ball on the ground.
away_pitcher_note: Enright will have his contracted selected from Double-A Mobile to make the start. A second-round pick in 2007, the right-hander was 4-1 with a 2.88 ERA in 14 starts for Mobile this season. Enright is known for having pinpoint command.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson tossed a no-hitter in his last start against the Rays on Friday. While he did not allow any hits, Jackson did walk eight and hit a batter so the effort took him 149 pitches. With that in mind, the D-backs are giving him two extra days rest before this start.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda was a little too fired up facing the Yankees, walking the first two batters and allowing a first-inning homer. He settled after that and the Dodgers rallied for a win that wasn't his most impressive. He was nailed by a line drive last year in Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez has been pretty consistent all season. His ERA continues its dip after stellar starts against American League East giants, New York and Tampa Bay. Most recently, the veteran right-hander allowed just one earned run in a six-inning win over the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw pitched well enough against the Yankees to win, and would have if Jonathan Broxton had not blown a four-run lead in the ninth inning. It was Kershaw's first start without a walk. He's fourth in the league in strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: While his ERA remains uncharacteristically high, Haren hasn't allowed more than four earned runs in six straight starts. In his previous outing against the Dodgers, on June 1 in Los Angeles, the righty threw eight scoreless innings but received a tough-luck no-decision.

Kennedy will be pitching on a ton of extra rest. The young right-hander last started on June 26 against Tampa Bay. Kennedy, who hasn't had many speed bumps this season, walked a career-high nine and used his extra time in between starts to iron out his mechanics.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since May 26, Gorzelanny threw 77 pitches over five scoreless innings vs. the Pirates. The lefty, who has taken over Carlos Zambrano's spot, faced the D-backs May 2 and picked up the win.

home_pitcher_note: Enright will make his second career start and, if it's a good one, will be the D-backs's No. 5 starter for the foreseeable future. On June 30 in St. Louis, the right-hander allowed one run in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Silva notched his 12th quality start in his last outing vs. the Reds with a season-high 7 2/3 innings. He hasn't won since May 29 because of a lack of runs. Silva has a 2.90 ERA in nine starts at Wrigley.

home_pitcher_note: Friday against the Dodgers, Jackson didn't have the best follow-up to his June 25 no-hitter, but he still ended up with the win. In five innings against Los Angeles, he allowed four earned runs. He said afterward that he was battling his mechanics on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Technically, Dempster had a quality start in his last outing, but it was ugly. He was charged with five runs, but only two were earned vs. the Reds. He struck out nine, matching a season high.

home_pitcher_note: Don't judge Lopez's solid 2010 campaign by his most recent start. Saturday against the Los Angeles Dodgers, the veteran allowed nine runs, but just two of them were earned. The D-backs infield committed five errors behind him (and a sixth after he left).
away_pitcher_note: Consistently, Sanchez has been able to give his team at least six innings an outing. He has reached that mark in four straight starts. The team, however, is 2-3 in those outings. That's despite four straight quality starts. The team is 8-8 in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sunday against the Dodgers, Haren allowed just one run on six hits over seven innings but didn't factor into the decision. Eighty-two of his 117 pitches were strikes. He has spun three straight quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Home runs have been problematic. In 17 starts, Nolasco has yielded 20. Consider a year ago, he yielded 23 in 31 starts. In fact, In 103 2/3 innings, Nolasco has surrendered more homers than walks (19). Still, he has won three straight, striking out 11 at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday against the Cubs, Kennedy allowed a season-high seven runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings; he struck out six. The D-backs' No. 3 starter yielded four-plus runs in back-to-back outings for the first time all year. Throwing quality strikes is his panacea.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran makes his final start before the All-Star Break. With 89 1/3 innings, he's already well surpassed his innings (49 2/3) in an injury-plagued 2009. He's gone exactly six innings in three of his past four starts and is 2-1 in those games (the team is 3-1).

home_pitcher_note: Enright will be making his third big league start after being called up from Double-A Mobile. In his last start against the Cubs, he cruised through five innings before allowing three runs and being knocked out in the sixth. Enright is known for having pinpoint control.
away_pitcher_note: Nothing is official, but the team is leaning toward giving the 21-year-old right-hander his first big league start. He has appeared in three games as a reliever since being promoted from Double-A Jacksonville, where he was 5-1 with a 2.03 ERA in 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garland was bitten by the long ball in a loss to Washington on July 7, as four of his six earned runs were a result of a season-high three home runs allowed. Garland made two starts against Arizona in April and gave up nine runs in nine innings, but only two were earned.
away_pitcher_note: Haren opens the D-backs' second half. The veteran right-hander is winless over his last five starts despite his 3.10 ERA over that span. He scattered 10 Marlins hits in his last outing and pitched into the seventh inning for the fourth straight game.

home_pitcher_note: Richard has scuffled in his past two starts, allowing a combined 11 runs on 15 hits. His walks (seven over those two starts) have crept back up, meaning his fastball command isn't what it was when his ERA was 2.74 on June 30.
away_pitcher_note: One start after he was flabbergasted by his defense's franchise-worst six errors, Lopez received 10 runs of support in seven frames on July 8 against Florida. One fantasy stat he won't provide: Ks. He whiffed three batters or less in five straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Correia had an interesting outing in his last start against the Rockies. He allowed five runs in five innings, but had a season-high eight strikeouts with one walk. Where Correia got in trouble was when he elevated a few pitches as he allowed two home runs.
away_pitcher_note: After three wins in three straight starts against his former clubs, Jackson didn't fare as well against Chicago on July 7. The righty yielded five runs over five frames and walked four. He has issued three-plus free passes in seven of his last eight outings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy was arguably the team's best starter in the first half, though he struggled near the end. Recently, he's gotten some extra days off as they try to limit his innings total. He picked up the win in his last start when he allowed two runs over 5 1/3 frames vs. Florida.
away_pitcher_note: After a tremendous start to the season, Pelfrey has failed to complete five innings in each of his past three starts and failed to log a quality start in four of his last five.

home_pitcher_note: Enright will be making his fourth start since being called up June 30. He started the final game before the break and suffered the loss despite allowing just two runs over five innings. Not overpowering, but he has good control. He has walked two in his past 10 2/3 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Earning the first start for the Mets out of the break, Dickey was again brilliant, pitching seven innings of one-run ball. The only problem? Tim Lincecum of the Giants was better, meaning Dickey must seek his seventh win once again, this time against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Haren opened the season's second half on Friday in San Diego. He allowed six Padres runs over five innings and is winless over his last six games. The veteran right-hander had twirled consecutive quality starts to begin the month of July after his sharp June (2-2, 3.19 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the second half, Niese was again strong, limiting the Giants to one run over seven innings. But Barry Zito was even better, preventing him from recording his seventh victory. Niese will now look to do so against a D-Backs team he has never faced.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez's issue with the long ball continued on Saturday against the Padres. The crafty righty yielded four in his six-inning start at pitcher-friendly PETCO Park and has allowed 23 total dingers in 19 outings this season. He is 1-2 with a 5.94 ERA in three July starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cain also began the second half on a high note, making only one mistake -- allowing a two-run homer -- in seven stellar innings against the Mets. The win broke a five-start winless drought for Cain who, in his last start against the D-backs, threw a one-hit shutout.

home_pitcher_note: Sunday in San Diego, Jackson allowed four runs on nine hits over 6 1/3 innings. He has allowed at least four earned runs in three straight starts. Walks are a part of the problem: Jackson has issued three-plus free passes in four straight outings.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez was part of an epic pitching duel against the Mets' Johan Santana in his last outing, taking the no-decision. Sanchez allowed two runs, coming on a ground-rule double and solo homer, and only four other hits in seven innings, striking out five and walking one.

home_pitcher_note: Ian Kennedy was solid, not special, on Monday against the Mets, allowing one run on four hits over five innings. He picked up back-to-back wins for the second time this season. The club is continuing to monitor his second-half workload, hence his 86 pitches against New York.
away_pitcher_note: In Bumgarner's last outing, the rookie left-hander earned his third win and first against the archrival Dodgers. He allowed two runs -- one earned -- on six hits in 5 2/3 innings, being removed after tiring in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: In his fourth career start Tuesday vs. the Mets, Enright was at his best. The right-hander twirled a career-high eight innings, retiring 14 in a row at one point, and held the Mets to one run (a solo dinger) on five hits. He also struck out a career-high eight.
away_pitcher_note: After two outstanding outings, Lincecum took a step back in his last start, giving up five runs in 4 2/3 innings against the Dodgers. Lincecum struggled in his last outing against Arizona on May 20, giving up five runs on five hits in only five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels looks like the pitcher that dominated the NL in 2008. He allowed just one hit and one walk in eight scoreless innings Thursday against the Cardinals at Busch Stadium. He dominated a tough lineup in brutal heat, and has shown signs of breaking through.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez assumes the slot of Dan Haren, who was traded. On Thursday vs. the Giants, Lopez suffered his second straight defeat, yielding three earned runs on five hits, including another homer, over seven innings. He said he needs to improve upon controlling the running game.

home_pitcher_note: Doc finally got some run support Friday and shut down Colorado for his 11th win. A five-run fifth gave him a cushion, only the fourth time in his past 14 starts he's received more than three runs of support. Halladay hasn't faced Arizona since '04.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson pitched well enough to win on Friday against the Giants. He just didn't field his position: two throwing errors toward first base led to three runs. He also yielded two Aubrey Huff solo shots and has allowed five home runs over his past three starts, all losses.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick proved to some that it was a mistake to demote him following his poor start in St. Louis. His inconsistency is still troubling: he's gone 6-plus innings and allowed two or fewer runs eight times; in his 11 other starts, he has an 8.73 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is expected to join the D-backs on Tuesday and will make his Arizona debut against the Phillies two days later. The lefty is coming off a strong start on Friday. He allowed one Rangers run on seven hits over seven innings and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: After struggling through a four-game span when he allowed 50 baserunners and recorded only 44 outs, Pelfrey pitched five solid innings on Saturday at Dodger Stadium, giving up two runs on six hits and two walks, one intentional.
away_pitcher_note: Saturday against the Giants, Kennedy yielded four runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings and picked up the loss, thanks to a lack of run support. The young righty pitched into the seventh for the first time in five outings.

home_pitcher_note: The Mets used their Monday off-day to skip Takahashi's spot in the rotation, giving the lefty some rest. Takahashi has allowed six runs in three of his last five starts and is the leading candidate to move to the 'pen if the Mets acquire a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Enright has been nothing if not consistent since his June 30 call-up. The rookie righty has allowed three earned runs or fewer and gone at least five innings in each of his first five Major League starts, earning himself stability in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Niese has allowed three runs or fewer in each of his last six starts dating back to June 27 and has helped solidify the back end of the rotation along with R.A. Dickey.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson was acquired by the D-backs on Friday from the White Sox in a deal that sent Edwin Jackson to Chicago. The 23-year-old started 2009 in Class A, but rocketed all the way to the big leagues. His fastball and changeup are his best pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez took the loss in his last outing when he allowed four runs on seven hits in five innings against the Phillies on July 27. Lopez issued an uncharacteristic five walks in that game. Lopez was a non-roster invite to Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching a complete-game win, Hernandez had a rough outing last Wednesday vs. the Braves. In the 3-1 loss, the righty allowed three runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings. Hernandez is 10-7 with a 3.74 ERA in 20 career starts against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders was acquired from the Angels in the deal that included Dan Haren. Saunders' first outing for the D-backs was a good one as he allowed just two runs and did not walk a batter while fanning four in seven innings against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen looks to continue his success after one of his best outings of the year. The lefty allowed three runs on five hits in six frames in Washington's 5-3 win vs. the Braves. In four career starts against the D-backs, Olsen is 0-2 with an 8.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy did not have his best stuff his last time out, but battled his way through six innings against the Mets to earn the win. He allowed three hits and walked four while allowing five runs in six innings. He's won three of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen is coming off arguably his best start of the season. In the Nats' 8-1 win against the Phillies, he outdueled newly acquired Roy Oswalt.  Stammen allowed only one run on five hits in 6 1/3 innings. He has never faced Arizona in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Enright said he had to grind his way through his last start, but allowed just two runs over six innings against the Mets at Citi Field. Enright was promoted from Double-A Mobile June 30. In five starts he has yet to allow more than three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler will make his third Major League start of 2010 against Arizona. He has allowed one run in nine innings this season. He's still seeking his breakout MLB moment after achieving consistent success at the Minor League level.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson held the Mets to one run on three hits over eight innings in his D-backs debut on Sunday. He said the key to his success was command of his fastball; the rookie right-hander won't blow batters away, so he needs to spot it.
away_pitcher_note: Garland out-pitched Josh Johnson on Sunday, allowing three earned runs on five hits in six innings to earn his 10th victory. He last faced the D-backs on July 16, giving up three hits and one run over six innings in a win.

home_pitcher_note: The long ball continues to haunt Lopez. He allowed two more solo shots on Monday and has allowed one or more dingers in six straight starts. Lopez said he is aware of the unseemly total but is wary of becoming a nibbler.
away_pitcher_note: Richard picked up his ninth victory in his last start but yielded a season-high 11 hits and allowed 14 baserunners over 5 1/3 innings. The offense picked him up, as Chase Headley and Will Venable each had three-run home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has been outstanding since the D-backs acquired him from the Angels in a deal that sent Dan Haren packing. In two starts for Arizona, Saunders has allowed three runs in 16 innings. He tossed a complete game last time out vs. the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Latos failed in his bid for victory No. 11 against the Dodgers in his last start, allowing two runs on four hits over six innings. He struck out six, but two walks in the second inning led to the two runs he allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson has been so-so on the mound this season but he's been excellent at the plate, including his start at Wrigley Field on Tuesday in which Narveson's RBI single loomed large in a 4-3 win. He's batting .313 on the year with four RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has not been sharp in his last three starts, going 1-2 with a 7.02 ERA over that span. In his last start against the Nationals, Kennedy allowed four runs on eight hits in just four innings as the club continues to try to limit his innings.

home_pitcher_note: Through five innings on Wednesday, he outdueled Ryan Dempster, but a big sixth inning did Parra in as he gave up five runs in the frame and six overall in the Brewers' 15-3 loss. Parra is 1-0 with a 0.86 ERA in three career starts against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Enright has pitched very well since being called up from Triple-A Reno. In six starts, he has yet to allow more than three runs in a game or last less than five innings. Last time out he beat the Nats, allowing two runs on six hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bush missed the Brewers' series in Arizona earlier this season, but he's 5-1 lifetime against the D-backs with a 3.65 ERA in seven starts. He has 6.5 strikeouts for every walk against Arizona hitters, by far his best ratio against National League teams.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has impressed. In two outings since being acquired July 30, he has allowed two runs on six hits in 15 2/3 innings against the Mets and, more recently, the Padres on Friday. Only concern: He's a flyball pitcher about to pitch at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf cites a quicker rhythm for his improvement since a blow-up game at Pittsburgh on July 21, in which he surrendered 12 runs on 13 hits. In three starts since, he has a 2.29 ERA and 13 strikeouts versus only two walks.
away_pitcher_note: The good news first: Saturday against San Diego, Lopez didn't yield a home run for the first time in seven starts. Now the bad news: Thanks to another bullpen blown save, he picked up another no-decision and hasn't won in five outings.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan was impressive in his first win since being sent down to Double-A Harrisburg on June 21. In the Nationals' 6-3 victory against the Dodgers on Friday, he gave up three runs -- two earned -- on five hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: After two stellar outings to begin his Arizona career, Saunders back-pedaled Sunday. The lefty yielded six Padres runs (five earned) on eight hits in six frames. In his second start as a D-back on Aug. 3, he held the Nats to one run in nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis' struggles continued in his last start during an 8-3 loss to the Dodgers. The righty allowed five runs (two earned) on five hits in four innings. Marquis is 2-6 with a 4.12 ERA in 11 career starts against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling early due to grip issues caused by the heat and humidity, Kennedy settled down Monday against the Brewers, going six innings and keeping the D-backs close enough for a late rally. He took the loss on Aug. 4 against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg looks to rebound after the worst start of his career, an 8-2 loss to the Marlins on Tuesday.  Strasburg gave up six runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings for his first loss since June 28. He has never faced the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: In his eighth career start, Enright extended his string of starts with five innings or more and three or fewer runs allowed. He has reached that mark in each of his first eight Major League starts and is one of two active players to do so.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching seven strong innings, Hudson allowed just two runs on seven hits while walking one to go with a career-high nine strikeouts on Tuesday. It was his third straight start of seven or more innings since he joined the D-backs on July 30.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo's loss on Wednesday to St. Louis was only the third time in his last 13 starts that he didn't get at least six innings. After having Colby Rasmus down 0-2, his 3-2 sinker was launched for a fifth-inning grand slam with two outs.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching in 87-degree heat and 55 percent humidity, Lopez was affected by the elements on Thursday and struggled early, giving up six runs on six hits in the first two innings. He lasted just five innings, giving up seven runs on seven hits.
away_pitcher_note: Over his last three starts, totaling 17 2/3 innings, Volquez is 2-0 with a 1.53 ERA. "Every time I pitch, I get into a better rhythm and good tempo in the game," said Volquez, who is six big league starts into his return from Tommy John surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders' past two starts haven't been as impressive as his first two with the D-backs, but he has kept his new team in the games. He allowed four earned runs in six innings against the Nationals his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: This will be his ninth start this season and first since a win on Aug. 8 vs. the Cubs in Chicago. On July 10 in Philadelphia -- Wood's third big league start -- he had a perfect game going into the ninth that was broken up by a Carlos Ruiz double.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy appeared to be back on track after his Saturday start in Washington. He yielded just two runs in seven innings and struck out seven. It was his first quality outing in nine tries. He's faced Colorado twice already this season and is 0-1.
away_pitcher_note: In both starts filling in for the injured Aaron Cook, Rogers has given the Rockies a good opportunity to win. He's 1-0 with a no-decision, combining for seven earned runs in 11 2/3 innings during the stint.

home_pitcher_note: Mr. Consistent has yielded three runs or fewer and gone at least five innings in each of his first nine MLB starts, though he has just three wins to show for it. The rookie right-hander will be making his debut against a loaded Rockies lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez was, again, denied his franchise- and big league-best 18th win of the year when Clint Barmes missed a popup and Huston Street blew a save in the ninth on Sunday. He struck out 10, his second-highest strikeout total of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson deserved his fourth straight win Tuesday against the Reds, but he didn't get it. He held the NL's top offense to three runs in seven innings and struck out a career-high 10 but picked up his first loss in an Arizona uniform.
away_pitcher_note: Called up from Triple-A Tuesday to face the Dodgers, Chacin was sharp for three innings, struggled to get out of the fourth and ultimately allowed five runs. He is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA in three appearances against Arizona this season.

home_pitcher_note: Richard has won his last two starts, including a gem at Wrigley Field on Aug. 18 when he one run on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings. Richard got a lot of flyouts and typically fares better when he's getting ground balls. Still, it's an encouraging sign.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez is winless in his past seven starts, including his five-inning effort Wednesday against the Reds. Lopez allowed two home runs and now has yielded the most (30) in MLB. He's faced San Diego twice this season and is 0-1 in those starts.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc wasn't as bad in his last start as he was on May 21 against Seattle when he allowed eight runs, but he did surrender seven runs to the Brewers. He said afterward that he didn't have command of any of his pitches, including his plus-change.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders pitched through flu-like symptoms on Thursday against the Reds. He allowed four runs in a six-pitch span but would get through six innings. Nevertheless, he has lost three straight starts after a great first impression with the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Correia saw his bid for an 11th victory disappear early as the Brewers got to him in the early innings in his last start. Correia was without a breaking ball for most of the start, a pitch that had worked in the second. He's 5-2 in the second half.
away_pitcher_note: Friday against Colorado, Kennedy left his pitches up and had communication issues with catcher Miguel Montero. Despite it all, he gave up just three runs on 10 hits over five frames and kept his club in the game.

home_pitcher_note: The losing streak continued for Lincecum in his last outing, when he gave up four runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings to the Cardinals. In his last outing against the D-backs, Lincecum held them to two runs on nine hits in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Enright is alright. The rookie right-hander stood toe to toe with Ubaldo Jimenez on Saturday, yielding one Rockies run in 6 2/3 innings. He has begun his MLB career with 10 straight starts of three runs or less allowed in five or more innings.

home_pitcher_note: Technically, Zito will be working on only two days' rest. But his previous appearance was a one-inning relief outing Wednesday in which he threw only 26 pitches. It amounted to a glamorized between-starts bullpen session.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson shut down the Rockies for seven innings on Sunday. He allowed just four hits and, throwing more sliders, struck out nine. In his first five D-backs starts, the rookie righty has gone seven or more innings and yielded three runs or less.

home_pitcher_note: August has been a mostly subpar month for Giants starters, but not for Cain. He's 2-2 with a 2.76 ERA this month. Cain's coming off a strong eight-inning outing against Cincinnati in which he struck out four of the last six batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Lopez failed to make it into the sixth inning for the fourth straight outing, giving up five runs in 4 1/3. On July 22 against the Giants, Lopez took the loss, allowing three runs on five hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Since allowing three runs in his first 17 innings with the D-backs, Saunders has struggled mightily, giving up 23 runs (19 earned) in the 21 innings that have followed. The Padres reached Saunders for six runs (five earned) over six innings on Aug. 8
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc bounced back from a miserable outing in Milwaukee with a win against the D-backs. He could not retire Stephen Drew, who went 4-for-4 with two homers and two doubles, but was effective otherwise. In all, he allowed three runs in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing against San Diego, Kennedy stifled the Padres through seven scoreless innings. The right-hander allowed only one run, striking out 12 on 105 pitches. In three career starts against San Diego, Kennedy has a 1.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Correia allowed a career-high nine earned runs in his last start against the D-backs and now gets the task of facing them again, this time at Chase Field. Correia said his fastball command wasn't bad and credited the Arizona hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Enright took down another ace in his last start, besting Tim Lincecum on Friday in San Francisco. Enright tossed seven shutout innings, holding the Giants to only six hits, all singles. The rookie right-hander has yet to face San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: What more is there to say about Latos? The 22-year-old got a no-decision in his last start, vs. the Phillies, but allowed one run on five hits in seven innings. It was his 13th straight start of allowing two or fewer runs. He lowered his ERA to 2.29.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Hudson continued his consistency by working at least seven innings for the sixth consecutive outing in a 5-2 win over the Giants. The young right-hander held San Francisco to two runs on four hits, striking out six and walking one.
away_pitcher_note: Myers has pitched at least six innings in 27 consecutive starts, breaking Larry Dierker's franchise record. Dierker did it over a span of two seasons in 1969-70, but Myers has pitched at least six innings in each one of his 27 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: After struggling through his previous four starts -- posting a 7.77 ERA in that span -- Saunders was solid on Monday, limiting the Padres to two runs in eight innings despite giving up 10 hits. He has never faced the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Norris had throw at least six innings in seven consecutive starts before going 5 2/3 innings in Sunday's loss to the Mets, during which he allowed eight hits and five runs in 5 2/3 innings. He's 4-1 with a 3.65 ERA in seven starts since July 28.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez took a no-decision in his last start against the Giants. The right-hander struggled the second time through the lineup, giving up four runs in the third inning. He exited after four, allowing five runs on eight hits while striking out three.
away_pitcher_note: Happ is coming off perhaps the best game of his career. He threw a two-hit shutout Monday against he Cardinals, facing just 28 batters. It was his fourth career complete game and third shutout. He's 4-2 with a 3.32 ERA in seven starts with Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy enters this start on a roll. He has won his last two starts and has won his last three decisions. He had probably his finest outing of the year Aug. 26 at PETCO Park, when he tossed seven shutout innings and fanned 12.
away_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old rookie pitched well enough to win in his last outing, yielding one run in six innings before the Giants emerged with a 5-2 victory over Colorado. Bumgarner has thrived on the road, where he has posted a 5-2 record with a 2.62 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Enright has made 12 starts since being called up from Double-A and has yet to give up more than three runs or go fewer than five innings. He also faced Tim Lincecum on Aug. 27 and got the win thanks to seven shutout innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum put his horrid August behind him in his first September start as he outdueled Colorado's Ubaldo Jimenez in a 2-1 Giants victory. Lincecum worked eight innings in that gem last Wednesday, yielding five hits and striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson deserved a better fate in his last start against the Astros, when he left with a lead only to have the bullpen give it up. He faced the Giants on Aug. 28 at AT&T Park and allowed two runs over seven innings in an 11-3 win.
away_pitcher_note: Zito ended the Giants' run of four consecutive quality starts when he lost to the Dodgers, 4-2, on Friday. Desperate for offense, manager Bruce Bochy lifted Zito for a pinch-hitter after four innings.

home_pitcher_note: With six effective innings in a win over the Padres on Sunday, De La Rosa improved to 3-2 with a 3.12 ERA, a .234 batting average against and 54 strikeouts to 25 walks in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders rebounded Saturday against the Astros, tossing two-run ball over seven innings. The lefty was coming off of a rough August, in which he went 2-4 with a 5.08 ERA. Then an Angel on June 26, he beat the Rockies with a solid seven-inning start.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez earned elusive win No. 18 on Monday against the Reds, striking out eight but walking six. It gave him the NL lead in wins, making him the first Rockie to win 18 in a season. He took a 3-1 loss in his last meeting with the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Sunday against Houston, Lopez had his best start in six tries but still left empty-handed. He held the Astros to three runs in six innings. The righty has not won since July 8, a span of 10 outings. He set a new career high in home runs allowed, 33.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie has been stellar in his last four outings, going 3-0 while striking out 24 batters in 26 innings. He's allowed just four earned runs in that span, including two in his last time out against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy threw eight scoreless innings against San Francisco on Monday, but ended up with a no-decision in the 2-0 loss. He allowed two hits and two walks while striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo's 4 1/3-inning outing on Wednesday was his shortest since May 31. This will be Arroyo's fourth attempt at tying his career high of 15 victories.
away_pitcher_note: After not allowing more than three runs in his 12-start big league career, Enright yielded six runs on nine hits in six innings in a 6-3 loss to the Giants Tuesday. His command was off, and his changeup wasn't sharp, resulting in four home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Wood received a no-decision in his last outing, a 6-5 loss at Colorado. He pitched the first five innings and gave up three runs after the Reds had jumped out to a 5-0 lead.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson pitched seven innings of one-run ball to beat the Giants Wednesday and avoid a sweep. He allowed five hits and two walks while striking out three, using a fastball-changeup combination early in the game before going to his slider.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey is coming off a seven-inning, one-run performance in which he struck out a career-high nine batters against Pittsburgh. He is now 6-0 lifetime against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders struggled in Colorado, having his shortest outing of the year at 2 1/3 innings. He gave up seven runs (four earned) on five hits and four walks. Saunders struggled with his command, falling behind consistently in counts.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez will be making his second start since returning from a Minor League assignment at Class A Dayton. He lasted only two-thirds of an inning in his last outing before being optioned, the shortest of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez held his own in a pitcher's duel with Ubaldo Jimenez on Saturday, holding the Rockies to two runs on seven hits and a walk in 6 1/3 innings, but he was saddled with his sixth straight loss.

home_pitcher_note: Burres has been one of the Pirates' best pitchers since taking Jeff Karstens' spot in the rotation. In his last two starts, the lefty has combined to allow just two runs on nine hits in 13 innings. He has struck out nine and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has pitched 14 scoreless innings over his last two starts, allowing just two hits each game but leaving with a no-decision as the D-backs lost both games following his departure.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald takes a string of 17 scoreless innings into his next start. The righty has been terrific lately and has lowered his ERA with Pittsburgh to 3.49. McDonald has also been efficient. He needed just 100 pitches to finish eight innings on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: After an outstanding first 12 starts after being called up from Double-A Mobile, Enright has struggled mightily in his last two. In those two outings, he has allowed 11 runs over nine innings. Last time out he gave up five runs in three innings.

home_pitcher_note: There's a chance Duke won't still be in the rotation, but if he is, it can't get any worse for the lefty. He's not fooling anyone (opponents are batting .326 against him) and has lasted a combined 4 1/3 innings in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson limited Cincinnati to four hits and a walk in eight shutout innings. He led Arizona to a 3-1 victory over the NL Central-leading Reds on Tuesday. Hudson, 24, has gone at least seven innings in eight of his starts with the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders was shaky early, but he settled down in the middle innings Wednesday against the Reds. He allowed seven runs -- four earned -- on nine hits in 7 1/3 innings. After allowing four runs in the first, Saunders pitched into the eighth inning.
away_pitcher_note: In desperate need of a long outing, the Rockies got 7 1/3 innings of solid work out of De La Rosa in a 9-6 win against the Padres on Sept. 15. He's 4-0 in his last five starts, all of which the Rockies have won.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez turned in his third straight solid outing as he pitched the D-backs past the Reds on Thursday. Lopez allowed one run on eight hits over seven innings. Over his last three starts, he has a 2.79 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez, of late, has had to deal with "traffic" on the bases, as manager Jim Tracy put it, and he hasn't been the dominant force he can be. Still, he's one win away from his 20th, and he's showing he can be effective even without his best stuff.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy continued his late-season surge in Pittsburgh on Friday night. The right-hander allowed two runs -- one unearned -- and five hits in six innings of work and received a no-decision as the D-backs fell 4-3.
away_pitcher_note: In a limited start, Francis threw 62 pitches (41 strikes) in three innings, making just one serious mistake -- a two-run homer to Miguel Tejada -- against the Padres, taking the loss. His command was solid, as he struck out two and walked none.

home_pitcher_note: Enright lasted 3 2/3 innings and was tagged for six runs on six hits in a 9-6 loss at Pittsburgh on Saturday, continuing a rough patch since pitching brilliantly in his first 12 starts after being called up from Double-A.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw was moved up in the rotation so his following this one would come against the contending Rockies. He'll pitch here on regular five days' rest, and he's dominated the D-backs this season with a 2-0 record and 1.64 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson, 6-1 with a 1.65 ERA 10 starts, has yet to hiccup as a D-back. Most recently, he limited the Pirates to one run on three hits in 6 1/3 innings. He's had this degree of success relying mostly on his fastball-changeup combo.
away_pitcher_note: Ely's lost six of his last seven decisions in the Majors, but he threw one of his best games of the season against the D-backs in June: He threw seven two-hit, shutout innings in a 1-0 win the Dodgers took in extras at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders had his second-best start as a D-back on Tuesday against the Rockies. He allowed one run on six hits in eight innings and broke a personal two-game losing streak. He said attacking the strike zone led to his success.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley has lost six of his last eight decisions through August and September, but he's pitched better than that. He's struck out at least six in each start this month, two of those fewer than six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Despite allowing one earned run against the Cubs, Sanchez took his first loss since Aug. 13. He allowed four hits and struck out six in 5 2/3 innings. On July 23 against Arizona, Sanchez lasted only five innings, striking out 10 in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez allowed four first-inning runs against Colorado on Wednesday. To his credit, he threw four stellar frames before leaving with a stiff right hand, which was struck by a Ubaldo Jimenez breaking ball.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants opted to flip Lincecum and Madison Bumgarner in the rotation to put Lincecum in line for a potential one-game playoff. If needed, the Giants also could throw Lincecum on three day's rest in a must-win season-finale against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: It's simple: If, in his last start of 2010, Kennedy keeps his pitch count down, he could go seven or eight innings. If he doesn't, expect a repeat of his four-frame, one-run outing against the Rockies on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: On a day when the wind was blowing out and the Giants' bats were hot, Bumgarner threw seven shutout innings against the Cubs, allowing only seven hits and striking out nine. In his last outing against the D-backs, he threw 7 1/3 scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Enright is on track to finish well. After going 0-3 with a 12.08 ERA in three previous outings, the righty returned to form on Friday, limiting the Dodgers to two runs in eight innings. He is 1-1 with a 3.79 ERA in three starts vs. San Francisco.

home_pitcher_note: Ely gets the late call to start in place of Clayton Kershaw. Ely is looking to leave management with a positive memory of a season that deteriorated. He's lost eight of his past nine decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Kroenke gets the start in place of Daniel Hudson, who was shut down with a finger strain. Kroenke made both of his Major League appearances out of the bullpen, allowing seven hits, four earned runs and a homer in 1 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley gets a final shot at the D-backs after the bullpen blew a victory for him in Phoenix on Sunday. After having a second-half 5.20 ERA last year, Billingsley has reversed course with a 3.05 ERA in the second half this year.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders has been up and down in 12 starts for the D-backs. He was somewhere in between on Sunday, allowing two Dodger runs in five innings. But he threw 90 pitches in those five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly, an expected free agent, makes what could be his final start for the Dodgers. He pitched a gem at Coors Field in his last start, allowing one run over eight innings. A win will give him double figures for an eighth consecutive season.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez was signed to a Minor League contract during the offseason and has wound up leading the team in innings pitched. After slumping in August, he has rebounded recently and pitched well his last time out, against the Giants.
