home_pitcher_note: Once upon a time it was believed effective pitching at Coors was impossible, but Jimenez dispelled that by going 9-2 with a 3.19 ERA. It'll be Jimenez's second straight Opening Day start. Last year, he held the Crew to one run over six frames.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy, who was Arizona's most consistent starter in 2010, is making the first Opening Day start of his career. Last season against the Rockies, he was 0-1 with a 3.46 ERA in five starts. In two starts at Coors Field, he compiled a 2.45 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: As a solid No. 2 pitcher in the rotation, De La Rosa is expected to dominate more often than not and make adjustments when he doesn't have his best stuff -- an aspect of his game that has improved in the last three years.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson was acquired by the D-backs last July in a trade with the White Sox. In 11 games for Arizona, Hudson went 7-1 with a 2.45 ERA. Hudson tossed seven shutout innings in his lone appearance against the Rockies in 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin was part of the Rockies' scouting emphasis on aggressive pitching. Last year as a rookie, Chacin showed he wasn't scared to attack hitters at Coors. He went 5-5 with a 3.98 ERA in 15 home games, and struck out 72 against 33 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders was acquired by the D-backs last July in a trade that sent Dan Haren to the Angels. He is the most experienced of Arizona's five starters. With the D-backs in 2010, he was 3-7 with a 4.25 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wells won the fourth spot with an impressive spring. He needed to rebound after going 8-14 in 2010; he'd won 12 games in '09. The right-hander had to work for the spot as there was competition for the final openings in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders was scheduled to pitch Sunday's finale with the Rockies, but weather postponed the contest, so the D-backs left-hander will make his 2011 debut in Monday's series opener with the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Andrew Cashner, who won the fifth spot over Carlos Silva, will make his first big league start. He was used strictly in relief in 2010, posting a 4.80 ERA in 55 games. He made three starts this spring, but the Cubs do admit he's a work in progress.
away_pitcher_note: Enright made his big league debut in 2010 and was outstanding in his first 12 starts before tiring down the stretch. In each of those starts, he threw at least five innings and gave up three or fewer runs.

home_pitcher_note: Ryan Dempster tries for win No. 1 in his second start after he was hurt by two homers on Opening Day. He gave up six runs on six hits and four walks over 6 2/3 innings. Let's see if manager Mike Quade asserts himself more if the righty struggles.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga beat out Aaron Heilman for the fifth spot in the rotation. He was acquired in January from the Tigers in exchange for a pair of Minor Leaguers. Last year, he came within one out of a perfect game.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy made the first Opening Day start of his career last Friday in Colorado and allowed four runs (three earned) in six innings. Kennedy was originally scheduled to pitch Wednesday but was pushed back due to Sunday's postponement.
away_pitcher_note: As part of some tinkering to the Reds' rotation, Wood is getting an extra day of rest since his last start on Saturday. The club is trying to preserve him from running into any fatigue.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson pitched well in his first outing against the Rockies on Saturday, but he did not have his usual command. The right-hander allowed three runs on six hits in six innings. He went 7-1 with a 1.69 ERA for the D-backs in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo felt some weakness in his previous outing on Sunday because of a bout with mono. But he showed no ill effects as he pitched seven strong innings. All of the six hits against him were for extra bases, but the damage was kept to a minimum.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders suffered through a miserable spring beset by the flu and ineffectiveness. His first regular-season start against the Cubs on Monday was a good one, as he gave up just two runs over six innings. Saunders was 1-3 with a 12.46 ERA this spring.
away_pitcher_note: During his six-inning winning performance Tuesday vs. the Astros, Leake had success with his cutter and slider. His sinker, which he was overthrowing at 92-93 mph during Spring Training, has also improved and he's getting ground balls.

home_pitcher_note: Enright makes his first home start of the season vs. the team he had faced in his big league debut last June 30. Enright made an immediate impression in that Busch Stadium debut, holding the Cards to a run and four hits in five innings for a 4-2 win.
away_pitcher_note: McClellan will have a hard time topping his first start, when he tossed six very strong innings. Arizona is a tough place for pitchers, and it's been especially tough on McClellan in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga beat out Aaron Heilman for the fifth spot in the rotation. He was acquired in January from the Tigers in exchange for two Minor Leaguers. Galarraga got the win against the Cubs on Wednesday allowing four runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter will be looking for a little luck. He's turned in two fine starts, allowing three earned runs, but he hasn't gotten any help. The Cardinals are 0-2 behind him, scoring four runs in two games for their ace.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy started both Opening Day and the home opener for the D-backs. He matched his career high by tossing eight innings against the Reds on Friday. He had a good breaking ball and fanned nine, while walking just one.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook isn't where he wants to be yet, but he got a little closer in his second start. He still needs to refine his command, though -- Westbrook has walked nine batters in 10 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson pitched well in his last outing against the Reds but came away with a loss. He allowed just two runs on three hits over seven innings with both the runs and two of those hits coming in the first inning.
away_pitcher_note: Cain has picked up where he left off last season, opening the year with a pair of quality starts. He recorded 11 consecutive scoreless innings before surrendering his first run of the season in Saturday's win over the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders' last outing is one he'd rather forget. He struggled to find his release point and wound up allowing six hits and five walks while lasting just three innings. He allowed just two runs in six innings in his first start.
away_pitcher_note: Zito showed potential in his first two outings. He yielded three first-inning runs in his season debut at Los Angeles before working five shutout innings. Then he allowed one run in five innings to St. Louis before surrendering three in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: Enright has allowed four runs and lasted six innings in each of his first two starts, with the D-backs coming out on the losing end of both. He is looking for his first win since Sept. 1, 2010, against the Padres. He is 0-6 since that outing.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has worked only eight innings in two starts. Opponents are batting .406 against him. But in his previous outing against Arizona last Sept. 30, he allowed one run in five innings to win a key game in the Giants' drive to the NL West title.

home_pitcher_note: This will be LeCure's third start in place of the injured Johnny Cueto and Homer Bailey. He allowed just one hit and one run in his last start against San Diego, but got a no-decision in an 8-2 Cincinnati win in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga was saved by his offense in his last start against the Cardinals. He allowed five runs on nine hits and threw 99 pitches in lasting the requisite five innings in a 13-8 win. He had a solid first outing against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo had trouble with his location against Pittsburgh in his last start and was pulled after giving up five earned runs on nine hits in four innings. He gave up his first two walks of the season and surrendered two homers.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy had a miserable start last time out vs. the Cardinals. He allowed a career-worst nine earned runs in just three innings, struggling with his command. Lance Berkman's grand slam in the second was the key blow.

home_pitcher_note: Leake had his second quality start in three appearances last time out, limiting Pittsburgh to two runs on four hits in six innings. He struggled with his command for one inning but was otherwise sharp.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has struggled in the first inning this year. Of the 10 runs he's allowed, five have come in the opening frame. He has not gotten much run support as the D-backs have scored just one run in his 19 innings on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's struggles continued last weekend in a loss to the Braves, who tagged him for 11 hits and four runs in five innings. And it doesn't get any easier. In seven career starts against the D-backs, Pelfrey is 0-5 with a 6.69 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders battled in his start Saturday against the Giants. He allowed 14 baserunners in 6 2/3 innings, but was helped when the D-backs turned five double plays behind him. Two of the five runs he allowed came after he departed.

home_pitcher_note: Recalled from Triple-A to replace the injured Chris Young, Gee held the Braves to one run in 5 2/3 innings last weekend in Atlanta. He'll receive one more start against the D-backs, a team he's never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Enright cruised through the first five innings of his last start against the Giants, allowing just one hit -- a homer by Aubrey Huff. He ran into trouble in the sixth, though, allowing three more runs before being pulled.

home_pitcher_note: Complaining about a poor grip, Niese walked five in six innings last Tuesday, but managed to hold the Astros to just two runs. He'll look for similar damage control against the D-backs, who touched him for seven runs in a game last August.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga pitched six solid innings on Tuesday night in Cincinnati, allowing three runs on four hits. He retired 10 of the last 11 batters he faced while striking out six to move to 3-0.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy followed up one of his worst outings with one of his best. After allowing a career-high 9 earned runs in three innings in his previous start, Kennedy gave up just one run on four hits in 5 1/3 innings on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Lee followed his shutout on April 14 against the Washington Nationals with six innings Wednesday in a victory over the Milwaukee Brewers. He got the no-decision, but he allowed eight hits and two earned runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson retired 12 straight during one stretch on Thursday at Cincinnati, but he couldn't overcome a nightmarish first inning in which he allowed four runs on three hits and walked three, including two with the bases loaded.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt bounced back splendidly from a strained lower back Thursday in a 3-0 victory over the Padres at PETCO Park. Oswalt allowed just one hit and two walks in six scoreless innings. He struck out seven. He said afterward he had no back issues.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders pitched well against the Mets his last time out, but came away with a no-decision thanks to a bullpen meltdown. Saunders allowed just two hits through the first six innings before being removed after a walk to lead off the seventh.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels pitched brilliantly on Thursday in a 2-0 victory over the Padres at PETCO Park. He allowed four hits and three walks (one was intentional) and struck out eight in eight innings. Hamels threw 126 pitches to help out the Phils' overworked 'pen.

home_pitcher_note: Enright struggled to finish off innings against the Mets in his last start. All five of the runs he allowed came with two outs. Enright had trouble locating his breaking stuff early, and was missing his spots throughout the 5 2/3-inning stint.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe being on the road will get Dempster back on track. He is 0-2 with a 7.91 ERA in three starts at Wrigley and 1-0 with a 7.15 ERA in two games on the road. He lost to the D-backs on April 6, giving up 10 hits over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga struggled with his location against the Mets in his last outing on Sunday and paid the price, allowing six runs and lasting just three innings. Four of the runs were unearned due to an error behind him.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano's winning streak ended in his last start against the Dodgers. He had gone 10-0 since last Aug. 14, but was rocked for five runs in the first. He is 2-2 with a 4.50 ERA in six games vs. the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy pitched the game of his life in his last start, striking out 10 in a complete-game shutout of the Phillies. He commanded all of his pitches, especially his curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Garza is still looking for that elusive first win with the Cubs. In his last start against the Rockies, he gave up five runs -- one earned -- on three hits over six innings. For the season, he's struck out 41 over 30 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson gave up at least one run in the first inning for the fifth time this season but showed poise in his last start against the Phillies to earn his first win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Coleman, whose previous start was rained out, was roughed up in his last start on April 22, giving up six runs on six hits over 2 2/3 innings. All of the hits and runs came in the third inning. He threw 90 pitches, including 51 in the third alone.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has struggled at Chase Field this year having allowed 15 earned runs in 15 innings. On the road, he has allowed three earned runs in 12 innings in starts for a 2.25 ERA. Last time out, he allowed six runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With Ubaldo Jimenez still searching for his first win of the season, De La Rosa has been the team's de facto ace this season. The lefty has allowed just nine earned runs in 31 innings, and leads the team with 29 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Enright picked up the win in his last start against the Cubs on Friday, his first victory since Sept. 1, 2010. The right-hander pitched more aggressively and with a better tempo at the urging of manager Kirk Gibson.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin was a hard-luck loser in his last outing, giving up three runs while striking out a season-high eight and walking none over seven innings in a 3-0 loss to the Pirates. He is 1-1 with a 2.03 ERA in two starts at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: The focus has been on Kennedy's past two starts, both solid, in his first two outings as a new dad, but he's been nails all season. Deduct one bad start (nine earned runs in three innings), and he's 3-0 with an ERA of 2.00.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel has given up just two runs in his last 13 2/3 innings. Although he has to break a habit of giving up runs in the first inning, Hammel has been staying in the strike zone, and is able to use his full complement of pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Stauffer was in line for his first victory in his last start, but reliever Luke Gregerson allowed an inherited runner to score. Still, Stauffer pitched well, allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings. He struck out seven for a second straight start.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga is growing increasingly aware of the need to keep the ball in the park. Even though eight of them have been solo shots, the Majors-leading 11 homers he has given up have accounted for 15 of the 21 runs scored off him.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres rewarded Moseley for a hard-luck April with plenty of offense in his last start to ensure his first victory of the season. Moseley did his part, tossing seven shutout innings in a victory over the Dodgers, striking out six.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson, who won his first May decision, has struggled to set the tone in the first inning this season because of command issues, but he has been very effective in the later innings.

home_pitcher_note: Harang was roughed up for a second straight outing, allowing two home runs one start after serving up three long balls. He did settle down to retire 12 of 13 batters at one point, but still lost to the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders pitched well at Chase Field for the first time this year in his most recent outing, but the D-backs won late, and he was not able to get the win. Going into that game, Saunders had a 9.00 ERA at home and a 2.25 ERA on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum might be baseball's best .500 pitcher. He has recorded six of his 29 double-digit strikeout games against Arizona. Of his 14 appearances against Arizona, 12 are quality starts. He has won four of his last five decisions against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy battled in his last start, pitching his way into and out of trouble, stranding six Rockies through the first four innings. Kennedy ended up allowing just two runs in six innings, as the D-backs rallied for a 3-2 win in 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: This is a big start for Sanchez, who disappointed manager Bruce Bochy with a perceived lack of concentration in his last outing at New York. Pitching at home might help Sanchez, who's 18-15 at AT&T Park and 18-26 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga struggled to throw strikes in his last outing. He walked six Padres (one intentionally) in 4 1/3 innings. He has struggled to keep the ball in the park this year, having allowed 11 homers.

home_pitcher_note: Cain will make his second appearance of the six-game homestand. Interestingly, throughout Cain's Major League career, his performance in day games (23-24, 3.38 ERA) is similar to his results at night (36-40, 3.49).
away_pitcher_note: Hudson is on a roll. After losing his first three starts of the year, in large part due to poor run support, he has won his last four. In his last start against the Padres, he tossed seven shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw kept the damage to a minimum and overcame a pair of first-inning walks to pitch into the seventh inning vs. the Mets. He still has occasional wildness that runs up his pitch count, but he's matured enough to keep those from ruining a start.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is still looking for his first win this year. Last time out against the Padres he allowed four runs in the first inning before settling down. By then it was too late, as the Padres won, 4-3.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley was in charge against the Pirates through seven innings, when a controversy over an umpire's call created a lengthy delay. When he resumed pitching, he allowed a walk and an RBI double and was removed in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter is making his first big league start. Called up on April 15, he has been outstanding in seven relief appearances. His funky over-the-top delivery can be deceptive for hitters. He throws a fastball, changeup and curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly held the Pirates scoreless until the sixth inning, when he allowed two runs, one on Andrew McCutchen's home run. Manager Don Mattingly said Lilly is showing a pattern of weakening when he reaches the third time through a lineup.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy was outstanding in his last start as he matched Tim Lincecum pitch-for-pitch. The two each lasted eight innings, and the Giants eventually won, 1-0, in the bottom of the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga has struggled with his control and in giving up the long ball this year. He has allowed 12 homers, which at the time of his last start was tied for the Major League lead. He lost to the Giants in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Richard, a ground-ball pitcher, got plenty of those in his last start, only they ended up as hits as he allowed seven earned runs on 10 hits in 3 1/3 innings to the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson threw a career-high 117 pitches vs. the Giants on Thursday and got the loss after allowing three runs on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings. Struggling with his fastball command, he gave up two runs in the seventh that proved to be the difference.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer, the most reliable member of the rotation, was staked to a 5-0 lead against the Brewers, but allowed six runs and was gone in the sixth inning. It was the most runs he's allowed in a game since Aug. 26, 2007 (11 against Phillies).

home_pitcher_note: Saunders, still searching for his first victory of the season, allowed four runs on six hits last Friday against the Dodgers. The left-hander beat the Braves in June 2008, shutting them out over 7 1/3 innings as a member of the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Considered one of the game's top prospects, Teheran will be making his second spot start of the month. The 20-year-old showed good poise while allowing three earned runs and working 4 2/3 innings in his May 7 big league debut in Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter blanked the Dodgers on two hits in his first career start Saturday, striking out three and walking none in a no-decision. Collmenter has not allowed a run in 7 1/3 relief innings this season at Chase Field.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has impressed his teammates with the competitive fire he has shown while winning each of the five decisions garnered through his first six starts. His sinker has helped him escape a fair amount of jams this year.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy is beginning to hit his stride, striking out eight batters and allowing only four hits in each of his past two starts, the latest a 4-1 victory over the Dodgers on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Duensing had his first bad outing of the season, when he allowed seven runs on eight hits and two walks against the Jays on Sunday. He'll start the first game of Interleague Play for the Twins this season against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: The D-backs will call upon Micah Owings, who has a 3-1 record and a 4.85 ERA in seven starts at Triple-A Reno, to make his first start of the season. Owings has started 45 games in two seasons with Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Baker kept the Twins in the game vs. the Mariners on Monday, giving up four runs while striking out eight in six innings, but was outpitched by Michael Pineda. He's struck out 22 batters over his last three starts, but has only a 1-1 record.

home_pitcher_note: After throwing a career-high 117 pitches on May 12, Hudson showed no ill effects in throwing seven innings of one-run ball against the Padres on Tuesday. He struck out six, walked two and earned his fourth win in his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano returned to form against the Mariners on Tuesday, striking out nine and walking just one over seven solid innings to outduel Felix Hernandez. He'll look to build on that outing against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies elected to use both De La Rosa and Jhoulys Chacin in the doubleheader, meaning the team will use Greg Reynolds as a spot starter Saturday. De La Rosa was very sharp in his deepest outing of the year (eight innings, one run) last time out.
away_pitcher_note: On Thursday, Collmenter picked up where he left off in his first start, pitching another six scoreless innings. The rookie allowed two hits and struck out one against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin was part of the Rockies' scouting emphasis on aggressive pitching. Last year as a rookie, Chacin showed he wasn't scared to attack hitters at Coors. He went 5-5 with a 3.98 ERA in 15 home games, and struck out 72 against 33 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders was acquired by the D-backs last July in a trade that sent Dan Haren to the Angels. He is the most experienced of Arizona's five starters. With the D-backs in 2010, he was 3-7 with a 4.25 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: For the fifth time in nine starts, Hammel allowed two earned runs or fewer in his last appearance, but left with a no-decision and has only two wins in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy picked up his second win in a row on Friday, pitching 7 2/3 innings against the Twins. The right-hander struck out three, walked one and allowed four runs on six hits. He is 0-1 with a 3.55 ERA in seven career starts against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Mortensen made yet another compelling argument for long-term inclusion in the rotation, despite taking the loss Saturday. The righty left the game tops among Major League rookie starters with a .186 opponents' batting average.
away_pitcher_note: In his first big league start in two years, Owings threw 5 1/3 innings and didn't factor into the decision against the Twins on Saturday. He allowed four runs (three earned) on seven hits, struck out three and walked one.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros have lost Myers' last five starts as his ERA jumped from 3.72 in April to 5.00 in May. He tossed five scoreless innings Saturday against Toronto before allowing five earned runs in the sixth and seventh.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has been on a roll of late. He is 4-1 with a 2.27 ERA in his last five starts. In his last start vs. Twins he allowed two runs in eight innings. In his start before that, the Padres managed just one run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Norris boasts the NL's best home winning percentage since the 2010 All-Star break (.875), holding opponents to a Major League-low .183 average in that span. He pitched seven innings in the Astros' 4-3 walk-off win Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Duke is making his first start of the season. Broke his left hand early in spring when hit by line drive. This will also be his first start in a D-backs uniform after being acquired via trade from Pirates in November.

home_pitcher_note: Happ allowed one earned run but five total runs on Tuesday night vs. the Dodgers after a third-inning error led to a grand slam. Happ is 1-2 with a 3.18 ERA in his past three starts and 1-1 with a 2.77 ERA in his career against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter suffered first loss in his last outing against the Rockies last Tuesday at Coors Field. In two starts prior to that he had not allowed a run in 12 combined innings. Called up from Triple-A April 15 and used in relief in first seven games.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has settled in after a rough start to the season. Last time out he earned his first win, holding the Rockies to just two runs over eight innings at Coors Field. In his last two starts, he's allowed three runs in 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad comes off yet another impressive outing, giving up two runs in six innings at AT&T Park. He struck out six in a no-decision. Volstad has gone six innings in three of his last four starts. At Arizona, he has made one start, taking a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy beat the Rockies in his last start, allowing just one run over eight innings in a 2-1 win. He's won his last three starts, and last five decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Dominant all month, Sanchez tossed a five-hit shutout at San Francisco on Thursday. He struck out eight and improved to 2-0 with a 2.05 ERA in May. Sanchez has two complete games this year. The other was a one-hitter vs. the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson labored through six innings on Friday against Houston but earned his third straight win. He allowed five earned runs on eight hits, struck out four and walked one. The right-hander is 4-2 with a 3.29 ERA at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez had a string of 11 straight scoreless innings snapped in his last outing. He yielded two solo homers vs. the Dodgers in a no-decision. In his past two outings, Vazquez has given up two runs in 13 innings with 10 strikeouts and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: In his D-backs debut, Duke blanked the Astros over seven innings, allowing three hits, striking out four and walking one. Duke also helped his cause with a three-run homer, the first of his career. He has a 5.19 career ERA against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old Zimmermann makes his first career start against the D-backs. Zimmermann posted a quality start in each of his past five outings, but has just one win to show for it as Washington's run support has been lacking.

home_pitcher_note: After winning his first two starts while allowing no runs in 12 innings, Collmenter was touched for five runs in his third start and two on Sunday in Houston. He went six innings, struck out five and allowed four hits, but got a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Maya makes his seventh career start after his 2011 debut Sunday vs. the Padres. Maya cruised his first time through the San Diego lineup, but allowed the heat to get to him in Washington and left after allowing four runs in 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders picked up his second consecutive win on Monday, throwing six innings and allowing four runs on seven hits to the Marlins. He struck out seven, walked two and has pitched at least six innings in his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez spent the 2007 part of 2006 in Arizona after the D-backs claimed him from Washington off waivers. Hernandez has a 4.23 career ERA at Chase Field. He is 11-7 all-time against the D-backs, but has not won this season since April 28.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander hit a bump in the road on Tuesday, allowing three runs on five hits in five innings in a 5-2 loss to the Marlins. Kennedy struck out four and walked three. He has a 4.91 ERA in two starts against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis outpitched the Phillies' Cliff Lee in his previous start and continues to be the lone Nationals starter to regularly receive run support. But he has a 2-7 record in 12 career starts against Arizona and has never won in the desert.

home_pitcher_note: Correia notched his eighth win of the season Wednesday night against the Mets by giving up two runs in six innings. Correia is sporting a 3.40 ERA and has won his last three starts. He is 4-8 with a 4.80 ERA against Arizona lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: After holding opponents to three runs or less in six consecutive starts, Hudson has hit bumps in his past two starts, allowing five and four runs, respectively.

home_pitcher_note: The wheels fell off in the sixth inning of Malholm's last outing against the Mets on June 2. He allowed four runs in the frame, three earned, to finish with six earned runs in 5 2/3 IP. Current D-Backs are 10-for-44 against him without a homer.
away_pitcher_note: In his third start for the D-backs, Duke returns to Pittsburgh, where he spent the first six seasons of his career. In two starts for Arizona, Duke is 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA. He allowed four runs on 10 hits to the Nationals in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens continues to hold down the rotation's fifth spot as well as the Pirates could want. He lasted a season-high seven innings in his last start and threw more pitches (97) than he had in an outing since June 1, 2010.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday, Collmenter picked up where he left off before allowing two earned runs in back-to-back starts, blanking the Nationals over seven innings. The right-hander allowed only three hits, struck out five and lowered his ERA to 1.25 on the season.

home_pitcher_note: Dominant in May, Sanchez started off with a tougher June. The right-hander gave up five runs in five innings with five strikeouts in a no-decision against the Brewers in his last start. He was 4-0 (1.66 ERA) in May. Sanchez beat Arizona on May 31.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders kept his string of solid starts going by escaping two jams in seven solid innings, combining on a four-hitter that lifted the Arizona Diamondbacks to a 2-0 win over the Washington Nationals on May 4.

home_pitcher_note: After three straight strong outings, Vazquez hit a skid in his last start, allowing six runs in four innings against the Brewers. The veteran's last win was on May 21 against the Rays. He had a no-decision at Arizona on June 1.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy yielded one earned run over seven innings as part of a no-decision against the Nationals on June 5. Kennedy struck out three, walked three and gave up five hits. He is sporting a 1.08 WHIP and a 3.01 ERA on the season.

home_pitcher_note: As MLB debuts go, Hand certainly had a memorable and successful one. The 21-year-old, called up from Double-A to fill Josh Johnson's rotation spot, allowed just one hit in six innings. It happened to be a homer to Alex Gonzalez. Hand struck out six.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson yielded three runs (one earned) over seven innings in a no-decision loss against the Pirates on Tuesday. Hudson struck out seven while giving up just one walk and three hits.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco went 7 1/3 innings and gave up two runs on eight hits with five strikeouts in his last start, a no-decision against the Braves. He exited the game trailing, 2-0. The right-hander is 5-1 with a 3.38 ERA against the D-backs in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Duke scattered nine hits and one run over seven innings of work against the Pirates on Wednesday, but got stuck with a no-decision against his former team, as Arizona would lose, 3-2, in 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter continued his string of impressive outings, hurling five-plus innings and throwing 102 pitches as he settled for a no-decision in a 2-0 victory at Pittsburgh on Thursday. Collmenter has allowed just four total runs in his six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cain had his best start of the year Wednesday, striking out 11 over nine innings, the 13th complete-game effort of his career. Cain had all four pitches working, got the first-pitch strikes he wanted and even aided his own cause with an RBI double.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders was hurt by the home run in his last outing, a 6-4 loss to the Marlins in Florida. Saunders, who had won his previous three decisions, allowed three homers, accounting for all five of the runs he allowed on 10 hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has set new standards for futility. He has absorbed four defeats while allowing one earned run or fewer. The last pitcher to lose that many games despite such stinginess? Teammate Matt Cain in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy battled on a hot, humid South Florida night in his last outing against the Marlins. He picked up the win despite allowing five runs over eight innings. Most of the damage came on back-to-back homers by Gaby Sanchez and Mike Stanton.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong's streak of allowing one run or fewer ended at six in a row in his last outing. Vogelsong still owns an ERA of 0.99 in his last seven starts. He's 2-0 with a 3.27 ERA in his road assignments.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing four earned runs in a no-decision against the Marlins on June 1, Hudson pitched six innings of one-run baseball and picked up the victory against Florida on Sunday. For the second straight game, he struck out seven.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander bounced back nicely from a rough debut, when he allowed five runs on seven hits over four innings against the Braves on Aug. 20. In his second start, he blanked the Nationals over six innings, striking out four and walking four.
away_pitcher_note: Cook gave up five earned runs on 11 hits in a no-decision Aug. 24 against Houston. Cook is 6-4 with a 5.48 ERA in 23 career appearances (21 starts) against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter cashed in his third consecutive solid start on Friday against the Padres, pitching six scoreless innings, allowing six hits, striking out four and walking none in a win. The rookie is 5-0 when he doesn't issue a walk.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers seemed headed for victory in his last start against the Dodgers but a bad inning that included a disputed balk call ruined things. Rogers still seeks consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Cain threw eight innings Sunday, allowing two runs while striking out six batters, but did not factor into the decision of an eventual loss to the Astros. Cain is 3-1 against the D-backs this season despite a 4.50 ERA and 1.35 WHIP in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders picked up his first win in his past three tries in a 3-1 victory over the Padres on Saturday. The left-hander allowed only one unearned run over seven innings while scattering four hits, striking out three and walking one.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum gave up a career-high three home runs Monday against the Cubs, taking the loss after yielding five runs (four earned) in six innings. He is 0-1 with a 1.20 ERA, 0.80 WHIP and .140 opponent's average in two starts against Arizona this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy picked up his National League-leading 17th victory on Sunday, pitching seven innings, allowing one run on six hits, striking out seven and walking none. He has pitched seven innings or more in seven of his last nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong lost his third straight start Tuesday, giving up three runs over five innings against the Cubs. The right-hander admitted he has been rushing his delivery, trying to throw "really good pitches" every time instead of just hitting his spots.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson continues to emerge down the stretch run. On Monday, he pitched seven innings, allowed no runs on three hits, struck out eight and walked three as he beat the Rockies for his second straight victory. He is 1-2 against the Giants this season.

home_pitcher_note: Imagine how good his numbers would look if not for an 18.00 ERA in the first inning this year. Rogers bounced back over the next five innings in his previous start, limiting the D-backs to one run over those frames.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander picked up his second consecutive win in three big league starts on Tuesday against the Rockies, pitching six innings, allowing two runs on nine hits while striking out three and walking one.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel had been removed from the rotation last month because of his year-long inconsistency. He is back because the Rockies are trying to monitor the innings of second-year RHP Jhoulys Chacin.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter has won his last two starts and has pitched well in his last five. His last start was against the Rox, and he allowed two runs on five hits over six innings. Collmenter allowed five runs in 4 1/3 innings at Coors Field earlier this year.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood threw seven scoreless innings in his last start, a win at PETCO Park over the Padres, and has been solid since joining the Rockies' rotation last month.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders suffered the loss in his last start against the Giants. The left-hander was under the weather and allowed four runs (three earned) over 5 1/3 innings. Saunders has a 5.05 ERA in six starts since the end of July.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy picked up his NL-best 18th win in his last start against the Giants at AT&T Park. Kennedy allowed one run in seven innings as he outdueled Tim Lincecum. Kennedy has won 10 of his last 11 starts and leads the Majors in win percentage.
away_pitcher_note: A 37-pitch first inning against the Rockies led to defeat on Saturday in San Diego. The lefty regularly threw 93 mph and had five strikeouts but wasn't as accurate as usual. He gave up five runs.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson has pitched well in his last three starts, going 3-0 with a 1.19 ERA. Last time out he held the Giants to one run on three hits over seven innings. In three starts against the Padres this year, Hudson is 2-1 with a 2.25 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Latos found the command on his curveball and slider -- a pitch that has largely eluded him in 2011 -- in his past start against the Rockies, striking out eight and allowing two runs in seven innings for his first win since Aug. 7.

home_pitcher_note: Miley has pitched well in his last three starts after struggling in his Major League debut. The left-hander is 3-0 with a 1.89 ERA in those three outings after allowing five runs over four innings in his debut against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer allowed two monster home runs to the Giants' Pablo Sandoval in his last start, as the two traveled a combined 816 feet. All told, Stauffer allowed four runs on seven hits with one walk in six innings in taking a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter deserved a better fate last time out as he held the Rockies to just one run over 6 1/3 innings. The right-hander left with a 3-1 lead but watched the Rockies rally for seven runs in the eighth and win 8-3.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc allowed four doubles and four earned runs in a five-inning start on Tuesday against the Giants. The left-hander allowed a two-run homer to Brett Pill in the first inning and yielded a total of eight hits in his 10th start in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: The 35-year-old has failed to pitch beyond the sixth inning in three of his last four starts, yet is 2-0 in that span while his team is 3-1. Lilly has not allowed more than three runs in eight consecutive starts.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander has responded well after an awful 0-3 April and has won 10 of his last 19 decisions. The last time out he defeated the Rockies in Denver, allowing three runs on seven hits with a walk and four strikeouts in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley has failed to pitch beyond the fourth inning in his last two starts. Among his problems lately has been an inability to put away hitters on two-strike counts. The D-backs are the last team he beat, on Aug. 5.
away_pitcher_note: In only his second full season, the right-hander has become one of the premier pitchers in the Majors. He has only lost once since July 3. He pitched into the eighth inning Thursday against the Padres, allowing only one run on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw brings his Cy Young campaign home, seeking his 19th win, which would be the most for a Dodger since Ramon Martinez won 20 in 1990. For quality-start buffs, Kershaw has 11 in his last 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has stayed toe to toe with staff mate Ian Kennedy, as the pair has combined for 35 wins. He pitched his third complete game of the season Friday against the Padres, allowing one earned run and five hits, while earning the win.

home_pitcher_note: Stauffer earned a no-decision in his last start against the red-hot D-backs, allowing three runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings. Stauffer hasn't won since Aug. 18 and, after a strong start, is 0-3 with a 7.58 ERA in four starts since then.
away_pitcher_note: Miley scuffled in his last start against the Padres when he allowed five runs on eight hits over five innings. Prior to that outing, he had won three straight starts and allowed just four runs over 19 innings.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc won for the first time since Aug. 18 when he allowed four runs on four hits in 5 2/3 innings against these same D-backs in his last start. LeBlanc took a shutout into the sixth inning in that start.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter was roughed up in his last outing against the Padres at Chase Field. The right-hander allowed six runs on seven hits in lasting just four innings. Prior to that outing, Collmenter had held the Padres scoreless in seven innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Harang battled through the first three innings in Monday's loss to the Giants before settling down in the fourth and fifth. But it was too late at that point, as Harang had already given up four runs on six hits and two walks while striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders has won his last two starts and three of his last four. Last time out against the Dodgers he allowed two runs on four hits over seven innings. The lefty has a 2.05 ERA in three starts vs. the Padres this season.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Kennedy's second attempt at win No. 20. Last time out against the Dodgers, he allowed four runs on seven hits over six innings. All four runs came in the first inning. Kennedy will be facing the Pirates for the first time this year.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first start since Aug. 28 due to soreness and arm fatigue, Karstens was knocked out by St. Louis after 4 1/3 innings on Tuesday. He has given up nine runs in his past eight innings across two starts -- both against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson allowed just a single in the second and two walks after a rough first inning before he departed following the seventh inning in Los Angeles his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Morton returned after nine days off and was much more efficient than he had been recently. Though he walked three, Morton made it through seven innings with 94 pitches and three runs allowed. He's won just twice since June 15.

home_pitcher_note: A 28-pitch first inning in which Miley gave up three hits and two runs to the Padres led to defeat on Friday at PETCO Park, but the rookie left-hander showed poise in shutting out San Diego over the next five innings.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling in his previous six starts this season, Ohlendorf was efficient and effective for seven innings in Los Angeles. He picked up his first win, allowing two runs and throwing only 72 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders was determined to throw strikes last time out -- Sunday in San Diego -- because the D-backs had lost three games in a row and the second-place Giants were surging. The lefty responded by coming within one out of a complete game.
away_pitcher_note: He's 4-1 with a 3.97 ERA in five starts this season vs. the D-backs and 2-0 with a 4.26 ERA in two starts at Chase Field, where he last pitched June 14. Cain gave up two runs in eight innings and won Sept. 2 at AT&T Park in the Giants' 6-2 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy will be making his last regular-season start and should set up perfectly for a probable Game 1 of the NLDS on Oct. 1. Last time out, he threw eight innings of one-hit ball against the Pirates to notch his 20th win of the season, whiffing 12.
away_pitcher_note: In what figures to be a crucial start against the D-backs, the rookie left-hander will aim to reduce his walk total after issuing six free passes over 4 2/3 innings against the Rockies on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter allowed the Padres a cheap run on two bloop singles sandwiched around a hit batsman. He also gave up two solo home runs over the seven innings at PETCO Park, one off a changeup to former D-backs second baseman Orlando Hudson.
away_pitcher_note: Despite his .500 record, Lincecum has recorded his second-best ERA thus far for a single season. The Giants have scored two runs or fewer in 20 of his 32 starts. When they score more than two runs for Lincecum, he's 12-2.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson has lost his last two starts, but has not pitched poorly as he compiled a 3.75 ERA in those games. Prior to that stretch, Hudson had won four straight starts, including a complete-game 3-2 win over the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: In four starts since being called up Sept. 1, Eveland's results have been mixed. The 27-year-old lefty was dominant in his first two and got knocked around early in the next two.

home_pitcher_note: Parker will be making his Major League debut. The right-hander was the D-backs' No. 1 pick (ninth overall) in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft. Parker, who was 11-8 with a 3.79 ERA in Double-A, missed the entire 2010 season due to Tommy John surgery.
away_pitcher_note: Tuesday's start might be Kuroda's last in a Dodgers uniform, as he has yet to decide whether he'll return to L.A. or Japan next season. He's been solid his last two times out, both wins.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has been outstanding in his last four starts, going 3-0 with a 1.88 ERA. Last time out vs. the Giants, Saunders got a no-decision despite allowing just one run over seven innings. The D-backs eventually prevailed, 3-1, in the West clincher.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly brings down the curtain on the Dodgers season. In his last 10 starts, Lilly has a 2.32 ERA, bringing his ERA down almost a full run. He's come up with a new grip on a slider that he credited for 6 1/3 scoreless innings in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo will start his second Game 1 in three years, but the circumstances are vastly different. He was one start removed from knee surgery in 2008 when he took the mound in Philadelphia and gutted through four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy, a 21-game winner and a major part of the D-backs' success, is expected to take the ball in Game 1 in what will be his postseason debut. He went at least seven innings 20 times in 33 starts this season and allowed one run or fewer in 16.

home_pitcher_note: After coming through with a win on the final day of the regular season, Greinke will make his second consecutive start on three days' rest and likely will not go much deeper than the sixth. Greinke will be making his first career postseason start.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson will start Saturday's Game 2, something that had been assumed all along. The right-hander, who was 16-12 with a 3.49 ERA this season, was roughed up at Miller Park on July 4 as he allowed six runs (five earned) on eight hits in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter was promoted from Triple-A Reno on April 15 and stabilized the back of the rotation. His funky, over-the-top delivery was picked up throwing tomahawks in the woods as a kid. He did not allow a run in 14 innings vs. Brewers this year.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum was touched up for seven runs on 10 hits over 4 2/3 innings in his last start on Sept. 26 against the Pirates. He has excelled on the road this season, posting an 8-3 record with a 2.21 ERA. He will be making his first career postseason start.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders suffered a bruised left hand when he was jammed with a batting-practice pitch prior to the season finale. The left-hander faced the Brewers on July 20 at Chase Field and did not get a decision after allowing two runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf does not garner nearly the buzz of the Brewers' top three starters, but he led the team in innings this season. He also has postseason seasoning -- two starts for the Dodgers in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo was stellar over eight innings in Game 1, allowing only four hits and matching Don Sutton's franchise postseason record with nine strikeouts. Six of Gallardo's whiffs came on called third strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy would like to redeem himself after an uncharacteristically poor outing in Game 1 in Milwaukee. He allowed four runs in Arizona's 4-1 loss. The big blow of the game was a two-run homer by Prince Fielder in the seventh inning.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy will be making his second successive Opening Day start. He finished fourth in the NL Cy Young Award voting last year after winning 21 games. Kennedy was dominant against the Giants in 2011, going 3-0 with a 1.22 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum has had mixed success in three previous Opening Day starts. He received a no-decision while yielding three runs in three innings in 2009 vs. Milwaukee, blanked Houston for seven innings in a victory the following year and then lost in L.A.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson spent his first full season in the big leagues in 2011 to form a potent 1-2 punch with Ian Kennedy. He also won the Silver Slugger Award last year. Hudson faced the Giants four times last year and was 1-1 with a 2.93 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: As excellent as Bumgarner was in his first full season, it's easy to forget that he lost his first six decisions in '11, so he's striving to avoid that kind of start. He posted a 5-7 record on the road in '11, though his ERA was a respectable 3.31.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter started the 2011 season in the Minors, but became a key contributor when he was recalled in April. He faced the Giants three times (two starts) and was 2-1 with a 4.50 ERA. One of those wins came in his Major League debut on April 17.
away_pitcher_note: Lifetime, Cain owns a 30-38 road record, though that has improved to 18-17 in the past three years. That includes a 6-6 effort in '11. Like many power pitchers, Cain needs time to get going. His April average of 6.6 K's per nine frames is his lowest.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez cruised through the first three innings on Opening Day against the Dodgers, striking out five. His command went awry in the fourth as he walked four, two with the bases loaded, as L.A. undermined what was shaping up to be a strong start.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill came over from Oakland in an offseason deal that involved highly regarded pitching prospect Jarrod Parker. Last season for the A's, Cahill was 12-14 with a 4.16 ERA. This will be his first career appearance against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Luebke struggled in his first start of the season, allowing five earned runs on nine hits in 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Dodgers. Luebke, whose fastball was up in the zone, threw 24 pitches in the first and finished having thrown 86.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders re-signed with the D-backs as a free agent after the team non-tendered him in December. In 33 starts last year, he compiled a 3.69 ERA. Saunders dominated the Padres last year, going 3-1 with a 1.47 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bass gets the start in the final game of the series against the D-backs, filling in for Dustin Moseley, who is on the disabled list with a shoulder injury. He impressed the team in Spring Training and figured to be a rotation candidate at some point.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy didn't feel like he had his best command during his Opening Day start against the Giants, but he still managed to allow only three runs over 6 2/3 innings. In three starts against the Padres in 2011, Kennedy was 3-0 with a 1.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio struck out four and held Houston to one run and five hits over seven innings, but he didn't get a decision in his return from injury Sunday. He relied on his fastball and can really be effective if he works in his slider at the right times.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson got the win against the Giants last Saturday when he allowed four runs in 6 2/3 innings. The outing took a turn with two outs in the seventh when he allowed a two-run homer to Brett Pill. He was 1-2 with a 3.72 ERA against the Rockies in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin threw 90 pitches and issued five walks in four innings of his initial 2012 start, a 7-0 loss to the Giants in the home opener. A mechanical issue of his body getting ahead of his arm arose and robbed him of arm-side command.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter suffered through a tough spring and his woes continued into his first regular-season start. He allowed six runs (five earned) in three innings last Sunday against the Giants. The D-backs think Collmenter may have been pressing.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies had Pomeranz throw four innings for Double-A Tulsa on Tuesday as a tuneup. He didn't give up a run, although he had problems controlling the movement of his fastball. The Rockies will be careful with Pomeranz, a rookie, all season.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill had an odd start in his first outing with the D-backs on Tuesday night. He walked six, but he managed to allow just one run over six innings and none of the walks wound up scoring. Cahill said he "had no idea" where the ball was going.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders was impressive in his first start of the year, as he tossed seven shutout innings against the Padres at Petco Park. The left-hander allowed four hits and walked two while striking out four. Saunders did not face the Pirates in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Veteran lefty signed to set a pace for a young staff certainly has, but only in hard-luck losses. Seeks to avoid a repeat of last season's 0-4 start.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy beat the Padres in his last start allowing just one run on five hits over six innings. One of his finest starts of 2011 came against the Pirates when he fanned 12 and allowed one hit in eight shutout innings.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens has endured rough first innings in both of his starts before settling down, and it upset him enough to make a point of changing his mindset.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson suffered through a miserable start on Friday against the Rockies. He had trouble finding his release point and couldn't get in rhythm, allowing six runs in 3 2/3 innings. Last year in two starts vs. the Pirates, Hudson was 0-1 with 3.00 ERA
away_pitcher_note: Two straight solid starts to begin the season is a welcome novelty for McDonald, still considered the difference-maker for the Pirates staff.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter has struggled in his first two starts of the season. He lasted three innings in his first start and four in his second. Considering he also had a poor spring, it's possible he could be pitching for his spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Minor produced the finest start of his young career as he limited the Brewers to two hits in 7 1/3 innings his last time out. This marked the first time he had worked into the eighth inning. He has improved as his confidence has grown.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill bounced back from a six-walk outing in his first D-backs start by throwing 7 1/3 innings against the Rockies on Sunday. He earned his first win of the season by allowing just one earned run on four hits. Cahill has never faced the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Beachy aggressively attacked hitters while throwing just 46 pitches in the final four innings of Sunday's start against the Brewers. He allowed three hits while lasting seven innings for just the third time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: After leaving Spring Training with 7.98 ERA, Saunders has dominated in first two starts of the season. He got his first win Monday, against the Pirates, limiting the Bucs to one run on six hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson showed more velocity with his fastball and was in command for most of the season-high seven innings pitched against the Mets on Monday. But he was doomed by a hanging curveball that resulted in a sixth-inning home run.

home_pitcher_note: Winner of 15 of his last 16 decisions, Kennedy is coming off a subpar outing by his own standards in allowing eight hits and four runs through six innings in a no-decision against the Pirates on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado has won his first two starts of the year and three of four dating back to last year. The 22-year-old is still primarily a fastball-changeup pitcher. He is trying to gain confidence in a curve he occasionally shows.

home_pitcher_note: With Daniel Hudson on the disabled list, the D-backs will turn to reliever Wade Miley for Monday's opener with the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Kyle Kendrick will fill in for Cliff Lee, whom the Phillies placed on the 15-day disabled list on Saturday for a strained left oblique. It will be Kendrick's first start of the season. He started 15 games and went 8-6 with a 3.22 ERA last season.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter took the loss on Thursday against the Braves but turned in a much better outing than in his first two starts. He gave up four earned runs on six hits through 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Worley struck out a career-high 11 in seven innings and picked up his first victory of the season on Thursday against the Padres. He also dealt through vision issues when his goggles got foggy.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing just two runs in his first two starts for the D-backs, Cahill gave up seven to the Braves on Friday. Only four were earned, but Cahill took his first loss of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Returning to his hometown San Diego in his last start, Hamels battled, allowing a run and six hits in six innings against the Padres. He struck out four, walked one and was called for two balks.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano has strung together three straight quality starts, and yet the right-hander seeks his first win. He suffered a hard-luck loss at Washington in his last outing, giving up one run on two hits in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders was a hard-luck loser Saturday against the Braves. He threw seven solid innings, allowing just two earned runs on six hits. Through 21 innings this season, Saunders has given up three earned runs total.

home_pitcher_note: Dominating is the best way to describe Sanchez's first three games, yet he has just one win. In 19 1/3 innings, he has 19 strikeouts and just four walks. He's scattered 16 hits, and has two straight no-decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy snapped the D-backs' five-game losing streak on Sunday, pitching seven innings vs. the Braves and giving up three earned runs on nine hits. He hasn't lost a regular-season decision since Aug. 18 against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: It was the Josh Johnson of old in his last start, but the ace wasn't rewarded with a win. JJ had a no-decision after allowing one run and striking out nine in 6 2/3 innings. JJ exited with the lead. His last win remains April 19, 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Miley started in place of the injured Daniel Hudson on Monday and tossed six shutout innings against the Phillies. He made the team thanks to a strong Spring Training, and his first three appearances of the year were in relief.

home_pitcher_note: All four of Buehrle's outings have been quality starts, yet the veteran has one win and three losses. Buehrle is coming off a tough setback at New York, giving up two runs in seven innings. He has never faced Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin will be making his Major League debut. He is taking the place of Josh Collmenter, who was sent to the bullpen. Corbin was impressive in Spring Training, and in his first four starts for Double-A Mobile, he had a 1.67 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann tossed six innings against the Padres to earn his first win in his last start. He allowed one run on four hits, striking out six and not issuing a walk, and also drove in a run with a single.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill allowed four runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Phillies in his last outing. He's lost his last two starts while allowing eight earned runs in 11 innings. In his first two starts, he allowed two runs in 13 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rebounding nicely from his previous start, in which he gave up five runs in the first inning, Jackson threw 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Padres, marking the eighth time in 19 games that a Washington starter had blanked the opposition.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is coming off his third career shutout and perhaps his finest outing as a pro, as he handcuffed the Marlins in Miami. He lost his only start at Nationals Park last year after allowing four runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler pitched six innings, allowing three runs on five hits against the Dodgers on Friday. He had a tough time stopping Matt Kemp and Andre Either, who went a combined 4-for-6 against the southpaw.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy said after his last outing that he's felt like he's had his "C stuff" in each of his starts this year. The right-hander left his outing against the Marlins with a 2-0 lead, but the bullpen was unable to close it out.

home_pitcher_note: Gee threw a career-high 116 pitches in last Saturday's win over the Rockies, escaping an early jam to last seven innings. But his next start will come against the D-backs at Citi Field, where he is 0-2 with a 7.50 ERA so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has been outstanding both as a reliever and starter. He replaced the injured Daniel Hudson in the rotation and has not allowed an earned run in 12 1/3 innings. In his last outing against the Marlins, he allowed one unearned run in 6 1/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Not counting Santana's one poor outing in Atlanta, he is 0-1 with an 0.79 ERA in four starts, with 29 strikeouts and 10 walks in 22 1/3 innings. He is 2-0 with an 0.62 ERA in four career starts vs. the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin was called up from Double-A Mobile to replace Josh Collmenter in the rotation, and in his first start, he allowed three runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings in Miami. Corbin pitched his way into the club's plans with a strong Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey took a no-hitter into the sixth inning of his last start in Houston. Dickey got a no-decision, working six innings while allowing three runs on three hits. He struck out six and walked two.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill had his finest outing in a D-backs uniform when he held the Nats to one run on six hits in 7 1/3 innings. At times this year, Cahill has struggled with his command, but he seemed to put it together in Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders had to battle in his start against the Nats in Washington. The left-hander allowed two runs on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings. Saunders made his lone career start against the Cards last season, and tossed five one-hit innings to get the win.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn became the NL's first five-game winner in his last start. He retired 15 straight at one point and continues to baffle hitters with his three fastballs and two offspeed pitches. Lynn has allowed more than one run in a game only once.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy felt like he had his best stuff of the year his last time out, but wound up dropping his first regular-season decision since Aug. 18, 2011, a span of 12 starts. He allowed two runs on four hits over seven innings vs. the Nats in a 2-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook allowed as many earned runs in his last outing (four) as he had in his first four starts combined. That was largely due to elevated pitches and a so-so sinker. Westbrook is 3-0 this season against teams not from Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Miley will be making his fourth start since taking Daniel Hudson's spot in the rotation. In his last start against the Mets, he allowed four runs in six innings, with all of the runs coming in the third. Miley has also made three relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse was tagged with his first loss of the year at Houston, May 4. He lasted five frames giving up a season-high seven hits. For the second start in a row, Lohse allowed three earned runs. He'd allowed three total in his previous four starts starts.
