away_pitcher_note: Francis gave up five runs in five innings in his last start, at San Diego, but left the game with the lead, although he didn't figure in the decision. Francis had given up three or fewer runs his previous six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miley picked up his 11th win of the season on Saturday against the Astros, making him the winningest rookie pitcher in D-backs history. He allowed just one run over seven innings and struck out a career-high nine batters in the process.
away_pitcher_note: It will be the Major League debut for the 23-year-old right-hander, the Mets' first-round pick, seventh overall, in the 2010 Draft. Harvey made 20 starts for Triple-A Buffalo and went 7-5 with a 3.68 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter rejoined the rotation when Trevor Bauer was returned to Triple-A. After struggling in his first four starts, Collmenter has a 1.51 ERA in 15 games (four starts). He beat the Astros in his last start, allowing two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Niese delivered his second consecutive quality start on Sunday, holding the Dodgers to three runs on eight hits in seven innings of work.  He took the no-decision as New York went on to lose in 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has started to look like the 2011 version of himself after an inconsistent beginning to 2012. In 16 innings over his last two outings, Kennedy has allowed just three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Young didn't allow a hit over his final six innings on Monday after surrendering two first-inning runs.  He struck out seven in what was his second consecutive start against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has pitched well in three starts since coming off the disabled list. In those outings, he has a 3.79 ERA. In his last start against the Rockies, he allowed two runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey allowed four earned runs in six innings against the Nationals on Tuesday, scattering eight hits in just his second loss of the season. In five starts in July, the knuckleballer has allowed 19 earned runs in 26 1/3 innings, for a 6.49 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Aaron Harang deserved a better fate in St. Louis, allowing only two hits in 7 1/3 innings but coming away with a no-decision. He had a rough time in his only start against the D-backs this year, allowing five runs on nine hits in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill continued his first inning struggles in his last outing against the Rockies. In surrendering one early run, the 24-year-old lifted his season total in the opening frame to 17 earned runs in 20 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chris Capuano will try to rebound from his worst start of the season against the Cardinals, although most of the hits were flares and bouncers. But he admitted that as the game wore on, he "got sloppy with my location."
away_pitcher_note: Miley pitched well enough to win his last start, vs. the Mets, but he got only one run of support in his sixth loss of the year and third in his last five starts. Since the All-Star break, he hasn't given up more than three runs in a start.

home_pitcher_note: Rookie Stephen Fife is the fifth starter as of this writing, although the club is trying to add one via trade. He's made two Major League starts, drawing All-Star opponents Roy Halladay and Matt Cain, and outpitched both in no-decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin, who will be recalled and join the D-backs' rotation while Josh Collmenter returns to the bullpen, is 0-1 with a 3.24 ERA is two appearances (one start) against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Joe Blanton was originally slated to pitch, but he was traded to the Dodgers, so Kendrick makes his first start since July 6.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy appears to be finally hitting his stride. He is 3-0 with a 2.42 ERA in his last three starts. Last time out against the Mets, Kennedy allowed three runs, all of which came on solo homers by Ike Davis.

home_pitcher_note: In his third start back after a seven-week stint on the DL, Halladay struggled early against Atlanta. Doc allowed three runs on six hits -- two home runs -- over seven innings. A positive sign is that he set down the last 10 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is an innings-eater who has lasted at least six innings in his last seven starts. In four starts since coming off the disabled list, Saunders has a 4.15 ERA. This will be Saunders' first appearance against the Phillies this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lee looked like his old self in his last outing, shutting out the Nationals over seven innings on Tuesday to earn just his second win. The former Cy Young Award winner allowed just five hits, struck out seven and walked only one.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill has struggled to find consistency this year. He pitched well in his last start, as he allowed just one run on six hits over six innings against the Dodgers. He allowed four runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Phillies on April 25.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard's stuff doesn't square with his numbers, one reason he keeps getting the ball. But the fact is while pitching for a contender, the lefty leads the Majors in losses. Hasn't lasted five innings in half of his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miley was outstanding in his last start against the Dodgers. He allowed just one run -- a homer by Mark Ellis -- over eight innings while striking out seven and walking one. He tossed six shutout innings against the Phillies on April 23.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens goes after his fifth straight win -- across seven starts -- hoping this start vs. Arizona is healthier than the first: He left an April 17 start in Phoenix with shoulder inflammation that would keep him out for more than two months.
away_pitcher_note: Promoted from Triple-A Reno to start Wednesday, Corbin combined with three relievers to throw a two-hit shutout against the Dodgers. The left-hander lasted six innings, striking out five and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander ousted from the rotation two weeks ago gets to make a cameo start, in search of a seventh straight victory, no less. He has a 4-2 record at home, with an ERA (3.62) nearly two runs better than on the road (5.34).
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy beat the Phillies on Friday to extend his winning streak to four consecutive starts. He wasn't at his best, but allowed just two runs on seven hits over six innings. He struck out only one and issued two walks.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty makes his first PNC Park start since his July 24 trade from Houston. He comes off a sharp start against the Reds, in which in seven innings he allowed three runs -- two of them on a home run by his pitching opponent (Mat Latos).
away_pitcher_note: Saunders pitched well in his last outing, allowing just two runs over 6 1/3 innings against the Phillies. Unfortunately for him, he faced Roy Halladay, who blanked the D-backs in a 3-0 Arizona loss.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill pitched well his last time out, against the Phils, allowing three runs over seven innings, though he wound up with a no-decision. Cahill faced the Nats earlier this year and got the win after allowing one run on six hits over 7 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg was back on his game Sunday against Miami, striking out six Marlins and allowing only three hits over six scoreless innings. The young ace has thrown 127 1/3 innings on the season, and his 11.3 strikeouts-per-nine leads the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Miley has pitched his way into consideration for the NL Rookie of the Year Award. In his most recent outing, he did not get a decision but allowed just one unearned run in six innings. He has allowed one earned run in his last 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson struck out eight Monday in Houston, but he worked up his pitch count to 106, cutting his night down to just 5 1/3 innings. He has lasted 5 2/3 and 5 1/3 innings in his past two starts, respectively, but threw more than 105 pitches each time.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin has made two starts since being called up from Triple-A for his third stint with the D-backs this season and has allowed just two runs over six innings in those outings. He has never faced the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Detwiler put together another dominant seven-inning start Tuesday in Houston, inducing 12 ground-ball outs with his power sinker and four-seam fastball. The lefty has a 2.55 ERA since June 24, and the Nats have gone 6-2 in those eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly's rotation spot could be lost when Jaime Garcia comes off the DL, and Kelly's last start didn't help his case to stay. He allowed a career-worst seven runs (four earned) and failed to go more than six innings for the first time since June 16.
away_pitcher_note: After posting four straight quality starts, Kennedy struggled his last time out against the Pirates. The D-backs gave him a two-run lead in the first, but he surrendered five runs on eight hits over four innings for his ninth loss of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright has recently looked much like the ace he once was. His record is even for the first time this season and his ERA has not been lower since 2010. In his last five starts (36 1/3 innings), Wainwright has allowed just seven earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders continues to put together a strong second half of the season. The veteran lefty hasn't allowed more than four runs in a start since May 13. Moreover, he has pitched at least five innings in every outing since May 7.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse allowed just one run in seven innings, but he was outdueled by Phillies starter Roy Halladay in a 3-1 loss at Citizens Bank Park in his last start. The Cardinals have won seven of his last nine starts as he has gone 6-0 with a 2.52 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Since moving to 6-7 on July 2, Cahill has alternated each start since with a win then a  loss. The good news for Arizona is Cahill is slated for a win after losing to the Nats his last time out. He allowed four earned runs and six hits over six.

home_pitcher_note: Since losing his last four starts in July, Keuchel has a 3.75 ERA in two starts in August but is still searching for his second career win. He hasn't won his since throwing a complete game against Cleveland on June 23.
away_pitcher_note: For the second consecutive game in which Miley has started, the D-backs committed three errors on Saturday with the NL Rookie of the Year candidate on the mound. Miley surrendered six runs, but only four were earned as he lasted just 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles is beginning to gain some consistency and stay away from the big inning. In his last two starts, he's allowed just 11 hits and struck out 11 in 14 innings. He hasn't won since June 26, a span of eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin is in his third stint with the D-backs this year. In three starts since his last recall, he is 2-0 with a 1.89 ERA. Last time out against the Nationals, Corbin allowed just two runs on four hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga finally got the walks under control in his most recent start, on Monday against the Cubs, but he was burned by a pair of two-run homers. He's yet to pitch deeper than 5 1/3 innings in four starts with Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has struggled to find consistency this year after winning 21 games in 2011. After winning four straight starts and compiling a 2.54 ERA, Kennedy pitched poorly in his next two starts. He has allowed an NL high 23 homers.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders' left-hand was hit by a comebacker in his last start, but he should be ready to go on Monday. The left-hander gave up five runs over six innings in that start, the most runs he's given up since May.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to a seven-inning, two-run effort his last time out, Buehrle earned his first win in six starts and snapped a three-decision skid. The win gave him 10 in a season for the 12th straight year, tying CC Sabathia for the longest active streak.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill was solid in his last outing, going six innings and allowing one run on five hits against the Cardinals. He has given up 12 homers in his last 11 starts, but didn't give up one on Thursday in St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco pitched a complete game in his last start, but lost, 5-3, to the Rockies at Coors Field. He threw 74 of 107 pitches for strikes, and tied his season high with seven strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Angels in the 2010 trade for Dan Haren, Skaggs will make his long anticipated Major League debut on Wednesday. In nine starts at Triple-A Reno this season, Skaggs boasted a 2.91 ERA with 45 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Tigers in July, Turner will make his Marlins debut in Game 1. If he remains in the Majors, it will be decided partly by how he performs. He started three games for Detroit. At New Orleans, he was 2-0 (1.98) in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Armed with a sub-3.00 ERA, Miley will try continue his run as a surprise candidate for National League Rookie of the Year. In his last outing, the left-hander allowed just one run over six innings against the Astros to earn his 13th victory.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc works the second game of the doubleheader. Run support was an issue for him in his first three starts. He gave up only one run in each, but he had one win. At Colorado his last time out, he gave up five in five innings, picking up the win.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin is 3-0 in four starts since rejoining the D-backs from Triple-A Reno. His last time out, he allowed four runs over seven innings in a win against the Astros. Corbin allowed one run in a 4 1/3-inning relief stint against the Padres this year.
away_pitcher_note: Stults gave up five runs in six innings in a no-decision against the Giants on Saturday. That broke a streak of six straight outings of giving up two runs or less. Stults had given up just one run in 13 innings over two starts prior to that outing.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has battled inconsistency throughout 2012. In his last start, he allowed one earned run in six innings against the Astros. Kennedy is 6-0 with a 2.34 ERA in nine career starts against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Richard is coming off a typically strong outing, as he turned in eight innings and allowed no earned runs, while throwing 72 strikes in 111 pitches. His 176 innings were tops in the NL as of Sunday, and his 15 quality starts lead the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill gets the call with Joe Saunders -- who was originally scheduled to make this start -- traded to Orioles earlier Sunday. Cahill will look to pick up his first win since July 30 against a Padres team he lost to on July 2.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez tied his season high with 10 strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings in a 3-1 win over Pittsburgh. It marked the first time in four outings that Volquez had gone beyond the fourth inning.

home_pitcher_note: The D-backs traded Joe Saunders on Sunday to make room for Skaggs in the rotation. The highly regarded lefty will make his second Major League start Monday after earning a win his first time out, giving up just two runs on three hits against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo retired his first 14 batters and 22 of 23 vs. the Phillies on Wednesday. He had all of his pitches working as he kept his sinker moving and had all sorts of off-speed stuff to keep Philadelphia hitters uncomfortable.

home_pitcher_note: Miley, likely a front runner for the National League Rookie of the Year award, will continue his candidacy coming off a stellar outing in his last start. The lefty shut out the Marlins over eight innings to earn his 14th win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto did not pitch at least six innings on Thursday vs. the Phils for the first time since July 8. He was in line for the win when he left after five-plus innings with a 3-0 lead, and victimized by a blown save for the first time all season.

home_pitcher_note: Since allowing just four earned runs over his first three starts after being called up from Triple-A Reno on Aug. 1, Corbin has struggled in his last two outings. The lefty has allowed four earned runs in consecutive starts, tossing just 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The wheels simply came off during Latos' previous outing vs. the Cardinals when he gave up seven runs over five-plus innings. Six of those runs, including two homers, came in the sixth inning, when he did not retire a batter.

home_pitcher_note: He hasn't been as overpowering as he was in last year's second half, but Kershaw has won five of his last six decisions and should receive some consideration for a Cy Young repeat.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy took his first career loss against the Padres in his last start, surrendering six earned runs and serving up three solo home runs in the process. Since the All-Star break, Kennedy has given up 14 long balls.

home_pitcher_note: Seeking his 10th win, Harang allowed two home runs to the Marlins. No shame in having Giancarlo Stanton go deep, but his big mistake was a two-run homer by Rob Brantly, his first in the Major Leagues.
away_pitcher_note: Lasting just 3 2/3 innings his last time out, Cahill surrendered four runs on eight hits to the Padres in his shortest outing in over a year. The right-hander hasn't won since July 30, when he beat the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett had an adequate Dodgers debut at Coors Field, allowing three runs and one solo homer in 5 2/3 innings. He's no longer overpowering but has a varied arsenal of pitches the Dodgers hope will keep games close.
away_pitcher_note: Hindered by an error and a home run by Reds pitcher Bronson Arroyo, Skaggs took the first loss of his career in his second Major League start in his last outing. The lefty has given up just four combined earned runs in his two starts, however.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano's numbers have declined after a hot start to the season. He has gone 2-7 with a 5.20 ERA in his last 10 starts and he allowed six runs in six innings in his last appearance. His ERA has risen from 2.62 to 3.58 over those 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has worked his way into the NL Rookie of the Year discussion. He deserved a better fate in his last start against the Reds when he allowed three runs in seven innings. In his two start prior to that, he allowed just one run over 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zito's 2 1/3-inning effort last Wednesday at Houston was his shortest start since a 1 2/3-inning outing at Arizona on April 16, 2011, when he sprained his right foot. Zito's 5-5 with a 4.14 ERA at AT&T Park this year.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin was cruising along in his last start as he held the Reds to two hits through 6 1/3 innings. Things unraveled for him in the seventh and the Reds scored three runs on a pair of homers en route to a 6-2 win.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong has pitched six innings or more in 23 of his 25 outings. The Giants are 17-8 when he starts. Only once has he allowed more than one home run in a game. With his next victory, he'll match the personal best he reached last year.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy was masterful in his last start against the Dodgers as he tossed 6 1/3 scoreless innings to outduel Clayton Kershaw. In two starts against the Giants this year, Kennedy is 2-0 with a 2.51 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs scored five runs off Bumgarner last Friday, his second straight start in which he has allowed at least four earned runs. He has a 2.15 ERA at AT&T Park compared to a 3.93 ERA on the road and has posted a 2.71 ERA in 10 second-half starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill has not won since July 30 when he beat the Dodgers. Since then, he is 0-2 with a 5.08 ERA. This year in two starts against the Giants, Cahill is 0-2 with a 6.17 ERA. He allowed four runs over six innings at AT&T Park earlier this year.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner makes his first start since July 3, the day he suffered a strained right lat muscle that caused him to miss 51 games. He'll likely go five or so innings or 70 pitches. He started the season in the bullpen, but moved into the rotation in June.
away_pitcher_note: Skaggs will be making his fourth Major League start. He was acquired from the Angels in a Trade Deadline deal in 2010. The left-hander allowed one run over five innings against the Dodgers in Los Angeles in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: After tossing six shutout innings in his Major League debut, Kelly had trouble at Coors Field the last time out, allowing two home runs and five earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. He did limit all of his damage to one inning, a seven-run third inning.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has pitched his way into consideration for the NL Rookie of the Year Award. In his last four starts, he has a 2.28 ERA. Last time out against the Dodgers, Miley allowed three runs over 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Werner has been a hit since joining the team last month, allowing two runs in six innings in each of his first three starts. He struck out a career-high eight the last time out and befuddled the Dodgers with a sneaky fastball, changeup and slider.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin gave up four first-inning runs to the Giants in his last start but didn't yield another in his next four innings. He struggled in late August, but was 3-2 for the month. One of the losses was a four-inning, four-run showing against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has struggled to find consistency this year after winning 21 games in 2011. He allowed five runs on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings in his last start against the Giants. In his last start vs. the Dodgers, he allowed no runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers' ace was scratched on Sunday due to a sore hip that required a cortisone shot, but L.A. is hopeful that Kershaw will be able to take the mound on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill carried a no-hitter into the seventh in his last start, ultimately finishing with 6 1/3 innings of two-run ball against the Giants. That was a good start to September after an August that saw him go 0-2 with a 5.08 ERA in six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Aaron Harang allowed the first three hitters he faced to score in a loss to the Padres, then pitched out of trouble each of the next four innings in a game the bullpen lost. He's keeping the ball in the park, but his walks are up.

home_pitcher_note: Skaggs will be making his fifth Major League start against the Giants. He allowed five runs over in three innings at San Diego his last time out after working at least five innings in his first three starts.
away_pitcher_note: An errant changeup led to a wild pitch that cost Cain and the Giants a big run in his last start, when he allowed two runs in seven innings against the Dodgers. Cain is 12-0 this season when the Giants provide three or more runs in support.

home_pitcher_note: Miley has pitched his way into contention for NL Rookie of the Year honors. He got the win last time out against the Padres despite allowing five runs over 5 1/3 innings. His lone appearance vs. Giants this year was a four-inning relief stint.
away_pitcher_note: In one of his biggest wins as a Giant, Zito pitched 6 1/3 innings last time out in a 4-0 victory against the Dodgers and a three-game series win. The Giants have now won seven straight Zito starts even with his 4.53 ERA in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin allowed three runs over 5 1/3 innings in his last start against the Padres. He took the loss and has dropped his last three decisions. In two starts against the Giants, Corbin is 1-0 with a 3.75 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong is mired in a six-game stretch that has seen him post 9.56 ERA. On Monday, he missed locations on his arm side, after struggling glove-side in his previous start. He finished strong, though, retiring eight of his last 10 batters faced.

home_pitcher_note: Since August, Kennedy has alternated dominant outings with poor ones. Against the Padres and Giants, the right-hander allowed a combined 11 earned runs in just 11 innings. But in two starts versus the Dodgers, he tossed 13 2/3 scoreless frames.
away_pitcher_note: Stults doesn't have enough innings to qualify for the ERA lead, but he has a 2.57 ERA as a starter in the second half and has been one of the Padres most dependable starters, using a big curveball and a sneaky fastball to get a bevy of grounders.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill threw a shutout against the Padres on June 3, but since then, San Diego has beat the right-hander twice. In those two starts, Cahill allowed a combined eight runs in just 9 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching for the first time in 10 days, Volquez - who missed a start with a nagging blister - defeated the Cardinals in his last start, even though he walked six. Oddly enough, he's walked six twice in starts this season and won both games.

home_pitcher_note: Skaggs surrendered a combined five earned runs in his first three Major League starts but since then he has given up 10 runs in two outings. The Padres beat the rookie on Sept. 7, knocking him out after three frames.
away_pitcher_note: Richard picked up a win his last start, on his 29th birthday no less. It capped a hectic week as his wife gave birth to a son, Cashton. Richard has made all 30 of his starts. He's won five consecutive home starts but will be tested at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: The education of Pomeranz has been difficult. He has pitched as many as five innings just twice in his last 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Still in the hunt for National League Rookie of the Year, Miley pitched well enough to win his last time out, but fell victim to little run support. The lefty tossed seven innings, allowing three earned runs against the Giants, but lost.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has been one of Colorado's best starting pitchers since he returned August 21 from a right pectoral injury that forced him onto the disabled list for more than three months. In six starts since coming off the DL, Chacin has a 2.37 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin was dominant in his last start, holding the Giants to two runs in eight innings while striking out five. The last time the rookie faced the Rockies was back in May, when he surrendered six runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Francis stayed mostly ahead of hitters for five solid innings and held the Giants to two runs on six hits in his last start. However, he received no run support and absorbed the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching with the stuff that made him a 20-game winner a season ago, Kennedy has won three consecutive decisions. Over his last two outings, the D-backs ace has given up just one run in a combined 15 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood gave up three runs on eight hits in four innings in San Francisco Wednesday, with all of his runs coming in the first on a back-foot slider to Pablo Sandobal that would have hit his foot if he hadn't swung at it and sent it over the fence.
away_pitcher_note: Since going winless through August, Cahill has won his first three starts in September, throwing at least six innings each time. In 19 1/3 combined innings this month, the right-hander has surrendered just six runs.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum originally was scheduled to start Sunday, but received additional rest after the Giants clinched the NL West on Saturday. The two-time Cy Young Award winner has made seven quality starts in his last 10 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter is getting the start in place of Tyler Skaggs, who was scratched Monday night. Collmenter has made nine starts this year, but his last was on July 27. He is 3-2 with a 5.83 ERA as a starter and owns a 1.32 ERA in 17 relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Cain continued his excellence on the mound with an eight-inning effort in his last outing, holding the Rockies to one run on four hits. He improved to 5-0 with a 2.50 ERA in his last eight starts as he picked up his career-best 15th win of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Miley continues to make a case for himself for National League Rookie of the Year. In his last start, he allowed five runs in six innings to the Rockies at Coors Field but managed to come away with a win.

home_pitcher_note: Zito held the Rockies to two runs in 5 2/3 innings last Thursday, and the Giants have won in his last nine outings. The start was his 15th of the year in which he allowed two earned runs or fewer, which he has done in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin struggled to locate his offspeed stuff last time out against the Rockies at Coors Field and allowed five runs on nine hits in three innings. He faced the Giants the start before that and allowed just two runs in eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy pitched better than his numbers would indicate last time out against the Rockies at Coors Field. Kennedy allowed four runs on nine hits in six innings. In his two starts before that, Kennedy allowed one run in 15 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wood lasted only five innings in his previous start but didn't pitch all that poorly. A bases-loaded jam in the first inning hindered his pitch count, but he allowed only one run. He is 1-2 with a 5.51 ERA in his career against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill took the loss in his last start as he allowed two runs in six innings against the Rockies at Coors Field. Prior to that, Cahill had won three straight starts and had a 2.79 ERA in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Germano lost his last time out, giving up four runs on 10 hits in 5 2/3 innings against the Cardinals. He's pitched into the fifth inning in all but one of his 10 starts. The righty has a 5.24 ERA in five career games (four starts) against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter started in place of Tyler Skaggs last Tuesday against the Giants and earned the win allowing one run on two hits over five innings. Collmenter has made 10 starts this year and 17 relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Rusin will try to end the 2012 season on a positive note as well as give the Cubs something to remember when thinking about next year's rotation. The lefty gave up six runs over 3 2/3 innings in his last outing vs. the Rockies at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Miley looks to finish his season on a strong note after struggling in his last four outings. Miley has a 6.45 ERA over that span as his ERA has risen from 2.90 to 3.32. A good final start would help his chances to win the NL Rookie of the Year Award.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz held the Cubs scoreless for five innings, struck out three and gave up three hits and three walks while earning a win at Coors Field in his last start. It was Pomeranz's first win since July 6.

home_pitcher_note: After surrendering a combined 11 earned runs over six innings in his last two starts, Corbin will look to finish his rookie campaign on a high note. The lefty gave up five runs on nine hits the last time he saw the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin pitched five innings for the win against the Cubs on Thursday, yielding three runs on seven hits and four walks. He was effective when low in the zone, but he let hitters off the hook up in the zone when he had them at two strikes.

home_pitcher_note: With a win on Friday, Kennedy became the fourth pitcher in franchise history to record back-to-back 15-win seasons. The D-backs' ace joined Randy Johnson, Curt Schilling and Brandon Webb. Kennedy's latest start also pushed him over 200 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Francis joined the Rockies in June after beginning the year in Triple-A with the Reds and has generally pitched well, but struggled vs. the Dodgers in his last outing. Francis hopes for a good final outing, and is looking to re-sign with Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy was disappointed in his 2013 season, and it motivated him throughout the offseason. He has spent the spring making sure his breaking ball is ready in April. This will be his third straight Opening Day start.
away_pitcher_note: The Opening Day start will be Wainwright's third, but rain washed one out. With Chris Carpenter gone, Wainwright is the clear leader of this pitching staff. And another year from surgery, he expects to be more consistent.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill reported to Spring Training having lost around 15 pounds from last season, the result of some dietary changes. Last season, he faced the Cardinals once and allowed one run over six innings, but did not get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Following a season in which he had shoulder problems, Garcia reported to Spring Training healthy and looked strong in six starts. He can be a formidable No. 2 starter but will need to pitch better away from home.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy will be making his first start in a D-backs uniform after signing a two-year deal as a free agent during the offseason. McCarthy has spent the past seven years in the American League and has never faced the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: An 18-game winner last season, Lynn is beginning his second full year in the Cardinals rotation. He has a different look this year, though, after shedding 40 pounds over the winter in an effort to improve his stamina.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse will test the value of Spring Training. Two weeks ago, he was throwing simulated games against Scottsdale Community College. Now, having signed a three-year contract, he will open the year as the Crew's No. 4 starter.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off an impressive season that saw him finish second in the National League Rookie of the Year voting behind the Nationals' Bryce Harper, Miley makes his 2013 debut in the D-backs' road opener against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers' late-season fade in 2012 began with an eight-run stinker against the Rockies on Aug. 13, but now he gets another chance. Chris Narveson's move to relief opened a spot in the Opening Day rotation for 27-year-old Fiers.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin won the fifth spot in the D-backs' rotation by outperforming top prospect Tyler Skaggs and Randall Delgado in Spring Training. The left-hander finished camp with a 2.81 ERA over 25 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo goes from facing a team (the Rockies) who he's never defeated to another (the D-backs) who he's never lost to. He's 7-0 with a 1.09 ERA in nine starts against Arizona, including two games in the 2011 postseason.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy won his second consecutive Opening Day start by tossing seven innings and allowing just two earned runs to the Cardinals on Monday. The D-backs ace went 1-1 against the Brewers last season, with the win coming in Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill was cruising along in his first start of the year against the Cardinals before hitting a wall in the sixth. Cahill gave up a pair of runs in the sixth on a homer by Matt Holliday and allowed three runs in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: When Rodriguez won his season debut, it gave him six wins in a 35-game stretch dating to August, compared with five combined for other Bucs starters. He was brilliant in that debut, blanking the Cubs on two hits for 6 2/3.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy struggled in his D-backs debut, but after the game went 16 innings, many forgot at the end that he had even started. McCarthy allowed six runs on nine hits in five innings against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: McDonald was very encouraging in his first start of the season, allowing the Cubs two hits and one run in seven innings and retiring 13 of the last 14 men he faced. He's still trying to conquer road woes (career 14-20 with 5.30 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Miley struggled a bit during the spring, battling a dead arm for a stretch, but he showed no ill effects in his first start of the regular season. Miley held the Brewers to one run over six innings with eight strikeouts to get the win.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching aggressively without any thoughts of mechanics is paying off for the lefty. Including Spring Training and his first start, has walked three in his last 15 2/3 innings -- the most in-control stretch of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin served up eight hits and walked a batter his first time out against the Brewers but minimized the damage well, allowing just two earned runs over six innings to earn the win. Corbin went 1-1 in three starts vs. the Dodgers last season.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw has been nothing short of spectacular in his first two outings, allowing just six hits over 16 scoreless innings. In 14 career starts vs. the D-backs, he's 7-5 with a 2.25 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After striking out eight batters over seven innings in the opener, Kennedy struggled a bit in his last outing, surrendering four earned runs in six innings at Milwaukee. Kennedy allowed just two runs over 19 2/3 innings vs. the Dodgers last year.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing 10 hits in his first start, Ryu cut it down to three vs. the Pirates. He is new to the Majors but pitches like a veteran, even if his fastball would be more effective if he came inside more.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill had a disappointing start his last time out against the Pirates, allowing three first-inning runs and four overall in five innings. Cahill is in better shape this year, having dropped 12-15 pounds during the offseason.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett has allowed four home runs in 11 innings, which clearly is the major red flag after two outings. He's no longer the flamethrower he once was, but he was able to retire 10 consecutive Padres at one point during his last start in San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Nova returns to the rotation after his most recent planned start was rained out. He struggled in his season debut, on April 5 in Detroit, allowing four runs in 4 2/3 innings and not attacking hitters well.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy's last start was frustrating for him. He felt like he had great stuff, but he was unhappy with his pitch selection. He allowed five runs in the fourth, and after that, he mixed his pitches better and had better results.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia's fastball may still be down a few ticks, averaging 90 mph this season, but he is making it work, and he held the Tigers and Orioles to one earned run over his last 15 innings, with 13 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has picked right up where he left off in 2012, when he finished second in the NL Rookie of the Year voting. Last time out against the Pirates at Chase Field, Miley allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes couldn't remember a worse start than his previous one -- the Orioles slugged three homers and knocked him out in the fourth inning. He was slowed this spring by a back injury and hasn't yet looked ready for prime time.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin had one of the best starts of his young career last time, outdueling Dodgers lefty Clayton Kershaw. Corbin tossed six shutout innings as the D-backs beat L.A., 3-0. This will be his first start against the AL.

home_pitcher_note: After being spotted to a big early lead, Chacin began to labor and fight his control. but in the end, he looked good -- five innings, four hits, two runs and three strikeouts against two walks. Chacin has had three strong starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy was not happy with himself following his last outing against the Dodgers. It started out well, but Kennedy allowed two runs in the fifth and three in the sixth. Overall, he was touched for six runs in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Placing his slider and changeup and working in sync with catcher Yorvit Torrealba, De La Rosa struck out seven in six scoreless innings at San Diego in his last start, earning his first win since May 13, 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill was impressive in his last outing against the Dodgers. After struggling in his first two starts, he rebounded to shut out the Dodgers for 7 1/3 innings. Cahill did not get the decision in a 1-0 Arizona win.

home_pitcher_note: The righty has pitched five innings in each of his past two starts, including Tuesday, when he gave up six hits and four runs to the Mets (including two homers to David Wright). Nicasio has nine walks and nine strikeouts in 16 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy has struggled in his three starts for the D-backs after signing as a free agent during the offseason. He took the loss against the Yankees in his last start and was done in by a Robinson Cano three-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong recorded the Giants' lone quality start during the three-game series sweep they absorbed at Milwaukee last week. His only flaw in that outing was his inability to avoid the big hit. Three of the five hits he yielded went for extra bases.
away_pitcher_note: Miley pitched six shutout innings against the Yankees, then unraveled in the seventh, giving up a two-out double, walking the bases loaded, walking in a run, and allowing two more on a single en route to a 4-3 D-backs' loss.

home_pitcher_note: A trio of two-run homers by Milwaukee on Wednesday -- one in each of the first three innings -- put the Giants in an early hole and led the Giants to an 0-4 record in Cain's starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin was masterful Thursday, holding the Yankees to one run on two hits and three walks while striking out seven in seven innings. He threw with confidence, and is reaping the rewards of his 2012 rookie campaign.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old recorded the ninth double-digit strikeout effort of his career in his last start. Bumgarner had four of San Francisco's first eight quality starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy had a quality start on Friday at Coors Field, holding the Rockies to three runs on three hits and three walks in six innings.  He was effective with his fastball and changeup, creating deception and tallying six strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill said he was lost against the Rockies Saturday, despite yielding only three earned runs in seven innings.  His sinker went missing, disrupting his rhythm and leaving him without a put-away pitch, losing batters after getting ahead 0-2.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa pitched six scoreless innings against the D-backs on Saturday, extending his streak of consecutive scoreless innings to 17 and improving to 7-3 with a 2.23 ERA lifetime against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy had his best outing Sunday, yielding four runs on eight hits in six innings. The damage came in a fluky three-run third and on a Troy Tulowitzki solo shot. His command was good, as he didn't issue a walk.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio held the D-backs hitless for four innings Sunday, but gave up two runs in the fifth and was knocked out after throwing 96 pitches in 4 1/3 innings. He hasn't thrown fewer than 95 pitches in four starts, one of which went six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Miley was impressive on the mound and with the bat in his last start. He allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings against the Giants and hit his first career homer. Miley received a no-decision as the Giants rallied for the win.
away_pitcher_note: Francis will start on three days' rest after throwing 75 pitches on Tuesday in a doubleheader against the Braves and allowing six hits, including three homers, and four runs in four innings and losing, 4-3.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin could easily be 4-0, but the bullpen has allowed two of his late-inning leads to slip away. An improved breaking ball has helped Corbin as well as the confidence he gained from last year's big league experience.
away_pitcher_note: Garland gave up six runs in six innings on Tuesday and lost 10-2 to the Braves. He has pitched at least six innings in his three starts, his longest streak to begin a season since 2005, when he went that far in his first five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Since defeating the Cardinals on Opening Day, Kennedy is winless over his last four starts. To his credit, Kennedy probably deserved to pick up a win his last time out, tossing six innings and allowing one run against the Giants in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: With a no-decision or a loss, Cain would record his first winless month since April 2011. Yielding six home runs in his last three starts hasn't helped the three-time All-Star. His total of nine homers allowed in 2011 soared to 21 last year.

home_pitcher_note: After taking losses in three of his first four starts of the 2013 season, Cahill earned his first win of the year Thursday against Colorado, allowing just one unearned run over five innings. The righty went 1-2 against the Giants in '12.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner got off to a similar start last year, when he went 5-1 with a 2.31 ERA in his first six outings. Pitching on the road doesn't bother Bumgarner, who owns a 3.22 career ERA away from AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: The D-backs had high hopes for McCarthy when they signed him in the offseason. Through his first five starts with the club, the right-hander is winless. In each outing, McCarthy has allowed at least eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum is 64-7 for a .914 winning percentage when the Giants score three or more runs for him. That's significant, because he has received just 19 runs of support in his first five outings.

home_pitcher_note: It wasn't always pretty, but Marquis defeated the Giants the last time out, allowing two runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings with four walks. He got two big double-play ground ballS behind him to prevent further damage.
away_pitcher_note: Miley wasn't his normal strike-throwing self Saturday against the Rockies, walking a career-high seven batters including four in the first inning. The lefty still managed to keep Colorado from scoring, tossing 4 1/3 shutout frames.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty still has puzzling splits, with left-handed hitters batting .364 against him and right-handers hitting .306. The anomaly hasn't stopped opposing managers from stacking their lineups with righties.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin won his third game of the season last time out, tossing 6 2/3 innings and allowing two runs on nine hits vs. the Rockies. In each of his five starts in 2013, the lefty has thrown at least six innings and hasn't surrendered more than two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez saw a streak of 13 consecutive innings without a walk come to an end Tuesday against the Cubs after he was handed an eight-run lead. But he out-pitched Edwin Jackson to stay perfect vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Still winless since Opening Day, Kennedy will look to get back on track against the Padres, a team he is 7-1 with a 2.79 ERA in his career against. At Petco Park specifically, the right-hander is 3-0 with a 1.13 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano returns from the disabled list and a strained left calf muscle. In his only start for the Dodgers this year, he lasted two-plus innings trying to pitch with the injury.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill's last two outings have yielded odd outcomes. Two starts ago, he threw 105 pitches in five innings vs. Colorado and earned his first win of the year, then he tossed eight stellar innings vs. the Giants and used 88 pitches in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett gets an extra day of rest after going only four innings in a loss to Colorado. In addition to his struggles keeping the ball in the park, he's had big problems pitching with runners on base.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy is still looking for his first win as a D-back. In his last outing he left the game with a 6-4 lead, but the Giants rallied for the win. In one career start against the Dodgers, he tossed seven scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw is coming off another dominant start, allowing the Giants one run on three hits in seven innings of a no-decision. And he seemed to have found his missing curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has not been sharp in his last two outings. Two starts ago he walked seven in 4 1/3 innings yet managed to hold the Rockies scoreless. Last time out he allowed four runs in five innings in a loss to the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin has been the D-backs' best pitcher this year. In all six of his starts, he has gone six or more innings and allowed two or fewer runs. Last time out against the Padres, he gave up just one run over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels has been a hard-luck pitcher in his last five starts with a 2.31 ERA and allowing just 21 hits in 35 innings. He's 1-2 -- and the Phillies are 1-4 -- in those starts because his team has been shut out twice and scored just one run once.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy has not won since beating the Cardinals on Opening Day. Last time out against the Padres, he allowed five runs on five hits in 5 2/3 innings. He allowed six runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Dodgers earlier this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cloyd will take Roy Halladay's spot in the rotation, at least temporarily. He went 1-3 with a 5.40 ERA in six starts with the IronPigs, but had a 2.40 ERA (four earned runs in 15 innings) in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill has pitched extremely well in his last three outings, allowing just four earned runs over 20 frames. In his last start against the Dodgers, he allowed two runs on six hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lee needs to pick up the slack with Roy Halladay on the DL indefinitely with an injured shoulder. He allowed two runs in eight innings Monday against the Giants. It's a nice start, but they need him to get on a roll.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy is still looking for his first win in a D-backs uniform. He pitched better last time out against the Dodgers, allowing three runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings. This will be his first-ever start against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick continues to pitch well. He allowed six hits and two runs and struck out six in seven innings Tuesday against the Giants, leading a rotation without Roy Halladay. They will need more from him in the coming months.

home_pitcher_note: Miley rebounded after two poor starts to allow just two runs over 7 2/3 innings against the Dodgers last time out. His command was much better as he did not walk a batter and threw 75 of his 102 pitches for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Minor tossed seven innings Wednesday at Cincinnati to pick up his fourth win, allowing one run on four hits and three walks with seven strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: In all seven of Corbin's starts this season, the left-hander has tossed at least six innings and given up two runs or fewer. In his only career appearance against the Braves, Corbin threw three shutout innings in relief last June.
away_pitcher_note: While limiting the Giants to three runs in seven innings on Thursday, Teheran found comfort with a changeup grip he had used during his Minor League days. He has allowed two runs or less in each of his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy's last start began on the wrong note as he allowed a homer on the first pitch of the game and two runs in the inning. He settled down though and did not allow another run over the next six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson surrendered seven hits and six runs in Friday's fourth inning against the Giants, and he has now lasted fewer than five innings in three of his eight starts. He is 4-0 with a 0.94 ERA in five career starts in Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Miami's most consistent starter all season, Slowey comes off his roughest outing, five runs on 11 hits in 4 2/3 innings at Los Angeles. In his three previous starts, he gave up four runs on 11 hits in 21 innings. He had four straight quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill struggled with his command Saturday, walking four in five innings. But like he has all season, Cahill minimized the damage, surrendering only one run on three hits. In each of his last four starts, Cahill has allowed two or fewer runs.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler had a solid first start of the season (the second of his career). Although he lost in L.A., he gave up only two runs in five innings, throwing 79 pitches. It was his first start since April 14 with Triple-A New Orleans.
away_pitcher_note: Eight starts into his tenure in the desert, McCarthy is still searching for his first win with the D-backs. He probably should've gotten it Sunday, when he tossed eight shutout innings against the Phillies only to see the bullpen cough up the lead.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco, who has lost three straight decisions, experienced uncharacteristic wildness in his last start against the Reds. He walked in a pair of runs with the bases loaded. The right-hander has received just 17 runs of support in nine outings.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time in his career, Miley allowed seven runs in a start, losing to the Braves in a five-inning outing Monday. Walks have been a problem this season for the left-hander, who has issued 19 free passes in 48 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Garland, whose experience helped the Rockies in the early going, has lost his last three starts. He wasn't shelled in any of them, and in two of them, the opposing starter pitched well.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps one of the biggest untold stories this season, Corbin has begun 2013 by tossing at least six innings and allowing two runs or fewer in each of his first eight starts. His ERA ranks third in Majors behind only Matt Harvey and Clayton Kershaw.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin squandered a 6-0 lead vs. the Giants, allowing eight runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings.  He lost his aggressiveness and command in a five-run fourth, walking in a run and yielding a two-out RBI single to the pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy got back in the win column in his last start as he allowed three runs over five innings against the Braves. It was his first win since Opening Day. Kennedy is 0-1 against the Rockies this year with a 4.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After not yielding a hit in the first 6 2/3 innings against the Cards in his previous start, De La Rosa gave up four in the first two innings to the Giants and five overall. But he won, and will strive for better location this time.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill has been on a roll over his past five starts, compiling a 1.36 ERA to go with a 3-1 record. The only blemish for him has been his inability to be consistent with his command as he's walked 16 batters in that span.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy tossed a three-hitter in his last outing against the Marlins, a 1-0 win at Marlins Park. The right-hander has been on a roll allowing no runs in his last two outings, a span of 17 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Stults was sharp his last time out against the Nationals, as he carried a no-hitter into the sixth inning. He allowed one run over eight innings, the deepest that he's worked into a game since 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Miley pitched well enough to win last time out but did not get enough support as he lost a 2-1 decision in Miami. Miley has struggled to find consistency this year after finishing second last season in NL Rookie of the Year voting.
away_pitcher_note: Cashner continues to shine since being moved into the starting rotation. He's allowed two or fewer runs in five of his six starts and has a 2.80 ERA as a starter. He has plus-velocity but his changeup has been devastating.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin's stellar start to the season reached a new high his last time out when he tossed his first complete game of his career, fanning 10 Rockies in Colorado. The D-backs are 9-0 when the lefty starts.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis continues to prove to be a good value at $3 million as he won his fifth consecutive start the last time out against the Cardinals. He has five consecutive quality starts and opponents are hitting .227 against him.

home_pitcher_note: Pegged by MLB.com as the D-backs' top prospect, Skaggs will make his 2013 debut Monday, filling in as the extra man for a doubleheader. The lefty competed for the final spot in the club's rotation in Spring Training but lost out to Patrick Corbin.
away_pitcher_note: Perez is joining the rotation after making just four starts in the Minors. He missed the first month of the season because of a broken left arm sustained in Spring Training. But he pitched seven scoreless innings for Triple-A Round Rock on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing no more than two runs in a start five straight times from April 25-May 17, Cahill took a step back his last time out, in Colorado, tying a season high by allowing four runs in six frames. In 15 starts vs. Texas, he's 9-4 (2.78 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: Darvish will make his first start at Chase Field. He is 3-1 with a 1.95 ERA on the road this season. He's 2-1 with a 3.54 ERA in four starts in May. He's allowed a .192 batting average to opposing lineups this month.

home_pitcher_note: Grimm is 2-0 with a 3.46 ERA in his last two starts after snapping a three-game losing streak. He is 2-1 with a 2.79 ERA in three starts at the Ballpark in Arlington. Opponents are hitting .284 off him but just .240 with runners in scoring position.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy saw his career-best 18-inning scoreless streak end on Friday vs. the Padres, but he still won his second consecutive game, allowing just one run over seven innings. In 11 career appearances vs. the Rangers, McCarthy has a 3.97 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: McCarthy saw his career-best 18-inning scoreless streak end on Friday vs. the Padres, but he still won his second consecutive game, allowing just one run over seven innings. In 11 career appearances vs. the Rangers, McCarthy has a 3.97 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Garza was frustrated after his first start when he only lasted five innings. In his last outing against the Reds, he was pulled after throwing 92 pitches over four innings. He did strike out seven, but also gave up four runs in one frame.
away_pitcher_note: Miley was touched up for seven runs in just 3 2/3 innings his last time out, against the Padres, matching the shortest start of his young career. All of the runs charged to the southpaw came with two outs as he lost his third consecutive game.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija is coming off his first shutout, a two-hitter against the White Sox. He struck out eight and was efficient, throwing 108 pitches. He altered his mechanics and made a slight adjustment to his hands, which has helped his fastball command.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy had his last start pushed back due to a cut on his right index finger he suffered while washing dishes. In his last outing, Kennedy surrendered four runs (three earned) in six innings vs. the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson is hoping for a sunny day. Rain has interrupted his past two starts. He needed nature to intervene May 23 after giving up four runs over three innings vs. the Bucs. Last Tuesday, rain halted his start vs. the White Sox after 2 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin has won each of his last six starts and delivered quality starts in all 10 of his outings this season. His only other career appearance against the Cubs came last July, when he tossed one perfect inning against them.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Lynn pitched three hitless innings before surrendering two earned runs on eight hits and one walk over the next four. But a four-run eighth inning prevented a second blemish on Lynn's 7-1 record.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill was set to pitch Sunday against the Cubs before Wednesday's game was rained out and pushed his next start to Monday. He is 0-1 with a 3.06 ERA in three career starts against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: The bullpen cost Wacha a win in his Major League debut Thursday, though he made a nice first impression. He retired the first 13 batters he faced and allowed only two hits over seven innings, while not walking a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Skaggs will be recalled from Triple-A Reno to start. He started Game 1 of last Monday's doubleheader and held the Rangers to three hits over six shutout innings. The lefty lost out in the battle for the No. 5 in the rotation this spring.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly is making his first start of the season. He allowed 14 earned runs and walked seven while striking out 19 in 18 2/3 innings of relief work this year. He went 5-7 with a 3.53 ERA in 16 starts in 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has been struggling of late, going 0-4 with a 9.14 ERA over his last four starts. Last time out against the Cubs, he allowed two runs in the first inning and five in the third before tossing four scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: A rainout pushed the Miller's last start from Friday to Saturday, but the right-hander still pitched seven shutout innings, holding the Giants to six hits and one walk while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy pitched well over seven innings against the Cubs his last time out. Three of the four runs he allowed came in the first. Kennedy was scratched from his start prior to that after cutting his finger while doing dishes.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin has had an outstanding start to the season. He is the second Arizona pitcher to ever begin a year 9-0, and the nine wins lead the Majors. Corbin allowed four runs in six innings in his last start against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Cain is coming off of one of his worst starts of the season when he allowed seven runs at St. Louis on Saturday. Cain has always been steady against Arizona, as he has a 13-6 record and 3.47 ERA to prove it.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill struggled with his command in his last start against the Cardinals. He lasted just five innings and allowed five runs on nine hits. Cahill walked three in that game and did not strike out a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner excels against the D-backs, as he has posted a 3.08 ERA in 11 games (10 starts) against them. This season he has thrived, allowing just one run in 14 1/3 innings against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Skaggs, who was called up last week to pitch in place of injured right-hander Brandon McCarthy, will be making his third start of the season with the D-backs. He allowed five runs on six hits over 5 2/3 innings at St. Louis his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin excelled last Sunday in his first start since Sept. 28, 2009, and has a chance to claim a regular spot in the rotation until Ryan Vogelsong (broken right hand) heals. Gaudin has been respectable on the road, where he has compiled a 3.27 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw made 120 pitches in six innings on Wednesday, his shortest outing since going five innings on April 23. The southpaw has faced the D-backs twice this season, striking out 13 in 14 1/3 innings with a 2.51 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Miley earned his fourth win on Wednesday, allowing three runs on 11 hits and a walk with three strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings at St. Louis. He also was victorious on May 8 in his most recent start at Dodger Stadium, tossing 7 2/3 innings in a 3-2 win.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke fired seven scoreless innings to beat the Braves on Thursday, his longest outing of the season. The right-hander is 0-3 with a 7.90 ERA in five career starts against Arizona. He's 3-0 with a 1.99 ERA at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy is looking to rebound from the worst start of his career, a 12-8 loss at St. Louis on Thursday. He gave up 13 hits and 10 earned runs, both career highs, in just four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu was charged with one run on six hits, six strikeouts and one walk in 7 2/3 innings of his no-decision against the Braves on Friday. In his last two starts, Ryu has 13 strikeouts and one walk, and the rookie has a 1.97 ERA at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: After struggling a bit in his return from the DL on Aug. 17, giving up four runs in five innings to the Pirates, Cahill has been much better his last two times out, allowing just one run in a combined 11 innings. He'll be on seven days' rest.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong allowed two hits in eight scoreless innings Sunday against the Pirates and won, 4-0. He's 1-0 in his past two starts with a 1.20 ERA (two earned runs, 15 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Because of an off-day and a quirk in the rotation due to an 18-inning game, Corbin will have two extra days between starts, and that may be coming at a good time. In five August starts, the lefty is 1-2 with a 5.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Petit pitched for Arizona from 2007-09, mostly as a starter. He posted a 9-19 record with a 5.05 ERA in 56 appearances, including 35 starts. In 25 career appearances at Chase Field (15 starts), he's 4-7 with a 5.99 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After struggling in his first four starts following a two-month stint on the DL, McCarthy returned to form his last time out vs. the Padres, tossing seven strong innings and giving up one unearned run en route to his first win since May 24.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers will get at least one more chance to start vs. Arizona. The righty was stellar when he first became a starter in May, but he's allowed four or more earned runs in all but one of his past five, and has been in and out of the 'pen as a result.

home_pitcher_note: Since the beginning of July, Miley has been arguably the D-backs' most consistent pitcher, posting a 2.29 ERA over that span. The southpaw is 2-0 in four outings against AL East teams this season.
away_pitcher_note: Redmond enjoyed a bounce-back outing against the Yankees five days after a tough start vs. the Astros. The righty allowed two earned runs and struck out seven in 5 2/3 innings. He's now allowed three earned runs or fewer in eight of his nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado was having a disappointing month in August up until his most recent two starts in which he decided to wear his prescription glasses on the mound. The result? A combined 13 innings allowing four earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle continues to be the Blue Jays most consistent starter since his rough start. The veteran left-hander has a 2.14 ERA over his past nine starts, including seven shutout innings vs. the Royals in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong's offspeed pitches lacked sharpness in his last outing -- he said that his mechanics deserted him occasionally -- but he still recorded his third quality start in a row and fourth in his last five performances.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill pitched well against the Giants, allowing three runs over 6 1/3 innings. In his outing prior to that he was forced into relief duty in an 18-inning game against the Phillies, throwing four scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Petit has won consecutive starts for the Giants, tossing six innings of two-run ball in both Arizona and Colorado -- very difficult ballparks for pitchers. In three outings this year he has 23 strikeouts and just four walks.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin struggled in his two most recent starts, allowing a combined 13 earned runs in 10 1/3 innings. The D-backs will monitor him closely in this start for any signs of fatigue as they consider reducing his workload down the stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Returning from his first-ever DL stint, Cain takes the ball vs. the D-backs, against whom he's 14-6 with a 3.39 ERA. Cain hasn't pitched since being hit by a line drive on the right forearm Aug. 22.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy pitched well last time out against the Jays. He allowed two first-inning runs and then shut them out until allowing a two-run homer in the ninth. This is McCarthy's second start against the Giants in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants have won just once in Bumgarner's last nine starts, but that's through no fault of his own. The 24-year-old southpaw has posted a 2.77 ERA in that time, but has been given just 20 total runs of support.
away_pitcher_note: Miley pitched poorly his last time out against the Jays. After allowing a run in the first, he lost his composure during a frustrating second and allowed four runs. The 1 2/3-inning outing was the shortest of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco, who has earned three consecutive wins and was 5-0 with a 1.64 ERA in six August starts, will try to improve to 8-1 since joining the Dodgers. He held the D-backs to one run in seven innings and went 2-for-2 with an RBI in his Dodgers debut.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado recorded a quality start in his last outing against the Blue Jays and has given Arizona solid starts in each of his last three, though he's 0-1 in that span. He will be making his third career start against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez last start was a forgettable 7-5 loss on Wednesday at Coors Field in his first start for the Dodgers. The right-hander allowed one run on four hits in 6 2/3 innings and earned the win against the D-backs on May 5 while still with the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill struggled somewhat in his last start but won the game thanks to some help from his defense and his ability to keep the ball on the ground. He's won his last three decisions despite 13 walks in 27 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu (stiff back) was scratched on Friday but says he is ready to go for Wednesday's finale with the D-backs. The rookie left-hander snapped a two-start losing streak with a solid 6 1/3 innings against the Padres on Aug. 30, picking up his 13th win.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin has lost his last three starts but looked a lot better in his last start, when he allowed three runs in 8 innings. He pitched against Yusmeiro Petit, who had a near-perfect game. He has walked two and struck out 11 in his last 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has been outstanding in two of his last three starts and in the other he tossed a complete game allowing two runs in the inning and two in the ninth. He held the Giants to one run over eight innings last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood's last start was delayed by a bruised right thumb, but he had no issues because of it. Chatwood held the Padres to one run and five hits in six innings, with two walks and two strikeouts, but didn't figure in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: Miley pitched well his last time out as he held the Giants to two runs over seven innings. He did not get a decision in the game, which went 11 innings. He has allowed one run in 12 1/3 innings against the Rockies this year.
away_pitcher_note: In his first outing since July 7, Oswalt entered in relief and pitched three solid innings before giving up four runs while recording just one out in his final inning. Oswalt hopes more stamina will give him greater effectiveness.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado struggled his last time out against the Dodgers. He gave up four homers and lasted just 2 2/3 innings. He has allowed 1.8 homers per nine innings this year. This is his first appearance against the Rockies this year.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin held the Giants to one run and four hits and struck out five in seven innings in his last start. The performance lowered his road ERA for the season to 2.10, and his ERA in August and September is 2.24.

home_pitcher_note: Since returning from the DL on Aug. 17, Cahill has been steady for the D-backs, giving up four or fewer runs in all six of his outings. The righty has credited a lot of his recent success to finding a more consistent arm angle to release from.
away_pitcher_note: Ryu returned Wednesday from an 11-day layoff due to a stiff back and allowed three runs on 10 hits in six innings against Arizona. The rookie has lost three of his last four starts. He has a 6.55 ERA in two starts at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Just two weeks ago, the D-backs were considering shutting down Corbin or moving to a six-man rotation after the left-hander began to show signs of fatigue. In his past two starts, however, Corbin has allowed just four combined runs in 14 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke is unbeaten in his last nine starts, posting a 1.58 ERA during that span. The right-hander has gone at least six innings in 13 consecutive outings. He's allowed two earned runs in 14 innings against the D-backs this season.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has been on a roll of late, posting a 2.10 ERA in his past four starts. He is 2-1 over that span and took a no-decision his last time out when he gave up two runs in six innings to the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Fife gets the spot start to give Clayton Kershaw some extra rest. Fife has been roughed up for seven runs in five relief innings recently, but he's a creature of habit who is more comfortable starting.

home_pitcher_note: By winning his 10th game of the year his last time out vs. the Rockies, Miley joined Randy Johnson as just the second left-hander in franchise history to win double digit games in consecutive seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco had his shortest outing in two years Saturday, recording four outs and allowing seven runs against the Giants. He's 8-2 with a 2.63 ERA in 13 starts with the Dodgers and 3-0 with a 0.83 ERA in three starts against Arizona this year.

home_pitcher_note: It's a nice chance to rebound for Chacin, who yielded seven hits and six runs (four earned) in just four innings while losing to the D-backs at Chase Field. Before that, he went at least seven innings in nine of 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: This will mark Delgado's second straight outing vs. the Rockies as he held them to two runs on five hits in six innings his last time out to earn his first win since Aug. 2. The righty has allowed a combined six homers in three starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh was effective in place of Jorge De La Rosa Monday, allowing one run over five innings in a win over the Cardinals. It was his best start with the Rockies so far, but he's searching for his first win this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill beat the Dodgers in his last start and will be looking to win his fifth consecutive decision when he faces the Rockies. He is 1-2 against them this year but hasn't faced the club since May 22.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio limped through one of his worst outings of the year Tuesday, allowing eight runs over 2 2/3 innings. He walked three and struck out two in his shortest outing since June 25, when he was demoted to Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: The next inning Corbin completes will be his 200th of the year. The lefty is coming off the shortest start of his career, allowing six runs on seven hits over just two-plus innings vs. the Dodgers on Tuesday. Corbin is 3-0 vs. the Rockies in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Stults limited the Pirates to two runs over five innings in Tuesday's 5-2 victory. Stults allowed seven hits and a walk, but he struck out five. A Marlon Byrd two-RBI single in the third inning accounted for the only runs he allowed.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy has given the Padres trouble in two starts this season, winning twice while allowing one earned run in 14 innings. The right-hander has rebounded from a five-game losing skid to win three of his last four decisions. He's posted a 2.50 ERA over his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ross was terrific on Wednesday, allowing just two runs on three hits while striking out seven in seven innings of a 3-2 win over the Pirates. He didn't issue any walks, needing only 90 pitches to get through seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Miley was not sharp in his last start against the Dodgers. He allowed three runs and lasted only five innings. Miley walked four and did not get a decision as the Dodgers won to clinch the division.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy will make his final start of the season at Petco Park, which has been kind to him since he was obtained from the D-backs. In five starts at Petco, Kennedy has a 2.86 ERA. In four road starts, he has a 6.95 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado was hurt once again by the home run in his last start. He didn't get a decision in the D-backs' 9-4 loss to the Rockies at Coors Field, and he has allowed 22 home runs in 111 1/3 big league innings.

home_pitcher_note: Erlin continues to impress in a late-season stint. He tossed 7 2/3 scoreless innings the last time out against the Dodgers, tying his career-high with seven strikeouts. He has a 1.80 ERA in his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: The season has not gone the way Cahill had hoped due to injuries and struggles with his mechanics, but he has pitched better of late. In his last eight starts, he is 5-0 with a 2.64 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin looks to finish his outstanding 2013 season on a positive note. He is over the 200-inning mark for the first time in his career. His last two starts have not been very good, though, as he has allowed 10 runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg returned to the mound Sunday after missing each of his past two scheduled starts with right forearm tightness. In his first start in two weeks, the right-hander allowed three earned runs on six hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy's last outing may have looked far different numberswise had the Padres' Nick Hundley's ball been one foot farther to the left. Instead of being foul it was a three-run homer and he allowed four runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Haren made what might have been the final home start of his Nationals tenure. He worked six solid innings but once again didn't keep the ball in the park, allowing three earned runs on two homers. In 29 starts, Haren has given up 28 homers.

home_pitcher_note: Miley pitched well his last time out, tossing six shutout innings against the Padres. He faced the Nationals earlier this year in Washington and allowed three runs (two earned) over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Left-hander Gio Gonzalez was scratched for the season finale because Davey Johnson was guaranteed to finish his career at least 300 games over .500. Roark has seven wins and could be part of the rotation next year.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo will be making his D-backs debut. The right-hander was signed to a two-year contract just after Spring Training opened. He was set back a bit during the spring with a bulging disc in his back.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum's continuing his transition from power pitching to a finesse-oriented style. He still had enough on the ball to strike out 193 in 197 2/3 innings last year. Lincecum had a rough spring (6.52 ERA in five starts), which is typical for him.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies believe the key to consistency lies in his full offseason of conditioning. The last two winters were spent coming back from injuries. In Spring Training, he developed confidence in a split-finger off-speed pitch.
