away_pitcher_note: McCarthy pitched better than his numbers would indicate in his first start of the year against the Giants. The right-hander had a tremendous spring and looked sharp in his debut despite the five runs he allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was efficient through six innings in his first start, and he was hurt by bad luck and an error in his 4-3 loss to the Marlins in his first start. He'll need to stick to his ground-ball style in his first Coors Field start.
away_pitcher_note: Miley allowed four runs in the first inning last time out against the Giants and then shut them down for the next six innings, giving his team a chance to rally. Miley started on Opening Day for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson's sparkling Giants debut last Wednesday in Phoenix included seven strikeouts. That was the most by a Giant without allowing a run in his team debut since Juan Marichal fanned 12 while one-hitting the Phillies in his first big league game.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill's last outing wasn't a work of art, but it got the job done. He walked three and allowed four hits, but only two runs over six innings against the Giants. Command is the key for Cahill and caused him problems in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: A encouraging aspect of Lincecum's 2014 debut last Thursday at Arizona was his zero walks in six innings. That would continue a positive trend for Lincecum, who reduced his walks-per-nine-innings rate last year after three consecutive increases.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Giants as they worked him into deep counts consistently. It was his first start in a D-backs uniform. Arroyo was bothered by a bulging disk during Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants' No. 5 starter believes that a flaw in his pitching mechanics which has previously bothered him -- he won't specify what it is, though he has complained about balance -- has accounted for his inability to work deeper into games.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado did not have good results in his first outing of the season. He allowed six runs on 10 hits in just four-plus innings vs. the Rockies. Delgado must keep his fastball down in the zone to be effective.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has had a frustrating first two starts. He pitched well through six innings before unraveling in his debut. Then Saturday against the Rockies he seemed to be cruising before the Rockies broke it open in the fourth and fifth innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ryu is coming off a rough outing that saw him give up six runs on eight hits in two-inning start against the Giants. He shut down the D-backs, allowing only two hits in five scoreless innings in Game 2 in Australia.

home_pitcher_note: Miley got the starting nod on Opening Day after an injury to Patrick Corbin, and he has pitched like an ace this year. He was responsible for the team's first two wins, the most recent against the Rockies at Coors Field on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke is coming off a six-inning, 6-2 victory over the Giants in which he struck out eight and didn't walk a batter. He opened the season with a five-inning, 3-2 road victory over the Padres. Greinke struck out five and walked two in that start.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill is facing an important start as the team is growing impatient with his struggles. In his last start against the Giants, Cahill lasted just 3 2/3 innings and allowed five runs. Command is the key for Cahill.
away_pitcher_note: Haren doesn't throw hard like the ace he once was, but he's allowed only one earned run over 12 innings in two starts. He'll be facing his former team for only the fourth time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter steps into the rotation in place of Randall Delgado, who struggled to go past four innings in his first two starts. Collmenter last started a game in 2012, but he had a six-inning relief appearance last year.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler's return to Atlanta, his hometown, soured quickly last Wednesday when he gave up four runs in five innings. He'll look to change things against a D-backs team that mustered only one run off him in 6 1/3 innings of a start last August.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo is getting an extra day of rest this time through the rotation. The right-hander is behind the other starters after missing time this spring with a back issue. He picked up the win against the Giants in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Mejia is no stranger to a high pitch count, totaling 101 and 98 in his first two starts of 2014. However, the right-hander has managed to limit the damage, as the Mets have won in both of his outings.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has had a frustrating season to this point. He has allowed five runs, six and six in his first three starts of the year despite feeling like he's thrown the ball better than that.
away_pitcher_note: Lacking his usual control, Gee uncharacteristically walked four batters in an abbreviated outing on Friday against the Angels. Next up are the D-backs, whom he held to two runs in seven innings during their only meeting last year.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Greinke's second consecutive start against the D-Backs and he can't get enough of them, going 3-0 with a 1.78 ERA in four starts for the Dodgers against them.
away_pitcher_note: Wade Miley struggled with his command in his last outing and the Dodgers made him pay. L.A. tagged him for five runs on eight hits in five innings, matching Miley's shortest outing of the season, also vs. the Dodgers on Opening Night in Australia.

home_pitcher_note: Haren battled in Arizona and escaped multiple jams against his former team, stung in particular by Eric Chavez's three-run homer, but did just enough to get his second win.
away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger will be making his first big league start. Promoted from Triple-A last week, he made his first appearance Monday in relief of Josh Collmenter. He allowed two runs on six hits over three innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Dodgers were pleased to see Beckett rebound with an effective start against the Giants, holding them scoreless for five innings despite walking five and hitting a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter will be making his second start of the year after beginning the season in the bullpen. In his first start, on Monday against the Mets, he allowed three runs on five hits over four innings before reaching his pitch limit.

home_pitcher_note: Wood scattered 11 hits over 5 2/3 innings in his last start against the Yankees, who only scored two runs off the lefty. He's 1-4 in five career starts against Arizona with a 6.33 ERA. Maybe being at Wrigley will help. He has a career 3.78 ERA there.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo will be making his fourth start of the year. He was roughed up in his last outing against the Mets, allowing nine runs in 3 1/3 innings. Arroyo was limited during Spring Training by a bulging disc in his back.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel is holding batters to a .143 average in his three starts this season. This will be his ninth career start against Arizona. So far, he's posted quality starts in each of his outings. If the cool weather continues, he'll benefit at Wrigley.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy pitched well enough to win last time out against the Mets, but his offense could not get the job done. McCarthy allowed three runs in 5 2/3 innings. In two career games (one start) at Wrigley Field he has a 2.45 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: Miley was outstanding in his last start against the Dodgers, allowing just one run on two hits in six innings. He wound up with a no-decision after Scott Van Slyke homered to tie the game in the seventh.

away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger made his first Major League start Saturday against the Dodgers. He cruised through the first three innings but allowed a three-run homer in the fourth and was chased from the game in the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter was shifted to the rotation to take the spot of Randall Delgado. In his two starts he is 0-2 with a 6.30 ERA. Last time out it was a three-run homer by Yasiel Puig that spoiled an otherwise good start.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez hopes to bounce back after allowing nine hits, six runs, one walk and striking out three in just four-plus innings Sunday at Coors Field. He entered the afternoon with a 3.86 ERA, making it his worst start of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo was set back this spring by a bulging disc in his back and is just now rounding into the form most pitchers have at the end of Spring Training. He allowed five runs in 5 1/3 innings last time out against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Lee continues to roll. He is 2-2 with a 1.20 ERA in his last four starts. In 30 innings in those four starts, he has allowed 33 hits, four earned runs, one walk and has struck out 37.

home_pitcher_note: Miley received a no-decision his last time out against the Cubs when he allowed three runs over five innings. Command has been an issue for him this year as he has walked 16 running up his pitch count early in games.
away_pitcher_note: Morales has held opponents to two runs in 13 innings over his last two games. By relying on his fastball, he held the Giants to one run over seven innings Tuesday while lifting the Rockies to a 2-1 victory at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Bolsinger is making his third start since being brought up to replace Trevor Cahill in the rotation. He earned his first win last Thursday in Chicago, allowing a run on four hits with two walks and seven strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chatwood, who had pitched solidly and efficiently in his previous two starts, gave up three home runs and five runs in six innings of a no-decision against the Giants on Wednesday. But he also escaped bases loaded with no outs.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter is making his fourth start since coming out of the bullpen to replace Randall Delgado in the rotation. He won his last time out on Friday night against the Phillies, tossing six innings of scoreless, four hit ball.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles pitched seven strong innings, held the Dodgers to two runs, struck out four and forced 11 groundouts in his last start -- a no-decision in a Rockies win. Lyles has given up two earned runs in 14 innings his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner has allowed four earned runs in each of his last two starts, though he felt his overall stuff was good the last time out against the Nationals. The nine hits he allowed in that game tied his season-high. He also had five strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo is coming off his best outing of the year. He held the Phillies to two runs over 6 1/3 innings Saturday and was in line for the win before the bullpen suffered a meltdown in the eighth.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy was dealing the last time out, throwing a season-high 117 pitches, allowing one run over seven innings in a victory over the Nationals. He struck out nine and didn't walk a batter in one of the best starts for the team this season.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy deserved a better fate his last time out. He allowed just two runs over seven innings with 12 strikeouts against the Phillies, but came away with the loss as A.J. Burnett and Jonathan Papelbon combined on a shutout Sunday.

away_pitcher_note: Miley said he felt like he had his good stuff working in his start Monday against the Rockies, but he was hit hard, allowing seven runs on 10 hits over six innings. He is 1-4 with a 4.04 career ERA in six starts at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is on track to make his next start despite leaving his last start in St. Louis after three innings with a bruised thumb. The right-hander has faced the D-backs four times in his career, compiling a 3-1 record and 2.48 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger will be making his fourth big league start. In his last outing against the Rockies, he allowed four runs on nine hits over five innings. Bolsinger's best pitch is his cut fastball and he has a decent curve as well.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada struggled with command of his changeup and curveball in his last outing in Cincinnati and took the loss after allowing three runs over six innings. He has pitched at least six innings in all but one of his starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter had to battle in his last start against the Rockies. He gave up four runs in the first three innings before tossing four shutout innings. He has a 1.23 ERA in his career against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta put on a one-man show in his most recent outing in Cincinnati, throwing eight shutout innings while driving in his team's only two runs in a shutout win.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo is finally feeling healthy after suffering a bulging disk in Spring Training and a virus in late April. He tossed a gem his last time out holding the Padres scoreless on just three hits over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Minimizing the damage would be the best way to describe the righty's no-decision during the White Sox surprising 4-3 comeback victory in Cleveland Sunday. Rienzo allowed seven hits and four walks over 4 2/3 innings, but yielded just three runs.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, McCarthy picked up his first victory of the season after five losses, limiting the Padres to just three hits in seven scoreless innings when the D-backs hung on for a 4-3 win. He walked one and struck out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana was as good as he's been all season, holding the Cubs to one hit over seven innings. That one hit was a leadoff double from Jeff Samardzija in the sixth. He struck out three, walked three and threw 95 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has not won in five starts since his last victory on April 6. In his last start on Sunday, Miley was unable to hold a 3-1 lead, but did not get a decision in Arizona's 4-3 loss to the Padres. He allowed three runs on six hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Noesi still has not won over his past 15 starts but made a major contribution to a victory over the Cubs at Wrigley Field. Noesi, who is moving back to a starter in-season, raised his pitch count to 81 and allowed just one run over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson was recalled from Double-A Mobile last week to provide length in the bullpen. He was not needed in relief so he will start Sunday in what was Mike Bolsinger's spot. Anderson had a 0.69 ERA in six starts for Mobile.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter survived a rough first inning in his last start and managed to keep the D-backs in the game, which they rallied to win late. Of the five runs he allowed in that first inning, only one was earned.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann hasn't given up a run in his past two outings (10 1/3 innings pitched), but his last start, on May 5, was cut short due to a lengthy rain delay after four innings. He tossed a seven-inning, two-run gem in a win against Arizona last year.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo had his best start of the year last time out against the Brewers. He allowed just one unearned run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings. After a injury-marred Spring Training Arroyo appears to be rounding into form.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg posted season highs of 7 1/3 innings and 114 pitches in his latest start on May 7, a win against the Dodgers. Over the past four outings, he has a 2-0 record, 1.37 ERA, 1.19 WHIP and 31 strikeouts in 26 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy cruised through the first three innings last time out against the White Sox. But in the fourth, nine of the first 10 batters in the inning got hits and McCarthy was forced from the game after the seven-run outburst.
away_pitcher_note: Control eluded Fister on May 9 as he made his Nationals debut after sitting out five-plus weeks with a lat strain. He left too many balls up in the zone, going 4 1/3 innings and allowing seven runs, five earned, on nine hits, including three homers.

home_pitcher_note: Miley, who allowed two runs in seven innings vs. the White Sox in his last outing, is facing a familiar foe. He has made three starts vs. the Dodgers in '14, and won his most recent one on April 18. In his career vs. L.A., he is 3-3 with a 3.96 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke is coming off a victory over the Giants in his last start, on May 10. He allowed two earned runs in seven innings, striking out eight. In two starts against the D-backs, he's 1-0 with 16 strikeouts in 11 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie will make his second start of the season and his first start at home. Anderson allowed one run and two hits in 5 1/3 innings against the White Sox on Sunday in his big league debut. He struck out six.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw went seven innings in a no-decision vs. the Giants on May 11, striking out nine while allowing three earned runs despite zero walks. He beat the D-backs on March 22 in the season opener in Sydney before going on the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter battled his way through five innings in his last start vs. the Nationals. He didn't have his best command, and the Nats made him pay for it with a series of extra-base hits that led to a no-decision. He's 1-2 with a 4.28 ERA in six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren went seven innings, allowing three earned runs, to beat the Marlins on May 12. He won against the D-backs on April 13 in his only start against them this season.

home_pitcher_note: A blown save cost Wainwright the chance to be the National League's first seven-game winner on Tuesday. He has allowed only three runs in six starts to teams not named the Cubs and has pitched at least seven innings in all but two of his outings.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo has been on a roll of late. In his last three starts he is 3-0 with a 0.39 ERA. Last time out against the Nationals, he tossed a complete game, allowing one run on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: The Cards won behind Wacha on Thursday for the first time in his last six starts. Nevertheless, Wacha has made seven quality starts and has yet to allow four runs in any outing. He allowed six runs in 4 2/3 innings against Arizona last year.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy had his finest start of the year last time out against the Nationals. He allowed just one run on two hits over eight innings but did not factor in the decision. Three of his last four starts have been quality ones.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn allowed two runs over seven innings in a 5-2 victory against Atlanta on May 16, picking up his fifth win of the season. The win was Lynn's first since April 19. He is 2-0 with a 2.37 ERA in five games against Arizona (three starts).
away_pitcher_note: Miley was roughed up in his last start by the Dodgers as he allowed four runs on seven hits in six innings. In two starts before that, he had pitched well, compiling a 3.21 ERA over that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Colon has been wildly inconsistent. In his five losses and one no-decision, he holds a 6.59 ERA. In his three wins, he owns a 1.23 mark. About the only thing consistent has been his control, with one or zero walks in eight of his nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson is making the third big league start of his career. He was impressive in his debut holding the White Sox to one run over 5 1/3 innings. Last time out against the Dodgers he gave up five runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After his latest loss, Wheeler hypothesized that opposing hitters have learned to sit on his fastballs in fastball counts. He will look to mix up his repertoire in his next start against the D-backs, the only team Wheeler has beaten this season.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter picked up the win in his last outing as he gave up three runs on four hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Dodgers. All three of the runs came via two homers, one by Hanley Ramirez and the other by Adrian Gonzalez.

home_pitcher_note: With Dillon Gee still nursing a strained lat muscle, Montero will receive at least one more start. After giving up five runs over 4 1/3 innings last time out, he'll need to prove he deserves to stay in the rotation over fellow rookie Jacob deGrom.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo did not have his best stuff last time out against the Cardinals and he allowed five runs on nine hits over seven innings. The D-backs were one-hit that night by Adam Wainwright in a 5-0 defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Because of Friday's rainout, Matsuzaka will make his first big league start of the season. Matsuzaka has pitched exclusively in relief since mid-April, never throwing more than 56 pitches in an outing, but he could throw up to 100 on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: The D-backs are adding Spruill to their roster as the 26th man. With the Reno Aces, Spruill has appeared in 12 games with a 2-1 record and a 4.72 ERA in 34 1/3 innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy, who took a no-decision in his last outing after allowing one run in six innings vs. the Cardinals, is 3-1 with a 1.67 ERA in four career starts vs. the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Ross went seven frames in Wednesday's loss, the sixth time in his last eight starts he has gone seven or more. In those, he is 6-2 with a 2.32 ERA. Going into Wednesday, he used his slider a League-high 326 times, according to Baseball Prospectus.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Cardinals, Miley allowed three runs on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings. He's given up three runs or more in four of his last five starts, and Miley hasn't picked up a win since May 10 against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Stults allowed five runs his last time out, the third time he has done so this season. He didn't allow a hit until the fourth inning the last time out against the Cubs but it all snowballed from there. He's winless in five road starts in 2014 (0-4).

home_pitcher_note: Anderson's last start actually didn't happen. He tossed three shutout innings against the Mets before rain came and forced the game to be postponed. Because it did not last five innings, the game's statistics were wiped out.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer came up big in a pinch last week against the Cubs, as he threw five scoreless innings on short notice. Stauffer filled in for injured lefty Robbie Erlin and allowed four hits with one walk and five strikeouts in getting a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter had one of his best outings of the season his last time out. Against the Mets, he went six innings and surrendered only two runs. Collmenter has given up three or fewer earned runs in four of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cingrani allowed four runs on seven hits over six innings in a loss to the Cardinals on May 24. In his lone start against the D-backs, on Aug. 20 last season, he gave up a run on two hits in 3 2/3 innings before leaving with a strained lower back.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo left his last start, a no-decision against the Mets, after six innings of one-run ball. The right-hander has been working deep into ballgames -- he has pitched at least six innings in his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Leake allowed two runs on seven hits while striking out a career-high-tying eight batters over six innings against the Cardinals on May 25, but took the loss. In five career starts against Arizona, Leake is 2-0 but has a 6.10 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy was inconsistent in his last start, giving up five runs on nine hits in 6 2/3 innings Monday against the Padres. In two career appearances (one start) against the Reds, he has pitched three innings and given up seven runs.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto works with little margin for error. He has a 1.83 ERA but only a less shiny 4-4 record because of bogus run support from his lineup. In five of his 11 starts, the Reds have scored three runs or fewer -- including a pair of 1-0 shutout defeats.

home_pitcher_note: Miley struck out a career-high 11 in his last start against the Padres, but did not get a decision in a 4-3 loss. All three of the runs Miley allowed in that game came in the third inning, as he allowed four straight hits.
away_pitcher_note: In his last four outings, Simon has bookended two great performances with two lousy ones that brought early exits. During his 3 2/3 inning, five-run start vs. the Dodgers on Tuesday, he left several pitches over the middle of the plate - especially w

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa escaped a bases-loaded, no-out jam in the third inning and held the Phillies to one run in six innings of a win in his latest start. He is 6-0 with a 1.80 ERA in his past seven starts, despite a middle finger bruise.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson has had a good start to his career, winning his first three starts. But he has been the beneficiary of superb run support. In his last two starts, the D-backs have scored 30 runs behind him while he has given up nine (six earned).

home_pitcher_note: After an effective first seven starts, Lyles has struggled through his last three turns, giving up 10 earned runs and 11 walks over 14 1/3 innings. He lasted just five in a no-decision at Philadelphia on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter had the best start of his career Thursday, tossing a complete-game shutout and facing the minimum while giving up three hits. He was the 13th pitcher since 1914 to face the minimum while giving up three or more hits.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio had given up one run in the first four innings against the Indians in his last start, but in the fifth he yielded four runs on five hits that included three doubles and a home run before being pulled.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo picked up the loss in his outing against the Reds on Friday after giving up a grand slam to Reds catcher Devin Mesoraco. Despite giving up five runs, he went seven innings for the fifth time in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy's ERA jumped from a season-low of 4.67 on May 21 to 5.20 after his last two outings, in which he gave up a combined 10 runs and 18 hits while struggling to avoid big innings.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran recorded his Major-League leading 11th quality start when he limited the Marlins to only two runs in 7 1/3 innings last Friday. Miami's two-run first snapped Teheran's streak of 15 straight scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Miley picked up the loss after giving up four home runs to the Reds in his last start, but he has also been mowing down batters. Despite a no-decision and a loss, the left-hander has struck out 20 hitters in 13 innings in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Santana put a nightmarish stretch behind him in his most recent turn, recording his first quality start since May 10. Since compiling a 1.99 ERA in his first six starts, Santana is 1-2 with a 7.83 ERA in his last four outings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has won all four of his big leagues starts this year. Last time out against the Rockies in Coors Field, he allowed just one run over six innings. He is not overpowering and his changeup is his best pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Harang has given up two runs or fewer in eight of 10 starts, a trend that falls in line with his 3.20 career ERA in 101 1/3 innings against Arizona. He walked four on Sunday after walking a combined seven in his previous seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter struggled in his last outing -- a five-inning outing at Coors Field. However, he still picked up the win as his offense supplied him with 16 runs of support. Collmenter has otherwise been consistent and hasn't lost a game since April 20.
away_pitcher_note: Since allowing seven runs in one-third of an inning on April 18 in Oakland, Cosart is 3-3 with a 2.96 ERA in his last eight starts, during which the club is 3-5. He's allowed three runs or fewer in each of his last eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo had two of his worst starts of the season in back-to-back outings against the Reds and Rockies, giving up nine runs to the two teams combined. Arroyo has faced the Astros 31 times, the fourth most of any team and has a 4.04 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Since being moved to the rotation on April 20, Peacock is 2-3 with a 4.27 ERA in eight starts. In his last three outings, he's 2-0 with a 3.06 ERA, having allowed 17 hits and six earned runs in 17 2/3 innings. Houston is 3-0 in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel has been the Astros' best starter this season. He's given up only five earned runs in his last three starts, including a complete-game win against Seattle on May 25 when he gave up only one unearned run.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy deserved a better fate his last time out against the Braves. He allowed three runs over 6 1/3 innings, but two of them came on a homer by Jason Heyward on a pitch that was up and off the outside corner of the plate.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman has struggled mightily in his last two outings. He gave up nine runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Orioles on June 1. His last outing may have been as bad, but he didn't last as long, giving up three runs in 1 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Miley pitched well enough to win his last time out against the Braves, but had to settle for a no-decision as the D-backs rallied to tie the score in the bottom of the ninth and won it in the 11th. Miley's last win was May 10.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw struck out nine without a walk in a five-inning complete game thanks to a rain-shortened win in Denver on Sunday. He has struck out nine batters five times this year, including his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson continued his season-long hot streak in his last outing against the Braves. In seven innings, he gave up five hits and two runs. Anderson will look to stay perfect on the year. His record is 5-0 with an ERA of 3.14.

home_pitcher_note: Haren earned his first win since May 12 by going 5 1/3 innings and allowing two runs on five hits against the Reds on Monday. In six career appearances (five starts) against the D-backs, Haren is 4-2 with a 3.60 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter's first loss after winning four in a row came in his last outing against the Astros. In seven innings, he gave up three runs and seven hits. The loss moved him to 4-3 on the season with an ERA of 3.65.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett went six shutout innings Tuesday, allowing two hits while walking one and striking out seven in a win over the Reds. In 10 career starts against the D-backs, he is 2-5 with a 3.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo had one of his best outings of the season in his last start against the Astros. In seven innings, he allowed one run and six hits. The win moved him to 6-4 on the season with an ERA of 4.22.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has more hits (three) than wins (one) this year. He allowed five runs on eight hits over six innings his last time out against the Astros in Houston. His win came on May 3 in San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta bounced back from an iffy start to throw 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball against the Mets on Wednesday. The right-hander's ERA dipped to 2.90 and his WHIP to 1.23. In six road starts this season, Peralta has finished the seventh inning once.

home_pitcher_note: The D-backs called up Bolsinger on Tuesday to replace the injured Bronson Arroyo in the rotation. Bolsinger had a five-game stint with the D-backs earlier in the season, but he had a 1-2 record and 6.08 ERA before being sent to Triple-A Reno.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time in three starts, Lohse was very good Thursday, limiting the Mets to an unearned run over eight innings. Lohse, whose 1.04 WHIP is the best in Milwaukee's rotation, has pitched into the seventh inning in 10 of 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miley has not won since May 10. The long ball has been a problem for him this year as he has allowed a whopping 16. His last time out, against the Astros, he allowed four runs on seven hits (two homers) in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garza's troubles throwing to bases hadn't hurt him this season before Friday, when his two errors contributed to four unearned runs in seven innings against the Reds. The Brewers mounted a comeback to take him off the hook.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson won his first five starts in the big leagues, but his streak ended against the Dodgers on Friday night. He did not have command of his fastball and lasted just five innings, allowing two runs on four hits and four walks.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo appears to be entering a midseason surge. Over his past two starts, he has allowed one run on 10 hits in 14 innings, with 16 strikeouts. "For our success, [we need] for him to be 'that guy,' " Ryan Braun said.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter had a frustrating start last time out against the Dodgers. Pitcher Dan Haren's three-run double capped a four-run fourth inning as Collmenter allowed six runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: As always, Lincecum must watch out for Paul Goldschmidt, the D-backs first baseman who's batting .542 off him (13-for-24) with seven homers and 17 RBIs lifetime.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran reversed some of his middle-inning struggles against the Brewers on June 16, but he couldn't improve his won-less record, going seven innings and giving up three runs but getting a no-decision. He has not recorded a win since May 3.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on the road has been a challenge for Vogelsong, who has a 4.88 ERA in six starts outside of AT&T Park this year. By contrast, his home ERA is 3.33 in eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bolsinger replaced Bronson Arroyo in the rotation after he was placed on the disabled list with a sprained UCL. In his first start back from Triple-A Reno, Bolsinger went 6 1/3 innings and gave up three runs in a loss to the Brewers on June 17.
away_pitcher_note: At this point, Bumgarner is pitching for a spot on the National League All-Star team. It would be his second such distinction in a row. The last Giants lefty to make two All-Star teams in a row was Mike McCormick (1960-61).

home_pitcher_note: Miley has struggled with the home run ball this year. He has allowed 17, which is just four shy of his total for all of 2013. Last time out against the Brewers, he allowed three runs over 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson has been inconsistent for much of the season, but he turned in one of his better performances last time out, holding the Angels to one run on four hits over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has lost his last two starts after winning the first five of his big league career. He probably deserved a better fate his last time out against the Brewers as he allowed just two earned runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kluber took a hard-luck loss against the Tigers on Friday, spinning seven innings of two-run baseball while fanning six and walking one. He has given up 11 runs over his last 23 2/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Ross has been tagged with the loss in three of his four June starts, with the other a no-decision, largely due to a lack of run support (three total runs scored) and poor fielding behind him (12 unearned runs allowed in 2014, most in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander, who is tied for the Major League lead in losses, notched his only win this season against the Padres on May 3, but he has struggled lately, giving up five runs for the fourth time in six starts against the Giants on June 21.

home_pitcher_note: Stults has recently incorporated a higher leg kick into his delivery, and it paid off Sunday in arguably his best start of 2014. He pitched a season-high seven innings and allowed just two runs, but still picked up his MLB-worst 10th loss.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Collmenter battled through five tough innings against the Giants. But his latest appearance came out of the bullpen against the Indians in the 14th inning of the D-backs' 9-8 win, in which Collmenter picked up the victory.

home_pitcher_note: What a big league debut it was for Despaigne against the Giants on Monday, as he tossed seven scoreless innings, allowing four hits with 11 ground-ball outs. He threw various pitches from different angles and changed his velocity often.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old rookie is coming off the best start of his short Major League career. Despite being saddled with the loss, Bolsinger pitched 7 2/3 innings against the Giants on June 22, giving up only one run on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Locke goes on two days' extra rest since earning his first win, and in 10 starts with more than five days of rest the results have not been pretty (2-5, 5.00 ERA). But he's been a new pitcher all around since a Minor League detour.
away_pitcher_note: Miley is searching for his first win since May 10, a span of eight starts. Last time out he allowed five runs (four earned) over four innings against the Indians. He has allowed a whopping 17 home runs this year.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has morphed into quite a power pitcher in his last five starts, with 39 strikeouts (versus nine walks) in 32 innings. Yet he will be trying to avoid a third straight loss. Has allowed one homer in PNC Park in 44 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson won his first five big league starts, but has now lost his last three. Last time out against the Indians he allowed four runs on seven hits over five innings. This is his first look at the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Little attention was paid when Worley was acquired from the Twins in late March, but he has been an instant hit, with three straight super-quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy is still looking for his first win over a team other than the Padres. Last time out, he held San Diego to just one run over seven innings. McCarthy's name has been mentioned prominently in trade talks.

home_pitcher_note: Santana came into his latest outing on the heels of a three-game losing streak. Over that span, he posted a 5.47 ERA. But after twirling 6 2/3 innings of two-run ball vs. Philly on Saturday, Santana has strung together two straight quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Collmenter won his last time out against the Padres. It was his third win in a nine-day span -- one of those came in relief in extra innings. He was first D-back to do that since Randy Johnson in the 2001 World Series.

home_pitcher_note: Harang found himself in a handful of jams during his last outing against Philly, but avoided the big hit as he threw seven innings of two-run ball in the win. The veteran right-hander has allowed two earned runs or fewer in 13 of his 17 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger has pitched well in his second stint in the Majors this year. In three starts since his recall, he has a 2.70 ERA. He does not have a win to show for it as the D-backs have scored two runs in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wood struggled to communicate with recently promoted catching prospect Christian Bethancourt early in his most recent start before the two finally got on the same page. The left-hander retired the final 11 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Miley had his finest game of the year last time out, taking a two-hit shutout into the ninth against the Pirates. Two batters into the ninth, Miley was removed and the Pirates rallied for a 3-2 win.

home_pitcher_note: After winning the first five starts of his big league career, Anderson has lost his last four, including his most recent outing vs. the Pirates when he lasted just 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler tossed his third straight quality start Wednesday against the Phillies. He pitched six shutout innings and allowed three hits and a walk while striking out seven. Hitters are batting .225 against him, which is the lowest mark in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Nuno makes his debut with the D-backs after being acquired from the Yankees for Brandon McCarthy on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: In his return to the rotation Thursday, Hand threw 99 pitches in five-plus innings. Holding a 2-0 lead in the sixth, he loaded the bases with no outs and was eventually charged with three runs and a no-decision. The lefty is 1-11 in 18 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter's first-inning woes continued in his most recent start, snapping a streak of three consecutive victories. He owns a 6.00 ERA in the first frame compared to a 3.61 ERA in all other innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi has worked at least six innings in four straight starts. But he has just one win to show for it. Miami has lost the other three. Eovaldi opened the road trip giving up three runs in six innings at St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has shaved nearly a run off his ERA while allowing one earned run in 23 1/3 innings spanning his last three starts. If Lincecum can win, he'd equal his highest victory total by the All-Star break since he was 9-4 in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Bolsinger got the run support in his most recent start that he lacked in his previous two, but he surrendered seven runs (five earned) against the Braves. He has pitched at least six innings in three of his past five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong has compiled a 3.06 ERA in 10 starts this year at AT&T Park, yet the Giants are 4-6 in those games. He has allowed two home runs in his last 14 games after allowing five long balls in his first four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miley is coming off two strong starts. Last time out in Atlanta, he held the Braves to one run over 6 2/3 innings. The start prior, he allowed just two runs over eight innings while striking out 10 Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Oddly, Bumgarner has struggled at pitcher-friendly AT&T Park this year, where he's 3-5 with a 5.16 ERA. Lifetime, he owns more sensible statistics at home, where he's 26-21 with a 3.18 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Nuno was acquired July 6 by the D-backs from the Yankees for Brandon McCarthy and cash. He was impressive in his debut, tossing seven shutout innings against the Marlins. He is starting in place of Chase Anderson.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill will make his first Major League start since April 15 on Friday after seven outings with Class A Visalia and Triple-A Reno. Cahill struggled in his first Major League stint this year, but he had a 3.49 ERA in six starts with Reno.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson is coming off his worst performance of the season -- a 3 2/3-inning outing that included nine earned runs, seven hits and four walks in a loss to the Braves. Of his 19 outings this year, only five have been quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miley ended the first half on a high note, giving up only three runs in his last three starts. In 21 2/3 innings in his final three outings, he struck out 22 Pirates, Braves and Giants batters and lowered his ERA from 4.78 on June 24 to 4.18.
away_pitcher_note: Wood struggled against the Braves last Sunday, giving up seven earned in the first three innings. He's 2-4 with a 5.29 ERA in six career games vs. the D-backs, including a nine-strikeout performance in his first win of 2014 in April.

away_pitcher_note: Morales' last appearances was a credible one in relief. He replaced an injured Brett Anderson and held the Cubs to one run and two hits in three innings, and he was in position to win before bullpen woes led to a 12-inning loss.

away_pitcher_note: Miley gave up two more home runs on Aug. 10, a regular problem for him this season. He went six innings against the Rockies, giving up three runs.

away_pitcher_note: Cahill has turned in four straight quality starts. He was demoted to the bullpen in April and to the Minor Leagues in June. Last time out against the Marlins, he allowed two runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Hernandez didn't have his best stuff in his third Dodgers start. He allowed eight hits and four runs (three earned) in five innings against the Padres. But Hernandez has pitched well in his last seven starts overall, going 4-1 with a 2.36 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: The rookie turned in his most efficient outing of the year against the Giants on Monday by using 90 pitches to finish seven innings. He gave up two earned runs and struck out seven while snapping a five-game losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has struggled with his command in his last two outings, walking a combined seven batters in only seven innings. The results have not been pretty, as he has allowed 11 runs (10 earned) in those two starts.
away_pitcher_note: He'll start despite leaving his previous outing early with a thumb contusion that was reminiscent of the thumb issues that prematurely ended his 2013 season. He's allowed three earned runs or less in eight of his last 10 starts.

away_pitcher_note: Entering his last start, Cahill was on a roll, picking up five straight quality starts. That came crashing to an end in his outing against Dodgers on Aug. 26, as the former All-Star gave up eight runs (six earned) in 3 1/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Collmenter has thrown gems in his last two outings. After pitching 8 1/3 innings against the Padres on Aug. 22, he faced the Rockies in his last start and gave up one run on two hits in a game the D-backs eventually won on a go-ahead grand slam.

home_pitcher_note: After three consecutive so-so outings, Kennedy rediscovered his mid-90s fastball on his way to a gem in a no-decision against the Dodgers the last time out. He allowed one run on four hits in seven innings with three walks and eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado will be making his first start since April 10. He made two starts to open the year and compiled an 11.05 ERA before being sent to the bullpen. An improved breaking ball has earned him another chance.

away_pitcher_note: Nuno had arguably the best start of his career against the Rockies on Aug. 30, pitching eight innings and giving up only one run on two hits. However, the Rockies shut out the D-backs, who are now 1-9 in Nuno's starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: After being on the DL for 15 days with a strained right gluteus muscle, Ryu was triumphant in his return. The left-hander held San Diego to one run on four hits in seven innings, striking out seven to earn his 14th win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson pitched well his last time out against the Rockies, allowing one run over six innings. The outing came on the heels of two sub-par performances for him. Anderson has exceeded his innings total from a year ago.

away_pitcher_note: Cahill has struggled with command in his past two starts. Last time out against the Padres, he walked six in four innings. Prior to those starts he had put together a string of five straight quality starts.

away_pitcher_note: Miley went seven innings on 85 pitches in his last start, allowing the Padres one earned run, but got a no-decision. He last won July 30 at Cincinnati, allowing no earned runs in 6 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Collmenter allowed one earned run in seven innings in his last start to beat the Padres, 6-1. He's one victory from a career-high, and 3 1/3 innings shy of matching a career-best 154 1/3 innings pitched set in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy threw six stellar innings against a very good Tigers lineup in his last start. He allowed two unearned runs, struck out three and walked zero. The veteran looks rejuvenated since his insertion into a playoff race at the Trade Deadline.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado returned to the D-backs' rotation Sept. 4 vs. the Padres, allowing no earned runs in five innings to win, 5-1. This will be just his fourth game started during a season spent mostly in the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Nuno has been outstanding since coming over from the Yankees in a July deal. In 11 starts for Arizona he has a 3.16 ERA, but does not have a win to show for his efforts as the D-backs have struggled to score runs for him.
away_pitcher_note: Stults has a 4.86 ERA and 10 losses away from Petco Park but has kept the Padres in both of his starts against the D-backs this season, posting a 3.97 ERA. His ERA in the second half is more than a run better (3.74) than the first half (4.98).

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has impressed since being called up from Double-A Mobile in early May. Last time out against the Dodgers, he allowed just two runs on four hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ross had his club-record streak of 14 consecutive quality starts end the last time out against the Rockies when he couldn't get the final out of the sixth inning. He allowed three runs over 5 1/3 innings, three runs on a second-inning home run.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill is still a work in progress after a midseason demotion to the Minors to work on his mechanics. He has walked 10 batters in his last two starts spanning 9 2/3 innings. He has not won since Aug. 15.
away_pitcher_note: Despaigne was outdueled by Clayton Kershaw for the second time this season in his last outing. The right-hander had problems locating from the get-go, leading to a 4 1/3 inning start in which he allowed seven runs (six earned) on eight hits.

away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong described his last outing, also against the D-backs, as "wildly effective." He threw 6 2/3 scoreless innings, but will look to have better command this time. He's 1-1 with a 3.91 ERA in four 2014 starts against Arizona.

away_pitcher_note: After excelling against Arizona in his last start, Peavy improved to 5-1 with a 1.12 ERA in his last six starts. In nine starts since being acquired by the Giants at the Trade Deadline, Peavy has allowed 15 earned runs in 59 innings.

away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Bumgarner became the fifth left-hander in franchise history to reach the 200-strikeout plateau in a season. He's 4-2 with a 2.73 ERA in 11 games (10 starts) at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Flande has a 5.73 ERA in his eight starts and has made six scoreless relief appearances. But he replaces Franklin Morales for this start, and the Rockies haven't given up on counting on him for rotation depth in 2015.
away_pitcher_note: Nuno has been a hard-luck loser in several of his outings with the D-backs, but his last start was one of his worst since joining the team in July. The southpaw surrendered six runs to the Padres in only five innings of work Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles has devoted the latter part of this season to learning to mix in his newly developed changeup, and he is getting the hang of it. In a loss to the Cards (three runs in six innings) he got grounders with the changeup.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie Anderson will make his last start of the year against the Rockies as the D-backs try to limit his innings. While he hasn't gone deep into games lately, he also hasn't given up more than two runs in any of his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Butler will be making his first start in the Majors since surrendering six runs in 5 1/3 innings in his debut against the Dodgers back on June 6. The Rockies' No. 2 prospect has a 3.58 ERA in 18 starts at Double-A this season.
away_pitcher_note: After a string of solid starts in August, Cahill has had a rough go of it in his last four outings. He has not pitched more than 5 2/3 innings since Aug. 20, and he has a 9.53 ERA in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Despite setting a career high with seven strikeouts, Bergman allowed six runs to the Dodgers last time for his worst start since returning from a fractured non-pitching hand. He allowed one run in 5 1/3 innings in his only previous start vs. Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Miley recovered from a poor outing against the Giants on Sept. 9 with a stellar performance vs. the same team Monday. Miley commanded his pitches well and went seven innings without issuing a walk -- the first walk-free game he had since July 1.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco has been pitching better recently and was solid against the Tigers on Tuesday. He threw eight scoreless innings in a no-decision and has a 3.09 ERA over his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: There was some talk that Collmenter was fatigued after he struggled against the Marlins on Aug. 17, but in his five starts since then, he has compiled a 1.01 ERA. Last time out, he allowed two runs over eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gibson struggled early against the Tigers but settled down to get his 12th win. The right-hander gave up four runs on seven hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chafin will be making his third big league start. He tossed five shutout innings on Aug. 13 before returning to Triple-A. He was recalled in September, and his last time out, he allowed two runs over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes has been Minnesota's best pitcher this season and will get one more start. The right-hander has gone at least eight innings in eight straight starts and has a 2.65 ERA over that span.
away_pitcher_note: Nuno is looking for his first win in a D-backs uniform after coming over from the Yankees in July. In 13 starts for the D-backs, he has a 3.78 ERA. Last time out against the Rockies, he allowed three runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill desperately would like to finish what has been a dreadful 2014 season on a positive note. After putting together a few good starts, he has a 9.00 ERA over his past two. His last win was Aug. 15.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Wacha's final chance to prove himself ready to be a factor in October. He threw 78 pitches on Saturday (his most since returning from injury) but is still searching for crisp command, especially with his changeup.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a frustrating season for Miley, who has not been able to put together a stretch of consistent success. After pitching well two starts ago against the Giants, he allowed six runs in 4 1/3 innings against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn is winless in his last three starts even though he has given up five runs over those 21 innings. He has allowed three runs or fewer in 28 of his 32 starts and should surpass the 200-inning mark for the second time in his career.

away_pitcher_note: Greinke has won three straight decisions although he had to battle to make it through six innings in his last outing against the Angels. His 1.68 ERA continues to lead the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Corbin's 16th start after missing all of 2014 and the first three months of this year following Tommy John surgery. Though he didn't pitch well his last time out, the five starts prior he had a 1.44 ERA.
