home_pitcher_note: After a win on Opening Day with seven strong innings (one earned run on two hits), Kershaw allowed four runs on eight hits in six innings on the road against the Rockies. He'll look to bounce back as the Dodgers begin a six-game homestand.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke beat the Indians in his last outing, allowing just one run over 6 2/3 innings. He has pitched well in both of his starts this year after an uneven 2016 campaign. This will be his first time facing Clayton Kershaw.

home_pitcher_note: Maeda has struggled in two starts this season but picked up the win in his last appearance at Colorado. He's lasted just five innings in each start and has allowed seven runs on 11 hits. Opponents are batting .306 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin was outstanding in his last start against the Indians, allowing just four hits over six scoreless innings in a 3-2 Arizona win. He struggled last year and finished the season in the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Rich Hill will be activated off the disabled list to make this start, after missing one turn with a recurring finger blister. Hill?s signature curveball is hard to hit, but it?s also hard to throw without tearing up his finger.
away_pitcher_note: Walker had only himself to blame for the 4-1 loss he suffered in his last start. His bases-loaded throwing error on a dribbler to the right of the mound started a chain of events where all three runners scored.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy, who missed most of the past two seasons following Tommy John surgery, has been a pleasant surprise so far. He's coming off a strong effort against the Cubs at Wrigley Field with six scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ray got the win in his last start against the Giants as he tossed 6 2/3 shutout innings. Ray did walk five, but managed to get himself out of a couple of jams.

home_pitcher_note: Cosart made the most of his fill-in start, tossing four scoreless in Colorado and earning himself a more permanent spot in the rotation as Luis Perdomo deals with shoulder inflammation. Cosart has added a biting slider to his arsenal this year.
away_pitcher_note: Miller held the Giants scoreless for four innings in his last start before a three-run fifth spelled the end of his night and led to a 6-2 loss. Miller was impressive this spring and in his first start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander is searching for consistency after an up-and-down first three starts. He tossed 6 2/3 scoreless against the Dodgers, but sandwiched that start with two rough outings on the road. In 14 games against Arizona, Chacin owns a 3.04 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke struggled in his last start against Clayton Kershaw. His location was not sharp and the Dodgers did a good job of making him come into the strike zone with his fastball. He allowed five runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Through three starts, Richard, a sinkerballer, has been a ground-ball machine, recording 36 groundouts compared with just four outs in the air. He allowed just two fly balls in his most recent start in Atlanta -- but both left the yard.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin was not sharp last time out against the Dodgers. He allowed five runs (three earned) on nine hits over six innings. He has a 3.86 ERA in six career games at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: Walker had it working in his last start against the Dodgers allowing just one run and striking out seven over five innings. He probably would've pitched longer but he felt some back stiffness so the team played it safe.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time already, Wood subs for Rich Hill, who is on the DL with a finger blister. In his other start, Wood made it into the sixth inning against the Cubs and was charged with only one earned run, but he walked five.

home_pitcher_note: Ray did not get the decision last time out against the Dodgers, though he allowed only two runs (one earned) over six innings. He struck out 10 in the game, which the D-backs rallied to win 3-2.
away_pitcher_note: Maeda was the surprising workhorse of the staff last year, but he hasn’t made it past five innings yet in three starts this year. He’s allowed a home run in each of those games and he gets two extra days of rest this time.

home_pitcher_note: Miller beat the Padres in his last start, flashing a fastball that touched 99 mph. Miller allowed just one run of 7 1/3 innings to become the first D-backs pitcher to work into the eighth inning this season.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy struck out eight in five innings against the D-backs, keeping the Dodgers close and continuing his impressive comeback season. He’s the only starter on the club other than Kershaw to pitch at least six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke takes the hill for his fifth start of the season after twirling an eight-inning complete game in his previous outing against San Diego. He’ll look to get revenge on the Padres after his one-run gem resulted in a tough-luck loss.
away_pitcher_note: He’s only made four starts, but thus far Chacin has posted drastic home/road splits. He has yet to allow a run in two starts at Petco Park, but he’s given up 13 in 8 1/3 road innings. Chacin, a former D-back, owns a career 2.83 ERA at Chase Field.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin pitched well at San Diego in his last outing on Thursday, but he still suffered his third loss of the year. Historically, he's pitched better at Chase Field (15-19, 3.62 ERA) so he’ll be happy to face the Padres at home this time around.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander continues to induce ground balls, and his 67 percent GB% is tops in the National League. Through four starts, Richard has already induced six double plays. He’s struggled a bit at Chase Field, however, with a 5.20 career ERA

home_pitcher_note: Godley takes the spot of the injured Shelby Miller in the Arizona rotation. In his last start for Triple-A Reno, Godley allowed just one hit over seven shutout innings. He struck out seven and did not walk a batter.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran righty spent three seasons with Arizona, from 2012-14. His transition back to the rotation has been a seamless one. He owns a 3.44 ERA in three starts and completed his first seven-inning outing since 2014 in Friday’s win over Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Walker’s D-backs career has gotten off to a relatively slow start, but the righty has faced the Giants and the Dodgers twice in four starts. He will mix things up by facing the Padres, who he’s gone 1-1 with a 1.50 ERA against in two career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Oddly enough, Weaver has posted the same line for three straight games. He’s pitched six innings and allowed two earned runs in each. All 10 earned runs Weaver has given up this season have come via the seven home runs he’s allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Although the Dodgers scored five runs off Ray in his last start, the left-hander got the win thanks to an offense that scored 12 runs. He tossed 5 1/3 innings, allowing nine hits and striking out six batters.
away_pitcher_note: The left-handed rookie has been up and down in his four starts but is coming off his best yet -- seven scoreless innings against the Giants on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke was outstanding last time out against the Padres, as he struck out 11 and allowed just one run on six hits over six innings. He has pitched well in four of his five starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson effectively used his fastball-changeup mix for the better part of his last outing, against the Nats, but became undone in the sixth. The lefty has given up four runs or more in each of his five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin allowed two runs on eight hits over seven innings against the Padres in his last start. He fanned seven and walked a pair. The left-hander had his slider working in that game.
away_pitcher_note: Marquez made his 2017 debut amid frigid temperatures and in the rain on a 90-pitch limit Tuesday against the Nats, allowing 12 baserunners and eight runs in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Roark looks to keep his perfect record intact while turning the table on his recent command struggles. In his past two starts, the right-hander allowed five earned runs across 11 2/3 innings (3.86 ERA), but walked seven batters in the process.
away_pitcher_note: Walker toes the rubber on the heels of an eight-inning, two-run gem in which he didn’t walk a batter and tied a career high with 11 strikeouts. The 24-year-old righty will be making his first career start against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 4.57 ERA in 2016, the highest mark for a season in his Nationals career, Gonzalez has rebounded in a big way to being ’17. The lefty is 3-0 with a 1.62 ERA through five starts and he’s completed at least six innings in each.
away_pitcher_note: Ray, who makes his third start away from Chase Field, has fared better on the road so far this season. The left-hander is 1-0 with an 0.71 ERA on the road vs. 1-1 with a 5.60 ERA in three outings at home.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer is set to face the D-backs, who drafted him No. 11 overall in 2006, for the sixth time in his career. The Nationals’ ace has been masterful vs. Arizona, going 4-0 with a 2.65 ERA against the club in five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Shipley will be making his 2017 debut after posting a 3-1 record with a 4.18 ERA over 28 innings for Triple-A Reno. With Shelby Miller out, the 25-year-old will get a chance to stake his claim to a rotation spot.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson has yielded nine homers in 30 1/3 innings. Some stretches have been solid, but the lack of location on the fastball and downward bite on his changeup have left him fighting to stay in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke will get a second crack at the Rockies in as many starts. This time he'll look to keep the ball in the yard, as the Rockies hit a trio of home runs off him in his previous outing.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood was hitless through five innings against the Padres on Tuesday night, but walks were creeping into the performance. Then he gave up five runs in the sixth. He has allowed nine homers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin will look to duplicate his stellar performance against the Rockies in his previous outing, when he tossed 6 1/3 shutout innings and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: The day he learned he had earned NL Rookie of the Month honors, Senzatela held the Padres to three runs (two earned) in six workmanlike innings in a 11-3 victory. He has gone at least six frames in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Walker is coming off his shortest outing of the year Tuesday, lasting just 4.2 innings and throwing a season high 117 pitches against the Nationals. He has yet to be credited with a win on the road in 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Ray was dominant in his last outing against the Nationals. In six innings, he allowed four hits and a walk, with 10 strikeouts, and both runs came as the result of questionable defensive plays behind him.
away_pitcher_note: After battling pitch-tipping, then fastball command in April, Verlander is showing signs of rounding into form around his usual time. He has tossed seven quality innings his past two starts, beating Cleveland last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Godley will be called up from Triple-A Reno to start. This is his second audition in the battle to replace the injured Shelby Miller in the rotation. On April 26 against the Padres, Godley allowed two runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Boyd has pitched deep into each of his past two games but been stung by low run support. He's gone 14 2/3 innings combined over those two outings, allowing six earned runs on 12 hits and five walks while striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke is bouncing back in a big way to start the season after a down 2016. The veteran went 13-7 in '16 despite a 4.37 ERA, his worst since 2010. This year, however, he’s trending back toward his old ways, going 3-2 with a 3.09 ERA in 7 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cole was at his best against the Brewers last week, allowing just one run, a solo homer, in seven innings. Despite his 1-3 record, the right-hander owns a 2.37 ERA through six starts since his five-run Opening Day outing.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin makes his eighth start of the season on the heels of his worst outing so far in 2017. The lefty allowed a season-high eight earned runs while tying a season low with four innings pitched in a loss against the Rockies on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Glasnow tossed a career-high 6 1/3 innings his last time out, but was undone by a solo homer and the Pirates’ defensive miscues. The rookie is making his first appearance against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Walker finished April with his best start of the year, going eight innings with 11 K's in a win over the Padres. Since the calendar flipped to May, the righty has struggled to work deep into games, having to be pulled after 4 2/3 and 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Williams makes his second start after opening the season in the bullpen. He hopes it goes better than his first effort, when he was charged with six earned runs on seven hits and a walk in three innings Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Ray was not sharp in his last start against the Tigers, issuing five walks over five innings of work. That outing came on the heels of a dominant performance against the Nats, in which he fanned 10 in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nova has allowed more than two earned runs in only one of his previous seven starts. On the season, he is 3-3 but with a 2.23 ERA and has 29 strikeouts to just three walks.

home_pitcher_note: Godley will make his third big league start of the year and his second straight in place of the injured Shelby Miller. Last time out against the Tigers, Godley allowed just one run over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: In nearly every one of his first six starts, Wheeler has battled the same issue, struggling to complete six innings in less than 100 pitches. He made modest strides in that department last time out, needing 95 pitches to get through six.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke flirted with a no-hitter last time out against the Pirates. Gregory Polanco got the first hit when he led off the eighth with a home run down the right-field line. Greinke struck out 11 and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Taking the rotation spot of Rafael Montero, Milone held the Giants to two runs in five innings his most recent time out. If he continues submitting outings like that, he should hang onto a starting job until Steven Matz is ready to come off the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin picked up a win against the Pirates in his last start thanks to a big night from the offense. The D-backs scored seven runs in the third and four in the fourth to give Corbin plenty of support.
away_pitcher_note: It has been a trying few weeks for Harvey. After serving a three-game team suspension, Harvey walked five and allowed five earned runs over five innings in Milwaukee. He is 0-3 with a 10.43 ERA over his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran righty is coming off his best start of the season, in which he allowed one run over six innings against the White Sox, his first outing without allowing a homer. Weaver’s 51 HRs allowed since the start of 2016 are the most in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Walker was not helped by his defense in his last two starts. He's allowed seven runs over those outings and only four of them were earned.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander set a career high with nine strikeouts in his last start. He’s whiffing hitters at a 24 percent clip this year, up eight percent from last season, largely because he’s honed a sharp slider to complement his sinker.
away_pitcher_note: Ray has struggled in his last two starts. He allowed five runs over five innings against the Tigers and then gave up four runs and lasted just four innings last time out against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty struggled to command his offspeed pitches in the first inning of his last start, allowing five runs in the frame. But he would settle in for six innings. Richard’s home ERA is nearly a point and a half lower than his road mark.
away_pitcher_note: Godley will make his fourth start in place of Shelby Miller, who is out for the year after Tommy John surgery. Last time out, Godley allowed just one run in 6 2/3 innings against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start Greinke allowed four runs in 6 2/3 innings against the Mets. It was just the second time this year that he allowed four or more runs in a game. Greinke has won his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, who hasn't won since April 24, takes on the D-backs in the series opener of an Interleague series in Phoenix.

home_pitcher_note: Over his last three starts Corbin has allowed 16 runs in 16 innings, causing his ERA to rise from 2.29 to 4.38. Corbin got a no-decision in his last start against the Mets, in which he allowed four runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Covey, who has a 7.64 ERA in his first seven starts of the season, will look for better results Tuesday when he faces the D-backs for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado will start in place of Taijuan Walker, who is on the DL with a blister. This will be his first start since Aug. 22, 2015, and the game will likely be a bullpen game given that he has not thrown more than three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana was virtually unhittable in his last start against the Mariners, allowing one triple over eight innings. Quintana struck out seven and allowed one run, but finished with his 61st career no-decision, the most in the Majors since 2012.

home_pitcher_note: After posting an 8.24 ERA in his first four starts, Davies has begun to settle into a groove. He is 4-0 with a 3.38 ERA over his last five outings, including a win in San Diego last week in which he completed six innings for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: Ray bounced back after a couple of poor starts to dominate the Padres. He allowed just two hits over 7 2/3 scoreless innings at Petco Park. Ray walked three and struck out six in the win.

home_pitcher_note: Guerra, who strained his right calf during a third-inning at-bat on Opening Day, returns to action after a seven-week absence. He threw 91 pitches in his second rehab start, so he won’t be on a strict pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Godley has pitched well since replacing Shelby Miller in the rotation. Last time out he gave up three runs on eight hits over seven innings as he was outdueled by San Diego's Clayton Richard.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson had a 1.12 ERA after his first four starts but has gone backward since then. Including a loss at Wrigley Field in which he surrendered a season-high six earned runs, he owns a 7.30 ERA in his five most recent outings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has been on a roll. He's won his last four starts and his last five decisions overall. Initially it was his slider he credited for the streak, then his changeup, now he feels he has all his pitches working.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson is still seeking his first win of the season at Miller Park after taking a loss against the Blue Jays in the opener of this homestand. Fourteen of his 16 walks this season have been issued at home.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin battled in his last start and managed to get through six innings against the White Sox. Chicago touched him for eight hits and three runs, but Corbin managed to get the win in a 5-4 Arizona victory.

home_pitcher_note: Williams is coming off one of his best starts of the year, having struck out a career-high six while scattering six hits and allowing three earned runs in five innings. He was strong in his last outing vs. Arizona, striking out four in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado's last outing earned him another start on Monday, manager Torey Lovullo said Friday. In his first start this season on Wednesday, Delgado allowed just one run and three hits over four innings in a win over the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Nova pitched 8 1/3 innings in his last start and has worked at least six innings in all 10 of his starts, including his last outing vs. the D-backs, on May 14. In that game, Nova struck out four and allowed three earned runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ray provided the D-backs with seven scoreless innings against the Brewers on Thursday. The lefty dealt nine strikeouts, allowing zero walks, and has a scoreless streak of 15 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl struggled in his last outing, allowing eight hits and five earned runs in just 4 1/3 innings against the Mets on Friday. He has never faced the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Godley lowered his ERA under two after dealing six scoreless innings against the Brewers on Friday. The right-hander has recorded a pickoff in back-to-back games and has four straight quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Locke, on the DL with left shoulder tendinitis, is set to be reinstated Thursday. The lefty last appeared in a big league game on Sept. 24 for the Piates vs. the Nationals. He had a 1.77 ERA in four rehab starts.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke's five-game winning streak was snapped in a 6-1 loss to the Brewers on Saturday. The righty dealt three perfect innings, before allowing five earned runs. In the month of May, Greinke finished 4-1 with a 3.28 ERA and 44 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Urena set career highs for strikeouts (seven) and walks (six) in his last start. He has been able to effectively minimize damage since joining the rotation, but he hasn't gone as many as six full innings in three straight outings.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin went less than six innings for just the third time this season in his last outing vs. the Brewers, yielding seven earned runs in four innings. He'll try to improve after a month of May in which he posted a 9.00 ERA in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez has plenty of history vs. the D-backs, facing them 10 times in his career with a 2-2 record and 3.94 ERA in 61 2/3 innings. He registered his first win of 2017 in his last start and has thrown six innings in each of his past four outings.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado's second start of the season went swimmingly, striking out eight and allowing one earned run 5 2/3 innings. He earned that second start after a strong spot start in place of Taijuan Walker (blister).

home_pitcher_note: With Justin Nicolino on the DL, Worley moves from the bullpen to the rotation, and he will make his third start since being called up from Triple-A. He last started May 27, giving up two runs in five innings vs. the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: A top pitcher for Triple-A Reno, Shipley looks to rebound from his only start with the D-backs this season. It was a four-inning outing against Washington. He went four innings, giving up five hits, six walks and three runs in a loss.

home_pitcher_note: With wins in each of his last three starts, which preceded a three-game skid, Ray looks to keep the win streak alive. He did not allow a run in any of the three wins, going 23 2/3 innings, allowing just eight hits and three walks while fanning 25.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie righty has dazzled with eight strikeouts over five innings in each of his first two starts. In MLB history, only Stephen Strasburg and Masahiro Tanaka have begun their careers with eight K's in each of their first three starts.

home_pitcher_note: A winner in five of his last six starts, Greinke won his most recent outing by throwing seven innings in Miami, giving up just four hits and one earned run. He struck out eight and walked only two.
away_pitcher_note: The righty sinkerballer is inducing grounders at a 66 percent clip this season, and his effectiveness at the bottom of the zone was on display in his last start when he threw seven innings of one-run ball against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin looks to snap a two-game losing streak during which he's yielded 19 hits and 12 earned runs over his last nine innings. He last won on May 23, limiting the White Sox to three runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty has allowed just one run in each of his two starts against Arizona, including a 96-pitch complete game on May 21. Richard’s 58 percent ground-ball rate is tops in the National League among qualified pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado shifted from the bullpen to the rotation after Taijuan Walker was placed on the DL with a blister. In three starts since, Delgado is 0-1 with a 1.80 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Davies faced the D-backs on May 25, he allowed three earned runs on seven hits over six innings. But in his latest start, a win over the Dodgers on Sunday, the right-hander did not allow a hit for 4 1/3 innings and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: Godley took a no-decision after a quality start his last time out, May 31 against the Pirates. This will be his seventh start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: The split-finger specialist struggled with command against the Giants, throwing only 52 of 90 pitches for strikeouts. That lower-than-usual strike percentage meant Guerra wasn’t able to consistently get to his splitter, a strikeout pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Ray has won four straight starts and allowed one earned run over that span, in 30 1/3 innings pitched. He tossed seven shutout innings vs. the Brewers on on May 25.
away_pitcher_note: With 7 2/3 more scoreless innings against the Giants on Tuesday, Anderson extended his scoreless streak to 21 2/3 innings over his last three starts. He has 22 strikeouts and five walks in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Farmer will make his third start of the season with a 13-inning scoreless streak, tied for the longest in the American League and the longest by a Tiger at any point this season. He also has 16 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke is coming off a win against the Padres in which he gave up three earned run in five innings, tied for his shortest outing of the season. In 28 career games against the Tigers, Greinke is 13-7 with a solid 2.79 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann is coming off his best back-to-back starts of 2017 -- allowing three runs over 12 innings. Current D-backs batters haven’t seen much of him, going 11-for-51 (.216) combined.
away_pitcher_note: Walker will make his first start in nearly a month after developing a blister in a start at San Diego on May 19. Walker has cleared all of the hurdles the club asked him to, but he is expected to be on a pitch count watch for this outing.

home_pitcher_note: Nola followed arguably the best start of his career June 6 in Atlanta - one run in eight innings - with a loss Sunday in St. Louis. He allowed three runs in five innings, and hasn't pitched more than five innings in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin's win over the Padres on June 8 was a step in the right direction, being the first game in 6 starts in which he did not allow a homer. He is still looking to right the ship, however, having allowed at least 3 earned runs in 7 straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff is still searching for that elusive first win of 2017. He's the first Phillies pitcher to go winless in his first 13 starts since Cliff Lee in 2012. He holds a 5.46 ERA at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Godley is coming off one of his best starts of the season, giving up two runs on two hits in 6 2/3 innings to earn his second win. It was his first start back in the rotation after a brief stint at Triple-A while the D-backs needed bullpen depth.

home_pitcher_note: Lively could post his fourth straight Major League start of seven innings with at most three earned runs allowed. He has a 3.00 ERA after three starts to begin his career.
away_pitcher_note: Ray has won each of his previous five starts, and has allowed just one earned run during that span. His ERA has dropped from 4.57 to 2.62 during this run, since giving up nine runs in a two-game stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Two games, opposite experiences for Marquez against Arizona. He fanned eight in six scoreless innings at Chase Field on April 30, then gave up five runs in six innings May 5.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has been one of the National League’s best pitchers this season, but a big inning with five earned runs hurt him in his last start against the Tigers on June 13. Greinke allowed just two runs and struck out seven in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hoffman gave up seven hits and three walks in five innings in his last start, at home against the Giants. The good news was he escaped the trouble and gave up just one run.
away_pitcher_note: Walker will be making his second start since rejoining the D-backs rotation after a blister landed him on the DL. Walker allowed one run on six hits and had six strikeouts against Detroit in his first game back.

home_pitcher_note: Senzatela's strikeouts are trending up -- 12 in the last two games, but he managed just 10 total innings and gave up 13 hits and nine runs.
away_pitcher_note: Godley has not allowed more than three runs in any of his starts this year. Last time out against the Phillies, he allowed one run on five hits over 5 2/3 innings. This will be his first start against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin's normal day would have been Thursday, but he flipped spots with Zack Godley. This will be his second straight time facing the Phils. Corbin allowed two earned runs over six innings and got the win last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Leiter makes his first big league start after posting a 4.74 ERA in 12 relief appearances earlier this season with the Phillies. He just threw six scoreless innings in his last start with Triple-A, but still has a 5.93 ERA in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ray has been on a roll over his last six starts, going 5-0 with a 1.06 ERA. All those games were Arizona victories. He got a no-decision against the Phillies in his last start, allowing four runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ben Lively could become the first Phillie to post five straight quality starts to begin his Major League career since 1943. He'll face the D-backs for the second consecutive time after giving up three runs in six innings in the series finale Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado has shuttled between the bullpen and starting rotation, depending on need. He is making a spot start in order to give the rest of the starters an extra day of rest. His last start was on June 9.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson hopes his last start gets him back on track. He allowed one run in seven innings against the Cardinals after posting a 6.89 ERA in his previous nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke's last start fell apart in the eighth inning, when Rockies third baseman Nolan Arenado drove home two with a triple. Greinke had allowed just two runs to that point.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta has looked like a different pitcher in his past two starts. He has struck out 19 batters in 13 innings. He has 10 swinging strikes on his four-seamer in each of those starts. His previous high in a start: five.

home_pitcher_note: Walker has bounced back nicely in June after missing nearly a month with a blister on his right index finger. He is 2-0 in two starts this month with a 3.27 ERA with 14 strikeouts in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his career, Martinez has made four starts and three relief appearances against the D-backs, with a 2.86 ERA in 28 1/3 innings. He hasn't faced Arizona since a May 2016 start in which he allowed four earned runs in five innings.

away_pitcher_note: Oviedo will look to put behind him a string of rough outings, though he picked it up with his last start at Triple-A. In his last MLB start, the No. 9 prospect said he tried to get too perfect in avoiding meatballs, which manifested poorly, with three earned runs across just two-plus frames.

home_pitcher_note: Frankoff is making his third big league start. In his last start he took the loss, allowing five earned runs over four innings at Coors Field. Frankoff made two relief appearances for the Mariners in 2020.
away_pitcher_note: Let down by his offense, Wainwright earned a no-decision Sunday despite eight shutout innings of one-hit ball vs. the Cubs. It was his second consecutive scoreless home start and a rebound from his previous outing, when he was tagged for six runs in four frames in San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock had been scheduled to start Thursday, but he was scratched that morning after becoming ill (non-COVID related) the previous night. Peacock has appeared in 10 games (two starts) for the D-backs this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kim was one pitch away from completing six innings for the first time this season on Monday, but a fateful changeup chased him after 5 2/3 frames and handed him his second straight loss. The lefty has issued six walks over his last two games.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly has been the D-backs' most consistent pitcher this season. In his last start against the Giants, he allowed two runs over six innings, lowering his May ERA to 3.52. Kelly's last win came on April 27 against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: deGrom had been scheduled to start Sunday's series finale against the Braves until rain washed that one away. He'll instead receive an extra day of rest before taking on the D-backs, whom he's already beaten once this season.

home_pitcher_note: Smith opened the season in the rotation, but he was moved to the bullpen after one start in which he allowed four runs (three earned) in three innings against the Padres on April 3. He then posted a 2.70 ERA in 18 relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Although the Mets have won three of Stroman's last four starts, those victories have come against three of the Majors' worst lineups. He'll face a stiffer test against the D-backs and their roughly average offense.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has struggled in his past two starts, allowing 14 runs (11 earned) over 10 innings in losses to the Rockies and Cardinals. Those outings came after he had a 1.32 ERA in his previous six starts.
away_pitcher_note: It's been a rocky sophomore season for Peterson, who has scattered some strong starts among a series of poor ones. Peterson has yet to throw more than 93 pitches in any start, and oddly, lefties are hitting .341 against him.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers have pitched their starters on extra rest for most of this season, but Anderson will be on a standard five-day schedule after throwing 85 pitches in 3 1/3 innings in Game 2 of a doubleheader at Washington on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: In his season debut last Thursday, Duplantier gave up four runs and seven hits in 4 2/3 innings, striking out five in a no-decision to the Cardinals. He'll open up the road series for the D-backs in what will be the fifth start of his young big league career.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta has featured a slider and changeup more often than a heater this year, but when asked what's been working best, the answer was still his fastball. Among qualified starters, only Jacob deGrom has a higher strikeout rate than Peralta's 37.2 percent.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock was victorious in his last start for the D-backs on Sunday, throwing six innings and giving up two runs. He has found some success pitching away from Chase Field this season, posting a 0.79 ERA in 11 1/3 innings on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Woodruff has delivered 10 straight quality starts, the eighth pitcher in franchise history to do so and the first since CC Sabathia had 13 in a row in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Kelly will look to bounce back after giving up five runs on nine hits in 6 2/3 innings against the Mets on Monday. Despite struggling against the Mets, Kelly has given the D-backs some durability, going at least six innings in each of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Burnes has had to work harder in recent starts, going 0-3 with a 3.86 ERA in his last five outings compared to a 0.37 ERA in his first four games of 2021. He has at least seven strikeouts in every start this season.
away_pitcher_note: Smith is making his second start since returning to the rotation. He opened the year in the rotation, but he was shifted to the bullpen after one start. Last time out against the Mets. he allowed two runs on three hits and one walk over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bassitt is coming off his shortest start of the season, going just four innings against the Mariners in his last outing. Since the beginning of May, Bassitt has only walked five batters and allowed three home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Duplantier will be making his third start of the year for the D-backs. Last Thursday against the Brewers, Duplantier allowed five runs over four innings. In two starts for Triple-A Reno this year, he had a 7.71 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Manaea pitched a masterpiece in his last time out, throwing a shutout with eight strikeouts against the Mariners. In his last four starts, Manaea owns a 1.69 ERA with 25 strikeouts to seven walks.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock was uncharacteristically erratic in his last start against the Brewers. The rookie came into that outing having walked three batters all season, but ended up walking four Milwaukee batters. In four starts this season, Peacock owns a 3.86 ERA across 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly has been a workhorse for the D-backs, having gone at least six innings in five consecutive starts. Since the start of May, Kelly has a 4.36 ERA across 43 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohtani is coming off a strong start against the Mariners, striking out 10 batters without issuing a walk over six innings. He allowed two runs on four hits and picked up his second win.

home_pitcher_note: Smith will be making his third start since rejoining the starting rotation. He opened the year as the No. 3 starter, but he was moved to the bullpen after his first outing. Over his last two starts, he is 0-1 with a 2.70 ERA and 10 strikeouts in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cobb has pitched well over his last four starts, logging a 2.25 ERA and 26 strikeouts in 24 innings. He went seven innings in a win over the Mariners on Saturday, though he was hurt by a grand slam.

home_pitcher_note: Duplantier is making his fourth start of the year for the D-backs. In his previous start on Tuesday against Oakland, he allowed four runs on two hits while walking three over three innings. He has not lasted longer than 4 2/3 innings in any of his starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Sandoval has fared well in his four starts this year with a 3.15 ERA and 19 strikeouts in 20 innings. He struck out 10 over six innings against Seattle in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: After going 5-0 with a 1.75 ERA over his first six starts of the year, Wood has hit a rough patch, going 0-3 with a 7.29 ERA over his past four outings. He is 5-4 with a 2.96 ERA in 19 career outings (11 starts) against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock was forced to leave his last start against the A's when he was hit on his pitching hand by a comebacker with two outs in the second inning. This is his sixth start of the year and first career appearance against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Littell will make his second start as the Giants' opener this season, with left-hander Sammy Long likely serving as the bulk guy out of the bullpen. The two combined for five innings of one-run ball on one hit against the Rangers on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Young will make his first start of the season and his first since last September.  In four career starts vs. the Giants, the lefty is 2-2 with a 4.35 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: DeSclafani tossed his second shutout of the season in his last outing. He allowed just two hits while fanning eight at Nationals Park. The righty will face the D-backs for the seventh time in his career, owning a 2.70 ERA against the club.
away_pitcher_note: Kelly allowed three runs on four hits over five innings last time out against the Angels. He faced the Giants on May 26 and allowed two runs on five hits in six innings. He has not recorded a win since April 27.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman took his first loss of the season last Saturday, when he allowed two runs over four innings against the Nationals. He is 3-1 with a 2.43 ERA in six career games (five starts) against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: The D-backs' ace will make his much-anticipated return after missing the last month with a right UCL sprain. Gallen's last appearance with the D-backs came on May 7, when he allowed one earned run across six innings to the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Since transitioning back to the starting rotation, Smith has done a solid job of helping eat up innings. In his last three starts, Smith has a 4.40 ERA across 14 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After being dominant through May, Bauer has struggled to find success in June. In his last two starts, Bauer is 0-2 with a 5.11 ERA. He has struck out 15 in 12 1/3 innings of work, but has also walked six. Opponents have a .300 batting average off the right-hander in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock, who has been thrust into rotation duty due to injuries, will look to turn around what has been a rough June. In three starts this month, Peacock has allowed nine earned runs in 11 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Buehler has been the Dodgers' most consistent starter this season and he'll look to extend his streak without a loss to 23 consecutive regular-season starts.

home_pitcher_note: Young will make his second start of the year. His first came five days ago, when he tossed four innings before turning things over to Corbin Martin. It's likely that the D-backs will do something similar with Young this time around.
away_pitcher_note: Gonsolin has struggled with his command since being activated from the injured list. In his two starts this season, Gonsolin has walked eight over 5 1/3 innings. He has also recorded nine strikeouts and has posted a 3.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly faced the Brewers earlier this month at American Family Field and did not factor into the decision. He allowed five runs (four earned) over six innings in that game.
away_pitcher_note: After a pair of rough starts against the D-backs and Reds, Anderson was brilliant over seven scoreless innings against Cincinnati on June 15, yielding just one hit while walking one and fanning nine. He went 4 1/3 innings against Arizona on June 3, giving up three runs on eight hits.

home_pitcher_note: Gallen is making his second start since being activated from the injured list. He has had two stints on the IL this year. In his first start back against the Giants at Oracle Park, Gallen allowed four runs on four hits in 2 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta looks to keep his breakout season rolling, coming off another great start in which he gave up two runs on five hits over seven innings against the Reds on Wednesday, walking none and striking out six. His last start against Arizona was on June 4, when he yielded one run on one hit, walking three and fanning nine over 7 1/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Smith will make his fifth start since rejoining the rotation and his sixth start overall. Last time out against the Dodgers he allowed just one hit over six shutout innings. Smith faced the Brewers earlier this month and allowed one run over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff looks to bounce back from a rough start at Colorado, when he gave up five first-inning runs in a 7-3 loss to the Rockies. He'll be making his second start against the D-backs in 2021, having given up two runs on six hits, while walking one and striking out nine on June 5.
